I have several apps that can open pdf files on my device, from an ebook reader to an office app, so I was not sure why I would need another pdf reader. When this app popped as the FAOTD though I figured I would try it out; I am extremely impressed.The app really stands out on two fronts:  TTS let's you pick any TTS installed on your device, including custom and paid ones; other pdf apps I have used force you to use the built in Android one or their own voices which are usually terrible. Pdf Max let's you use your own.Second, it's hands down the best pdf app for markup, offering just about everything you could want for document review.  While I personally don't have much use for those features, if you work with pdfs regularly this is the app you want.The app works flawlessly on Nexus 7 2013, with no lag opening or scrolling through pdf.  Overall if you do a lot of document review and markup, you will appreciate what this app has to offer.Thank you dev and Amazon.

column2: Tools work great but loses files
column3: The app works great for reading and annotating PDFs.  I have a Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1, and I'm finding it fairly intuitive to use the tools to mark up PDFs with the stylus.  But there is a bug or some other problem that has caused me a big headache.  Twice, my marked-up document has disappeared from storage, causing me to have to redo hours' worth of work.  This happened with two different documents.  I carefully saved after each change I made, and I made note of the file name and location, but the next day, in each case, the file was completely gone.  I searched through my entire file system and did not find it, and the storage location itself (PDFMax folder on the internal storage card) had been wiped.Until I find an alternative app, I am saving to my Dropbox account, which is slower and very clunky, and apparently has not saved the changes I re-made after losing the original file.  I really need an app that will reliably save changes and not delete files.  I thought this was it.  It is not.  Too bad, because other than that big deal-breaker, it works very well.

Has a lot of good features. I cant zoom out so that the entire slide fits the height of my screen.  This is not a problem when in vertical mode though, everything is smaller (as expected), but that's why I prefer to edit in landscape mode. When switching from horizontal to vertical mode (vice versa) it teleports your view to somewhere else on the slide and zooms in...this is really annoying especially when annotating/editing.While free hand draw is amazing for writing out text with a stylus, however, the most important feature: typed text option(they call it freetext) does not even come close. The font color default is white...annoying when your first typing out text. The textbox that forms around the typed text is too big, I hate having to resize it to size of text, should make it automatic like in Adobe PDF. The fill in background color option for the textbox is extremely buggy especially when viewing in edit mode. The color wheel is weird and doesn't properly show no color option. There are no options to change type of font, font size, or highlight/underline (etc) the text you've typed out.There's no "save as" option though there is a backup option before each initial edit. The only way to save your file is when you exit the pdf.I can't tap to turn the page, only swiping can do that right now. They should add in the option of "viewing mode" aka full screen mode or maybe just have an area of the screen where I can just tap to turn page instead of bringing up the annoying edit UI.Any edit you make on this app does not do well with other pdf apps such as Adobe PDf app as mentioned by another reviewer. The edits are not visible on Adobe PDF. Not sure if the edits are shown on the computer.They should add more options so I can customize it to my liking.I think I'll stick with the native Adobe PDF app to annotate my lecture notes for now because it's simple and reliable.

column2: Nice app except for one BIG thing
column3: This would be a fantastic app except for one big thing ... highlight, underline and strikethrough all all yellow! That's fine for the highlighter. Strikethrough should be red; underline should be green or bright green. It is impossible to see either of these two on a white background (not all pages are viewable in night mode) and this is how other apps like Adobe do it.Currently, to use underline or strikethrough, you longpress on the word, drag the tabs and then tap on underline or strikethrough. Then you have to tap elsewhere on the page; and then retap the word so it in an editing box, select the color pallete and set the strikethrough or underline color ... EVERY TIME!There are no options to set the default colors of these three actions, and that's what is keeping it from being a great app.

column2: A high quality PDF reader that works fairly well!
column3: Update 6-17-2015I rescanned this software after I reinstalled it.  I did this due to several reviews that claimed malicious code was added like access to your accounts and other items.  While there were some changes to the permissions. they are not catastrophic or particularly invasive and I believe they were added for licensing purposes.  I added more data on the permissions below showing the older and the new permissions list..++++++++++++++++++++++PDF files are very common and I use them all of the time.  I get documents, books and forms from many companies in PDF format and having a good PDF reader is very helpful on your tablet.  This reader is a nice powerful PDF reader and it allows you to mark up your PDF file read and annotate it.  You can even add a voice memo to the file.There is a navigation bar on the LH side of the screen and you can even word search.  You get a full set of tools to use on the PDF and you can copy text, paste, delete, email, rotate the page or even extract pages.This is an office tool that everyone needs for their tablet or smart phone and here is a free offer to get it so you should download it.  I experienced one problem using it on my Samsung Tab 4 when the app stopped working and shut down,  for that I will delete one star.  I had a 232 page document loaded at the time.Original Permissions May 19, 2014:* Record audio* Read and write to external storage* Internet accessPresent Permissions on June 17, 2015:• Read phone status and identity• Record audio• Modify or delete the contents of your USB storage• Full network access• View network connections• View WIFI connections• Install shortcutsThe app does contain a code called Crashlytics but it is targeted at collecting crashlogs to see the possible bugs in their app.The app installed 59.90MB on my device and I have 19.06MB in my device memory and 31.62MB on my SD card.The app also contains Dropbox which is a sharing service to share documents with other people.

Here is a quick summary below:Pro:-Very fast pre-rendering of pages at a low-resolution-Large thumbnail pages on the side bar for quick preview of pages before and after the current pageCon:-Problem displaying text boxes created by other PDF programs without re-adjusting the box size (when text border is being used)-Problem displaying continuous fine lines when the page is zoomed out to show the larger extent of the page-Problem locating the annotations correctly created by other PDF application such as EZ PDF.-Lack the ability to adjust font size for typed notes.Device used to try the program: Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 (10 inch display with 1280x800 resolution)Other full version PDF apps tried before: ezPDF reader, Office Suite, PDF to Go, Polaries Office, Quickoffice, Adobe PDFFULL REVIEW:I have tried many PDF apps before and the one thing I wished most of them have is the large thumbnail display of pages at the side bar like the popular desktop PDF programs such as Adobe PDF and Bluebeam. This features allows users to quickly look up information and have a better sense of where one is at within a chapter. Thus, I decided to give this app a try since I noticed it has the ability to display large thumbnail preview in the side bar.After playing the app for a while, I was disappointed. As listed above, this app has issue displaying text boxes created by other applications. If the box is not large enough it will not show any text inside at all unlike ALL other programs that I have tried. Another disturbing shortcoming is its inability to show fine lines without breaking. I have scanned images of books with tables and charts that appear to have missing borders when  zooming to show the full extent of the page. Worst of all, when loading file with large page size (30" x 42" drawing with vector lines generated by AutoCAD or Revit), the drawings become almost unreadable because I can barely see the lines when the page is zoomed out to show even just a quarter of the drawing. Another glaring problem is the inconsistency to display text and object created by other programs. In one instance, when opening a PDF file annotated by ez PDF, half of the texts and annotations are displayed at a completely wrong location. Finally, I did not find any property menu that allows a user to change the font size of the text annotation. The lack of this particular function forces me to cram large text on document with small page size. On the opposite hand, the single sized text annotation on documents with large page format becomes difficult to find.In short, those flaws make the program not the best choice for users who intent to make a lot of typed annotations and wish to open documents with diagrams, tables and graphics (such as textbook and technical documents). And it is a poor choice for those who would like to open large architectural or engineering drawings especially when the drawings were already annotated by other programs before. I will rather stick to other programs for now before those issues have been resolved by the developer.

column2: One of the Best, and I Have MANY; also NO BAD PERMISSIONS!
column3: Even more popular than Microsoft Word documents are PDFs. In all likelihood, PDFs are the most abundant forms of standalone document people encounter in their daily lives.[PRIVACY: Zero problematic permissions! Yay!]This means a PDF reader is exceedingly important.  This one is more than a reader, it is a powerful annotator, which is one step down from a full-blown editor.  As far as annotators go, this one is very powerful.  It has the usual highlights, bookmarks, and comments. It also has shapes, free style, and many more annotations. It even allows different color combinations, coming close to an image editor in this fashion.Hidden, though, are even more powerful tools, such as the ability to copy, rearrange, concatenate (combine), delete, split (extract), and so forth.Instead of using my tablet for testing, I chose to use my phone which is a ZTE 5" Virgin Mobile Supreme / Sprint Vital.The app handled a >100MB file with hundreds of pages and chock full of images. It handled it so well, in fact, that even my more powerful Samsung Note 10.1 using RepliGo Reader doesn't do as well!The Dropbox integration works very well, and is very helpful.By the way, unlike RepliGo Reader which required me to have an internet connection the first time I used it, this didn't require any internet access or account.Two of the best features involve audio. You can attach a voice memo; I didn't test more than a few seconds, so I'm not sure how long of a message you can embed.  The second, and even better, feature is the TTL voice reading which works quite well. It highlights the passages it is reading, too.  The only downside is that you can't pause and resume, which admittedly is a big deal, and one that hopefully will be implemented.There are a couple more downsides: the resolution of scans are poor due to heavy compression.  Also, there are no instructions and no settings.  I'd love to have more control over certain things, and some documentation would help people find those deeply hidden yet so helpful tools.Despite these downsides, this is an extraordinary PDF tool!  I really like my RepliGo Reader, but this will replace it as my go-to PDF tool from here on out.SUMMARY: More than a PDF reader, this is a powerful PDF tool, giving your Android as much power as any PC annotator I've found.BOTTOM LINE: Get it. column2: NOT COMPARABLE TO iOS version! LOOONG WAY TO GO!
column3: I bought this Android App because I have worked with the iOS version a lot (on my iPhone). It wasn't quite as good as Good Reader (which I use on my iPad and has Dropbox SYNC!) but the iOS version is one of the better PDF annotating apps for iOS. And I have tried many PDF apps on both platforms before.Since they advertise  "PDF Max is the 5-star rated, full-featured PDF reader used by millions of iPhone/iPad users world-wide and now available for Android"  I was happy to get at least that much PDF functionality for my Android device and went ahead and bought it.BUT BOY, WAS I DISSAPPOINTED!A lot of things that made it great on iOS are simply not there or don't work properrly:- NO TABS for multiple open documents!- Poor file browser which quits when you try to open a document that is located deeply within your folder structure- Slow rendering of certain PDFs (in comparison to the iOS app BUT ALSO IN COMPARISON WITH OTHER ANDROID APPS such as Adobe Reader, RepligoPDF Reader, ezPDF Reader Foxit Mobile PDF etc...- When you select the freehand annotating tool and set its opacity to anything other than 100% it seems to work but after saving it it will be back to 100% and therefore cover any text / element you really wanted to be visible- No step-by-step undo button during highlighting and other annotating tools- Undo button on freehand annotating tool doesn't work most of the time.- Frequent crashes of the app when working with larger size PDFs- Problem locating the annotations correctly created by other PDF application such as EZ PDF.- Lack the ability to adjust font size for typed notes.For anyone that has professionally used the iOS version (or the all time best GoodReader app) this app is unacceptable!It is so not comparable that I WOULD LIKE MY MONEY BACK and if the app would have been advertised in such a way on the Apple App store they would have reimbursed me!Again, even if they advertise it this way, THE ANDROID VERSION IS NOT COMPARABLE TO THE iOS VERSION!In my opinion it is simply NOT READY FOR PROFESSIONAL USE !

column3: This is a pretty solid alternative to Cloud Print for devices on the same subnet while bridging to CP for off-network access. It offers a variety of detection/connections options including a wizard that instantly found all the printers on my home network - although some were inaccurately identified as "WiFi" devices when they are actually network printers hardwired to the router. Device configuration options are far superior to Cloud Print and are similar to what you might find in the 'properties' dialog on Windows (eg: paper type, size and duplex settings). Supports most Android apps either via dedicated print (eg: Gmail) or sharing links (look for Hammermill in list of destinations) within the app. Supports preview - woohoo! Does not interfere with the operation of my device, doesn't constantly run in the background and only displays a single non-intrusive ad after print job has been submitted. Works on Kindle HDX along with several relatively standard Android devices. Downside: configuration options can be confusing (-1 star) so plan to spend a few minutes learning the app after novelty of actually being able to print to the device of your choice wears off. This appears to be a sponsored version of "Print Hand" which is a paid app that offers no appreciable benefits IMO.

column2: I was extremely impressed with how easy it was to set up and use
column3: Works great for me printing email, .pdf files, calendar items, contacts list, word processor documents, etc.. I have a Samsung Galaxy Tab 4, printing on a Canon Pixma MG6320. Some useful points:When I first installed it (leaving the default settings) it found the printer, but nothing happened when I tried to print the test page. But I remembered an earlier reviewer had said to change the app Protocol setting to "IPP" so I did that, and the app has been printing fine since.Here is how to access its print function from within other apps. If clicking on Print within another app does not do it for you, click on Share instead and Hammermill should be listed as an option; clicking on that takes you directly to Preview and Print.If that doesn't work either, click directly on the Hammermill app from your Home screen. Look to see if the app/file type you want to print from is listed down the left (that is how I print from the Calendar and Contacts apps that came with my tablet). If the app/file type is not listed, click on the Files option in the list and look for the file name that you want to print; click on that file and  the Preview and Print screen should appear.Once you are on the Preview screen, you can choose the printer, paper size, and a few other options, but it's not until after you hit Print that you will be asked for the number of copies and page range to print.This a fantastic app, very useful, and the only ads you have to look at are for Hammermill paper.

column2: Takes over your computer without permission
column3: I bought this so I could edit MS Office docs on my Fire Tablet. Then I decided to add a copy on my desktop. When I download an MSOffice doc from the web, it automatically opens in OfficeSuite. In order to open it in Word, I have to "save document." I cannot click on the document immediately, or OfficeSuite will load it. I must then go to File Explorer, open the Download folder, right click on the document, and manually CHOOSE Word. I have been unable to find any workaround.I am more than frustrated. I am angry, and I've paid money for the "Premium" version that has strong-armed itself to the front. Perhaps OfficeSuite is the ONLY option for FIRE users to edit MSOffice docs. But now I have ruined my desktop computer. Buyer beware. column2: Better Than Most, But Needs Work
column3: Sadly, word processing for Android is still pathetically lacking. OfficeSuite 8 not only has some lamentable glitches, it lacks some crucial features such as a good ruler, a drop-cap feature and spell check, which it continues to advertise. By the latter, I mean a red sqiggley line under misspelled words. The app also doesn't presently have close quotes options. For example, the Android keyboard comes with open quotes keys [“] and [‘], but lacks corresponding closed quotes. A decent word processor should provide users with both. Like MS Word, it would be great if it automatically had a "Smart Quotes" feature.Now for the glitches.First, the text on my Kindle Fire HDX, 4th Generation, often shimmers and vanishes for a moment, then returns when I navigate  up or down a page. And when adding a page break to fix widow lines, it always inserts an entire page, which I have to go back and manually delete. Also, when I copy formatted text and attempt to paste it into a document, the app removes the formatting. That means major reformatting of footnotes, quotations and so forth, which is a major hassle. The reformatting is complicated by the fact that text is a bit difficult to select. And every once in awhile, part of the text for some inexplicable reason changes size, but can easily be changed back. Another glitch.This app has been around for some time, yet it's still acting more like a beta version. Android will never be able to compete with iPods until it gets a bullet-proof word processing and office suite. Whether this will be it remains to be seen.

column2: Without Track Changes, the OfficeSuite Free is unworkable deadweight.

I'm a bit bemused by the myopia of whoever is in charge of the rollout of carrots-for-customers at MobiSystems, Inc. Not even a 15-day trial version with Track Changes mode? Or Insert? Or Review? MobiSystems is - ostensibly - targeting OfficeSuite at professionals and semiprofessionnels, who prefer to check out the competence and minutiae of an editing suite before plonking down the money for the full-blown version. This penny-pinching isn't what I expected. Uninstalled without a second thought.

Tap on the printer to submit a print job.

What the heck happened to just being able to BUY a piece of software?These people need a couple of million bucks of investment money so that they can do some more development on this software so that it WORKS, and works COMPLETELY before they start selling it. As it stands, it needs a LOT more development. While SOME small parts of it DO work, it is NOT a replacement for microsoft office. This app had everything I wanted.I draw abstract things, so precise lines, tools, and colors wasn't what I was really looking for. However, while the app isn't the most professional, the smoothness and variety of options astonished me. I've tried quite a few drawing apps, and I have to say, this one is my favorite. I love how my sketches seem to almost happen by themselves! The feel of the sketch brush  really gave me confidence in my drawing. I've never been able to sketch something on my phone that wasn't overtly simplified and cutesy. This app changed that for me. I'm a fan.

I'll admit it up front -- I'm a sucker for draw-and-paint programs on mobile devices. There's something deeply satisfying about noodling around on a touch screen, building up an image. You learn early on that you can't expect to make anything as detailed or realistic as you can with physical media, or even a PC-based drawing program hooked up to a drawing tablet. But that's just the nature of the beast. They're built for different purposes.Sketch Guru is the latest offering from Bejoy Mobile, a company that specializes in simple drawing programs for mobile devices. In some ways, this is simpler than most. There are no layers, for instance -- everything is created on a single plane. There is no flood-fill tool. There is only a color palette, a color-sampler tool, and a set of brushes.But what brushes they are! These are not your normal set of smooth-or-fuzzy lines, virtual mimics of physical media such as pencils, marker pens or brushes. They are computational brushes, brushes driven by algorithms that transcend mere imitation. The "furry" ones sense the presence of nearby lines, and generate cross-linkages to them. There is a brush that creates a regularly-spaced grid of concentric circles. There is a brush that draws a swath of crosshatching, like loosely-woven cloth. The result is that even simple doodles acquire a subtle complexity, effects usually associated with much more sophisticated media.There are three other features that boost this product from 4-star "Like it" to 5-star "Love it". The first is the "Rainbow Color" option, a feature used in many of Bejoy's products, which cycles the color through the spectrum as you draw. Lifting your finger from the touch-screen changes the color. This is more of a gimmick than a serious tool, but it's a heck of a lot of fun. And, with careful selection of the algorithmic "brushes", it can create some stunning effects.The second "5-star" feature is the ability to send a drawing directly into another program. I have been pairing Sketch Guru with Autodesk's SketchBook Mobile, a more sophisticated drawing program. There, I can add new layers and work up the raw sketches from Sketch Guru into something more complex. The export doesn't always work properly, but it's worth fussing with it.The third "5-star" feature is the price. This is a free app. As in, actually free, not "freemium", where you get the basic program free but then need to purchase add-on features. You can't get any better than that!

column2: Pretty awesome for the price of free!
column3: I just downloaded this app, and so far it lives up to my expectations. I'm in college for an art related degree, so I'm pretty knowledgeable when it comes to digital painting programs. I was looking for a free painting app that I would be able to create decent quality digital sketches with. I haven't tried out many others, but I was happy to see this one offered a lot of the things I was looking for. Here's a list of pros and cons I've thought of after exploring the app for a few minutes.Pros: Better brush selection than I expected. Some of them seem a bit impractical for serious art, but for something creative and fun, its pretty cool!Ability to adjust brush width and opacity.Effective color selection. I haven't figured out if colors picked may be saved for easy reselection, but if so that would be a super bonus.Ability to undo stepsI haven't explored the eraser tool, but its good that its thereThe video playback is super cool, but I haven't figured out if the videos are able to be saved.I haven't explored what the photo editing feature does, but its cool to know its there.Ability to save. Note: images seem to save only as a PNG file.I didn't spend much time testing it, but it seemed to run pretty smooth with no lagging or choppy lines.If the eyedropper tool works like any other program with an eyedropper tool does, it should be to select colors from your image. I haven't tried it yet, but if that's what it does, bravo to the developers.Cons: Upon first opening the app, it looks like a kids doodling app.The ads are annoying, but to be expected with a free app.No layering features for the serious digital artistsIf there's no way to save the video playback, I think it would be something the developers should add in an update.Another note for the developers. Maybe add an option to save the file as a jpg.This is what I came up with on first impression. So far it seems pretty useful. For the price of free, its great, and I think its worth trying out.

column2: Love this app, but needs something

What I mean is, when you use a photo you can press an icon that looks like 3 papers, and doing so makes the photo go on and off the canvas. I'd like to be able to do this with my regular drawings, only, it can give me the option to choose another drawing from my gallery, so that way I can combine some incomplete drawings on the same canvas to make one, completed image. I'm sure this is probably a feature on the pro version, if there is one, but I still think it would be nice to have those options on the free download as well. So yeah, 4 stars for an amazing app that just needs some minor adjustments in the next update, please and thank you. This is a pretty solid alternative to Cloud Print for devices on the same subnet while bridging to CP for off-network access. It offers a variety of detection/connections options including a wizard that instantly found all the printers on my home network - although some were inaccurately identified as "WiFi" devices when they are actually network printers hardwired to the router. Device configuration options are far superior to Cloud Print and are similar to what you might find in the 'properties' dialog on Windows (eg: paper type, size and duplex settings). Supports most Android apps either via dedicated print (eg: Gmail) or sharing links (look for Hammermill in list of destinations) within the app. Supports preview - woohoo! Does not interfere with the operation of my device, doesn't constantly run in the background and only displays a single non-intrusive ad after print job has been submitted. Works on Kindle HDX along with several relatively standard Android devices. Downside: configuration options can be confusing (-1 star) so plan to spend a few minutes learning the app after novelty of actually being able to print to the device of your choice wears off. This appears to be a sponsored version of "Print Hand" which is a paid app that offers no appreciable benefits IMO.

column2: Works great for me printing email
column3: Works great for me printing email, .pdf files, calendar items, contacts list, word processor documents, etc.. I have a Samsung Galaxy Tab 4, printing on a Canon Pixma MG6320. Some useful points:When I first installed it (leaving the default settings) it found the printer, but nothing happened when I tried to print the test page. But I remembered an earlier reviewer had said to change the app Protocol setting to "IPP" so I did that, and the app has been printing fine since.Here is how to access its print function from within other apps. If clicking on Print within another app does not do it for you, click on Share instead and Hammermill should be listed as an option; clicking on that takes you directly to Preview and Print.If that doesn't work either, click directly on the Hammermill app from your Home screen. Look to see if the app/file type you want to print from is listed down the left (that is how I print from the Calendar and Contacts apps that came with my tablet). column2: Good, but weak on handling of incoming calls.
column3: I'm using this app on a Kindle Fire HD 7.Skype, in general, is excellent. This version of Skype app for Fire is only OK.It works well for making outgoing video/voice calls, and texts.If the Fire is locked, incoming calls/texts aren't notified and don't appear until you unlock and open the Skype app, at which time they appear as missed calls.IF the app is OPEN and TOPMOST on the screen (or the top app in the open-app-stack), it works fine for incoming calls. Incoming text messages appear almost instantly, but without any sound notification, so you need to watch the screen if you're expecting a message.If the app is either not running at all or not on the top of the open-app-stack, incoming calls aren't notified at all.Also, even if the app is open and topmost on the screen, calls to a Skype phone number from a mobile or landline phone (as opposed to from a Skype contact) don't appear on the Fire (but you do eventually get a "missed call" indicator).All-in-all it appears to be well behind the Skype app on other devices; I don't know if that is because development is lagging or because the Fire simply doesn't have the capability to respond to incoming notifications.

Since Skype isn't available through the BlackBerry World App Store in Canada, it had to be downloaded through the Amazon App Store on my Uncle's BlackBerry. Basically, my Uncle lives in Canada, and he's not tech-savvy at all. I live in the US (SW Virginia), so I had to walk him through downloading Skype over the telephone. For some odd reason or another, Skype isn't available for BlackBerry devices in Canada. However, my Uncle has a newer (and I use that term loosely) BlackBerry "smartphone" on the Rogers network which includes the Amazon App Store. Considering the fact that he's not a tech person, he doesn't have an Amazon account. I had to "loan" him mine to download the app. After about an hour of hearing things like "There's no 'download' button, only a 'get app' button." or "Am I paying for this? I already pay too much." the application was finally installed on his phone. I set up his Skype account remotely to avoid any more unnecessary confusion, and I sent him the login information. As soon as he accepted my friend request, we were talking face-to-face over 800 miles away! Now, considering that my Uncle lives out in the boonies of Ontario, the call has dropped once or twice. But the overall is surprisingly good from a BlackBerry to my iPad 2. Sometimes we even talk through my Samsung Galaxy S6 or my Acer Aspire | M laptop. The microphone quality sucks in-general on my laptop, but I use a USB Behringer Mixer with a RadioShack Vocal/Karaoke microphone to get the job done. All in all, Skype has served us well for many years. FaceTime, however, never worked right on my iPad 2. And since Microsoft and Skype are now partnered, it's easier than ever to use!

column2: Un fin parfaite pour un couple parfait
column3: Matthew Hamilton possède ce charme caractéristique des hommes qui sont sûrs d'eux sans cette arrogance que l'on voit souvent dans les personnages masculins dans la romance. Il n'en a pas besoin. Il est le Président des Etats Unis. Il a atteint la place qu'il souhaitait et ce qu'il voulait : aller jusqu'au bout de son mandat présidentiel, chose  que son père, Président avant lui n'avait pu faire.Matthew est ambitieux et envisage de grands changements pour son pays. On sent tout l'amour qu'il a pour sa patrie et ses électeurs croient en lui. L'amour et la confiance que lui porte Charlotte le transcende. Ils sont d'ailleurs tous deux dans la même dynamique, ont le même objectif : faire avancer le pays avant toute chose.Cette alchimie est superbe et les sentiments qu'ils se portent l'un envers l'autre sont vibrants à la fois de l'admiration qu'ils se portent et de cette passion qui les submerge. Ils sont complémentaires, forment un couple parfait qui soulève respect et admiration.On va les retrouver tels qu'on les a vus dans le premier tome, amoureux et occultant leur amour à leur entourage.Les descriptions de la Maison Blanche, du staff et de toute l'atmosphère qui entoure nos héros est parfaitement rendue par l'auteure. Katy Evans a effectué un travail de recherches extraordinaire, on s'y croirait.La seconde partie reste plus "classique" et forcément moins addictive. Tout semble également un peu trop simple, trop parfait et tout semble réussir à ce couple charismatique. Mais j'ai pris beaucoup de plaisir à lire cette duologie, surtout en pleine période électorale, française et alors que le nouveau Président des Etats Unis sera bientôt en poste. Cela nous fait rêver à un vrai leader, jeune et charismatique qui apporterait un nouveau souffle.

column2: Happy with voice calls, but app needs updating
column3: UPDATE 8/11/2016After writing my review below I have been experiencing problems with Skype on PC after five minutes after connecting.  I hear the voice of the other person, but the other person does not hear mine. I  have it installed in my computers and gadgets. I use it all the time. In my PC at least once a month for intercontinental chat about 1-2 hours long.Regarding Skype for PC, I am mostly happy with it. The quality of the sound is usually very good, with no return sound or delays nowadays, which used to happen often in the past. The line drops at times but rarely. In the last year, using this app *at least* once a month, I have had a bad experience just once.My main problem with the app is for voice+audio chats, as it is a pain in the butt: frozen images, or very slow movement or very bad quality image. I don't know if it is related to my Internet carrier or not, but it is most annoying. The result is that I don't make video-calls any more.Skype's interface for PC is a bit outdated, not clear enough and not customer friendly enough. The home screen should clearly show the options, voice call, video call, written chat alone, send photo and/or doco, plus the contact list on the side bar.My account is totally private, only close friends and family are there, I cannot be found by name or email. Yet, sometimes I get requests of people I don't know, spammers I guess, so I would like that scam to be out of my house and the portholes taking them there locked.I like that Skype asks me about the quality of the sound and call/video-call when I finish. At least they care!  I think that serves to improve the service and is specially important when I have a bad experience.

column2: Some things to note about the latest Skype version
column3: I have had a 32GB 8.9 HD kindle since it first came out in late 2012 & some earlier models. If you read through many of the reviews you should notice that most of the 5 star ones were written shortly after the release of the HD series in late 2012 & early 2013. On the other hand, the poor 1 & 2 star reviews were written since late 2013 & later.I would agree with this as it matches my own experience. The original Skype for the Kindle Fire HD series worked very well but an update issued sometime late last year changed all of this. There appears to be two main issues:1. SOUND VOLUME:Even if your volume is set all of the way up before launching Skype, conversations are barely audible. This may be because MS/Skype expect you to use ear buds which is a common way to use the app. If you in fact do this then you will find the audio level to be okay. HOWEVER, if you don't use ear buds then check the volume setting within Skype using the hardware volume switch and you will probably notice that the volume is way down around 25%. If you raise the volume to 100% using the hardware volume control then conversations can be heard okay just like the earlier version and it stays this way in subsequent sessions. They may have made the initial setting this way to prevent ear bud users from blowing out their ears.2. CRASHES:I don't know what to say about this except to confirm that I have had the same experience. Skype starts okay but invariably crashes (frozen screen, no sound, etc.) within 5 minutes and will then the Kindle will spontaneously reboot. This makes what is otherwise an excellent app next to useless.So, this problem has been around for over 6 months without being fixed. Amazon gets a failing grade from me on this issue as they should at least make the original version available for download from their app store for folks having this problem while they are sorting out the issues with the latest version.

I used chat to request reinstatement. The representative seemed unable to extract information despite a "Dick & Jane" narrative, asking off-base questions and even, well into the conversation, requesting my screen name -- provided on the transcript. It became apparent that, if not illiterate, the representative was trained to deflect callers and outlast any caller's attempt at redress.

column2: Good, but weak on handling of incoming calls.
column3: I'm using this app on a Kindle Fire HD 7.Skype, in general, is excellent. This version of Skype app for Fire is only OK.It works well for making outgoing video/voice calls, and texts.If the Fire is locked, incoming calls/texts aren't notified and don't appear until you unlock and open the Skype app, at which time they appear as missed calls.IF the app is OPEN and TOPMOST on the screen (or the top app in the open-app-stack), it works fine for incoming calls. Incoming text messages appear almost instantly, but without any sound notification, so you need to watch the screen if you're expecting a message.If the app is either not running at all or not on the top of the open-app-stack, incoming calls aren't notified at all.Also, even if the app is open and topmost on the screen, calls to a Skype phone number from a mobile or landline phone (as opposed to from a Skype contact) don't appear on the Fire (but you do eventually get a "missed call" indicator).All-in-all it appears to be well behind the Skype app on other devices; I don't know if that is because development is lagging or because the Fire simply doesn't have the capability to respond to incoming notifications.

column2: Happy with voice calls, but app needs updating
column3: UPDATE 8/11/2016After writing my review below I have been experiencing problems with Skype on PC after five minutes after connecting.  I hear the voice of the other person, but the other person does not hear mine. Also the line has started to drop. I keep my app updated in my PC and was quite satisfied with it until say the last month, when having a chat online has becoming too much of a hassle on my PC, but if I use my Skype for Android I have no problem.Please fix the app for PC, otherwise is worthless at present.PREVIOUS REVIEWI have used Skype since it first saw the light, many years ago. I  have it installed in my computers and gadgets. I use it all the time. In my PC at least once a month for intercontinental chat about 1-2 hours long.Regarding Skype for PC, I am mostly happy with it. The quality of the sound is usually very good, with no return sound or delays nowadays, which used to happen often in the past. The line drops at times but rarely. In the last year, using this app *at least* once a month, I have had a bad experience just once.My main problem with the app is for voice+audio chats, as it is a pain in the butt: frozen images, or very slow movement or very bad quality image. I don't know if it is related to my Internet carrier or not, but it is most annoying. The result is that I don't make video-calls any more.Skype's interface for PC is a bit outdated, not clear enough and not customer friendly enough. The home screen should clearly show the options, voice call, video call, written chat alone, send photo and/or doco, plus the contact list on the side bar.My account is totally private, only close friends and family are there, I cannot be found by name or email. Yet, sometimes I get requests of people I don't know, spammers I guess, so I would like that scam to be out of my house and the portholes taking them there locked.I like that Skype asks me about the quality of the sound and call/video-call when I finish. At least they care!  I think that serves to improve the service and is specially important when I have a bad experience.

column2: Some things to note about the latest Skype version
column3: I have had a 32GB 8.9 HD kindle since it first came out in late 2012 & some earlier models. If you read through many of the reviews you should notice that most of the 5 star ones were written shortly after the release of the HD series in late 2012 & early 2013. On the other hand, the poor 1 & 2 star reviews were written since late 2013 & later.I would agree with this as it matches my own experience. The original Skype for the Kindle Fire HD series worked very well but an update issued sometime late last year changed all of this. There appears to be two main issues:1. SOUND VOLUME:Even if your volume is set all of the way up before launching Skype, conversations are barely audible. This may be because MS/Skype expect you to use ear buds which is a common way to use the app. If you in fact do this then you will find the audio level to be okay. HOWEVER, if you don't use ear buds then check the volume setting within Skype using the hardware volume switch and you will probably notice that the volume is way down around 25%. If you raise the volume to 100% using the hardware volume control then conversations can be heard okay just like the earlier version and it stays this way in subsequent sessions. They may have made the initial setting this way to prevent ear bud users from blowing out their ears.2. As ever, the deletion of past instant messaging sessions is problematic, and has a different look and feel from both the windows,Win 8,  and iOS versions, each of which seem to follow their own path. Has been very reliable since dowloading however, the last update makes it impossible to start or join a call without immediately cutting out and saying contacts aren't reachable. This is such a shame as it means I'm unable to video call my elderly grandmother - not ideal at the moment!

Free video calls to anywhere in the world - what could be better? Charges for long distance calls, landline calls abroad are coming to an end, all thanks to Microsoft and Skype!However similar to Facebook and other social media websites, the reason this service remains free is mainly down to user data that Microsoft collects and later sells to third parties for profit. Who are these mysterious third parties? Not sure - but it's worth thinking about before using Skype (or any device, app or social media platform). The video quality and audio quality can sometimes drop mid-call. Calls randomly cutting out can occur and sometimes Skype does not pick your mic up at all on your laptop/ computer. I had to resort to downloading a previous version of Skype in order for my mic to work properly on Skype.In the age of smart TVs, Edward Snowden, data collection scandals etc, it's worth thinking about before using such an application. Is handing over private data worthwhile? That's the question! And depending on the type of person you are, there may be different answers to that question. All in all, Skype is a fairly useful and easily accessed service.

column3: First I appreciate what is given and Skype is a free service that lets me have video calls to people on the other side of the World.  Great.  But for me there are two problems with Skype.  One is the problem of getting things done: the layout, the ergonomics, the problem of finding how to do things.  With tasks like editing contacts I don't find it intuitive nor easy to get things done.  I like software that is simple, intuitive, and has the handles and nuts and bolts showing so you can see how to do things.  The other is the intrusive nature.  How do you turn it off if you don't want to be disturbed by incoming calls.  (With the PC version, signing out, closing it, and then right-clicking the icon and selecting 'quit Skype' doesn't stop incoming calls.)  And in the past I've had the problem where I was writing a document, typed a date, and Skype sprang to life and changed it into a Skype telephone number for my contact list.  Ughh!

Downloaded this free app to brush up on Spanish (that I studied {badly} in college for two semesters).  The lessons are short and easy to digest, but lack the sort of foundation necessary to learn a new language.I understood verb conjugation before opening this app; had that not been the case, this method may have proved exasperating.  In word matching vocabulary drills, the word "eat" pairs as a correct response to all of the following: como (I eat), comes (you {familiar} eat); come (you {formal} eat; comemos (we eat); comeis (you plural {familiar} eat); and comen (you plural/they {formal}) eat.  A more helpful approach would have been to match "I eat" with "como," "we eat" with "comemos," etc.Showing, not telling is the process used by Duolingo.  Unfortunately, forms of speech are presented without the most basic explanation that is essential to understanding a new language.

Don't get me wrong - I am thankful for free apps like Duolingo to help me learn beginning spanish. But after emerging into indirect pronouns, I see why so many people I have met through the years have only mastered declarative statements and simple questions.This is how spanish really is: the beginning is a little steep, like inching your way down that incline in the swimming pool. You know there's deep water somewhere in your future but you feel safe, as you're taking it in tiny tiny increments.Then you graduate, with absolutely no preparation whatever, into indirect pronouns. You slip off that shelf in the pool and suddenly you're in deep water. Nothing makes sense. And the sad thing is that Duolingo has not prepared you at all with ANY education about it.I have been studying spanish for years and got to this point in a couple of weeks. I have had to go to external sites to get the information I need about this.Duolingo is great but they need some in-depth education about hard things like indirect pronouns, where EVERY sentence is structured ENTIRELY different than in English.

column2: A little lacking, but otherwise good.
column3: I originally downloaded this app to help me brush up on my French, which is pretty rusty after 15 years of little to no use, and my Spanish, which is just a little rusty after a year of little to no use. I am somewhat pleased with this app. I don't like it as much as I like my French and Spanish classes, but as far as a language tutor, it's great. The only thing lacking in this app is that it doesn't explain the conjugations of verbs with respect to pronouns. For instance--and I'm going to use Spanish as an example here--it doesn't explain why the verb 'ser' gets conjugated to 'eres' when you say "tu eres," or why it gets conjugated to 'somos' when you say, "nosotros somos." If it explained the process of conjugation for each language, that would make the app SO MUCH better and also help newbies have a fuller understanding of the language they are trying to learn. Anyone who doesn't know the first thing about other languages is going to think that this app is great, but if you are like me and you have had formal classes before, you will know that this app is seriously lacking. Formal classes give you the fundamental principles of the language to help you, and one of those fundamentals is learning conjugation so that you will not only understand what you're saying, but WHY you're saying it that way. I know this app isn't the same as a formal class, but if the developers are going to market it as an alternative to expensive formal classes, then they need to at least offer better teaching tools within the app.

column2: Not for travel, or for serious language learning
column3: Most recently, I used Duolingo to prep for a trip to Mexico.  It wasn't until *Level 19* that I learned how to say "I don't speak Spanish."  Uh?This app is not interested in teaching you how to form a sentence.  (Whatever you do, don't use it for German, because it doesn't teach you anything about why you use certain endings when you do; I'm fluent in German and tried it in German and it was laughable.)  I'd forgive it that if it taught you enough to get by in a tourist context, but it doesn't do that well, either.  You may learn how to ask "How much does it cost?" by Level 10 or so, but you won't understand all the numbers, so when someone comes back to you in the language with an answer, you're clueless.  I used it before travelling to Italy, to Spain, to France, and to Mexico, at different times, and had the same experience. With Italian and French, fortunately I'd studied them earlier and just needed a refresher.  With Spanish, I passed all Duolingo's lessons with aces, and went well into the upper levels, but was basically unable to understand when I got to Spain or Mexico.  A program that teaches neither vocabulary nor grammar in any detail is useless in practice.

Previously I had contended with overly repetitive exercises and the app, which I find the most unfriendly way of doing any kind of learning. Of course, it might work for others but the approach of one size fits all flies in the face of any kind of understanding of how people learn.Coming to the real point of this review, I feel that I need to warn people of their customer service. However, when I found that the problems did not go away I found it to be really stressful to even try to get in contact with customer service. Mainly because there is none. Duolingo is over-reliant on a forum system whereby users have to work out problems for themselves, often scratching their heads over how to get help with an issue.When I finally did get a reply it was accompanied with an excuse about how emails can end up in the wrong intray (despite having resorted to Twitter, Facebook, through the website, app store reviews, trying to contact the CEO directly.) column2: Duolingo: A good way to learn the foundations of a foreign language
column3: Duolingo provides a free service for users to speak, write and understand foreign languages. It's available from a Web site and as an app for standard smart phones. It's a decent service, provided that you realize that it's still a work in progress. Issues I've observed after about 8 months:1. The translation is not always perfect. In some cases, the answers which are accepted are not proper English. In others, only very specific translations will be accepted. Some cases explain why an answer is rejected, but others will simply say the answer is wrong.2. There is a way to report translation issues which appears to be ignored for the more mature languages. There is no communication from Duolingo itself, so if the team actually DOES accept a suggestion or bug you will probably never know.3. There are still bugs with the service. Example: the "streak freeze" feature, intended to provide motivation by tracking continuous progress even if a person misses a day, does not always work. Some users will have it function, while others will return from a day at the beach to find their streak freeze gone and their count reset to 0.4. Not all languages implement all of the features. In more mature languages, you will have fluency as a rated percentage. You will not see this feature in more recently developed languages.5. Vocabulary varies by language. Outside of basic grammar, the lessons appear to be the choice of the community who collaborated to develop the training. As a result, there WILL be missing vocab.6. Pronunciation depends on the speakers. The service generally records two "native speakers" for the language. They may pronounce words slightly differently than the textbook version, or they may use a dialect. This can be an issue with languages where there are regional variations, such as Spanish.Bottom Line: Duolingo is an effective way to learn the fundamentals in a foreign language, but use it with reasonable expectations. column2: Babbel is Much Better and Worth The Low Price
column3: Free doesn't always mean professional or even good.  People are wild about Duolingo, but  I think they might be less enthusiastic if they had to pay for it--then the chorus of complaints in the comments sections on Duolingo might be louder and you might see a different set of percentages here on Amazon.I've spent several months each now on Babbel and Duolingo studying Dutch (my 4th language), and the experience is completely different. Babbel's Dutch is remarkably better and more fun than Duolingo, with features Duolingo lacks.  It's informative, engaging, more interactive, and very well designed.  Within days I learned things I never did in weeks of Dutch on Duolingo.  It's got great color graphics, a better user interface, and offers grammar and usage information right there in the lesson via pop-ups.  Babbel works on pronunciation, grammar, practical usage all at the same time, whereas Duolingo's Dutch was much too theoretical and artificial.  And Babbel has dialogues at the end of each lesson to help you remember the vocabulary by using it in a practical way. It also lets you go back and redo the specific parts of the lesson you got wrong, offers regular review lessons, and overall is much more organic and less mechanical feeling.  You get to learn idioms along the way and it feels as if you're in a fun classroom with an entertaining teacher.In contrast, Duolingo seems disorganized, difficult, and dull.  It has too many dumb sentences that supposedly make you remember vocabulary but that I found distracting.  The course overall was often too complicated and weirdly laid out.  Easy vocabulary followed difficult vocabulary and easy verb tenses followed hard ones.  It was frustrating--and I found other people expressing dissatisfaction in the comments sections, so I wasn't alone by any means. The moderators enjoyed being complimented  and that's when they seemed most helpful.  Express anything but thanks, however, and the rhetorical wooden ruler could come out.  Yes, these people are apparently volunteers, that's no excuse for a bad attitude and thinking that scoring points off a learner is "fun."  They also don't fully understand English idioms or ordinary usage, like the simple difference between "gold" and "golden."I wish I had tried Babbel first for Dutch and not wasted time with Duolingo's Dutch because I already have phrases in my head associated with lively, evocative photos and dialogue interactions, something that never really happened with Duolingo because of its inferior design.  And when it comes to translation?  Instead of insisting on overly literal translation into English sentences that don’t make sense, on Babbel they'll tell you what something means literally and what it means in practice, which makes a big difference.  The pedagogy is definitely more student-oriented on Babbel than Duolingo, and best of all you actually hear what the language sounds like.  Duolingo’s sound files are atrocious.  The sound files on Duolingo are great (with a variety of speakers) and there's voice recognition so you can practice at more than one level.  Reviews also let you work with flash cards if you want to.  Duolingo feels really Old School. Seriously, if you want to learn a language even casually, Babbel is worth it.  You get what you pay for.

This was once a great program but it has made itself incredibly boring. It gamified learning languages, making it into something exciting, thrilling, fun. Now it's incredible boring repetitions to learn even basic things is deeply demotivating, especially where mistakes are not corrected but allowed to remain in apparently unmonitored modules for three years at a time (the Italian subjunctive is bad enough without long-term uncorrected mistakes). I use to recommend this to my students; I do not do that anymore.  This used to be the language-learning equivalent of GTA 5; it is now the language-learning equivalent of driving across downstate Illinois.

column3: I want to use it when convenient and not be badgered by automatic emails when I don't. Deleted app after 3 days as a consequence!!!!!!

I really wanted this app but it looks like you have to be a member of face book and also give them your e-mail address if you want to proceed in getting the app open and I am not prepared to give my e-mail address to just anyone hence the one star.

Ok I haven't spoken French since leaving Brussels, but I'm sure when you work with adjectives, in French the adjective goes after the verb e.g one example I had to translate was, the big Apple - la pomme grosse but it said I was incorrect - it said la grosse pomme! Someone correct me if I'm wrong!
Unable to use this app without a facebook account.As I have no need or desire to create a facebook account, this app is totally useless to me.
