column3: Before you can even trial this app you are required to submit lots of personnel information.I presume this is so they can get money as you progress.

The app will not open into the actual tasks or activities after I have chosen my language no matter how many times I change the language of retry!😭👎U used to have this app and had no problems with it, so frustrating!😡

Tapping the app icon just sends me to the web-site.  There is no actual app!As this is the learning device for my son, I was expecting something I could at least load on his profile.Look a bit deeper and you see the most helpful comment is 5 years old - Obviously the app has taken a nose dive since then.
The app would be great - BUT this is NOT an app, just a link to the website. Pretty pointless tbh.

column2: I paid extra for this fire so I wouldn't get adverts
column3: And I got an advert for this on my front page, looking like I had already installed it. On the plus side, I was so annoyed I have worked out how to stop the intrusive adverts.  Get rid of Amazon insider.

I've been using Duolingo for a number of years now and it only continues to get better. While it's free I've been paying for the Plus level because people who build something this great should be rewarded.I've done French but mostly Spanish and every time I get close to the end it gets significantly expanded. I own Rosetta Stone but I haven't started it up in a long time because Duolingo is so much better.

This was a recent download to a third device. I have been using Duo and Duo Plus for about three years. I like it, and the more I stick with it, the more I like it. There are several approaches to learning and I need them all. There are many forms of assistance and practice. I think I will start making it a little more difficult to gain writing skills.  I will turn off some of the clues and try harder to dig deep and converse. I don't have a convenient Spanish speaker to learn with so I will use those features that fill that void the best.  I'm old, but not too hold to learn with Duo.

column2: It will help you to learn to read Spanish. Listening and speaking requires more than this.
column3: Duolingo is a great program. I have been learning with it for just over two years now (I upgraded to the Pro version) and by studying at home, with just Duolingo, I am now able to read some Spanish novels, read some magazines and newspapers, and I have a general understanding of the language.But ... if you really want to converse with others, you will need more than this to do that. When I listen to Spanish TV or music or a movie, I"m lost. I have Spanish speaking friends and if they speak slowly, I will understand but in order to respond, it will take me too much time to think about how to properly frame the response. If I were asked to write down my response, I could do that more easily than speaking.My point is, this is an excellent program and I enjoy using it and feel accomplished. But, to truly learn the language, you will need interaction with others who are fluent in the language.Let this get you started and, if you find yourself enjoying it, get a tutor, take a Spanish class, or travel and do some immersion learning. As you're taking lessons, Duolingo will help along the way.Great things about DuoLingo -** It has an active discussion group, so if you're confused about an answer, just click and you'll likely see 100's of posts about that issue.** It has a dictionary so that you can find words that are not part of your lesson** As you learn words, it adds them to your personal word list and shows you when you last used that word so that you can practice vocabulary that you might have not used in a while.** You can read stories that are based on your reading level; it is not just grammar.** The Android version is very easy but I prefer to use it on my laptop or Kindle. Fortunately, Duolingo has platforms for all as well as iOS.** It lets you set your own pace and will remind you daily if you've met your goal for the day. You can change the time you spend per day whenever you like.** Duolingo has a podcast as well which is good to practice your listening skills. It may be too advanced, but it's still good to help you learn the flow and tone of the language.I deducted one star because many people will think this IS the answer, when in fact it is only a part of the answer. The program also has a bit of trouble with voice recognition but then, it might be that my Brooklyn accent does not translate well into proper Spanish.

I love languages and have always wanted to learn several. Duolingo is easy and fun. The lessons are short so you can easily fit them in a busy schedule. And you want to do them. I've tutored to learn languages before but was always distracted. Now I have studied every day for almost two months and have just started studying two languages at once.

I am working on both Spanish and French right now.  They are both languages I've studied previously but need to refresh.  Duolingo is helping me and I enjoy the daily work.I have not yet tried a totally new language, but that will be next.  Thanks Duolingo!

This app is great.  I knew a bit of Spanish before but I started at the beginning.  I'm getting pretty good.I didn't think an app would work for me, (especially a free one)and it's difficult sometimes to remember the accents when I'm spelling.  But I'm finding it easier and easier to create my own sentences and can "translate" some of my children's books into Spanish.You have to make sure to go back and strengthen your skills once a week or so.

column2: Duolingo - Love it. Makes the learning fun
column3: Duolingo - Love it.  Makes the learning fun.  You can choose how much time you want to spend on it a day, that's so nice.  I've told friends and family about it and they all have started using it and are loving it.  You match words, you repeat words, you  translate what you hear in the language you are learning into English, and vice versa.  It really is a great app that really makes the learning fun.  I highly recommend it.

column2: Use it every day. Not sure if I'm really ...
column3: Use it every day. Not sure if I'm really learning the language (Italian), but I can recognize words and phrases after 1.5 years of daily use.

Hola! I bought Rosetta Stone and I got Duolingo as well (for free!!!!) Duolingo is better! If I'm unsure of the meaning of a word I can mouse over it and get the definition. If I translate a sentence wrong Duolingo tells me what was wrong and what it should have been! Rosetta Stone is good but lacks to help you get from Duolingo! Love little Duo the owl as well and  the e-mail reminders to practice. Duolingo just needs a few more languages but I guess that will come in the future. Adios!

I have been using this app for the past few months and it really works! I find myself understanding parts of conversations in Spanish when I'm out in stores or flipping through Spanish television stations. It's very simple and fun. More like playing a game than a tedious language lesson. The best part is I'm actually learning! I can't believe this amazing tool is free! Now there is no reason not to be multi lingual!

A free app that uses both written and verbal practice to help you learn several different languages.  Only two things I would want from it is an option to learn in lessons before exercises for practice, occasionally you get asked to translate words before you see them used but usually they appear in yellow and you can tap them,  and an option to use a different keyboard to correctly use the appropriate characters unique to that language.

Fun presentation mixing graphics, listening/speaking and reading to immerse students in a gradual escalation of difficulty within their chosen language course. The app doesn't overexplain like a textbook, so be prepared to just dive in!You can repeat any lesson when you need to, and you receive points for completing sections that you can use to unlock supplemental lessons like idioms.
its very cool b/c it's teaches verses that u can use. app is easy to use.

I like the format presented. The continued repetition supports easy retention. I also like how it introduces the Chinese characters very early. This makes it easy to read the charactersjust by sight. Sometimes one or two of the picture images are blank so unable to choose the correct answer. The downsideIs the chinese pronunciation does not sound authentic. There is room for improvement in this respect. All in all, It's fun using the program and as a beginner chinese student, I find it very helpful. MW.

column2: An easy and fun way to learn Spanish or many other languages.
column3: Spanish is the fastest growing language in America. We need to know enough to be conversant.Duolingo was my choice out of many to accomplish this task. It is fun and easy if you have the desire and discipline to do your homework every day, or even every other day. You can practice over and over until you speak Spanish like a native.Other languages are available too, so get ready to meet the world!

I love this app. It's just as easy and intuitive as Rosetta Stone only free and easy to use on my tablet and phone. It teaches and tests at a comfortable pace, often incorporating vocabulary and phrases from previous lessons to keep your old lessons from fading in your memory. I love the multifaceted style of typing, speaking, imagery and multiple choice. Did I mention free?? No ads. Seriously a great app. I'm brushing up my Spanish while discovering German.

Great app! Quick and easy way to introduce new language skills in just 5 to 10 minutes each morning while I drink my coffee. This would probably be more effective used alongside a full language course, but for those of us who don't have time it is an easier alternative.

I downloaded this app a year ago and was mildly impressed with the approach for picking up a second language so I uninstalled it.  I recently decided to give it another chance and was surprised how much more I enjoyed the process/approach for developing second language skills.  You are only as good as your study habits.  I'm a hit and miss user, so my skills have only marginally improved, but I see the real value this app provides.  Great App
I Went to click the get started and I put the language and it keeps bringing me back to start

It has helped me read, write, speak, and understand Spanish!I LOVE IT!!!!!!!YOU WILL LOVE IT!!!!!!!! ( ALMOST GARENTEED)(WARNING)...  IT IS SO ADDICTING!!!!!!! ;-) Which could be good or bad.☺I HOPE YOU LOVE IT!!! ...( It deserves it.)
When I enter the app and try to log in it refreshes and goes back to the menu. It's  really annoying. I turned my kindle off and back on, cleared my data and uninstalled it but it still won't work.

I really like this language app. It's got a couple of shortcomings but not many. Occasionally it will ask you to translate a word it has never shown you. Also some grammar rules aren't explained very well. Takes a few times going through each one before you really get it. But that's language for ya. Otherwise it's awesome. I can now understand a bit of german. Enough that if I was dropped in Germany I wouldn't be completely lost. If someone spoke slow and clear in German to me I would be able to somewhat understand. And that's after just a few weeks.

column2: Makes it easy to learn a language, has several language choices.
column3: Learning more words thru this app than any other. Really like it. Wish it was easier to start at the beginning, for review of words. Like that it goes from English to Spanish and back, then even incorporates spelling!

I have been using Duolingo for a week and love it.  I can set how much time per day to dedicate and the app creates lessons to fit the time limit.  It reminds you if you missed a lesson.  It says a phrase in the learning language and has you repeat it.  This really helps in retaining what you've learned. The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is because it docks me for misspelling certain French words.  But my keyboard doesn't have the punctuation required.  Awesome otherwise!
I've been using Duolingo for about 2 weeks now to learn Italian and feel like I am learning quickly. This seems to be a great way for me to learn.  Ciao!

column2: fun way to learn other languages
column3: Very easy to use, designed to be fun, and the program emails reminders to help you stay on track (because retention necessitates regular lessons).  I've taking Italian for about a year now and know quite a bit of vocabulary, but am only guessing at structure, which is why I gave  4 stars and not 5.  I wish that links to explanations of syntax and pronunciation would be added.

I love this language app. It is fun and easy to use with match the words, repeat phrases and type in translations. I just wish you could skip ahead to sections you really want to learn instead of going through the whole set.

This is more like practice than actual lessons, but it's a nice supplement for vocabulary and grammar review. Some of the Spanish to English sentence translations are too easy to guess out of the limited choices, because it's the only choice that makes any sense.  So sometimes it's just simple guesses rather than actually learning and knowing what the Spanish words mean. I love that it includes a spoken portion with the microphone, though!

My only quibble is that it doesn't really give any explanations.  When you guess incorrectly, and you do, sometimes have to guess because words are thrown in without introduction, it often tells you that you've used one form instead of another, but it hasn't explained how and when the forms are used.  I understand the natural learning strategy it uses, it does work, but I think I would catch on more with very basic usage explanations.  For free, though, this is a gift to the world.

column2: Great app for people who have a working  of the language. Still has some minor bug issues
column3: I am really enjoying getting back into learning German. But I couldn't get pass the third lesson. Every time I am in the middle of it it crashes. I have to shut down my kindle fire hdx. It has happened 5 times. I called mayday and they had similar calls from this app. They said it needs to be addressed with this company. If this can be fixed then I would give it a better rating. I do like the multiple formats. Pictures, German to English, English to German, and speaking German into the microphone. You have many languages to choose from not just German. I might brush up on my Spanish next if it can be fixed.Everyt

This is better than Rosetta stone! I've been working on the French for a month now and am able to understand quite a lot. It's fun quick and you can follow friends and their progress as well. It also lets you earn ringots which let you purchase some other levels such as flirting and phrases that are common in our language. Only complaint is they don't have a wide selection of languages.

column2: fun way to learn a new language
column3: My 1st grader wanted to learn a new language, a friend told me about Duolingo, thought I'd give it a try. I started doing it to stay ahead of him so I could help him if he needed it. Now my 5th grader is doing it to. We are having funny using our new language skills together. Bottom line it can help at a by age.My only 2 critiques would be, a better reward system to keep kids interested. Maybe a reference area to explain a little about how the words are formed to have a better understanding.That being said it is a Free app, so it is great!

It's a great app that teaches you different languages. But sometimes it can get confusing when you respond to a question it gives you it tells you your wrong and thEn it later tells you your right a different time. Besides it's small quirks I still enjoy this app. I use it and it's easy enough for my kids to use it as well.

column2: Sentences are sometimes odd but good app
column3: I'm currently using the app to learn 2 languages. The computer-created sentences can be a bit odd. I doubt that los pajaros leen el diario. (The birds read the newspaper.) The main thing keeping me from rating it 5 stars is that there is no alphabet tutoring for the languages. If I'm learning Spanish, it isn't an issue. But, what if I want to try Greek? What are the letters, and how are they pronounced?

Duolingo is a wonderful language app that teaches through immersion. One actually learns conjugation in the early lessons without being "taught" how to do so. It is terrific how each lesson seamlessly builds on the previous one and brings back vocabulary learned earlier on to keep it fresh in one's mind. My son is using it to teach himself French before he studies abroad this Fall and I am using it to dust off my college French that I took quite some time ago. I would therefore wholeheartedly recommend this app to someone either learning a new language or brushing up on an old one.

This is a great program to learn with. Try it and you will immediarely be learning a new language. Before you know it, you will make connections between words that are meaningful and easy to remember. There are a couple of glitches but overall, this is an incredible program.

If you want to learn a new language, this is the app for you! It makes it easy to learn a new language, and if you need to you can go back to re-read words. The only problem is that you can't learn very many languages, including Chinese/Japanese, which I wanted to learn. With how great all the lessons are, I assume they will be updated to have them in the near future. Otherwise, this is an AMAZING app!

I've always wanted to speak another language, but I could never find an app that made learning something new fun and easy until my grandmother showed me Duolingo. One lesson and I was hooked and showed all my friends.

column2: Excellent way to learn another language
column3: I really enjoy this app.  The lessons are short, painless, and fun.  The teaching is a mix of assorted styles that actually enhances memory retention.  I don't mind taking the few minutes needed to complete my lesson and I feel like I actually learned something when I'm done.  Make a Japanese app next!  I would get that one, too!

column2: Great practice and was surprised how much I remembered
column3: Got this to brush up on college French over 30 years ago......Great practice and was surprised how much I remembered.  Strength exercises are particularly helpful to keep what you've learned fresh as you progress through the lessons.

column2: Wow! I can't believe this free but it is.
column3: I have been through the lessons on food terms, animals and some other lessons. I can only say very simple sentences right now but it looks like it provides an extensive list of lessons that will come as I continue to work through the lessons. I have had some trouble with getting the hang of conjugating verbs which this program doesn't spell out for me. So, I would recommend this program to anyone who wants to learn a foreign language. Although it will take a large commitment to work at it.

I've had 7 years of Spanish classes to help me learn the language and I still cannot carry on a conversation. I downloaded this app with my former classes in mind thinking the basics were going to be extremely dull and basic  enough for a child to learn at a young age. I was wrong. It seemed as if you needed some sort of knowledge of the language you wanted to learn or else you'd get lost. This app is helpful so far and I am surprised at how much Spanish I remember during the lessons. The lessons seem to get longer as you progress, which I find to be a great idea in duolingo. I am impressed. I hope to learn more than I already know.

very cool and easy app to practice a language.  Only disadvantages is that if a language has unique symbols like umlauts, etc  the Kindle keyboard does not show those options. and Duolingo marks it incorrect.  Also, the microphone does not always work.

column2: Duolingo is an excellent language app
column3: Duolingo is an excellent language app! It covers listening, writing, reading and speaking. You complete excercises at your own pace.  It also  enables you to redo parts of already completed sections to refresh the vocabulary and grammar you have learnt. It is the best language course I have ever come across.It allows you to listen again to sections to be translated as many times as you want before translating. When you mouse over a word, the English is displayed so this helps you translate when you are stuck on a word you don't know. It also lets you learn  different languages at the same time on the one app just by switching the language at the push of a button! You are awarded "lingots" after completing each section which is an incentive to continue as you can buy different additional bonus sections with them. This is a really well thought out language course and to top it all it was a free app! well worth 5 stars!

Incredible learning experience, reinforces what you've learned, reminders to invest time in learning, encouragement, everything Rosetta Stone isn't, everything Pimsleur should be.  This is a great tool and free, not in the current meaning of free (i.e. free for a few days then pay), but free as in no cost - ever, no ads, no pushes to upgrade, the only investment that is required is your time (so I guess its not really free ...)

This app gives me a great experiences to learn new languages. It teaches me from the basics to the high level step by step. I would recommend to everyone who would like to learn new languages to strart with Doulingo first. Thank you so much for providing us an excellent service Doulingo!Kai 😇

This app is amazing! I t goes over everything you need to. Earning ingots makes it a fun experience. You also get to play with friends and family, make your own home page and it tells you when and if you need to go over lessons. I give this app a 5 out of 5 stars!

Easy and fun to use! I have my doubts I can really reach fluency with just the app, but my German reading skills have definitely improved. I may not reply well, but I understand more and can navigate my way around much better even after just a couple of days! It's super easy to get in a few minutes a day, and it's enough like a game that sometimes I'm on it for much longer.

This is a truly wonderful program, but I am not a texter, and typing answers on the Kindle is very tedious and frustrating to me.  I wish they would make this available on a regular computer, with keyboard and mouse access.  Too often a slight mis-tap gives me an incorrect response, and taps on a small word (like "I" or "a") simply don't take, and I have to keep tapping them over and over to get them.

This works very well and I use a little every day. I find I learn better with this than with Rosetta Stone. The comments provided when you make a slight error typing or in accents is very helpful. It graduates you to higher levels as you learn. This is very encouraging for learning.  Having you speak a sentence in the language and then grading your result is very helpful feedback.  This is provided free making one wonder what the business model is.

The content is beautifully crafted, grouped and presented. Following goldilocks "just right" feel -  my French lessons were complex enough to be challenging while simple enough to persist through the lessons- at least for me! Focussing on complete language development be it vocabulary, spelling, pronounciation or other aspects it also comes with fun bonuses like lingots - so, you just need to bring along willingness to learn when you come to the class! :) I would highly recommend duo lingo to all language lovers :)Merci beaucoup, duo lingo team!
It's free and helps the kid in spanish.

column2: I Wish I Knew About Duolingo Sooner
column3: If you're not using Duolingo, you should be. The App provides a simple way to learn any language. I have a set goal to practice French five minutes a day and often stay on the App longer because the interface is user friendly and even fun! I tell everyone I know about this App. Quit saying "I want to learn Spanish one day" and start now!

column2: I think this is a very good program. They use pictures
column3: I think this is a very good program.  They use pictures, voice recognition, and recorded voices to aid you with the learning.  The sound quality of the recorded verses isn't the best but you can more or less make out what they are saying.  The give you daily email reminders to prompt you to study.  The only down side to the program is the limit choice of languages.  Otherwise, a very good program for learning a new language.

My love of  Italian music prompted my learning the language.  I'm so glad I found this program!  Now I find myself singing along and understanding a lot of it already after only a few lessons!  The program is really easy and fun at the same time, making understanding of the language just fall into place!  My son now uses it and I have it on every device I have! Love, love, love it!!!

Fantastic, easy to learn program and fun. Besides the written language you also get voice prompts so you hear how to say it. By the end of the first lesson, I could say several phrases and even a week later I still remember them. That is pretty good for woman  of 61 who is on several medications that cause short term memory loss. If you don't have memory problems, you will love this! If you have memory problems, you will love this! Win Win!!!

column2: Great tool, but the Kindle version needs work
column3: I love this app! It's easy to use, and reinforces the things I've learned in  class. But, the Kindle version doesn't give the option of using accents (at least, it doesn't for Spanish). The windows and  apple version do. The kindle app doesn't mark answers wrong for not having the accents, so you can still use it and  learn, but I feel like it builds bad habits. And, I wish there was a "vosotros" option, rather than just the Latin American version.

column2: pretty good app for keeping your memory fresh
column3: I'm always skeptical of language apps because  they're usually pretty limited but this turned out to be great. I've been learning French for the better part of 8 years but I'm not constantly practicing like I should so those basic words and phrases start to fade but this has really helped in keeping my memory fresh. Only thing I don't like is that the vocal exercises are a bit difficult because the app doesn't always hear me properly.

column2: love this app, it goes great with the website
column3: I use this app a lot. It is one of the strongest tools I've found to get me practicing French on an almost daily basis. There is more to learning a language than just this but practicing consistently is extremely important. Sometimes I play more than I intend because I'm close to finishing a section or completing a level or even passing a friend. My only gripe is that the one in the Kindle store doesn't keep up with the Google Play store.

They really make you work hard to learn a new language. So many real life scenarios and as you progress so does the work. You can test out your skills with others threw the online community. You also can translate web pages to earn your keep. You can't get bored because there's always something new to do and learn. I like how it helps you learn even if your late in life trying to learn a second language.

I'd always wanted to learn a second language.  I have a Rosetta Stone program but was very frustrated with it.  They never speak English making it extremely difficult to understand the proper grammar rules.  Duolingo is a wonderful program in the fact everything is explained in English.  Give this program a chance!!  It is very entertaining and additive in a great way.  If you've always wanted to learn another language, give it a try!

column2: Fun, Easy to Use, and a Great Way to Learn!
column3: I came across this app, because I was looking for a way to learn German, but without having to pay the price of Rosetta Stone. This game was exactly what I was looking for. It is a great on the go app, and is very easy to use for all ages. You can learn almost any language using this device and FOR FREE. I like how the app has matching games, pictures, and even voice recognition to make sure you are pronouncing the words/sentences correctly! It also gives you the option to turn off the voice recognition. I am thoroughly impressed with what this app has to offer!

Duolingo is a fun and easy way to learn another language. It's a little easier on a computer, but fun the same. The only problem I have is I don't know how to delete languages on my account. Apparently I am learning four languages now. And, they don't state the word very clearly on French. But otherwise, muy bien!

Duolingo is such a great app for language learning that exposes you to a variety of languages.However, while playing on Duolingo, it is VERY important to remember to also use materials to supplement your learning! Just using Duolingo and nothing else won't help you much with understanding grammar. In addition, I would also recommend you to use the web version as much as possible! The mobile version is slightly easier than the web one because writing out a sentence is just tapping words. :)Have fun!

column2: EXCELLENT - levels get progressively harder, and it's all free
column3: This has been a great app to review and deepen my Spanish. It's similar to Rosetta Stone in some ways, but I actually like this (FREE) program better.  There are great exercises to work on grammar as well as vocabulary, which is important, and each "lesson" is pretty short, so you can easily fit one in every day.  You can test out of each level if you're more advanced, so it's not boring. Highly recommend!

column2: The only thing I don't like is when you push the button to hear the ...
column3: Well I just started using the program yesterday. The only thing  I don't like is when you push the button to hear the word phonetically it's not Audible.  Other than that I believe I will learn a lot.

So well designed.  I took French in high school, so I do believe it's easier for anyone who has already studied how to learn a second language.  But this program is so pleasant and the strategy is excellent.  I'm doing well and enjoying the process.  Some additional materials will be needed, especially for learning verb tenses and possessives, but I would recommend this program highly for all beginners.  And...........it's free !

column2: Best app I've seen to learn Italian
column3: This app has a nice combination of written, oral, and aural practice. Also, it does a nice job of mixing the words together so that I have to remember each word individually as well as phrases.I knew some Spanish, which may have made this a bit easier, but other apps I've used to try to learn some Italian (for an upcoming vacation) have been little more than glorified flashcards. This app makes me recall vocabulary while actually using it, which makes it more fun and interesting, thus I am learning and retaining more.

column2: this is the greatest app ever conceived. no, really tho.
column3: this is an a amazing app and I'm so glad SOMEONE finally had the good thought that paying at least $500 to teach yourself a language is ridiculous. ive done Rosetta stone and this is not only comparable,  but better. it gives you "lingots" as prizes for doing perfect on quizzes, and then you can use those to buy stuff for your character,  or even bonus lessons I already speak Spanish,  I learner it inhigh school andill admit,  I'm really good at language. but you don't have to be to use this thing. I also like that it keeps track of your progress on a graph. it makes me want to study harder and harder each day so I get more XP than I did the day before. it truly is an amazing little tool. I work as a receptionist and I study with this app probably about 4 hours a day. I think to learn a language effectively,  you really have to do it everyday. right now, i'm teaching myself Portuguese. I plan to work my way through all the romance languages.

I've been listening to German for years now. I started because I love music and as it stands I love musicals one of my favorites has never had an English translation. So I've watched it in German many times. I know the story so I can generally recognize some words. But when I started duolingo it's like it all clicked. Everything I already knew made sense and I was able to rapidly increase my skill and better yet...I did it for free. It's one of my favorite apps now not only because the presentation makes it easy to practice anywhere but also because it made practicing fun!

This is a fun way to practice language. I got it before I took a French class, and I learned a lot of vocabulary and had a head start, but I wouldn't recommend trying to learn a language just through the app because it is harder to learn the rules, conjugation, etc. You get much more out of it when you use the app alongside an actual class.

column2: Good for forming a habit of practice.

The downside....it has very few phrases that you would use in a real life situation..."The shark is red, I am a butterfly, the cats are drinking tea..." part of the reason language programs do so poorly in public school is because you learn very few ways to apply the language to real life. column2: This is a great app for learning languages

column2: Really Good Language Learning Free Program

At the beginning of the year I gave myself the goal of learning a new language to fluency every two years. I'm probably not quite on track for that, but nearly all of the gains I have made in Spanish have been because of Duolingo (the rest from Memrise, which is also a great tool). I spend about twenty minutes a day with it, whenever I'm sitting around doing nothing useful: bus rides, waiting for someone, resting in between working outdoors, etc. My Spanish vocabulary has grown remarkably in the past several months, and I never feel like it's a major chore to practice with Duolingo. The comments on every word or phrase are super helpful when I can't figure out why my answer was wrong. I'm sure there are things that could be better, but this is one of my favorite apps and I recommend it to everyone I know who wants to learn or practice a language.

Downloaded this free app to brush up on Spanish (that I studied {badly} in college for two semesters).  The lessons are short and easy to digest, but lack the sort of foundation necessary to learn a new language.I understood verb conjugation before opening this app; had that not been the case, this method may have proved exasperating.  In word matching vocabulary drills, the word "eat" pairs as a correct response to all of the following: como (I eat), comes (you {familiar} eat); come (you {formal} eat; comemos (we eat); comeis (you plural {familiar} eat); and comen (you plural/they {formal}) eat.  A more helpful approach would have been to match "I eat" with "como," "we eat" with "comemos," etc.Showing, not telling is the process used by Duolingo.  Unfortunately, forms of speech are presented without the most basic explanation that is essential to understanding a new language.

column2: but it's the best of what I've found so far
column3: This is a really helpful app for learning other languages.  The audio check on your speaking has very loose parameters for what is accurate that you've said and it has some other minor issues, but it's the best of what I've found so far.

I really like this app, it keeps me motivated, it scolds me if I miss a day. I have been using it for about 2 months now and am getting much better with my Spanish. The voice recognition doesn't work but not a big deal, I am still learning.

Love using this app. Language learning in the 21st Century. It's easy & fun. Hopefully the old days of studying from a text the size of a telephone book & cassette tapes are gone forever. column3: I want to give this five stars - if this were the iPad version, I would. I really love this game. It starts you off with words easy to pronounce, and it makes sure you can pronounce them too. Ever since I got this game I've been having fantasies of me going to France and having full conversations with them.

column2: This Is A Great App and You Do Learn
column3: Fun and addictive.  I do Spanish and French.  Recently I took a speed Spanish course on line.  After using this app for weeks, I was ahead of the game when taking the course.  I never took Spanish in high school.  So apparently,  I actually learned something from this app!  I already understood the grammar rules and I knew most of the vocab already.  If I hadn't been usiing Duolingual, the course would  have been much too fast and too short.  I averaged 100% on every times and only missed one question on my final exam!The exercises really don't change much.  You are given a sentence in either the language you are learning or your native language to translate. If you set it, the exercises will also include you having to repeat a sentence in the language you hear.  (You can opt out if you are in public place and don't want to suddenly shout out , "I see a green pig" in Spanish in public).  Sometimes the speech recognition is iffy.  Although it seems to work much better on my Kindle than my phone.  The game runs very smoothly and doesn't crash (there was a very short period when it was crashing after an upgrade).If you don't understand why you got something wrong, you can immediately go into a forum discussing the sentence.  Usually there is a Duolingo staff person explaining, why the sentence is the way it is. Sometimes the sentences are a little weird and not something you would do in real life,  Sometimes the translation in English is a little off.  Anyway, you do have an option to send a notice to Duolingo that your answer should have been accepted if you got it wrong.The game, um, app has rewards that keep you going.  You an earn lingots which you can use to buy stuff in the store.  You earn lingots for going through an exercise without missing anything.  You get three hearts for each group of exercises. You can buy an extra one in the store.  There is a social aspect in that you can follow others.  But I don't see the worth, unless they are avid users like I'm.  There's an incentive to use it everyday so you don't break your streak.  You can also get notification or email reminders daily.You learn through repetition until you understand the grammar.  No grammar is explained.  There are not list of conjugated verbs.  From the very beginning, you are translating sentences.Research this app there's a great story behind it.  Then go view the Ted Talk video.

column2: so good. Duolingo is an excellent program for all ages
column3: My eldest is using this program and she installed it on her 9 year old sister's tablet so that she could learn French as well. So far, so good. Duolingo is an excellent program for all ages. Now I need to download it to my phone and start practicing too!

I have tried a few different programs for learning language, but this is one I can stick with. You can put in some practice from your phone, tablet or your computer.  It only takes a few minutes each day.  You can do as little or as much as you want. If you go to the Duolingo web site they give explanations with each lesson about the constructs of the language.  Estoy aprendiendo a hablar espaniol con Duolingo.

column2: Great! But perhaps more language options?
column3: It's been super fun and easy to use! Both myself and my Step-Daughter are using it to help us learn Spanish! Although, I do wish it gave me the option to learn Korean as well. The only one on there says you have to already know Korean to use it. (??)

This program seems very responsive to individual strengths and weaknesses and makes addressing them great fun.  Can be addictive (an hour a day??) or just perfect for doing a little bit at a time and building on your skills at your own pace.  I actually look forward to these exercises every day!

I absolutely LOVE this!  I already have a little knowledge of the languages i an learning and i think that helps.  Seem like it might be harder of i knew nothing.  I like the items where i can select the words for the answers and put them in order more than when i have to type the answers because autofill and small typos kill me. column2: A 100% FREE learning app based off the famous website
column3: The Duolingo app is based off of the website with the same name. It currently has lessons in Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, and English. This is a complete course that teaches you a language in bite sized pieces with a fun method. You start at the bottom of a tree and work your way to the top where you can win a trophy. By the time you are done with your tree you will have 1500 words from the target language in your vocabulary. You'll able to read and write in the language and maybe even enjoy some television. How do I know? I've completed my Spanish tree and am now brushing up. I'm currently level 17 in Spanish. Yes, you level up, because this is a game-like environment designed to inspire you to try harder to learn faster.Duolingo can be free FOREVER because they use translations provided by users to sell to companies like CNN. You are providing a service (translating) in exchange for getting a service (learning a language).If you want to learn a language fluently on your tablet get this app and the Memrise app (which is also based off a free website).

this app is great!! It allows you to fully understand and learn a language for free. It is very easy to follow and has a listening activity and a hands on. The languages are Spanish,German,Italian,and French. This app also has visual to make it a lot easier to learn the language and alot faster. It has all of the aspects needed to make a very good app to learn a language on. SO WORTH IT & FREE HANDS DOWN BEST APP

I think I could actually get proficient in Portuguese within a few months if I work with Duolingo at least 30 minutes per day. That's not bad! I can imagine that kids would do even better than adults because they take to the technology so much easier. I hope they add more languages!

column2: I've enjoy the application for the different learning levels
column3: So far, I've enjoy the application for the different learning levels. It's a nice plus to connect with other that can "challenge" you in pursuit of achieving more in desired language. Not sure if one likes that it does the constant reminders of practice time, but sure every good application has ways of modifying things.

I had taken French years ago and started the French to see how much I remembered. I did pretty well! I love this app. I had heard good things about it and I can confidently add to the praise of Duolingo. The method for teaching is simple and allows you to learn how to form simple sentences from the get go. This is useful in order to see the grammatical structure in which sentences are formulated in whichever language you're learning. A feature that I really appreciate, and which is extremely helpful to understand mistakes, is the comments section. You can click to see what other learners have asked/replied to to the same mistake and even contribute to the discussion. For some learners this is a key point for the learning process. I highly recommend this app as an effective self study tool.

The duolingo is the best translator I have ever TRIED! (And believe me I have tried them all) The duolingo is 100% free! column2: for new and "just to brush up" learners

The creaters use Roedger's learning technique, which improves learning dramatically. My 10-year-old is a beginning learner, and he's picked up a lot of French. I love this app. I hope it stays free, without ads. I'd gladly pay for it.

I've used it on the web on my laptop, on my Kindle, and on my Android phone and while there are minor differences, it's easy to use on each of them.

column2: Great app for the casual learner
column3: I've tried the elementary levels of both French and German and have come to the conclusion that this is a great little app for the price. Kindle fire has no mic, so it never prompts me to do speaking bits. But I also haven't had a problem figuring out tenses or grammar, as the other reviews suggest. Very intuitive play. The only problem I have is that you need to do at least a little every day, or you will forget  what you learned. I don't think you will ever achieve fluency with a language app, but this will take you through a lot of the basic vocab and structure.

column2: Don't waste your money on something else.
column3: This is about the best imaginable app for what it does. I think it would be great if it had more languages (I.e. Mandarin, Aramaic, Arabic, Yiddish, Latin, Ancient Greek, Elfin, etc.) Using this helps a lot with reading, writing and understanding the chosen language. column2: Duolingo a good way to learn a language.
column3: This has been quite a surprise.  I thought maybe I could learn just a few words to help me when I travel but was happy to see that not only do I learn what can help me there but words that will help me converse with my gardner for example.  Although he speaks English he is more comfortable with Spanish and it gives me a chance to practice.  If you use the mic  you get feed back on how you sound when you speak and if you are pronouncing the words correctly.  You can't beat the price when companies that teach languages can charge hundreds of dollars.  I also like the convenience of having this on my Kindle so I can learn and practice whenever I want.  The only drawback that I can see is that they have a limited number of languages that you can learn at this time.

Like alot

column2: Helps for learning the basics for an additional language.

You have to finish the lesson to be able to start at the next one, if you quit or exit in the middle of the lesson, you have to start the lesson over, regardless how far you were. Love it though!

My favorite app. I regret buying rosetta stone... Rosetta stone does not allow you to use the app unless your paying extra every month. And their system is boring. In the other hand, Duolingo keeps you on your toes with daily challenges. And their owl is pretty cute.

column2: a great way to learn a new language
column3: I have been using duolingo to learn Spanish. I think it is the most intuitive way to learn a language other than immersion.  I like that you can go back and redo lessons if you take a break from it for a few days, and brush up on what you've previously learned. Sometimes I don't understand why my answers are incorrect, though and thst can be frustrating.

I have so much to say about this program, but I will keep it short. It has it goods and its bads. It assumes that you know some of the language already. The pronouns are throwing me for a loop. Very tricky and they don't explain that part too well. Other than that, I like being able to hear it, learn how to spell it etc. I am still plugging away on it. Wish me luck! Darned those pronouns!

column2: Duolingo is great! As a retired language teacher
column3: Duolingo is great! As a retired language teacher, it is obvious to me that this program is based on solid language acquisition principles. It recycles, recycles, and repeats per individual learning patterns. It's dynamic and exciting. Seriously! I've tried other language programs, and they're somewhat boring. You'll stick with this one!

Good app

This app is great, I am so excited to see if I can start understanding Spanish speaking people,and then be able to speak to them. I am 7 levels in and when we drive down the street, I can read the Spanish stores and know what it says, Exciting. The only thing I think would be better to know in the beginning is the numbers, alphabet, and how to pronounce them.
I've been using Duolingo for several years on my computer and have found it very helpful.  Now I can carry it in my pocket and practice, practice, practice even more -- it's wonderul.

Although I love having goals, I found this website a little off-putting when I was reminded at 11 pm that I had my quota of French yet to be met.  Although I had targeted 10 minutes per day for study, it many times took me 45 minutes to complete the two lessons each day, not something that inspires confidence.  I also found it difficult when new words or phrases would be randomly introduced without any predicate.  Considering that you have three possible mistakes in the course of 20 questions, new words at the end of a difficult sequence forced me to start again.  Slight spelling typos were also problematic when my i-Phone keyboard auto-corrected.  Although I love this concept, I think the program needs work.
Won't work on the Kindle fire. It just keeps going back to the first screen no matter how many times I pick a language. So frustrating!

column2: Worth the time spent practicing with it
column3: I used this to work on my once-fluent but rusty French before a trip to France, in conjunction with many other things such as watching youtube videos in French.  Alone it won't have you speaking good French, but if you need to brush up it's well worth the time you'll spend with it.  I didn't finish it before my trip and plan to continue with it for my NEXT (hopefully) trip to France.

Awesome refresher.Keeps you interested by rewarding you as you move along and allows you to set the intensity of the learning by setting minimum daily time goals. I enjoy the additional quiz options it gives to test your learning, and the hints if you are unsure of the correct word.

This app makes it fun to learn a language.  It has short lessons that help you to understand conversational Italian (my language of choice, but several others are offered). The lessons are well organized and build upon one another.  The format allows the student to have success, which makes you want to continue the process.  Since the format is similar to a game, it challenges you to go to the next level.  I also like the review process that allows you to go back to previous lessons. I'm currently on Level 3 so I don't know how comprehensive the entire program will be, but it definitely appears it will give you a very good foundation in a new language.  The only criticism I have is that the native speaker is sometimes hard to understand and I have to listen to her several times to make sure of pronunciation.  However, that is becoming less of a problem as I become more accustomed to her voice.

column2: Great for language review and getting started.
column3: It's good for reviewing infrequently used verb tenses and menus for travel. Pronunciation is included.Georges C

I was seeking a language app or program, and I discovered Duolingo in an online review. I studied Spanish, French, and German some years ago, and Duolingo provides an enjoyable way to review these languages.  It combines reading, writing, listening, and speaking practice in each lesson.The lessons are brief enough to complete in a few minutes, yet long enough to reinforce vocabulary and grammar retention.I installed Duolingo on my Kindle and iPhone, and I bookmarked the website on my tablet PC. The Kindle format seems to be the most convenient.I wish that Duolingo included Chinese.

I loved how this app built on previous lessons to teach grammar through use. I've been on the verge of true fluency in spanish for many years; reading and dreaming but never able to catch more than a few words in conversation or being able to speak. Duolingo was the perfect app for stitching everything together into a comprehensive whole. I've always struggled with grammar in spanish, and this app helped me develop a subconscious understanding. The only complaint I have is that there weren't formal grammatical sections. It would be nice to have lessons strictly on conjugation that I could practice.

column2: great for practice, short on grammar
column3: I love the lessons I've taken in Italian, but feel that figuring out the rules shouldn't be left to a forum of comments on each question. It wiuld be nice to have a place to go on the app to get straight up answers without relying on other amateurs. But for free....I'm pretty happy with it.

column2: Why did I spend $400 bucks of perfectly good beer money on Rosetta Stone?
column3: I've been doing the PC version of Duolingo for a half a year.  I wanted to keep up with my German skills after I had completed all 5 levels of Rosetta Stone and installing Rosetta Stone on my work PC was not gonna happen.  I saw an ad for Duolingo and decided to play with it.RS may be a little bit slicker but certainly not $400 slicker.  I was in Germany and found that the natives will try to humor you for a while but most of them speak better English than most Americans anyway..  If I had it to do over again I would have done Duolingo and spent the $400 on bier :)The android app is even better than the PC version.  I'm using it to review my college Spanish now and I've found it to be fun and slightly addictive.  Sometimes my 3 modules a day mysteriously turn into a half dozen.

column2: Duolingo is a great App to learn a new Language.
column3: I have tried this app once and am learning a little bit of the language I have Picked.  It has you do some learning one day and then you have to wait until the next day.  The only thing is that you can only learn one language at a time.  I would like to learn more that that.  But I guess I will wait until I learn this language and then go onto the next language I want to learn.

I love this app. I work on learning Spanish at least an hour a day. My vocabulary in Spanish is well over hundreds of words and phrases. Great for beginners like me who want to read, write and say the correct pronunciation of the words. I use this app along with a couple other free  (or nearly free, depending on where you get them) apps and books to better understand the rules of the language.

This is a great program. I hear the Spanish (my chosen new language) spoken & written. I have to speak it and write it. There's a good mix of all of these and I can go back and practice, practice, practice. It really is a lot of fun. I use it on the computer, which gives me the chance to use the special letters you need (accent marks, etc) and I now have it on my Kindle. It's different on the Kindle, but just as fun. Plus it's free!

Very easy to use with a friendly interface. It seems to use the right amount if repetition along with various methods of presentation to make sure you learn the concepts. Plus it's a fun way to learn. I recommend it to anyone wanting a low stress way of learning a language.
An excellent language learning program. I found it immensely helpful planning for a trip to Central America.

Fantastic app for easy learning...if ya want to work on it !!One major flaw for me is im learning Spanish , French and brushing up on Irish but the app regularly opens up in'learning English for Dutch speakers 'Takes a while to get back to my courses.This happens on my kindle fire 2014 hdand fire phone and for reference ipod touch 5th gen

I took French in high school but after many years of not speaking it I have forgotten a lot of what I learned. Duolingo is very easy and fun to use. The lessons slowly teach you more and more words and along with the images you can progress very quickly. I enjoy the fact that you can learn a few different languages. You can't beat a free language learning program especially since similar programs like Rosetta Stone cost a lot of money and work pretty much the same way this program does. I would recommend this to anybody interested in learning a second or even third language and for those who are learning English as their second language.

column2: Great Way to Learn New Languages
column3: I've actually not tried this out on my Kindle Fire yet, but I thought it would be a good idea to have it on there, just in case. I do have this app on my iphone though. I've found that it's a LOT easier and more motivating to use this app on mobile devices than it is to do it on the computer. Don't get me wrong, the website/computer version is good and well, but can be a little cumbersome. The app, if you've installed the right keyboards, which I don't think is very difficult (easy on the iphone, not sure about the Kindle yet. It was a Christmas present so I still am figuring it out), it changes automatically to the keyboard you need for each section of the lessons. I'm currently taking several languages, and it's nice to have the proper keyboard, a specified layout, and frankly, a whole lot less hassle.The downside is that the app takes longer to get the site updates. It took about a month for the app to acquire Russian for English speakers after the website launched it. If you don't mind that, then there isn't much of an issue, aside from actually learning the languages, which can be challenging enough, depending on the language and dedication you choose.

I use this mostly on my phone and tablet. Good for 4 of the languages I study.  More fun than games and you learn a lot on the 4 levels of language learning: reading, writing, listening, and speaking. I also recommend for my ESL students.

I've tried a lot of language apps, paid and free, and Duolingo is the best one.  Most language apps teach child-level vocabulary, one word at a time.  Duolingo uses complete sentences of increasing complexity from beginner lessons to advanced conversational language use.Every sentence of every lesson also has the option to discuss and comment.  If part of a lesson is hard to understand, people of mixed language levels including native speakers are probably already discussing it.Overall just a wonderful app, if you want to learn a language, get Duolingo!

column2: Using it 32 consecutive days & counting! Need prior knowledge! You will learn spelling and grammer! But doesn't explain/teach!
column3: Over 20 years ago, I lived in Italy for 4 years (not consecutive) and had several group lessons but despite the efforts of my various instructors, I just didn't have the patience to learn the grammar.  My knowledge of vocabulary was good enough for me to communicate and function but I never could get the hang of conjugating verbs, learning about the articles, and spelling words properly.  Later lived in Latin America for 4 years and that messed up my language skills big time!  So, now I speak both languages very poorly - just throwing out words to make a mishmash sentence.  A couple years ago I went back to Italy and they asked me if I could speak english because they couldn't tell if I spoke Spanish, Italian or some unknown language!  (Note: My native language is American English)So, I'm returning to Italy again for a 2 week vacation and I'm determined to be better this time and not embarrass myself.  So, I got Duolingo on Feb 20th and believe it or not, I'm truly addicted to the program!  I have a full time job and when I come home I'm tired and yet, every single day, I spend 1 hour to 2 hours working on these mini lessons from Duolingo!  Funny, they are kind of addictive.  They force you to learn the language by making you hear the language, speak the language, interpret the phrase back and forth between languages, to spell it properly, and put it in the correct order.  If you do it wrong more than 3x then, it kicks you out of the lesson and makes you start over, but the lesson is different the next time around.  Now, you would think one would get discouraged, I mean, I've had to redo some lessons about 6x, and yet, somehow, the way it is structured, it makes me want to keep at it and do it right!  I mean it is working on me, one of the most stubborn learners!So there are a multitude of topics at every level (beginning/intermediate/advanced) and within each topic they have 4-8 different minilessons in each topic.  It visually has a graph that shows you where you are at.  And, even when you think you are done with a topic (whew), every couple of days, that topic reopens and they make you practice it again so you don't forget!  Wow!  So, even with my background knowledge/vocabulary of Italian, I'm still at the very end of the beginners (Level 8; 335 words!) and I've been working hard for a month!  Oh, another downer is I was working on it for 12 days and suddenly it reset and told me I was back on day 1.  I thought it did that every 12 days but now it says I'm at 16 days. (IF ANYONE READS THIS FROM DUOLINGO; I WANT IT RESET TO FEB 20TH THAT I'VE DONE IT EVERY SINGLE DAY!).The downside is that if you have never ever studied a latin language this would be super hard for you.  I think if you already know a similar language like spanish and how it is structured, it will be easier for you.  However, if you are a person who has never studied a romance language and absolute beginner that only knows Ciao, etc..and hever had a lesson, then, you will have a hard time.  Also, if you are a miserable speller in your native language, learning to spell Italian will kill you because it is so difficult to get all of the vowels in the right place.  I have many times translated a very complicated sentence from english to Italian, only to get it counted wrong cuz I misspelled 1 letter!  But, it forces me to really think what I'm writing and how it all comes together to form a complete sentence.  Also, it really doesn't teach you the vocabulary or the grammar rules, at all.  I kept failing the lesson because I wasn't sure what some articles meant because they seem to mean different things at different times.  Yesterday, I finally broke down and got a grammar book so I can look up what all of the articles mean.  So, this program works for people who are already familiar.  I'm worried that when I get in the more immediate level, I might need to study before using this as it isn't really a good teacher - doesn't explain or introduce new concepts.  Good for people that really want to tighten up what they already know and go farther.

I am a beginner with the Spanish language. The structure of the lessons is confusing. Duolingo gets into the case structure too soon to suit me. Often I can not understand the Spanish phases. I must repeat them several times. I have had other Spanish software that I liked better.

column2: Easier to use than Rosetta Stone, and free!
column3: I am using this app to brush up on Spanish (learned 30 years ago) and German (picked up from my German family, but never studied formally).  I don't know how it would work for a language you were never exposed to before, but for brushing up purposes it is excellent.  You can easily test out of what you already know and focus on the areas that are weaker.  I also like that you are working on so many skills at once--from fairly passive translation (choosing from a list of English words), to straight translation in both directions, plus dictation and oral practice.  I mainly use it on my Kindle but also have it on my android phone.  Many thanks/muchas gracias/vielen Dank to the developers for keeping it free and ad-free!  Hoping they will add Russian to the list.

Highly recommended for anyone who wishes to learn any language.  There are many languages to choose from.  You can use this to learn not only how to spell the word but also how to say them.  It listens to hear if you have said something approximately correct and gives you feedback as to whether or not you said it right.  I learned quite a bit in a short amount of time.  This is perfect for those who want to learn a language from nothing out even those who haven't spoken said language in a bit and need some reminders.

I'm refreshing some lost subtleties in french and quickly developing my Spanish skills. I've tried many other methods with limited success. The reading, writing, listening, and speaking combination in this free tool is very effective.

I am enjoying using this program but I feel a real need to have some supplementary materials to be included.  I am having trouble with the 'past tense' and extra help is needed.  I will continue using the program but I don't feel as confident as when I first started that the comprehension is there.  Many opportunities for review which I appreciate.  Overall, a good program!

column2: Doesn't work on my Fire tablet
column3: I downloaded the app onto my son's Fire tablet with no issue, but when I go into the first lesson, the pictures are all blank.  A quick Google search tells me this is a common issue with this app on Fire devices.  I'm looking forward to trying again when the bug has been fixed.

Anytime I have to wait I jump on Duolingo and practice my Italian.  I love this app.  There should be a skip button though.  Sometimes I am in a place that I can't repeat the phrase in Italian.  Like an office lobby where I like to use the translate sentences and pairs.  That is the only thing missing.  I really love this app.

This app is great. I have been trying to learn Irish for years, and had basically given up.  A friend who was learning Welsh recommended Duolingo. My one major critique is that there isn't always audio to play what the words sound like. At times the corrections also feel a little nitpicky.  The reminders can be annoying, but they annoy you into practicing. (Except in the case of my wife, who Duolingo stated they were giving up on ) All in all, I use it every night and it keeps me engaged and learning.

I am shocked I was able to get this for free! Quite an amazing app. You practice a little every day, and it reminds you to practice, and tracks your progress. I like this even better the Pimsler CD set I tried years ago. Divided into categories, and uses pictures to help, I am blown away. This app makes learning a new language fun and easy. Try this before you buy an expensive language lesson set.

I had just begun the Rosetta Stone Spanish edition, and was looking for something to be sort of a "supplement".  My niece recommended Duolingo.  I am amazed at how good it is.  And it's free.  It's a terrific add-on to Rosetta Stone because it explains some of the grammar rules, where Rosetta uses strictly the "learn by doing" approach. I'm very, very pleased.

column2: A great app for learning a new language
column3: This is a great app for learning a new language. It's entertaining and I've learned far more than I ever thought I would. I'm not very good with picking up new languages, so if this app was able to teach me then it can teach anyone.

Its fun, but every single time I go onto the app Food 2 is weakened. I get every single one correct! I am learning Spanish. Plus it never makes it clear when to use escribe or escriben or escribed or whatever. Plus when it says to listen then type it in I can't because I'm in bed at night or in a public place. Also the idioms is just terrible in my opinion. It was a huge waste of time. I just hate it how I never get a word wrong but I still have to redo every lesson

This is a pretty good app to learn a few languages. I have not spoke any of the languages on the ap to anyone, so it is not exactly the app for me, but if you are going to a different countries with a different language this would not be a bad app to get for the trip.

I had purchased another language program but was having a hard time, as it was mostly just l listen and repeat. I had looked into Rosetta Stone but simply couldn't afford it. That said, I have found this app to be very helpful. I enjoy the speaking and listening exercises in both English and the language being learned that help me commit it to memory.

A girlfriend of mine and I are going to Europe later this summer, and I wanted to brush up on my French as she is fluent in German. It has been a great refresher course. I started out by trying to test out of some of the common phrases and found that I needed work on some of my tenses and grammar. The game utilizes both English and French (German, Italian or Spanish, depending on which language you choose to learn) words and sentences along with your device's built-in microphone to have you practice saying some phrases yourself. (This function can be turned off. If you're in a noisy, crowded place or don't want to be overheard.)The program, breaks down the learning of the language in much the same way as Rosetta Stone. That is to say that unlike your high school language teacher, you're not just learning active verbs or inactive verbs or pronouns in each lesson. You are learning phrases and how to build conversational structures.A couple of words of caution, however.The app assumes you have a basic understanding of the language you're learning. For example, I have a high school level knowledge of French, and this is been an excellent refresher course and brought back much of what I learned in school. However, when I switched over to try and learn a few German phrases so that I could be just as helpful on our trip, I found it more difficult and challenging to to engage with the program. That isn't to say, that someone could just try to pick up a language (for instance, I'm also working with the Italian section of the app. So when we go through Italy, I'll have some knowledge of the language.Second, the app won't let you advance to the next segment until you can complete the first without four or five errors per segment. Although it's not, strictly speaking, concerned with spelling as long as you're in the neighborhood, it will deduct points if you consistently spell something wrong or don't use the right accent over a letter.Overall though, I have really enjoyed using this and would recommend it to someone who wants to brush up on a language or learn key phrases in order to travel.

I absolutely love this app.  Unlike many it is free and is really effective.  I tried learning Swedish by book but, books they have limited information.  Such as, pronunciation.  So I tried this app after stumbling upon many other numerous apps.  Unquestioningly great!

I have tried to learn Spanish several times, taking classes, listening to tapes, etc. without much success. But with Duolingo I feel like I'm finally making some progress. I'm just up to the tenth lesson but I am amazed at the effectiveness of this painless app.
I'm working on learning French.  Very relaxed way to learn, and you don't realize how much you are learning at first.  Have recommended to others.

duolingo has created quite the little app. I have it on both my iPhone and kindle, so the platform is a little different.  I like how the iPhone has a male voice as well.It's a little addictive, just like a good interactive game should be.  I have definitel learned some since I started two weeks ago.  My only complaint is not having some words introduced before having to figure out what they mean.

Both my 12 year old son and I have been practicing Spanish with this app. It's been great. We've been learning a lot.He said it helps him with his Spanish class at school. The lessons are structured well with a lot of reinforcement. The achievement awards are a nice bonus!
Fast paced, done in bite size 5 minute packets, helpful in pronunciation and fun, fun, fun! I'm doing Spanish and German and can't get enough. Finally, a freebie is worth more than you paid.

column2: Best learning tool I have found
column3: A friend recommended this app to me, and I am so thankful. I have no facility for learning foreign languages.  I have purchased, and tried several language software products in the past, but given up.  Duolingo is different...it is entertaining, tackles new languages (and they have many to choose from), from many directions...visual, auditory, game type questions.  It helps keep me entertained and focused at the same time.  Who knows, after I master French, I might tackle Italian.

column2: one may be better able to read the language but speaking or understanding ...
column3: I think that it would be difficult to learn a language the way Dualingo is presented.  Words are introduced  tasking the learner to translate the word......so must guess what the word is and find out meaning by failing.  At the end, one may be better able to read the language but speaking or understanding the spoken language not so.much.

I love the ability to just poick up a new language in my free time and at my own pace. Right now I'm using this app to improve on my Spanish, learn more Portuguese, and start German. This app starts with the practical use of each language and gradually teaches other basics. The only element I would like more practice with would be just vocabulary on its own but for a free app I have no complaints!

Was turned on to this by my younger sister and I am now addicted. I have taken Spanish for 12 years, and this app has helped me strengthen my ability in not only speaking the language, but understanding it spoken at a normal rate. It's a lot of fun, too! Whether you are looking to learn a language, or to just looking to do something in your spare time, I highly recommend this app!

Duolingo is an absolutely incredible application. The fact that you can learn an entire language (or as many as yo I want to) on the go, and for free, is too awesome of this company. Learning a language isn't only fun, it's a great workout for your brain. If you want to learn a new language look no further. You have definitely found the right place, here at Duolingo.

I absolutely love this app! No matter what language you are trying to learn duolingo is the spot to be! I've learned so much and its fun too! I love that you can see how far along your friends have gotten and compete to be the highest rank. I also love that if you don't understand a phrase or a word you can click and see what other users said about this sentence and comment your question immediately. My only complaint is that the recorded woman speaking the phrases can be a little hard to understand sometimes. Overall I love this app and highly recommend!!! :)

column2: Great for refreshing or learning a new language
column3: Love it. I am using it to refresh my Italian that I learned in college 20 years ago. I wish that you could look up grammar rules when you mess up, or that you got a better explanation of the error when using the iPhone. When using Duolingo in larger screen like Kindle Fire you can read other peoples comments on a question or ask questions yourself. I wish the same function was available in the iphone.

I have wanted to learn Spanish for a long time, but could not afford most courses. I found Duolingo, and it is by far the best I have ever seen! I love it! And I am learning Spanish at my speed, and thoroughly enjoying it! Can't thank you enough! I am in my seventies, and actually learning a new language! Try it, you will not be disappointed!

column2: I am not learning Spanish, I am learning Iu ...
column3: I am not learning Spanish, I am learning Iu Mien, which is a language not commercially available.  However, I am using Duolingo as a template for learning phrases.  I translate from English and Spanish into my target language and it is very helpful.  It requires that I think about the grammatical structure as well as memorizing words in my target language.

A little rusty on my Spanish so i wanted to get better.  This program is great and free.  You can start with basics to refresh what you already know or you can skip to advanced.  The lessons have you translating from English into Spanish or Spanish into English.  They make a game of it so it's more fun to learn.  I recommend it to anyone who wants to brush up on a language or start learning a new one.

column2: Among the best language courses, yet free
column3: I've been exposed to quite a few language courses over the years and I have to say that this is a very effective method.  Duolingo is free, yet it surpasses the vast majority of expensive language courses.  I appreciate the flexibility of being able to do the courses online or as a Kindle app.  Duolingo is the obvious first choice when it comes to starting to learn a language.

column2: A great way to learn a language
column3: This is almost a painless way to learn a language.  It makes learning into a sort of a game with rewards and encouragement.  It keeps you coming back for the next lesson.  And better yet, it is free! Further, there the opportunity to ask questions and get answers from other students and native language speakers.  If you want to learn a language, try Duolingo.  I think you will like it.

column2: Top Notch, Brilliant, and You Become Part of  a Greater Whole
column3: This program works great, and covers everything: Reading, Writing, Listening and Speaking.The idea behind it is that if we get enough people learning another language, and then put those people to work translating web pages, before long the entire web will be available to everybody in all languages!!!This really is a noble goal.Go to the Duolingo web page [...], and see the film "This is how we do it."  This is what the internet is all about.I have it working on my laptop, Kindle Fire, and Ipad. Can't beat that.Much better than Rosetta Stone, which not only costs $$$, but also ties you down to one computer - a measly one seat license.Not Duolingo, as many devices as you want, and it syncs between all of them.Run your pointer - don't walk it - over to the Duolingo download page now!!!Walter

I can't use the conversational parts of this app. Otherwise, it's a pretty good app. It might be better if at some point it took you through the alphabet and how accents and pronunciation works (for Spanish). It's an easy system and I've always thought knowing that was helpful.

You match up words to pictures, type phrases in other languages, practice speaking with the microphone and you get instant feedback if you're doing it right or not. The great part is it's free! I also love the different ways you can learn the new words, like they say I  then you say it or they give you the English way and you have to type the Spanish way. I have only been using this app for two days. It is laid out pretty good, but it is difficult to judge it with only two sessions.
