column2: A not so mobile mobile app.
column3: While the workflows for this app feel better than the PC version of the software, the app is severely limited by it's requirement for an internet connection.  I started using the app at work, which luckily has WiFi, however as my device has no cellular connectivity, I have been unable to use it during my recent travels, nor will I be able to use it to study during the 12+ hours it will take to fly Germany,With the Kindle Fire version of the App, the only apparent need for the internet connection is to sync your progress to the Rosetta Stone servers,  which is useful if you are going back and forth between your PC and mobile device while learning.  However, even this functionality does not work reliably; in my experience the App and PC only synced automatically every third or forth attempt.  While the PC has a force sync option this is not available on the mobile app so you are forced to restart the application through the device settings and hope that your PC synced properly at home.With these issues in mind and the fact that I like to use my Kindle while away from work or home, I wish the Rosetta Stone would have chosen a different method to generate a micro purchase income from their users; such as charging a one time fee to download the App, or charging for some of their more advanced online services.  The fact that I can't use the App as a a true mobile learning platform is endlessly irksome.I also wish that Rosetta stone had built in better orientation support for the app.  I have yet to figure out how the app is determining it's orientation for the session, but more often than not, the app will be incorrectly positioned in relation to how I wish to hold my device.  This is especially troublesome when attempting to use the app while charging the device.TL:DR - While the orientation problems with the app can be annoying, the biggest limiting factor is the requirement for an internet connection.  Which if you are using a device without cellular support effectively makes your mobile device about as portable as your home PC.

they show photos, usually four, and then they have a phrase; you choose the photo that fits the phrase.  There is NO English involved, which seems daunting at first, and you probably will choose some (maybe many) incorrect match-ups between phrases and photos, but you will eventually choose the correct pairing and learn the work or phrase.I get why there is no English as in other products as it's really a crutch and I think will slow down learning, but at times it is frustrating when you see a word with another word, and then later on you see the same word with another word... like 'La femme' for one photo, and 'Elle femme' for another later on... haven't figured out what the significance of that first word is yet, and it isn't explained, so I did pick up two additional books; one is just a pronunciation guide, and the other is a dictionary.I found the second lesson confusing at first as I didn't know what they were expecting me to do, and with no English instructions it was fairly frustrating at first.  A few tries later I realized that they were just speaking phrases and they wanted me to choose the photo of the scene they were depicting, based on the limited vocabulary they had taught in lesson one.Overall, I'm very happy with it and think that I can learn the language by going through all five levels, which were in the set that I bought during a brief 1/2 off special.  Now, something that I believe about RossettaStone is this; this software system doesn't want to just help you learn some of the language, words, phrases, etc. but is teaching you to start 'thinking' in the language, and it's already working.  Yesterday I saw a small group of men chatting in line at the coffee shop and my brain didn't register 'men' it registered des hommes.  Ha ha ha.  Yikes.

column2: Makes Learning a New Language Easy
column3: Rosetta Stone really does make learning a new language easy and feels quite natural.The Kindle ap is excellent for learning the sounds, understanding the spoken and written word of a new language.The only real downside I've noted deals with keeping track of plurals, special rules, feminine versus .masculine or neuter and first person, second person, third person usages.  These are there and they are practiced but they are not clearly explained.  A great deal must be inferred.  But then, this is the natural way our babies learn their languages as well.  None the less, after the first few sections, I did pick up an inexpensive grammar book to answer and clarify some of these questions.By the way, Rosetta Stone is NOT free, only the mobile interface application is free.  But  I did not expect Rosetta Stone to be free.  It's a well designed, well presented study program.  I wouldn't expect this level of quality to be free.

Used Rosetta Stone for 3 1/3 years and finished the five levels of Mandarin.  Then I went to China for a month to study further.  I was very comfortable with the language, and people were amazed that all I'd done was "study online" (I did online lessons every week).  If you stick with it and do the online classes you'll learn your language in the speaking area.  I'm now reviewing grammar, as it isn't strong in grammar or writing characters, and I learned characters on my own.

This app is easy to use and you will learn beyond just basic phrases. However, if you are trying to learn a language you are totally unfamiliar with (I was raised in a Spanish-speaking USA territory, learned English as a second language, and I'm trying to learn Japanese on my own), a good university level/self-learning language study and workbook will be necessary. You will also need a good dictionary. Rosetta Stone will not teach you why the verbs and other conjugations are happenning, and you'll end up doing a lot of guesswork when dealing with past, present and future conjugations. As a companion of a college course curriculum or self-study college book, it will be great to have because you will practice pronunciation and reading aloud without having another person there, and it will correct you if you mispronounce words! If you are already familiar with the language, then Rosetta Stone will be all the refresher you'll need.

column2: Not free, not cheap, and a bit shady, but works as promised
column3: This app is fine. It is easy to set up, and delivers the content well. Be forewarned however that it requires a subscription fee to use it past the demo period. (Amazon needs to start differentiating between demos and apps in the titles, but that's another issue)The Rosetta Stone teaching method is the best out there for practical (i.e. non-academic) language study.That being the case, it is a shame that they use such shady (and as others have posted - greedy) business practices. This app is a perfect illustration: Rosetta offers this app as a "companion" to their desktop software (which itself is extremely expensive) , but then "pulls the rug" out from under their customers by charging more for it after the initial period. While not fraud (they do tell you up front), it does feel like a bit of a shakedown.This is in addition to the fact that they charge the same for their courses whether they're the physical product (disc), download, or online versions. All versions require internet access to activate them - so why is this?Moreover, the disc version I bought came encased in a shameful amount of cardboard and plastic. The contents consisted of two discs, a cheap (and unnecessary) headset/microphone unit, and a (also unnecessary) plastic activation card. These were inside a cardboard sleeve, which was in a plastic wrapper, inside a small box, which was in a larger box, which itself was surrounded by a cardboard sleeve, which was taped shut and shrink-wrapped. Seriously? C'mon folks -it's not like you're transporting the *actual* Rosetta Stone here. Someone needs to tell the Rosetta Stone folks that connecting the planet linguistically isn't going to mean anything if there aren't any trees left.They've got us over a barrel folks -their language method really is that good, but is it worth the cost? You decide.

column2: Will Not Work On The New Kindle Fire HDX
column3: Rosetta Stone is a great learning tool. I have subscribed to the online course for over a year now and my French has improved dramatically. However the Rosetta Course App is awful. It’s only designed for Android Operating Systems and is incompatible with the OS on the new Kindle Fire HDX. The app will crash everytime the program tries to load after I sign in. I wish I would have known that prior to purchasing my new Kindle Fire, for being able to learn on the go was the primary reason I even purchased the new Kindle.  I contacted the Rosetta Stone Tech Department regarding this issue back in January and was in contact with someone there throughout the first 3 months of 2014. The issue was resolved in late March 2014 when there was an update on the App that made it work with the new Kindle Fire. I was able to use the app finally and was very happy. However Rosetta Stone continued to make updates to the App and now it’s back to not working. I’m able to put in my username and password and then it will just crash on the load screen. I tried multiple times to uninstall and redownload the app to see if it will work, but it always does the same thing. I tried the App on my friends Kindle Fire HDX and again the same issue, the App won’t even load properly. This is a rip off! I tried contacting the Rosetta Stone Tech Department several times, was on the phone with them for hours, and I either got hung up on or had e-mails that were not returned for days or even weeks at a time. Considering how much I’m paying for this each month this is downright unacceptable. Very unhappy with this app and with Rosetta Stone’s tech department at the moment.

The price makes you want to scream but, once you give it a try ( I HIGHLY recommend the free trial before putting down your hard earned money ) and decide to buy, you'll know that you have made a wise investment if your intentions really are to learn a new language and speak it with confidence. The app itself works great. In a lot of ways, it is better than the desktop application. You can push through the lessons quickly on a tablet and the voice recognition on tablets seems to work really well. That's where the good traits end. I spent a lot of money on levels 1-5 (the French desktop application). 3 months of "online" access were included. That means in 3 months, I can't use this app anymore unless I pay even more money to access the features and course progress I have already paid for in the desktop version. If you're going to go with Rosetta Stone for learning another language, it's a great program. But don't count on being able to readily use this app. I believe you need another, separate subscription for any other languages you're learning (and have likely already paid for). The subscription is annual, so you will have to resubscribe every year if you plan on taking more than a year to learn the language or just want to brush up on your skills. Unless you're willing to pony up more dough for the subscription or just go with the online access itself and be willing to let that expire at some point, save yourself the trouble and get the desktop version. It's expensive, but it's also pretty good. Either that or, depending on the language, try something that is absolutely free like Duolingo first (also very good).

This is sort of an unfair review of TED Talks the Conference Provider (5 Stars - Controversial and enlightening). This is a review of the TED App and mechanism (Fire TV) used to watch TED Talks.I downloaded the TED App onto my Fire TV box. I have been enjoying the Curiosity Stream Videos just fine. However, when I tried the TED App I would get constant interruptions to download - because of "Network Error".I ran an experiment to eliminate various variables to reception. I used my desktop computer (intel i7 -fast) also wireless on the 5 GHz band as my Fire TV Box with 128G Memory Upgrade for Buffering, both in the same room. Both also on a 5 MBPS twisted pair internet provider feed (bandwidth concern). My PC with some video fades watched the same TED Talk all the way through without loading pauses.This leads me to conclude that there needs to be work on the TED App as far as the algorithm used for compression. Older U Tube videos also had the same issues.  And Yes I do need a Fiber Backbone upgrade for Bandwidth when it is available too.

column2: Quite informative - Just remember to think for yourself when watching these TED talks.
column3: Generally an entertaining/informative source.  Given the great diversity in topics there's a good chance that almost any viewer can find something of interest to watch.  Presenters for SOME topics may subtly tend towards a more Progressive ideological opinion, and I would prefer to draw my own conclusions from unbiased presentations rather than being told what to think by a few of these experts.

TED has a lot of great content. No video (by design) is more than 20 minutes long so, you can learn something new in less than a half hour investment of your time. You’ll be surprised how 20 minutes can change the way you see the world you thought you knew.

It used to be something special, to sit down and watch some of the most fascinating lectures on many a subject. Today, it has become a forum for product placement and half-thought-out ideas, soft-science and anyone who *thinks* he/she can do as well as the great first adopters of this great idea. It is no longer selectively showing excellent lectures. It's a shame that this forum has succumbed to its initial success. Where to go from here?

While I love the content, the app which I downloaded to my Amazon FireStick today just doesn't work. I've seen other reviewers describing the same problem: When I select a talk to watch, it plays for 1 second and then an error says something like "this video has been paused due to a network error". Then I click ok, and click play, and the video starts. But the red circling hourglass indicator remains on screen as I watch and will not go away. Soon the error occurs again, and again I press play and again the hourglass stays on as I watch the program. My bandwidth is variable, but it isn't low. When I test it, I always find my test app sees 10 Mbps on the first run, 20 Mbps on the second, 24 Mbps on the run after that, and about 34 Mbps on a fourth test. So my impression is that my phone company (AT&T) always gives up to 10 Mbps a new stream, and then bumps it up if the demand continues. Also if I try streaming HD video on another devices or if I don't, it makes no difference in the TED app errors, and the video on the other devices works perfectly regardless of whether the TED app is running.  So I conclude the app isn't able to handle changes in throughput, even though all my other devices and apps (with one app exception) work fine. I suppose it's also possible that AT&T is using software to sabotage the app, but that seems extremely unlikely in my opinion. So fix this app!

column2: It's easier to curse the darkness than light a candle.
column3: Do you know someone that seems to know something about everything? You know, someone always able to provide an interesting slant on the moral issues surrounding new technologies and the old problems they're solving. The first person to know about things beyond the cutting edge, who shares with you what Bill Gates, Stephen Hawking, or President Clinton think about issues facing the world. I can tell you something about that person: They know TED.TED is my daily moment of Zen; it's salt for the world, adding flavor to everything it touches; it's conference around the world discussing local issues that have, or will have, global influence; it represents the modern view of knowledge, that only by sharing and collaborating can we achieve the impossible, know the unknowable, where we can, as Aaron Sorkin wrote, look into the face of God.Lofty words.That is the TED spirit. Brilliant, talented, funny people that are experts, or often creators, in their field. You can watch Sergey Brin demonstrate Google Glass, Sir Ken Robinson telling you about how to save your child from schools (I'm a teacher, so no complaints), listen to Stephen Dubner prove working at McDonald's pays better than dealing drugs, or Mike Rowe sharing how important, and thankless, are Dirty Jobs. Musicians, artists, doctors, lawyers, politicians, authors, scientists... The list goes on and on. The topics cover, well, everything. I can't even begin to list the subjects that come readily to mind, just listing my favorites would take a page or two.Someone once said ignorance was bliss; today ignorance is criminal. Issues are facing the world that will affect humanity; some good, some bad, but all coming. Many of these issues require citizen involvement, which requires citizens to be familiar with the issues involved, which means, I suppose, if you want to be a good citizen of the world you must watch TED.I promise this: If you watch at least three episodes, they have a YouTube channel also, and you don't find yourself looking for more that interest you, then I will work hard to get a full refund for you (they're free).So what have you got to lose except some ignorance (remember, ignorance means you just don't know; if you've had the chance to learn something and you didn't, that's stupid).

column2: TED App Seemingly Ungraceful With Variable Bandwidth
column3: I love watching TED. I used to watch it on Netflix, but I watched them all and Netflix is slow to update their list. So I began to watch it on Youtube and playback was flawless, but the user interface for YT on the Fire TV Stick is not comprehensive enough that you can't read the descriptions. Now for the TED app on Fire TV Stick: nice interface, nice playlists, horrible playback. At best, streaming stutters (freezes and plays), at worst it stops playing or locks up all together. I would have to relaunch TED app to continue watching the talks. It is aggravating not being able to watch TED talk from beginning to end without the stopping. Oh and I forgot to say that once it freezes and continues playing, the spinning circle on the middle of the screen doesn't go away. GRRRR. It is necessary to stop playback and resume (sometimes that works) but at other times I have to quit the app and relaunch. Before you say, "your problem is your poor bandwidth", I say that condition might be true but after trying to watch TED on the TED app, I can follow that by play several TED talks in a row on YT with no problem. I think the TED app doesn't handle fluctuating bandwidth gracefully and the developers were too quick to publish the app. The TED app needs improving.

column2: Directions for how to access SEARCH on TED app
column3: If you like to learn new things, the TED TV app for Fire TV and Fire TV Stick is for you!  Released on January 23rd of 2015, this app seems to run smoothly and offers an enjoyable viewing experience on my Fire TV Stick. It's a small app (8MB) taking up virtually no space on the device, and it is user friendly for the most part.I do run into issues once I'm viewing a video with trying to get back to the main interface. I try the return button on the remote and sometimes get a black screen. If I hit the Home button and go back into the app and use the rewind button, I can get back to the main TED page. Weird!Other than this issue, I find no problems using and enjoying content with the app. It is a tad tough to figure out what to do to find more than the featured talks, but if you click 'down' on your remote you will eventually get to 'Trending' after you pass through your viewed videos labelled 'My Talks'.  Below 'Trending' you'll find 'Playlists' which highlight specific types of talks on various subjects like Sex, Insects, Tech, etc.There is a SEARCH icon in the upper right side of the screen, but it's tough to figure out how to get it to open.Here's how you open SEARCH:1. Get to the main TED screen with 'Newest Releases' showing.2. Click the upper part of the wheel on your Fire TV Stick remote (probably works the same on the Fire TV or use voice search feature) to 'up' and see the magnifying glass SEARCH icon (red background with white magnifying glass) grow slightly larger.3. Press the center of the wheel on your remote to open SEARCH.4. Press a second time on the center of the wheel to bring up a keyboard to enter info, then click NEXT to SEARCH.The app is stable and the content is amazing, but the SEARCH feature was tough to see and figure out for me. I hope this helps someone else figure it out a little quicker than I did!

column2: WHAT THE INTERNET AND TV ALWAYS SHOULD HAVE BEEN.......and finally ARE!
column3: TED is one of those rare things that Television and the internet always PROMISED to be but never quite made it the full distance. TED is a rare gem that (if explored enough) really has something for just about everyone. The topics are as educational as they are entertaining and they are always expanding and enlarging their intensive array of short but very full videos. For those new to TED, it is a fairly new concept of gathering some of the world's best speakers on a wide variety of topics and giving them somewhere in the area of 15 minutes to connect to their audience by relaying information that is the best of the best. For those who are new to this I'd say GIVE TED a try. The folks here are not trying to sell you anything or beat you over the head with intrusive ideas. They gently invite you to listen and learn and widen your horizons. TED has made me laugh, think more deeply and made me more appreciative of this amazing world we live in.

column2: Expand the mind - fire up the neurons - learn something new
column3: If you're interested in listening to and watching short and punchy lectures by some of the worlds leading experts/researchers/motivational speakers into a massive array of subject matter, then this is the app for you!I've been listening to TED talks for years and have this app on all my digital devices. I listen to the podcasts and have the station on the Tune In radio app.Yep I'm a big TED fan!The podcasts and radio station are great but you really need to be seeing the visuals during these lectures. This is where this app becomes a minefield of information on the Kindle Fire.Opening the app you're presented with a simple menu to navigate.You can do a specific search for a talk you may have heard about or you can choose from what's trending or from a scrolling list of TED playlists. Click on a playlist to open up several lectures on that given subject.There's some very interesting stuff here amongst around 2000 talks and lectures on things you will have never even thought about.Some of my latest fave talks are . . .- Looks aren't everything - believe me, I'm a model.- Want to help Africa? Do business here!- Questioning the universe (filmed by Stephen Hawking in 2008)- How to succeed? Get more sleep!- Why we have too few women leaders.- What do you think when you look at me?Cannot recommend this app enough to anybody who is interested in everything!

Have been watching talks on TED for many, many years and they just get more varied and more fascinating!Imagine my delight to discover that the TED app is available on the Amazon Fire TV :DNow I can sit at home and watch truly inspirational people sharing amazing insights on topics beyond my everyday experience.Eating breakfast? Many talks are 10 mins long!Washing up? You don't have to see the TV to listen to it!Nothing on TV? Watch a whole string of talks, on a subject!Feeling unmotivated? Load up one of thousands of talks that make you want to get out and start achieving!Assignment 'block'? Learn about something totally new, to get your brain-gears whiring!In short, the most fantastic resource of human knowledge, since the Internet!

column2: No more reading recipes. Just watch the video!! I LOVE IT!!
column3: I accidentally bumped into Food Network Kitchen 2 weeks ago (Jan. 2021) and it has CHANGED MY LIFE like nothing else in the kitchen has. I was down to Wawas gas station ready-to-go sandwich meals and could retire on what I've bought in Marie Callendar's Chicken Pot Pie boxes.My problem(s)? Which there are a GREAT many in the kitchen: I don't like reading recipes. I don't like listing out the ubiquitous "weekly shopping list" of necessary ingredients nor foraging the Walmart shelves figuring out where one gets the items. (Pro tip: Do you know where molasses is kept in the stores? Me neither.)SOMETHING had to give when I realized how upset I got when my local sandwich bar at the Wawas gas station was closed due to this pest called "Covid." I mean .. REALLY!!!I've had two large cookbooks I've owned for 5 years - still in their original saran wrap.  I could get full price for what they are worth today - mint condition. And they have big pictures in them - I think they do. Not sure. Never opened them. But much like people who join a gym with the intention to workout, the concept of cooking is "Nice."Forward 53 years (which I am today) and I have 2 siblings who do cook. But alas they live too far away for me to drop in for dinner. We all began sharing our recipes during Covid - to show off what we were doing in quarantine. They showed off their couscous on a bed of lettuce with fresh squash ... I showed off my latest Wawas $2 discount shortie sandwich - courtesy of the free gas app I had just joined.They showed off their fresh steamed asparagus with honey salmon while I showed off my grilled cheese sandwich with - might I add - a touch of melted butter (This was of course after I burned the first batch of bread by leaving it on high too long under the broiler).As you can imagine this gets embarrassing - me being the oldest sibling and all. My reputation was quickly falling to not relevant. And I'm a weight lifter to boot. It didn't help that my ex was a professional chef and I never needed to cook a thing. But this had to change.I went online researching recipe apps. I figured maybe I could at least READ a recipe on line. I looked up Betty Crocker (who, btw, is NOT a real person. Look it up if you don't believe me.). And I was bored with what I saw. More recipe reading. So I skimmed over the number of people who purchased the  various food apps - as I have more apps than I can count.I saw FNK - THOUSANDS of people!! I went .. "Hey, is that THE Food Network Channel?" I mean.. the BIG kahuna?WELL YES IT WAS!!!! Then I immediately felt dejected because I ain't no cook and I know the sandwich employees at Wawas by name. But curiosity got the best of me. I LOOKED. I OPENED the FNK APP. I saw my FAVORITE personality.. REE. I own her stuff from Walmart - all of it nearly (including the pie slicer!).I saw the videos. They were short. To the point (around 3 minutes) ... they told you the order of ingredients in the video. The FNK app created my grocery list FOR ME. I could easily add and remove items from the list. I could add my own custom items onto the list - food related or not. (Ya know - Qtips). t took me 15 minutes to figure out the app - it was EASY!!!!  ! can even call ahead now and have the ingredients all ready for me to pick up at my store if I don't want to do it myself. Free curbside service!I went HOLY COW ... KERI CAN COOK!!!!!Fast forward ONE week of owning this app ... and I have cooked meals that I can actually show off to my siblings (see attached photos - all made January 2021 in 1 weeks time. That easy! I never read a single recipe. I just follow the video. This FNK app is the bomb!!!!Best money I've ever spent on an app. And my goal is to no longer know the sandwich people at Wawas by name - not unless it's just to say, "Hi."

It’s stupid. You have to pause your remote, while you have egg guts and dough and what have you on your hands. 10 or 15 bucks a month for someone to read you a recipe, when you can print it off for free on the internet. Maybe they should spend more time feeding hungry people then trying to make a profit.

column2: Good product but I expect more from the Food Network
column3: First, let me say that this is a good product, not great. It marginally improves upon the foodnetwork.com experience on a tablet. It does the basics of allowing you to search for recipes on foodnetwork.com by show as well as save those recipes into a recipe box that are linked to the website. However, the recipe box does not allow you to create folders, only store in folders you create on the website so a little less functionality than the website.A nice (but incomplete) feature allows you to create shopping lists from recipes. However the app does not combine ingredients from multiple recipes so you have a short, concise list. It should also allow you to scale recipes based on the number of servings you would like to make.Likely the biggest complaint is that it has even less video than the website (i.e., no video at all from what I found...) Given that this application is published by the Food NETWORK you would think that they would have lots of video to include.  Also, when shows have multiple recipes that are pared together, there are no links from one recipe to another meaning you have to find it on your own.The app itself runs ok. It did crash once on my Galaxy Note 10. In short, I'd wait for them to put in a serious upgrade until paying the $1.99...

column2: From Recipe to Grocery List without Over-Buying
column3: You can use the grocery list as a running list of all one has in the house-what is crossed off is what you already have or don't need.  This is saving us from over - buying.  What is not to love about an app that scans recipes on web pages for you, saves them AND adds a recipe's ingredients to your grocery list?  This is not all - the app will sync your grocery list 2 your phone so you can do meal planning in the kitchen on a tablet then as you walk into the store, have your grocery list synced on your phone and you are ready to shop!

Love this app! It is so easy to use. Helps me stay organized and easily find a recipe with tags. Being able to clip a recipe I see on the internet and add it to my collections with pictures is wonderful!

I love this app!  It's perfect to store all of my recipes in one place.  It's such a chore to go from one website, blog, online recipe file to find the recipe you want.  Sadly I came across some of my old 'saves' to find the recipe has been deleted or the blog is gone.  This app keeps those recipes in ONE place along with my collection of pins from Pinterest.com. No more worries of loosing the recipes.A great feature of this app is that you can access the recipes offline.  This helps when you are at the grocery store to pick up the ingredients you need and there is no wi-fi.The larger Pictures and Grid View are a nice improvement.  I like having pictures for my recipes and being able to add pictures is a bonus.The added tag feature makes it even easier to find specific recipes without having to scroll through the hundreds of recipes I've saved.  (I'm actually over a thousand now:))The ONLY reason I didn't give it 5 Stars is that I can't use this app on my desktop or laptop (and currently not my Blackberry.  The app is only for Android devices).  I'd like to be able to add/edit recipes from there as I've been saving them in my bookmarks lists.  I ultimately emailed the recipes links to my email account and clicked the links from my kindle. I do understand from the Chef Tap website that this along with a cloud feature are two of the things they are working on.  Good.  I'll give you the fifth star when it happens :)  It'll be nice to share one recipe file across devices.  I've been due for a phone upgrade for awhile but I'd put it off waiting for the latest to come out.  The latest features on the new phones are great but since using Chef Tap along with a few other great apps from the Amazon App store I decided to upgrade to an Android phone instead of upgrading my Blackberry (kinda a tough thing since I've had a Blackberry for 10 years at least.)To save the backup file to my desktop I had to go through Dropbox because the app said the file was too big to send via email. This isn't really difficult so I don't count it against them.  I now use Dropbox for other things like sending my personal videos, pictures and other downloads to my desktop when I need more room :)  If you don't have a Dropbox account or don't want one you can manually save by connecting your device to your computer and saving the file that way.  The Faq page on Chef Tap has details.I recently saw from their FAQ page a way to transfer files from .txt .  This is an awesome idea I haven't yet tried.  But I will because I want to add my grandmother's recipe file.  Those are actually in a REAL recipe box on REAL recipe cards.  But that will be a project for another day.The Chef Tap FAQ page and Facebook page have lots of answers to help as well as being user friendly.  A really nice change from an app creating team:) They plan on adding new features and keep you up to date in a newsletter and on their facebook page and blog.  Looking forward to having the shopping list feature.Like I said earlier it's a GREAT app!  I don't mind the ads and usually don't but will pay for the ad-free just because the app itself is worth the money.

column2: Fast and easy way to save online recipes !!
column3: I have hundreds of cookbooks however Chef Tap is  a valuable app that  allows me to save recipes as they are shown from my web searches. I enjoy exploring advanced cooking techniques and being able to save recipes with the original formatting and illustrations allows me to save them. This is easy with the free app but I like the app so much that I have upgraded to the paid version to get the additional functionality. I use my Fire in the kitchen while I am cooking and follow the instructions for the technique and use the pictures to expertly "plate "the food as shown in the original recipe. I am currently exploring "sous vide" techniques with the Joule immersion circulator and there are an increasing number of recipes online for this method.
I love this app, but when I open it, it says there is an update and the version I have is going to expire. Yet no update in the Amazon store. What up with that?

This app does a great job of importing recipes from different sites. The developers are constantly improving this ability.  I love having my recipes in one location.  I had to upgrade because there is a limit to the number of recipes on the free version (100?).My only wish is for an option to categorize the recipes (appetizers, desserts, slow cooker, etc) .  However, it can be done by adding words within the recipes and the app does a decent job searching for matches.I have had a problem with the 12 tomatoes site if trying to import from a link there out of Facebook.  To solve it, just go directly to the 12 tomatoes site.

I shop every other week.  I love this app.  I pick my recipes for two weeks.  It adds ingredients to my grocery list and then I go to staples and add those to my list and I shop..  I've had to change categories on a few ingredients but tweeting is easy.  Love the recipe downloads.  I only wish there was a daily list for which recipe you are making that day.. no problem I just write it down, just would be a nice add on.

column2: Best app I’ve ever had and makes cooking so much easier
column3: I pin A LOT of recipes, but it seems to take a while to find and link to the recipe, if the link is still valid. Chef tap is so easy to use. Love itUpdate 1/8/21: I’ve been using paying yearly for this app for years now... which I don’t do for any other app, but I love this one because it is so easy to use. It gets rid of the hassle and disruptions of trying to use a recipe online, I can easily make changes, add needed ingredients to my grocery list, make a list of meals for the week, search my recipes by name or ingredient, add recipes from the internet by clicking the share button, categorize them anyway I want. I have over 900 recipes in it. The only thing I would like to change is to be able to print recipes to add with gifts and stuff.

The app has stopped working.  When I try to update, I get a message about "parsing" issues.  When I try to share a recipe, it forces close.  I used to love this app.  :(Updated July, 2015: They fixed it! It is now one of my favorite apps. I like the fact that it doesn't "sleep" when in use. No need to touch your device with dirty hands. I use it on my Galaxy Note 4...Further update September 2015, I may actually consider the pro version if it wasn't so expensive.  Even at 25% off for the first year, it seems a little pricey.  We'll see. I may need to bite the bullet...Five years later... I did consider the pro version and I absolutely love it! Unlimited recipes and I don't have to scroll through an entire life story. Just clip the recipe and you're done. Renews automatically every year. Well worth the roughly $20 a year.

I'm not a big app buyer. In fact ChefTap is the only app I've ever purchased. You can use it for free up to 100 recipes. After that you pay $12 yearly. That's $1 a month!ChefTap allows you to save recipes similar to pinterest saving a photo. It searches the webpage with your desired recipe and extracts the ingredients and steps along with a photo for reference. You can add tags to recipes to find ideas quickly. You can also search for an ingredient or mark recipes as favorites. When I find a new recipe I want to try, to clicks and it is saved.You can save the record you plan to make soon in one area and easily reference them when you are at the grocery store to make sure you didn't forget any ingredients. I have this on my Kindle and my iPhone and it really syncs between them.If you are like me and struggled for years to find a way to organize your recipes, look no more! Start with the free version and upgrade when you're hooked.

I love the paid version of this app. The free version is sh*t, but the paid version gives me the best recipe collector I've seen. I can collect recipes from anywhere and access them on any of my devices.

I can not say enough bout this app, one being free and other reason too. I like to add from websites like ChefTap allows from[...] , but it won't and I have Betty Crocker.com and other sites I get recipes from. Other than that I really, really like this app. I don't know about all the other apps like this except one and I don't like the other one at all. Went back to this one, over and over again, makes me want cook meals again, which had got to the point I hated it with a passion. So thank you to the creators of ChefTap! The down side is I had 500 recipes in this app until my Kindle fire crashed and had to be replaced. Once I retrieved it from the cloud, it will only allow the 100, which means there are some recipes that I have to go the website and write down the instructions or find another app I can download them into.

column2: A must if you like to cook
column3: This app is amazing.  I wish I could give it more stars.  You can scan the web and import any recipe that looks good.  Once you try the recipe, if you do not like it, just delete it.  Can always add your own favorite recipes and make changes to the recipes you have imported.  Recipies can be organized however you like.  There is an annual fee for this app and it is worth every penny.  Fee is much cheaper than buying cookbooks, magazines, etc.  The developers are very responsive.  I had some problems when I changed tablets.  Shawn got back with me promptly.  If you like to cook, this app is a must!
Really love this app. Love being able to have my recipes on my Kindle and so convenient in the kitchen.  I highly recommend this app. I have been using this for a couple of years now.

I gave this app 5 stars because of how it presents recipes, the ability to catagorize recipes, and being able to add new recipes from various sources. In short, this is like your own physical recipe box but tucked away in a Kindle.The app does acknowledge that recipes are not imported correctly. I think when recipes are set up as simply as possible (like on actual recipe websites) it works the best. I imported some recipes from a friend's blog (the main focus of which is not cooking) and they didn't import 100% correctly but it was easy to fix.Really, while things like that are a bit of a drawback the app tells you up front in the tour that recipes written in certain formats (such as being wordy) don't always import well. I wouldn't want to harsh on the app too much for something like that considering how it does import many things correctly.

column2: Love but I could madly love...
column3: I love Chef Tap App.  Pure and simple best app for recipes I have found.  And I have tried at least three others but I always go back to the Tap!  I would madly love with three changes or added features. 1) I wish the app could generate a shopping list from choosen recipes.  2) I wish there were subset tags.  For instance, Vegetables but within Vegetables could add corn and beans, etc. And 3) in a perfect world I wish I could share a recipe with a friend in a recipe template.  When I share now the email is one big text.  I wish what I sent them was in "recipe card" format.  In the most perfect world it would be in a template I could customize with my name and  cutesy photo!  I brag about how wonderful the app is I think if when I shared a recipe it was in a nifty format more folks would want.  I know a lot of old ladies who do not easily change!I use Chef Tap with my Kindle and I did upgrade and am happy I did!Easily imports from most sources, especially easy with Pinterest on the Kindle.

This is my absolute favorite app. I love how easy it is to add online recipes by sharing them to chef tap. I also love how easy it is to search for recipes or ingredients. The only thing I wish it could also do is allow for uploading  or scanning recipes like Evernote does. Then it would be the perfect recipe app.

Fantastic customer service!  Unfortunately to find out if they had what I was looking for - I had to buy a year's subscription - only to find out that 1.  I had to update the software (which they updated on Aug. 29th, 2017) mind you I bought it on October 4th, 2017 and that the meal planner I was looking for had not been implemented.  Oh well.  It looks like a great app!  Just not for me at this time..

column2: Great way to save online reipes
column3: This s a great way to save online online recipes to access any time, even when offline. Its not perfect, I wish I could save personal recipes more easily. However, for most of my Ned's it works pretty well. I did pay for the upgrade so I can store more recipes and sync more frequently. I also wish I could clip re ipes on my pc or laptop without sending the file to another device which is why I gave 4 stars instead of 5.
I use it twice a week. Great for planning weekly meals as well.

column2: I use this ap a lot!
column3: I am impressed with this ap.  It is so easy to download a new recipe and then go to it in chef tap and categorize it.  The make feature really came in handy during the holidays.  It was nice to just access my list and keep on track with my baking and the meal menus.  This ap is accessible from your pc as well which makes it a little easier to add a favorite recipe of your own.  I use this ap almost daily to either browse new recipes, download new recipes, or access my already added recipes.  It is easy to scroll through the ingredient list or the instructions to keep on track with where you are at in the preparation of your dish.  Love it!

It was a joke.. It had to be.  my bad for buying it. What was I thinking...probably not thinking. I think it was meant to be a white elephant gag for a present that gets recycled from person to person.

I deleted all my other recipe apps after got this one.  It does it all!!!!  I can download recipes (complete with pics) from any website, sync my recipes across all devices and share them with friends and family.  It is great!!!

and I especially like to read recipes. I have had magazine pages and computer printed recipes piled up for years. This app is like someone put all of my recipes together in one place. Whether it's on another app or on the internet, I can move it to Chef Tap. I can even edit it if something isn't in the right order. I also like to read the reviews and edit based on what other people have or haven't tried. I only gave it 4 stars, but it should be 4 1/2. Until recently I couldn't figure out how to get recipes from the internet, only other apps. There was an upgrade not long ago and there was a video showing how to do it. Really like this app.

This is such a handy app!  I got it right before Thanksgiving (a bit over a month ago) and I just love it-- took me a little bit to figure out what was going on and how to use it, but after I did, I LOVED being able to save all my internet recipes in one place.  Also, for some reason, I am just incapable of following recipes exactly-- I'm always throwing in something extra, or leaving something out that I don't enjoy-- and you can edit the recipes to include these alterations.  Saving recipes is a snap and if I make one and decide it's a dud-- zap, it's deleted.  This is just great!  (I have a Kindle HD)

I use this app everyday. This is my 'favorites' recipe book. Whenever I . try a new recipe and it's a keeper...it goes into Chef Tap. I used to make my own 'favorites' recipe book in a binder with clear sheets to protect the paper recipes but now Chef Tap makes things simple and efficient.Now I just need to figure out how to copy and paste from my purchased kindle recipe books...not sure why this feature is not allowed but it's frustrating for adding to Chef Tap.Thank you Chef Tap! Their customer service is also top notch. I had trouble switching to their Pro when it came out and they helped get it taken care of right away!

column2: Really Enjoy—Although All “Clipped” RECIPES MUST BE CHECKED FOR ACCURACY
column3: I really like this APP.  Very addictive.  A couple of weeks after I loaded the free version, I ordered the premium package—to be honest, I think they wore me down with all their requests to order the premium package.Admittedly, there were many times within the first 2 weeks that I almost deleted this APP.  I would get very frustrated because I found it difficult to use.  It seemed that I could never find the specific instructions I needed.  I’m not very computer literate.  I would finally figure it out and see how simple the procedure was.  A couple of procedures I did not find for months, and then only by accident.  Made me crazy when I discovered how simple the procedures were; showed me how little basic computer knowledge I have.One other problem I find is that frequently Ingredients and/or Directions will be missing or mixed in under the wrong category (i.e., Ingredients mixed in with Directions, or vice versa).  RECIPES MUST BE CHECKED for missing Ingredients and Directions.Now, I love pulling up recipes to try.  And I find a new, to me, helpful APP procedure almost every day.  In fact, I have to watch myself.  For someone who is a lousy cook, I find that I am very addicted to the APP and can spend hours on the APP choosing recipes—if I allow myself.I have gone on a special gut/tummy healing diet called Specific Carbohydrate Diet.  I had never heard of this diet before (also suppose to be helpful for autistic children).  So I was surprised when this APP pulled up so many great recipes and websites.I would consider this one of the best purchases I made this last year.  Certainly one of the most enjoyable and useful.
Easy to use and very complete, with everything from importing and sorting recipes, tracking make lists and shopping lists.

Love this app. I have the premium and I have over a thousand recipes saved. It lets me categorize them so they are easy to find. I clip most of my recipes and for the most part it works wonderfully.  I also am on my third tablet and I love that it is easy to transfer your account to the new device. I definitely recommend this app.

column2: Love it, but a couple requests
column3: We have used this app for years and swear by it!  We even upgraded to the premium addition once we hit 1,000 recipes. The developers have made several great and timely updates, so I hope it isn't greedy to ask for a couple more?!?!First, a shopping list would be ideal. We plan our weekly meals in ChefTap, but then have to transfer the ingredients into another app in order to go shopping. Kind of annoying. Something simple like a check box next to each ingredient to add it to a shopping list and then the ability to sort your final list would be killer!Lastly, an Apple version of the app. I know this is an investment, but many folks have multiple devices and not being able to access the app from wherever you are limits its useability.Keep up the great work folks!!!

I've been using this app for a long time and really love it.  Having it on my phone as well as my tablet means I can use it anywhere.  Probably the best feature is that you can scale recipes up or down. Really useful!
A true virtual cookbook that works seamlessly across multiple devices with various operating systems & browsers! Full functionality for cooking and shopping. We use it daily and love It!

I love Chef Tap! It is so easy to import recipes from the web, including a picture, and once imported, it is easy to make changes to title, ingredients, and steps, so I can record my personal changes at will. I also really like how it keeps my Kindle from going to sleep while using the program when cooking. The step-by-step feature that keeps the list of ingredients visible is an added bonus. I used to use Big Oven on my laptop, but Chef Tap is so much more user friendly! As a cook who likes trying new recipes but wants to be able to track and recreate them, this is more than perfect. It is also very easy to type in those few old family favorites that don't exist online.

After studying several recipe apps, I settled on this one. It's been all I hoped for-- easy to use,  easy to navigate. It's super easy to import recipes from any site I've tried. The recipes come  through needing few adjustments, if any. If adjustments are necessary, they're very simple to make.  I do wish you got to store more than 25 free recipes, but to be fair, I haven't reached the limit yet. I've also been being conservative with the recipes I'm importing. But when I reach the limit, I like this app enough I'll probably pay for the subscription.

Central is a terrific app for managing recipes you enter by hand or find online.  Search features help you locate by keyword or ingredients.  Sometimes there are minor operational glitches, so not quite five star but developers quickly address any problems that users report.

column2: I use this all the time.
column3: I have used this for years and love it. Simple to use and very handy.  They also have frequent updates to address problematic web sites.

I started using this app but noticed my recipe photos were not syncing between devices.  I contacted the provider about the sync issue and the next update corrected the problem.  You have to find some of the free version limitations i.e. 100 recipes, weekly sync, no web import of recipe on PC but otherwise it works very well.  I have imported recipes from web sites without problems and have entered my own as well.  If there was a one time charge for premium (currently annual fee) I might pop for it.

I've been using Chef Tap for about a year now to get and store recipes. I love that it now stores to the cloud! This is the best and easiest recipe ever and I decided to finally upgrade about a month ago and pay the annual membership for the pro version to get unlimited syncing to the cloud and unlimited recipes. Best thing I ever did for about $16/year...it's definitely worth it. That's cheaper than my Netflix account per year! I definitely recommend getting this if you want a place to store your recipes.  Works great on my Kindle Fire HD!

column2: THE best recipe clipper by far!!!
column3: This is by far THE best recipe app out there. I have tried and uninstalled many apps to capture recipes from online. Not one of them, until this one has done so with a usable result. The closest I have seen is Pocket, which I still like very much for other articles, but not for recipes. With that one I would usually end up using the web view which takes away the recipe card aspect of the app.Mindframe Design has done a wonderful job with ChefTap. I can clip my grain free and raw recipes from the web, pick the picture I want to use, edit or change an ingredient or instruction effortlessly, change the recipe title and more. If anything is missing, it is easy to retrieve missing text and fix it, but this has only happened twice out of 78 recipes that I now have in the app.I love the ability to tag and then search, or choose a tag to see the recipes with that tag and also mark recipes as favorites.I also like the way you can mark the ones you want to make and just pull those recipes up.I use this app on my Fire Phone and on my Samsung Galaxy Tablet.I have not noticed anything that I don't like about this app yet.

column2: The best recipe storage app out there!
column3: I decided to try this app and was so impressed that I bought an annual subscription before I reached the storage limit.  I store apps clipped from the internet, from digital magazines, digital cook books and even enter my own original recipes.  I'm amazed at how accurate the imported recipes are.  The developers have done a really fantastic job with this app.
I love this app! You can download it inGoogle play and iTunes as well!To be able to have over 100 recipes,There is a subscription. But if you don’tneed over 100, it’s free!
Does what it says it will do. What's not to like?

....first of all it is amazimg how effortlessly (for the most part) receipes import into the program...and editing is a breeze....i love how i can change the picture and delete what i dont need in a receipe...folders are awesome, being able to create own and putting a receipe in multiple folders...the program dropbox has been a blessing for backing up my receipes...i have had to reformat my tablet on several occassions and cheftap is always there ready to import them again...i never have to print a receipe again and if i do not like it...i simply delete...no paper waste...thanks cheftap
I have this app on my Kindle. My only issue is that I can't update.

I love Chef Tap. It makes storing all my recipes in one place super easy.The import option from various websites is AMAZING and a wonderful time saver. The only reason I didn't give this app 5 stars is because of their lack of a cloud storage option. I have Chef Tap on my cell phone also but do not have access to all the recipes I have stored on my kindle. And when I upgraded to a Kindle Fire HD I had to go through quite a few easy, but annoying, steps to restore the recipes I had saved on my original Kindle. Altogether, though, it's a fantastic app and one I would've gladly paid for!

I have had Chef Tap for about 2 months now and like it better every day.  The upgrade was slightly hard to find for my Kindle Fire (have to look in the app store side bar for "updates") but the update was free and the app is even better now.  The new menus make categorization and navigation so much easier.  I have imported many recipes from the internet (The Pioneer Woman is a favorite) and it sure beats printing and keeping up with the recipe.  You can organize each recipe by as many tags as you want and create your own categories.  This is a plus for me because I can quickly find what I'm looking for.  I would say this is the most useful app on my Kindle Fire HD!

I am loving this app on my Kindle Fire so far! I bought my Kindle on Prime Day for $30 to exclusively use for recipes in the kitchen. I downloaded this app and splurged on the Pro membership ($20/year). Although I'm not crazy about the membership price, I am really liking the versatility of this app. So easy to input recipes -- and I loved that I could manually type in my personal recipes on the website and sync them to the app on my Kindle. I'm excited about using this in the future -- I especially love the "look" of the recipes when you pull them up (ingredients at the top, steps at the bottom). No more scrolling through Pinterest (HATE THAT!) or looking through blogs to find the real recipe.

column2: I used to love this app, too...
column3: Now that I have so many recipes in this app, suddenly I am being forced to either sign up for an account or stop importing recipes, period .... which is all his app does. Also, there have been insane amounts of updates in the past month. I will go back to e-mailing myself recipes or printing them out before I am forced to sign up for anything. The original app was great. But this is bad, moving into worse.

I LOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOVE this  app!  I don't have a Kindle, just a cheap run of the mill android tablet and this app works well on it.  It is simple to use (most of the time, some websites have weird configurations),  but most of the time it's great.  The only thing lacking imo is the ability to categorize the recipes,  such as  creating folders for breads,  desserts,  beverages etc.  Worth paying for with that option added. Maybe sometime soon?  Anyway,  great job guys.  My now favorite go to cookbook  app.
Uninstalled...(the last update took away features that you have to go pro now to use...😠).  I found another app that works much better...
I have had the Pro version for several years. Definitely worth the money! This app has never let me down.

I had to update my glowing review of this app because of the updates and changes they have made.  It is no longer user-friendly.  The ads, which were noticeable before, but small, are now annoying and often blocking area I want to read or edit. I absolutely love this app.  I have never had an app device before so I am new to this.  Because of frequent updates I lost my recipes numerous times.  They now have a subscription fee where you pay for a monthly or yearly subscription that expires, it is not cheap.  I would prefer to buy the app outright, that is not an option.I have since deleted this app from my device and found a different one.  I was SO, SO sad to let this one go.  It was my most used and favorite app on my Fire.Former review:  I cook differently than a lot of people focusing on healthy, fresh foods without the use of canned goods or processed foods.  These types of recipes are difficult to find in standard cookbooks and cooking sites.  But with Chef Tap I can read my favorite healthy cooking blog and instantly transport the recipe into Chef Tap, it is easy, painless and fast.  Editing is easy as there is an option to view the whole blog post and import any text that didn't make it into the recipe.You create your own tags and then you can add those tags to any recipe.  So I have my breakfast tag, beverage, salad, etc.  The recipes are searchable by its tag, but also by a title word.You can also add your own personal notes to any recipe which is a great way to make note of changes you made or even when it was prepared.I do have some wishes for the program:  I wish it did weekly menu planning including breakfasts.  I would also appreciate a generated shopping list.  And more than any other function I wish it could sync with a computer version and even a phone version.  I would LOVE this program on my browser.  Then I could STORE the recipes on my computer, but then access them from the Fire when I am in the kitchen.One of my biggest complaints is that the back-ups take a long time once you have several recipes in the program.  Additionally, the back-up runs automatically when you open the program so you can not access your recipes until it is finished backing up.  I would rather the back-up function operated in the background or even when the program isn't being used.  You can amend how you want the back-ups done and how frequently, which is helpful.My other complaint is that when you are making edits in your recipe you can't stay in an edit mode and have to click your options and start over for each step you edit.Overall it is the best recipe import program I have used including my experience with computer versions.

column2: The couple that developed this app are super. Wish I could meet them in person
column3: Use this app to put recipes on my tablet. Can't imagine not having it.  The couple that developed this app are super.  Wish I could meet them in person. Great support if you need it.

Love the program. Got it when you could store 100 recipes for free. What I don't like and won't do is pay a monthly fee to use it. Recipes can be saved to note pad and added to my Accuchef program I purchased for 20.00 years ago.

column2: This app is perfect for storing my recipes
column3: This app is perfect for storing my recipes. It syncs to an external website if you create an account so you don't lose any recipes in a phone crash. You can easily import recipes from a website link which is super convenient. I only wish you could store pictures of recipes for ease of uploading existing recipes. Overall, it's the best app I've found for storing my recipes!!

column2: Perfect to create my own cookbook
column3: I have been using this app since August 2012.  The creators of this app are so responsive to feedback.  If you have any tech troubles with any imported recipe, you can send them that link and they will look at it to see if they can solve it.I really love that I can import any recipe on the web and have it stored on my Kindle Fire.  If I am at the store, I can open Chef Tap and all my instructions/ingredients are there.This is very user friendly and worth a 5 star rating.  I'd give it 10 if I could.

I like this app. it's the only one I have found that allows me to import , tweek as I need, as well as manually put in my family favorites. Was a bit disappointed that I had to upgrade to pro after I had reached a certain number of imports, I would say let each customer back up themselves so the company doesn't have to incur the cost of cloud. But overall it's a great app to have if you like to collect recipes and cook. Beats pieces of paper laying around in a drawer unorganized.

After installing this app,find a recipe, open the Kindle "options" select "save to" and "cheftap".  It downloads the recipe to your Kindle then in a second or two, automatically imports to ChefTap (can take a minute). A successful import shows the dish name, a photo of the dish ( if available on the site), the ingredients, the preparation directions.  You can then edit it,add it to category(s), or find a photo if the webpage didn't have one, and add it.With the huge variety of web pages & their technical differences it is obviously going to be difficult to collect the right info, yet this app does most of the time. In the 6 months I've used it they have made many improvements in the importing accuracy and they track which websites don't import right then fix the process for that site. This app does something so complicated that I don't consider problems with a few websites (cookscountry.com is one of them) significant enough to take off a star, especially since they are so good about fixing problem sites. The down side is a Kindle problem not a Cheftap problem and that is that its a pain to enter my own or cookbook recipes since the Kindle doesn't support a keyboard (one finger typing a recipe is time consuming).I love this app and have recommended it to all my friends. I like having recipes in one place, on the Kindle, that i can use in the kitchen instead of paper or books. It makes the cost of the Kindle worth it to me.  I don't know of another app that goes to the website and imports both ingredients and directions with a couple of taps.  That alone makes it worth a lot, just in the time it saves me, as well as not having to print or get pen/paper, or track where I put the paper copy.The programmer is working on setting up cloud backup (a worry with the kindle) and each time you open the app it creates a backup and prompts you to send it to yourself until cloud saving is working. I do wish they had an option to use it on iThings as well as Android, but I will keep my Kindle for this alone if they never have an Apple version.I'm like the other reviewer who commented they couldn't believe this app hasn't gotten more attention. It is one of the most useful apps ive found and it is free.
Wish I had known about this year's ago, so nice not to have pages and pages of printed recipes.

I have been using this app for over two years. It certainly has continued to improve and evolve over time. Yes, to use the app for free, you can only have up to 100 recipes. I have found the annual renewal fee to be a minor issue. I am willing to spend a nominal annual fee to have the convenience of having my favorite family recipes, stored in the cloud and available on my tablet or smartphone at the touch of a button. I love being able to import recipes from different websites. No more newspaper clippings or recipe cards to lose. Also sharing a recipe with friends is a snap. Good investment for those who like to cook.

I absolutely love this app. It has a seamless interface that works well with my Kindle Fire. So quick and easy I couldn't believe it at first. I would go and peek at my recipe files. I recommend this app to anyone trolling the internet for new recipe ideas just click the share button on your tablet and select the Chef Tap app.I should also mention the formatting, Chef Tap re-tools and creates a clean, easy to read format for any recipe I've gotten from the Internet. Try it, I think you'll love it.
Easy to use, a great storage mechanism for recipes. Fabulous app.

column2: BUG still exists in this version!
column3: They said they fixed the bug in the version I downloaded, but IT WAS NOT FIXED.  I still have not received my confirmation email from cheftap.com which I need to use the app; so the app is useless to me.  I've even requested 3x for a new email confirmation -- nothing yet.  I'm deleting this app from my Kindle.  I found another cooking app which worked much smoother and no need for registering anywhere.
Can't get it to work.

I love love love this app! Previous to finding ChefTap, I had hundreds of internet bookmarks for recipes I wanted to try. ChefTap gathered them all up and they are in one convenient virtual cookbook of recipes that I know i love. If I make changes, no problem..changed right there. If I decide I don't like one after I try it...delete! It's very user friendly and super convenient. I have the free registered account. May be bumping up to pro! If you like to treasure hunt recipes, this app is a must!
I use this app almost every day. I love cooking and I love recipes. I can clip any recipe on a whim, even if I might not make it. When I do make it, I can scale it to my needs, modify, make it MINE!
My go-to app. Love the scaling feature.

I've had Chef Tap on my kindle fires for over 2 years. The newest version has made an already easy to use app easier, faster and more comprehensive. I've been a chef tap pro subscriber for a year. Well worth the $7.99 annual fee.

I love the ease of getting the recipe directly off a web page.  Also, it's great that you have access online on your computer. I would recommend this app to those that love collecting recipes and cookbooks. When I purchased a new tablet, one of my deciding factors was checking to see if Chef Tap was available for download on the new device. Ha ha but there you have it. Try it you won't be disappointed.

I use this app more than any other. I love the fact that I can pull a recipe off the web and everything is in one place. The "make" button is also handy way to organize a rudimentary weekly menu. If it had a shopping list I'd be thrilled (hint).I use this in my kindle and phone... I wish I could have all recipes on both devices, but that is not currently available. The only issue is remembering which recipe is on which device, and if it's on the kindle, I can't pull up the recipe at the store so I have to write down my ingredients beforehand. Otherwise I highly recommend this app!

I don't have internet at home, but was able to download all my Pinterest recipes onto my Kindle Fire HD from work. I used to have to remember to print a page or two to take home with me, so this is great!! I love that these are all hand-picked-by-me recipes that I wanted and not a book filled with only a few I might actually want to try. It's easy to sort and type in any that you already have at home. Home run of an app, I absolutely love it!

column2: just what I've been looking for
column3: I have been wishing there was a way to build a data base of recipes as a result of searching the internet. This program not only will help build a list of recipes, but it also helps build menus and gives the home cook a way to record successes and flops. Another reason I love this program is that I have only a little room for cookbooks and the good ones tend to run more expensive than I can afford right now. This allows me to build my own "cookbook". I like that.

column2: Great as a Free App - Even Better w/ Upgrade
column3: Great as a Free App - Even Better w/ Upgrade

This is such a great app for cooking. I'm not sure what my Kindle settings are at the moment, but when I use this app, the Kindle doesn't go to sleep. This is great for when my hands are messy, and I don't want to "wake up" my Kindle. I love the way this separates the ingredient listing from the cooking steps. I have recommended this to several friends. Also - you can change ingredients to your liking.

column2: Not what I was looking for
column3: This is not what I was looking for so take my rating with a grain of salt, pun intended.  I was looking for an app that would give me a list of recipes.  This will download recipes you find on the internet and keep them all in one place.  This is great for people who love to cook and go surfing websites looking for yummy recipes.  I cook because a like to eat, not because I like to cook.  I want the recipes to come to me.
I rely on ChefTap daily. It's easy to use, easy to clip recipes, and easy to edit for my own personal experience. I've been using ChefTap for four years now. Love it!

column2: great app for every day UAE
column3: I give the developers give stars because ( in my own experience) they were very responsive to my issues and fixed them right away (and that was around Christmas when I expected to wait due to the holidays).I do love the app, would give it five stars if I could make my grocery list from the recipes I want to make, and then add additional shopping items. I think the developers are working on something like that....It is just awesome to have my recipes in the kitchen off the counter, I don't have to turn pages, get books messy (I am not a neat cook!) and my four year old doesn't accidentally close to cookbook!It is easy to import and add manually.

column2: I have this on my phone and Kindle... very useful.
column3: I have this on my phone and my Kindle.I have my recipes with me to share with friends and family if needed, but can use one of my Kindles as a cookbook when in the kitchen.You can enter your own recipes, import them from websites, and so much more.

I love cooking and love trying new recipes. I have notebooks full of clipped recipes fully organized. Since going totally digital I have been searching for a great way to organize the many new recipes I try. Through trial and error with countless promising apps I had settled on evernote as my best option, but it had some issues with certain sites that required extra steps to make it available in the application.Well all that is over with Chef Tap. It is so easy to save recipes in a very readable and usable standard that is search able I may never go back. It is not perfect. A synching feature is sorely lacking as I use multiple devices. I would also like to see a desktop plug in for when I'm on my laptop.Still, all things considered it is the best app out there for organizing recipes. Now my only problem is keeping up with cooking all my new found dishes. What a terrible problem to have...

column2: Finally found a useful recipe app !!!
column3: Ever since I got my tablet I've been looking for a useful recipe app that I could download recipes from any site.  Chef Tap does everything I want it to do !!!  Plus, once I have the recipe downloaded I can edit it, add more pictures, and tag it.  I like how I can have the ingredients on one half of the screen and the directions on the other half.  If you need help with any of the functions it's easy enough to google Chef Tap help to get instructions and/or videos.  I was able to load and edit a recipe in under 3 mins.  There are other ways to download the recipe other than 'share' but this was the option I found easiest for me.
Not impressed, doesn't show up in  half the apps or pages as a choice like it should.
does not work on my tablet
Neat way to store recipes

Very easy to use, and lets the user store up to a hundred recipes for free. I might buy up into the premium, that's how much I like it, but I'm cheap. My only wish is that it could store videos of recipes. I've been using ChefTap for a few years now.

Love love this app! It isn't one with a gazillion recipes I'll never use but rather holds all my personal ones in one place. Exactly what I was looking for & free to boot! The import from new ones I see elsewhere & want to try is very easy. HINT: Make one of your tag catagories 'to try ' for a quick way to look up all those accumulated 'oh this sounds good ' ones when you're in the mood for something different!

This is a great app. Just go online with your Kindle, find a recipe you like, tap share, hit Chef Tap from the options and the recipe is sent to your Kindle and saved in the app. I use it all the time. Keep only the recipes you want. Save them from your favorite websites and authors. You can create your own organizational system for the recipes. Bottom line,just get it. Well , a low cal pumpkin pie awaits.
Kept the kids busy for a little while.  Nice app

I love this little app. I am hard pressed to choose my favorite feature...the ability for it to snag a recipe effortlessly from a webpage or blog or the ability to view the instructions either step-by-step or all at once. Best of all, it's free! The only enhancement I would love to see is the ability to select several recipes and then generate a shopping list like the Epicurious app. Thanks to the developer of this nifty little app.

column2: Exactly what I've been looking for!
column3: I have been using pinterest to find new recipes but found it cumbersome having to go to the individual websites for each recipe.  It was on my to-do list to download them all into some sort of cook book on my computer.  I downloaded this app without really knowing what it was.  I wasn't expecting much because it was free.  When I finally got around to looking at it, I was so excited.  It was exactly what I have been looking for.  The only improvement I would like to see is a shopping list function, but according to the website it is in the works.

I have used ChefTap since the first Kindle Fires came out. I have tried a few recipe apps, and this is my favorite, and now the only one I use for recipe storage and for cooking.The app is very versatile. You can add recipes by importing directly from a web page, or a file, or by typing it in yourself. You can keep photos of every recipe, even your own results photo. You can cook from the recipe proper, or from step by step view. You can edit, add comments, import additional links, star favorites, sort into multiple customizable categories, and add to a "make" list.Recent improvements include the ability to search for recipes directly from the app, sync your recipes to the cloud and across devices, and get rid of flash ads for a small upgrade fee. You can easily upload your back-up file to your personal file sharing service. I keep a back-up in Box, which has made the transition to replacement Kindles very easy.I have been cooking for 60 years, have a bookshelf of cookbooks, yet ChefTap has refreshed my passion for cooking by making it easy to source and try new recipes, and adapt and cook them. Bravo!
So easy to look up a recipe and to add new ones from the web and from my own collection. Rarely use an actual cookbook any more..Highly recommended.

Love this app.  It makes meal planning so easy.  We sit down on Sunday morning, scroll through our recipe tiles, pick five, and it creates a shopping list for us.  It's easy to add new recipes, and easy to favorite real winners so you don't forget to make them again.

I think this app has a lot of functionality on a Kindle fire! I am not overly tech savvy but, I can recognize capability. ChefTap does what it states it will do and, it does it pretty well.  I have successfully imported from numerous websites; I have also imported many non-food "recipes."  I really like the versatility and having the ease of several forms of entry/import.

column2: Down grading for changes to a paid subscription
column3: You can see my original review below this update.: what was once 4-5 star app has become a 2 star due to the change over to VERY expensive paid subscription if you want to have more than 100 recipes stored. Eleven to twelve dollars a year is ridiculous, I understand they need to make some money to be able to continue to improve and support this app but the cost is prohibitive to what this app does and I refuse to pay them their current fee just to store and import recipes from the internet. And I do not buy their excuse that there is no way they can afford to keep this app running without such a high cost. They do not need servers to store all our recipes, those get stored on our devices and do not cost them a dime. Yes they want to be able to fix bugs and make improvements but please do not insult my intelligence by saying they cannot afford to do it without having everyone shell out for their price. I have far more sophisticated apps on my devices that were free. Yes many of them are supported by larger companies but this program does not require as much tinkering at say a spreadsheet or WORD document writing apps. I might consider an annual fee that actually was fair(at least a 50% cut on their current fee would be smart.) but until that time I won't be upgrading and will just go back to how I used to do it with Pintrest.To sum up; in my opinion while this is a very nice app but it is not worth the price tag they set to upgrade to the "pro" version.Original 4 star review:I love this app it works very smoothly 80% of the time...I downloaded all my saved Pintrest recipes with very little corrections needed and adding new stuff is a snap. Where it loses a star is downloading from personal blogs like Blogger etc..I had to pretty much retype most of each recipe myself. Now some of this is probably due to the nature of my blog which has a lot of non recipe storytelling stuff mixed into my entries. But what bothered me was the random stuff this app did not load at all.
