I would rather it loaded my entire blog letting me delete what I did not want than for it to pick and choose what it wanted to collect.

This app is the perfect way to organize the recipes I frequently find online, wish to try and then forget where I found them.  Now when I find a recipe, I simply share the page to Chef Tap and I have only one place to look on my Kindle Fire, instead of digging through e-mails I've sent to myself or pages I've bookmarked.  If only I could put magazine couplings into it!!

I really like using this app because I can find recipes on the internet and put them into the app without any retyping.  The only problem I have run across is that the recipes sometimes just don't appear when it has finished downloading.  I simply try again and it usually works the second time.  I'm sure there are a lot of little things that could make it better but overall it is a very handy app which works pretty well.
I really enjoy using this app for cooking. I am able to easily import recipes that I find online and add them to my collection. The grocery list is great and works really well for me.
Love this.  Easy to use. Have been using this several years. Able to create categories (tags) which makes it very simple to find each recipe.

column2: Love It Enough to Pay for It
column3: The title says it all.  I don't pay for apps.  Seriously, I've paid for the grand total of three apps in my five years of smart phone and table use.  This is worth every single penny.  And if you don't want to pay, try out the free version first.  I'm willing to bet that after you've used it for awhile, you'll go ahead and buy that app.  It's that good.
My wife sends me recepies all the time. I use this to sort them and scan for an answer to "What do you want for dinner this week?"
It's awesome to pull my favorite recipes from online all into 1 place. The shopping list feature is convenient, too.

I think it's amazing how this thing works. It's easy and convenient to add, delete, or edit records. I also love that the link stats attached as well so you can reference the website of there are any issues with the download.My only complaint about the app is that it doesn't have a shopping list option so it can gather the ingredients to certain recipes you want to make. If the option is there, I haven't seen it yet. If it isn't there, it would be a really great feature to add! That way I won't have to use a different list for shopping. If I see the option for it, it'll be 5 stars.

I really like the way you can add recipes to this app from the Internet without leaving the app. It does freeze up at times which is why I'm giving it 4 stars instead of 5. I would also like it if I could add recipes from the Internet when not in the actual app and on my P.C. rather than my Fire. This might be available with the paid account. I haven't check that out yet.

I truly love this app. All my pinterest recipes plus additional ones, are stored on here. Since I carry my kindle in my purse I always have my recipes,  so if I stop at the store on my way home from work I just pull up recipe and shop. I can try new recipes and if we don't like them I just delete, no wasted paper, and ones we really like I copy and export to my computer.

I love that I can store recipes I've found online in a way that is easier to follow than is presented on the websites. It is much more practical for use in the kitchen than just using a tablet on the webpage.But its also wonderful for storing recipes that I've gotten through friends and family. Those are not on webpages but still important to me. I dont want to loose them...and once again they are stored in a way I can use them in the kitchenone thing I'd love to see would be a temp converter. That wound be really useful.

I was APPrehensive about this app but it sounded like what I had been looking for and it hasn't disappointed me. I am always looking up new recipes and then having to copy and paste to a new email and so far this app has made it so very simple for me.

I use Chef Tap on my second generation Kindle and Kindle HD also my android phone. Both my husband and I do the cooking in our house. We both love the ease of use and convenience of having our favorite recipes at our fingertips. I highly recommend upgrading to get the unlimited sync so you can sync across multiple devices. The formatting of recipes is great. Being a diabetic, I use the notes section to add nutritional info. And being able to create my own tags is invaluable. We have never had problems on any of our devices. And I use it so much, I don't know what I would do without it!

column2: This is the Recipe App you want!
column3: This is really good. Actually works, no glitches. It's free up to 100 recipes, even the pro version is reasonably priced. Copying 're pies from the internet is a breeze, and you can edit.No kidding, if you're looking for an app to save your 're 'recipes and easily collect more, this is it.

I love recipes and subscribe to multiple sites that send weekly recipes via email.  I also pin recipes in pinterest.  Having so many places to store recipes makes it difficult to retrieve them.  I found this app which allows me to consolidate all my recipes in one place.  It is very user-friendly and I don't have any trouble finding recipes now.
Can't recommend this app enough!  All 2895 recipes saved and organized. Shopping list for ingredients on my phone too. Totally awesome

It's so nice to have all my recipes in one place! It syncs with my phone, laptop, and kindle so I've got backups everywhere, and its awesome to be at the grocery store, craving something in particular, and be able to open up the recipe on my phone...voila, ingredients list!

Really liked this app. I liked having all my recipes right there with me. Then I found  I had to pay to get unlimited space. The pro version is 11.99 a year!! Say what?? Twelve dollars a YEAR for me to save MY recipes. Seriously??From now on I will just be taking screen shots of my recipes and saving them that way. Also I will be deleting this app.

column2: This is my go to recipe app
column3: I really like the import function and the ability to modify those recipes. I have been able to import cleanly from most sites like foodnetwork, epicurious, allrecipes, etc.  It does not import well from splendid table, so those have to be manually input.I also like the display in landscape mode where you're shown the ingredients on the left and the preparation steps on the right.Also, being able to back up your recipes is a nice feature.In the future, I'd love to see the ability to create a shopping list.This is a good solid app and has the potential to be great.

This is the most important app on my tablet. I have been using this app, since I purchased my first Kindle  Fire a couple of years ago. I am now using a new Kindle Fire and I upgraded this application. I love cooking, baking, and shopping using this app. I have close to 800 recipes and I add recipes daily.
Love it, use it often, great to have  my recipes accessible on all my devices.

I absolutely love this... so easy to import recipes and then revise to fit my cooking style and ingredients... so easy to put in recipes from scratch, too, and easily add pictures!  The app looks great, and I love that I can also input recipes from my PC with a full-sized keyboard too.  Simple and extremely useful -- my most-used app!

column2: Having a difficult time trying to figure this app out
column3: I just downloaded this app into my Kindle Fire HD.  I was so excited.  I went to Foodnetwork and imported a bunch of recipes that I use all the time.  My problem comes with trying to figure out how to use this app. It seems I can never find "home" when I need it and made categories, but can't seem to figure out how to get my recipes into those categories.  Right now I am frustrated, but hopefully with some time, I will figure it all out.  I have also, during importing recipes, gotten the "black screen of death" twice and also when viewing my recipes in the app, got the "black screen" twice.  I realize this program has a way to go to improve and I hope I can hang in long enough to see that day.  Right now, I love the "idea" of this app but don't "like" it.  LOL1/7/13 - Well, I played around alot with this app yesterday and am feeling more comfortable with it.  I still feel like it is clunky and not overly user-friendly, but am liking it more and more.  I really love the idea of not printing out so many recipes from Foodnetwork, and other places.  Now, I am giving it a "4 star" rating.

I can't tell you how much I love this app.  It's so much faster and easier to find my saved recipes with Cheftap on my Kindle fire than to go to Pinterest, find the right board, then find the recipe, and after that it still takes a few clicks before I have the recipe I am looking for.  Cheftap is fast and there is no Internet connection needed to use recipes that you have already saved.  I use this daily!

I'd been searching for an app to put all my recipes on and get away from paper recipes all over my house.  Once I understood how this works, I love it.  Especially since I get most receipes from other web sites.  You just click on the recipe, share it to a page and pick Chef Tap and it's there.  And their support system is great too.

column2: You need this app if you like to cook
column3: I love this app and the fast interaction to view and save recipes. The reviews and suggestions from other users is awesome and raises the usefulness to a high level above other apps. It is useful to surf for dinner ideas when you need a nudge to be creative.

This is a useful app that allows me to visit different cooking websites searching for recipes I want to try and then I can click on the recipe and Chef Tap copies it to a folder where I can browse without going back to the original website where it was listed.I can create tags (categories) for the recipes and even add my own notes.

I use Chef Tap for all my recipes. What I like most is that I can edit a recipe and change it the way I want. Wany times I edit a recipe and translate it into a different language, so my relatives can try them out too.

column2: I love it. I love how it syncs across devices ...
column3: I have been using this app for over a year now.  I love it.  I love how it syncs across devices and that I can access it from the web.

I love being able to do easily collect recipes from web sites. Everything works fine for me. I see some people have had problems with the app after a while, but things are fine so far. It is nice to have such easy access to recipes on my Kindle in the kitchen.

I use this app almost everyday!! My husband downloaded it for me so I would have a place to keep all the recipes I want off the internet. It works great and you can save any type of instructions, not just recipes!! I have not only saved recipes but jewelry making instructions, also. You can also put your own recipes in it. This app has many more options that make it very useful!!
I upgraded but even loved the free part. So easy to use and don't understand the reviewer who complained about "permissions".

Got this yesterday and have already loaded my favorite recipes from my computer. Just convert them to text files and import them. I also used Backup/restore to move all the recipes from my  android tablet to my Fire. And, of course, you can get recipes from the Web. Greatest app ever!

column2: Love having recipes available all the time
column3: It's great to have access to my recipes on Kindle Fire even when it's not on line.  Updated app is excellent.  It captures recipes more than 90% of the time, even some that appear in strange disorganized formats on the web.  It's pretty easy to edit and organize recipes and bring them together in one very convenient list.

column2: Didn't know I needed it. Use it all the time.
column3: This app is perfect for a cook like me whose always on the lookout for new recipes. You really do just tap and save the recipe. I downloaded it to my Kindle Fire and it works perfectly with most sites. I also reset my auto shut off time to 30 minutes so that I have plenty of time to do my prep work and start cooking with no annoying turn offs.TRY IT!

I come across recipes online all the time and would think, "hey that looks good". Then email it to myself and completely forget about it. With tapchef I just copy the url and load it in and it saves it in a nice format and includes the original link. I've been using it a lot for new meal ideas.

I LOVE chef tap! I don't cook without it...it is my favorite kitchen gadget! All my recipes on one easily portable place...easy to access, make changes, create your own recipes, etc. Oh, and my family lives how easily I can share my recipes. Thanks for this amazing app!!

column2: My go to recipe management app
column3: I have been using this app for at least three years and it is one of my "go to" apps. I have upgraded Kindle Fire tablets three times and with the ChefTap cloud, the migration has been seamless. I clip recipes at least 3 times a week, use it while cooking at least 5 times a week, updated recipes with my notes, and have added a few "family" recipes from scratch.  There may be other acceptable recipe management apps, but I'm so happy with this one, no need to try anything else.
Ok

Chef Tap is amazing!  If you browse recipes on the internet, you must have Chef Tap.  I enjoy the app Zite and often want to keep recipes from there and it is as simple as pressing "share" option and choosing Chef Tap.  The recipe is entered into ChefTap complete with photo. I have chosen to have the upgraded version that has an annual fee. It is better than a cooking magazine subscription, because every recipe is one that I have chosen. Money well spent!  Every time I bring another recipe into Chef Tap, I say, "I love this app!"

I don't usually write reviews but I need to share my honest opinion of Chef Tap which I have been using for 2 years.  It is wonderful!!!  So easy to use and simple!  I am now importing from my Pinterest boards!  Wow.  Love simply selecting "share" with Chef Tap of bookmarking the recipe page and the app will scan and import all the recipes I have saved in recipe boxes.  I use several cooking sites including Food Network, Epicurious, Saveur, Wms Sonoma,Big Oven, Martha Stewart, All Recipes, Pinterest, Bon Apetit, etc....  I import my saved recipes from all these sites and Chef Tap keeps them organized and easy to find in one place, a single app.I can't recommend this enough to anyone who truly enjoys cooking and learning new techniques or simply enjoys collecting recipes.  I have even saved cocktail recipes!  This imports photos as well!!!  And you can edit your recipes and add your own notes.  Excellent!I haven't upgraded to the Pro version yet as I am awaiting the invitation or word that a seamless transfer of my recipes will take place with a Pro account.  I hope this is the case because now that I can import my Pinterest board recipes, I will need more capacity!Great application!
IMO, this is the absolute best app for people who like to keep easy access to their recipes. It keeps the pictures, it keeps the ENTIRE recipes without having to have internet access.  I just love I.

While I like this app, and love that I am suppose to be able to import but it freezes or is slow quite often, with that being said, once it does import and I can use, it is a great program.04/06/13 Update:  Had to up my review of this program. since the initial update the program has been great.  I use it all the time when looking for a new recipe to try.

I have amassed quite a collection of recipes on my kindle fire.  The problem was I had them on several different apps, and a ton of bookmarks and saved blogs.  ChefTap enabled me to have all my recipes in one place.  they have thought of everything I might need, and for what they haven't thought of yet, they regularly update.  Awesome job!

Rewrite to my last review I had gave it 5 stars but now it's 2. Before I installed this newer version I could hold as many recipes as I liked ,now I am limited to only 100 recipes. If  we want more space we have to upgrade to pro, which I think is ridicules. I had 200+ recipes saved before this new addition and now I have to pay to store them. I will be looking for a new program and I will warn all of my family and friends who I recommended this app to about the changes.----------------------Love it' great way to store recipes I find online and ones I create myself.I'm clumsy, my paper cookbooks and written recipes would always get destroyed either by ripping or being stained. With this app I have them at hand at all times and if my device malfunctions I have backups to restore my recipes.

I first got this app on my kindle in 2012. This is quite a simple app, and yet it does so much. When I found recipes I would put them onto cheftap and it would store them not only ordered but in a easier format to read then the site. Then, when my kindle broke and had to be replaced, I had to erase all my data from all my apps. It was a relief, however, when I found that amongst all my erased apps, cheftap had stored my data to the cloud, and I still had my recipies!!! ALL IN ALL, CHEFTAP IS THE BEST APP I HAVE EVER ENCOUNTERED.
The app is great and easy to use. Great place to store recipes you see on the Internet.

I love this app, I use it EVERY DAY.  So nice to grab a recipe that sounds good then when the cooking or baking bug strikes-I get to work!  I did upgrade so I could keep up with over 800 recipes.Thanks so much!  I love the new app logo, too !!!!!

Love this app.  It puts all those scattered webpage recipes in one place with lovely format.  For the blog like recipes that it has some difficulty deciphering the recipe from the blog it allows you to edit and retrieve missing text.  You can tag your saved recipes to categorize.  All in all I love it!
One of my most favorite and used apps! So quick and simple! I highly recommend!
Have had this app (pro level) God yrs & have ALWAYS been pleased;  especially with the "support"!

column2: best app. ever for recipe collectors and cooks
column3: Can't say enough wonderful things about Chef App. Unbelievably useful and well done for recipe collectors and cooks. Because I can edit the recipes, I have been adding my weight watcher points plus to each recipe as well, adding another level of convenience. Love that I can share my recipes w friends and family. Wish this was available on-line.

I love the design and functionality of this app. I can't tell you how many 'recipe software' programs I have run through and lost for different reasons (Mastercook- bigoven) boo to both of you. I can't wait until Chef tap offers up the ability to sync up all devices!! Hope this will be a keeper for the long term. I've lost oh so many recipe collections.....

If you're looking for your own personal cookbook for your tablet, this app is IT!  I looked at several different apps and decided on this one because it is so easy to import recipes from nearly any source.  It also offers categorizing, which makes it a snap to find your recipes when you need them.  I'd give this 10 stars if I could.  LOVE LOVE LOVE it! (AND it's FREE!)

This app has helped me like to cook again, it very easy to use & to sync between my phone . computer & kindle.  It allows you to find recipes in many other places & to store thenm all in one place, plus it allows you to make a grocery list for those recipes & it FREE!

column2: I searched and searched and this is perfect!
column3: 5 stars all the way!  Easy to use and the syncing between my PC, Kindle Fire (which I keep in my kitchen) and my Android phone is great!  The clipping feature is amazing since a lot of my recipes are from the internet now I can go find them and clip then and throw away the STACK of paper I have printed.  And now I can instantly send my recipes to my friends at work.  We are mindless eating machines, LOL.  It is my new best toy. Finally all my recipes are getting organized  *SMILE*  Support is fantastic also and I hear a new addition will be a shopping list.  I am a graphic designer so I have a blast using my OCR software to add my typed recipes and finding pictures on the internet to add to my personal recipes is easy and fun.  And in the future I will start adding my own photographs.

I have downloaded a lot of great recipes from different websites and had no problems at all. Have already tried several recipes and think the fact that Chef Tap will hold the recipe on the screen until I have finished with it is a terrific plus. Since I am not a computer wiz by any means I was also very pleased at how easy it is to use.

This is a great cooking app.  Instead of trying to remember which website I saw that great recipe on, I can import it, or add my own and keep them organized the way that I want so I don't have to spend a lot of time looking for my favorites or ones that I want to try.

I have used this app for seven years and it is ,hands down the best recipe app out there. I have tried several others and none of them have the features and ease of use as this one. Boot only can I load recipies from anywhere almost, I can even input the old family recipes out of my recipe box. You can even look up inspiration right from the app. I have the pro version . I would be heartbroken if this app was no longer available.

I use ChefTap every day, both for importing from websites and typing in my own recipes. I've even loaded jpegs I took with my iPhone from a magazine in my doctor's office because I don't like "borrowing" her reading material. I just type in the name of the recipe and then load the photo of the recipe as the picture. Then later at my leisure I can type in the actual recipe.I am starting a paleo baking business and find ChefTap invaluable in tracking my recipes as I'm always experimenting, changing and tweaking them, so it's really useful in that regard. I especially like being able to add notes so I know what I changed and when.Most of all I LOVE that I can backup my database to Dropbox, and that ChefTap actually reminds me to do it. It saved my business when my Kindle Fire HD recently had to be reset to factory defaults. I lost the data in many of my other apps, but not ChefTap -- I just redownloaded the app and retrieved my database from the Dropbox cloud! What a relief!

I will take the time to give this app a good review because it makes it extremely easy to import your favorite recipes from the internet so you have access to them anytime you need. You just broke the internet on your mobile device, find a recipe you like, but share with Chef Tap, and voila! It's yours!

No website up and running as yet. I use my Kindle for my recipes, so don't really have the desire to browse for my recipes online and download them with this app. Prefer to use my laptop. The app I use now allows me to find recipes, download them, and synch them to my Kindle, most of them automatically, some copy and paste. But works for me.Also, the recipes with ChefTap are more difficult to read.Sorry, ChefTap, but I prefer PepperPlate!

Not kidding. I love this app. It's like having an ever-changing cookbook at my fingertips. But this cookbook contains only recipes I am interested in cooking. I could never remember where I saved different recipes online. Now they are all in one place.  I have been cooking so many new exciting  things since I downloaded this app!

Love that I can import any recipe from any website. The unlimited cloud storage is worth the subscription and access across all my devices. Love that the app prevents the kindle from turning off while it's in recipe mode. It's everything i need in a recipe app.One suggestion would be to have an easy way to double or halve a recipe.
A terrific little app. But Upgrade. It's well worth it, and sometimes they offer discounts.

My wife and I use this and love it. We use the same login so if one person adds a recipe it syncs to both devices. It does a good job of reformatting from the web, there's only been a few instances where it's had trouble. Overall it's a 5 star app for 0$. What's not to like?

I couldn't get this to work on my new Kindle. You have to use a browser to use pinterest but because I was using a tablet, they wanted me to use the app. Even after signing in, the full website wasn't available. I ended up deleting this app cause it wasn't worth all the trouble.

column2: A+++ quality but F- for now requiring payment
column3: I love this app and used to recommend it to everyone. It was perfect the way it was ; limiting imports unless you pay was displeasing. A one time fee is understandable but annual subscription is just wrong!! Havent yet found an app to replace but I am looking.Mainly unhappy about how it was done-suddenly telling me to import I need to make an account, then when I comply and try again tell me I have to 'upgrade' to a pro account to continue.  I totally understand increasing services means needing income to help cover time and energy, but perhaps leave it as is and only have people pay for those increased services if they want them!

I don't purchase many apps but this one is worth every penny of the pro edition.  The app description is accurate.  Now, I can access my curated recipes from any of my devices.  They are protected with cloud storage and local backup.  I can give my daughter access to them via the web.  Finally, I have effective digital tool for the kitchen.

i think this is the best app on my kindle fire. Recipes are quick and easy to import, and changing or editing them is equally easy. only one weird thing has happened-- when i imported a recipe from a text file on my laptop, it didn't correctly import the fractions. it was easily corrected and only took a minute.I do wish there was cloud storage or a pc version,  though. If something were to go wonky with my fire, it would be tough to get all this info back.Update: There is now both cloud storage and a pc version making it very easy to import recipes on my laptop. Paste the URL and the recipe is added to my kindle. All the recipes also can be accessed through my computer. I did upgrade to the premium version, so this may not be the case with the free version.

I love to cook, and ChefTap provides me with a simple, easy way to organize recipes I obtain from all over the web, as well as the ability to add in my own favorite recipes that I've either created or were handed down to me. With reminders to backup and it's own self-contained recipes, it has become my "go to" all purpose cookbook.

I've been with chef tap from the beginning...bugs and all. It took them a while to improve it but it is and always has been a great app. The best part is, with a very low membership fee ($11/ year), you have direct contact with the creators of the app to tell them your issues and can e-mail back and forth until the problem is resolved.Highly recommend.

I love this app. it is so easy to use and I no longer have to print out any recipe I find on-line and clutter my recipe box. I can organize them by category, so it makes them easy to locate. I have suggested this app to several people already. it's a must have if you like to cook and bake, and try new recipes.

If you're one of those people who are constantly on food websites and printing pages of recipes out, saving them as PDFs, or copying and pasting them into a master word document, this app will simplify your life (on mobile platform at least). I wish they had something like this ages ago. There are countless recipes I've lost or misplaced over the years that I originally found online that I can no longer locate. I hope this app will prevent that from happening again.The app works exactly as described. Depending on the way the website article/recipe is organized, it may import perfectly into Chef Tap, or it may need some tweaking by you post-import. I don't really think poor imports are a fault of the app, but rather the site you are importing from. I haven't created an account yet, but I assume if you want to keep your recipes beyond the memory of your device, or view them on multiple or alternative devices, you'd need to create an account.

I love this app.  I love the fact that I can copy a recipe from a website and then find it when there's no internet available.  I use it at our camper often.  I would like it to be a little easier to title/organize the categories and find them a little quicker.  But overall, this is an excellent application.

column2: all my recipes in one place!
column3: This is an awesome ap! Finally all of my recipes in one place from pinterest, allrecipes, and more! Upload process is easy, video tutorials helpful, and a piece of cake to modify your own recipes! I highly recommend and haven't encountered a single problem in the 2 months I've been using this.

I think this is a wonderful app but there are some problems with it. Sometimes it doesn't import a recipe properly and you have to do a lot of editing. And that in itself can be difficult as the editing process is confusing and I cant get it to do what I want. Also sometimes when I try to retrieve. missing text it gives me the wrong text.

column2: Very nice recipe organizer, cool functions, highly customizable...
column3: This is a really nice app to organize all your favorite recipes with photos.  It allows you to grab information from online or enter it manually.  It has a nice attractive layout and highly customizable.  Give it a try, I really like it, especially since its free.

This is the most easiest app to use. It's so easy to take a recipe from your email or from a website and have it created in Chef Tap. Literally no effort on my part. It imports the recipe, organizes it into ingredients and directions and you're done!  The editing feature is so easy and so convenient.I'm so glad I found this app. I use it A LOT!
Great app.

column2: Awesome App I Wouldn't Live Without
column3: I love this app. I've been using this now for a few weeks, and the only issues I have are; sometimes it down loads the wrong picture with the recipe, and it does not keep a backup onto the cloud. The 2nd one isn't all that bad, well worth the wait when they get around to it.

If you collect recipes online, you NEED this app! Find a recipe, click "share" and, voila! you've got it! You can even backup your collection, either as text or html file to use on a web page. Recipes can be categorized, are easily edited, and can import the recipe photo as well. I love this app!

This is a great app to organize all of those recipes I used to print off and just slip between the pages of my other cookbooks.  Now I can just tag a web page and sync it to the app.  It is a great way to have all of the recipes easily at hand and on the go instead of having to go to several sites.
How did I  ever do without this app? So easy to download recipes. And so easy to bring up when you need them!
Family likes it

simply put... the best recipe app out there. it imports recipes so well. keeps track of the recipes you are currently using and even (if edited properly) shows your recipe in a step by step mode. will recommend it to my friends, thanks for making it free too!

I have a shelf full of cookbooks.  This app has almost replaced them all.  Save recipes at the touch of a button. Tag recipes to find them easier.  Back up and save to Dropbox or other online backup service with two simple steps.  This is one of the best designed apps I have on both my Kindle Fire and Android phone.
I've had this app a couple years & use it daily. The devs constantly update & make it better. It is my go-to cookbook everywhere I go.

column2: This is an incredible recipe app.
column3: I installed this on my wife's Xoom and it is amazing. It is amazing how well it imports text into it's recipe format.  It also is mindboggling how well it extracts recipes from just about any source you're viewing on the web.  It's easy to use, works flawlessly and does what it says it would do.  Awesome!!!

This app is easy to use and one place to store, review,sort. add and adjust your recipes. Great photos and many ways to manipulate recipes.Select & separate out  recipes you plan to make, personalize tags, easily share favorites.  Importing from web is just a click away.  Each upgrade is better & better!I use this on my Kindle Fire. Give it a try - good stuff.

Unlike with other recipe apps, I can clip recipes from anywhere on the web to make a virtual cookbook! Plus you can sync with other apps and pinterest. I love the tagging feature, too. It's much more organized than other cookbook type apps I have tried.

so easy to use. find a recipe online, click on share with chef tap, give it a minute and the app will add it to your saved recipes. you dont even have to have it in perfect recipe form...the app works its magic and formats it for you. this is my fav and most used app on my kindle fire. love it!

I love that this is the place for me to merge all of my online recipes. It also makes it easy to input and organize all of my personal recipes. My only issue is recipes that I deleted showing up the next time I open the app. It may be user error, but I hope I figure it out soon.

Nice, easy app for storing recipes.  Only issue is recently notified there is an update and I should get update.  When I checked for updates under my account, there were none listed.  The way it is done with updates for books.  Will check app store and hope there is no cost for update.
Been using the app for a couple years. My go to app for saving recipes.

so my friend from Germany has a book were she can write down all her recipe her mom and others tell her. I couldn't find that exact book so I decided to see if I can find the next best thing and I found this app. Im always on it and I can get recipes off the Internet and the app also uploads apps for me. I enjoy it and I look at it every day

I love this app!  It does everything I need and my family and I can all use it!  So user-friendly and easy to upload from websites.  I have tried other recipe apps and ChefTap is my favorite by far!  Completely recommended!

I have liked this app from the start, and it keeps on improving.  More recipe sites and formats are covered in downloading.  More than one image can be loaded for complex processes.  The backup is fast and easy.Four instead of five stars because it keeps telling me I am over the online number of permitted recipes - but keeps on recording and backing up my collection.  An error or weird something?  Still works fine!

column2: Wonderful app but too high priced for me to buy subscription
column3: This is a wonderful app. Easy to use and to clip recipes. I love that I can have the app on all my devices. Sometimes I will just use my phone for following the recipe when I am cooking and other times, I like to use my tablet for easier reading. It has limitations on a few things, like syncing and the number of recipes that can be clipped. But it does not hinder me  much. If the subscription was around $10.00 a year, I would buy it, but they were asking $20.00 and my budget just does not allow me to pay much for luxury items like this. But if money was not object, I would definitely purchase the subscription because it is so worth the cost. No glitches, runs smoothly, no problems, so far. Lovin it!
I love love this app it's so nice to tap a recipe and have accurate save!

I've been looking for an app that does what you do! Yes, there's a learning curve, but once I learned your slightly quirky procedures, I was hooked. I especially like the categories. If I could recommend any improvements it would be to make editing just a little easier. But, I'll live with it - free is free!

I have only fidgeted with this app a bit, particularly playing around with entering custom recipes by hand. I was searching for an app mainly to function as my personal digital recipe book. ChefTap allows users to create/edit/categorize recipes with ease! With the option to categorize, you can essentially "tag" recipes to make them easy to find later. The only thing that would make this app perfect for me would be a shopping/checklist for ingredients. I will play more with it later, as I am about to slumber. But I will end my review on this note: I ABSOLUTELY LOVE THIS APP and HIGHLY RECOMMEND IT!
Great recipe app. Use it all the time. Love that keep it updated. Give it a try.
Not my cup of tea. Found some free apps that I like better!
This is the only cooking app I use on all of my mobile devices.  It allows me to easily copy recipes over from multiple sources and the user interface is intuitive. Highly recommended!

column2: Not very good search options or choices when it comes to recipes
column3: What they don't tell you is that you only get so many recipes free. After that you have to pay. Not very good search options or choices when it comes to recipes. Downloaded out of curiosity, but would look around for something better.

This app is the best recipe app I've found. I love that I can pull in recipes from the web and Interest, since that's where I find most of my recipes, and that the recipes stay open while I'm using them. You just need to remember to close them when you're done to keep your battery from dying.  I've had minor issues with ingredients and steps getting mixed up using the automatic import, only on a couple of occasions, and they were pretty easy to fix. It has a small ad box included, but I hardly notice it.  Of all the apps on my tablet, this is the one I use the most.

I've been using Chef Tap for a couple of weeks now and the longer I use it the more I like it. You can grab recipes from websites or drag files to the Chef Tap import folder when the Kindle is hooked up to a computer. That's how I transfer recipes from my recipe program on my laptop. I would recommend this app.
Great app. Replaced all the messy binders I had accumulated.

I work out in the middle of nowhere without internet access. I needed some sort of recipe app that allowed me to download recipes from online so I could access them offline. ChefTap not only allows me to do this, but also allows me to type in my own recipes and save them! I love this app and highly recommend it!

I really wanted an app that would allow me to both download recipes from the web and add my own recipes which are currently in either Word or Excel files.  It apparently will to the web, but can't import my recipes so for me it isn't that useful.  If you only went web recipes, it is probably OK.
Does everything I need it to do and I'm not spoiled enough to whine about paying a *dollar* a month for the privilege.
I use this app for all my recipes. Love it. Only wish it didn't have to reload every time you go out of the app.

column2: great but import from MS Word docs needs work.
column3: Capturing from a webpage is great on the Kindle Fire. Importing from existing recipe files in .docs format on a PC is frustrating. While I would like one repository I maintain my PC documents and Kindle versions separately for now.

I use a lot of Internet recipes and chef tap makes it so easy to store and organize them.  I really appreciate the easy to use format ...I just prop up the kindle fire on my work table and don't have to worry about turning pages of a cookbook or touching the computer with greasy fingers!  I've even imported some of my most used personal recipes so I don't have to look for recipe cards. its a great app!

column2: Good app for keeping recipients in one place.
column3: I find this app very easy to use.  The ability to import recipes directly from websites or Pinterest is probably the best feature in my opinion.Update:  I use this app almost daily.  I have added recipes that I had gotten from my parents and love the fact that you have the ability to group recipes together by type.  I tried many different apps and for me this is the best one out there.

column2: Using this app a lot and love it. I appreciate being able to sync when ...
column3: Using this app a lot and love it.  I appreciate being able to sync when I'm on different devices.  The ads don't bother me but I'll probably upgrade to paid version for more storage as this is a keeper.
This works pretty well. You can create recipes, store recipes and get recispes others have stored. My wife and I definitely use it.
All my favorite recipes in one spot , on a tablet I can set on the kitchen cabinet. What's not to like?

column2: Great way to keep track of your recipes
column3: I really enjoy Chef Tap, it is a great way to store your recipes. I used to have my laptop open and run back and forth between the kitchen and my computer to figure what the next step is but now it is much easier when I have this so open on my tablet.

Excellent app. Pulls recipes from websites and other apps with no problems. I rarely have to do editing to the recipes. I now use my Kindle as my main cookbook because of this app. I can see both ingredients and directions on one easy-to-read screen. Looks like the developers really listen to issues. Great job! It was exactly what I was looking for.
Awesome awesome app! Finally getting to save all my recipes is so easy! I love it!

Nothing but complicated and unwieldy. NEVER got any recipe right, don't see how this beats bookmarking or printing one out. Save the frustrations, whatever system you are currently using beats this by a mile.

column2: Love this app but updating problems & need more functions
column3: This app doesn't have a menu planning or grocery list function. I really need it. I tried opening the 'Make' function and using as a grocery list but it had me running all over the store as I hunted the ingredients for each recipe. I also tried hand writing all the ingredients needed and then typing into my grocery store app. Both attempts did notwork well and left me with missing ingredients, wasted time and energy, and more trips to the store.I love this app but now that I have all my recipes at my fingertips, I need more menu planning and grocery list functions. Chef tap has created a food monster in me - lol.I am also having problems with Kindle Fire updates. I have to completely uninstall and reinstall to update. This has been going on for several months. Very strange.

column2: Tells me to update, I hit update, then ...
column3: Tells me to update, I hit update, then sends me to my Amazon account, I have this app on a Kindle Fire, and all it does is let me know I own this app. No where have I found anything that will allow me to update and now I can't get into the app at all.

I love cooking, and half hundreds of cookbooks and recipe magazines.  But this app makes it so easy to put in one spot only the recipes you will use.  I will get rid of my cookbooks and magazines eventually, as I don't even use them anymore.
I like it, but I need to get used to using it
Love this app bc it holds all my recipes and its easy to use. No more looking for my favorite recipes. It's all on my ChefTap. It's like my own little recipe book, with what I like to cook.

I work in the food industry.  I like the convenience of this app.  I can separate recipes that I experiment with at work with ones I use at home.  I also like the way it can show you the procedures right next to the ingredients.  Well done.
Works well for a new user.Transfers and additions can be frustrating at first, but get easier.

I started to use this app for my Kindle Fire. the basic features works very well and was easy to use. I would definitely recommend for someone who gets recipes from internet.  I edit and change recipes, so this app works well for me.

This app is the best. I pay for membership because I have hundreds of recipes on it, add more every day, and cook from it every day. I'd be lost without it.  Love my cookbooks, but when I need to find something specific in a hurry, it's always Chef Tap.

I love this App. I can share recipes, create my own, capture pictures and recipes. what can I say.. This is a great App. I will keep this for ever !!  If you like to cook good, easy and fun food you will love this .

LOVE this App and use it for all my recipes...the only reason I did not give it five stars is because I can't save it anywhere. I already lost all my recipes once and I am hoping it doesn't happen again. Trying new recipes is now so easy, I love searching for new recipes...specifically since you can do it all from your App.

Great for storing all your favorite recipes! I wish we had an account you can create so you don't have to start over everytime you have to download to a different device. I first had it on my cellphone then had to download it again on my Kindle Fire and had to redoubt all my previously saved recipes. I'm probably gonna have to do it again if I get the new Kindle HD. Still worth downloading again though! Thanx.
Addictive way to save recipes... Motivates me to find recipes and cook more often.
Stopped working on kindle fire. Was my favorite but no longer saves or imports

this app can automatically add the inportant parts of a recipe you look up online at (exp.) allrecipes.com. You find a recipe you like just hit the browser menu upper right then hit share page and choose chef tap. It puts all the info into chef tap to use at anytime.
I could not get it to work.

Started with Pintrest and it was great! Some recipes didn't come over but the link did. As I am gluten free it is great to be able to edit the recipe. Just used this to add recipe from Food Rehab. I tell everyone about this app!

Love this program.  So easy to use.  Nice to have recipes at your fingertips, especially when travelling to see the kids.  It is a handy program to have with my Kindle,which I am never without.  Also the recipes are easy to read on the Kindle. Highly recommend it.

I love ChefTap. This is my go-to app for meal planning. I have imported recipes from various locations...Pintrest, AllRecipes, ZipList, etc. It's so helpful to have these recipes in one place.The one thing that would improve this app is cloud storage. I recently upgraded my ereader from a Kobo to Kindle Fire and had to reload all my recipes.

OMG! This is the greastest app I've ever had. I love trolling for recipes on the Internet but the amount of paper and ink is enormous! No more!  This app imports the recipe to a database and acts as a cookbook. You can organize with catagories and edit recipes to your heart desire. You can even back up the database. on a flash drive if you don't have an SD card like my Fire. (plug it into the comp, open the chef tap folder and send to the flash drive or whatever back up you want) this is great no matter how much I upgrade my device I can have my cookbook Love love love it!

column2: super for organizing multiple sites of recipe finds
column3: it is great for consolidating and organizing recipe finds from many sites.  only negative is it takes a long time to load and I have to tell my kindle to wait and not force close a couple times.  once it loads it works great though
What do you say about recipe books? You get a number of them and do research on the recipes/meals/desserts/drinks you desire and go to work.Can't do that without any recipe books.

Love this app. It's wonderful having my favorite recipes in one place. It would be nice to have a shopping list once you select what meals you want to make. Attaching recipes from Pinterest or other sites is really easy.

This is the best recipe app that I have found.  I am actually able to keep all my recipes in one place - I no longer have to look at five different websites when i know I've seen the recipe on one of those sites. I am able to import a recipe from anywhere on the internet just by selecting ChefTap from the share menu on the internet browser (I have also shared from other programs).  The ChefTap program is very smart - I have imported a recipe that was inside of a blog - it knows what the ingredients are to take, the name of the recipe, and the picture, without taking anything else from the site.  After the recipe is downloaded, I can edit it and/or change the picture.  I highly recommend this app.

I had this app on my first kindle fire and it allowed me to download as many recipes as I wanted. When I received the new Fire I  download this app on my Fire and it will only allow 100 recipes. I don't want to have to upgrade to the pro and pay a fee just to store my recipes.

column2: Finally a recipe app that gets it !!
column3: I've told so many people about this app, I just love it and it works beautifully. I noticed a lot of my friends sharing or pinning recipes on Facebook....so I told them about this app. Now all of their recipes aren't clogging up the news feed.

column2: If you have a pinterest account..
column3: this app is very handy.  I don't use pinterest except for searching recipes and I don't know how to navigate the site very well, so I love this app.  Anything I find from pinterest or other websites that I browse I share to Chef Tap and it formats the recipe for me and saves it.  The only problem I found is that the pages with multiple recipes don't save correctly, which is understandable considering it scans the text and pictures for you and determines what to save.  You can create tags for the saved recipes and search by an ingredient or type of recipe (gluten free or vegan for example) if you want something specific.  One of the best free apps I have downloaded on my Kindle and highly recommended.

This is the first app I've tried so I have nothing to compare to but I love it. I love the fact that I can easily copy recipes to the app. Love that I can edit the recipes to remember any changes made or want to make in the future. Very easy to use.

This is a great app. I really enjoy looking for recipes on the internet and bam, they are on my kindle in great format. Also, unlike what someone else stated, you can import recipes from emails and other programs. I'm surprised this app is free.
Couldn't love this more. Makes saving recipes blissfully simple.I highly recommend.

This is a free app, but once you hit a limit you can no longer save recipes.  Something to do with backup.  I figure if I want to save a billion recipes and then tragically lose them it should let me.  Chef tap does not agree.

column2: The app itself is very nice. The 3 stars is because at so many ...
column3: The app itself is very nice. The 3 stars is because  at so many recipes, you have to upgrade. It doesn't tell you what it will cost. It's like blackmail.

column2: Best app for clipping recipes from blogs
column3: Part of the reason I bought my Kindle Fire was to organize my digital recipes and have them available without needing to print. I experimented with a number of apps, some of which do things Chef Tap doesn't -- Chef Tap doesn't have a searchable database of recipes, or do menu planning, or create a shopping list for you.  IOW Chef Tap doesn't offer features I really wasn't interested in.When it comes to clipping recipes from blogs and websites, Chef Tap is magic. Somehow it finds the recipe hidden in wordy blog posts about the blogger's day and clips out exactly (and only!) what you need to know to make the dish. No other app, including Evernote, does that as well. I resisted paying for an account, but in the end, I decided it was worth it. The time it would take me to clip those recipes by any other means is worth way more (at least to me!) than $12.00 a year. Now I can sync to the cloud and access my account on the web, and my recipes are always handy on my kindle.

column2: wanted to like this product, not for $15.99/year subscription fee
column3: The customer service is horrible.  At first I thought the customer service was horrible, because I was not a paying customer.  So I decided to pay for a year to test out the product.  My youngest son wants to be a chef when he grows up, so I really wanted a great recipe tool.  So I paid my money, and reported the software bugs to the developer.  The programmer's bug fix completed trashed my database.  Images on my tablet were deleted, and all changes that I did to recipes on my tablet were erased.  I import recipes and then modify all of them to suit my family's needs.  Anyway, the programmer's response when I told him my database was trashed was to give me my money back (which I did not ask for), and to downgrade my account from a pro version (which I legitimately paid for) to a basic version (again, which I did not ask for).  Yes, once my database was trashed, I knew that I would never renew the subscription to this product.  But now I have to do it before I hit 100 recipes instead of having a year to find the right product.This product have too many bugs that can serious damage your database of recipes.  It is not worth the price, especially when the programmer wants you have to have a 20+ year relationship with his product.  Over 10 years, that is $156.  Over 20 years, it is over $300 for a simple database to store recipes.  After you reach 100 recipes in the database, you have to pay a yearly subscription fee of $15.99/year.  That is $156.00 over 10 years and over $300 over 20 years.The only software that I re-buy each year is tax software.  Everything else I pay for with a one-time fee, and I will upgrade when I believe that I need to upgrade.  If I need to synch my database on a cloud, I will do it on my own cloud.  I don't need or want to pay a yearly fee for each type of data I may want to back up on a cloud.I believe that programmers should get paid for software they develop, which is why when there is a paid version and a free version of a product for a tablet, I usually buy the paid version.  Plus, I don't want my kids exposed to ads.  But subscription software?  The product has to be a the best of the best, no stone unturned, you can't live without, level of product.  This product does not fill those requirements.

SUMMARY: I have used from Thanksgiving planning through to New Year's. Wonderful! I have never found an app of any kind worth the price of a "full version" or subscription, but I will be subscribing to the full version of Chef Tap.PROS: First and foremost, extremely accurate on big name sites, and surprisingly accurate on smaller sites (see "Testing Accuracy" below). Between the clipping and recipe sizing features alone, this app is amazingly handy.There is also an easy editing feature that allows you to make it your own, as well as a notes section if you want to leave the original unsullied. I like the ability to tag and synch, but haven't played with them much.TESTING ACCURACY: I clipped 75+ recipes from  about a dozen different "big name" sites (Betty Crocker, BHG, Tablespoon, All Recipes, etc) and a half dozen or so from smaller blogging sites (Home-ec101, Acadian Table, etc). I double-checked both the ingredient and instructions on every single clip.Bottom line, the accuracy of the app is tied to how "well-formed" the source website is.Here's what I found...1. One error on a big name site - a recipe missing its last step.2. Several errors on small blogging sites - missing or duplicate ingredients or steps.2. One annoyance - several recipes that had numbered steps were missing the numbers (not the content, just the number itself). This is a step above cosmetic, because it happened almost every time, even on well-formed sites.3. A few rare, random "cosmetic" issues - duplicate titles, bad line breaks, or random bolding.However, all errors can be corrected with the editing mode. In addition, because the link is included in the clip, you can go back later in case you think something is missing.CONS:Together, the following cons mean I am frustrated every time I try to use the app. If it were not so accurate and useful, this would be enough to make me delete it and move on to something else:1. Takes too long to load - my devices are fast overall, with this app being noticeably longer loading on all of them.2. Loads back to it's "home" location instead of back to the recipe I was last looking at. By the time it opens and I remember what recipe I was going to look at, I have forgotten why.3. Synching across devices is confusing, but I suspect that is due to the limitations on the free version.

column2: $20 PER YEAR AND Different PRO features for different platforms? No thanks

The price is nominal if you think about it and you get so much for your money.  I can scale recipes reducing human error, I can create shopping lists and a 'make list' so I don't forget what I wanted to fix.  I have lost beloved recipes in my home countless times... well no more.  They are right there on my phone and computer AND they are organized.  You can search for things in countless ways if you use the tags.  I just can't say enough about this app.  It is free to try and if you don't like all of the convenience and organization it can bring to your life then you don't have to buy it.  But for those of us that need it, it is well worth the current $1.60 per month.  Highly recommend!

column2: **Watch your generous donations build the pyramids..!**
column3: Although it's not identical, this game reminds me a bit of Heroes of Kalavela. It features the same kind of oddball mixture of game genres, all orbiting around a central, Match 3 core. The other genres (adventure, city building) are supposed to provide an interesting and engaging rationale for the dozens upon dozens of repetitive Match 3 rounds you'll be playing. However, if you like Match 3 games a lot to begin with, you won't need this rationale, and if you don't, the rationale/sideshow in this game probably won't be enough to keep you playing. What this game really is--and, in this, it's exactly like a thousand other games--is a surfeit of busywork game mechanics designed to coax your money from your wallet in all the usual ways. It's no worse than those thousand other games in this respect, but it's no better, either.Bottom line: if you like Match 3 games, the core gameplay here is solid and silly-free. If you don't, or if you're put off by stuff getting constantly thrown in the way of your Match 3 joy, you'll probably not be very long in invoking your Ultimate Spell of Uninstall. (And, obviously, if you're one of those who avoids coin whore, IAP games on principle, you'll want to miss this one out, although IAP's arent technically necessary in order to complete the game, AFAICT.)

column2: VERY linear, but may be fun for some.
column3: Cradle of Empires is a base building/match 3 game. When I got C radle of Empires, I was looking forward to a game that focused mainly on the base building game and not so much on the match 3 portion, but I was dissapointed to find it focusing mainly on the match 3 mechanic. At the begining you start off with one builing, and to get more you have to level up. To level up, you have to play the match 3 levels, which each building has 8 of. To even simply upgrade the building, you must get a 3 star on each of these levels. I am a person who does not like match 3 gameplay very much, and so I thought this feature really diminishes the base buildig portion of the game, which it does. So if you are looking for a base builder do not get this game. Also, the story of the game is totally pointless. Mostly, the people of your town, which there are very few of, just want you to find them some pointless item in one of the levels and your reward is just a bit of XP. The whole story of the game is just a collectathon. The game is also very linear because all you do is have someone tell you what to do, do it, repeat. So to me, this game was boring, linear, and pointless. The only reason I gave it a 2 star was because for some people, who like match 3 games more, might actually think this game would be fun and if the creators did a better jobs at the levels, I would too.

column2: Fun little game to pass the time.
column3: Fun little game to pass the time!  It takes the ever popular 'match 3' game style and gives more strategy and purpose.  Reminds me a lot of Gummy Drop if your familiar with that game,, just has a different scene and scenario.  I enjoy it, and if you give it a shot you probably will too.  The only set back, as with most of these in app purchasing games, is you can only get so far until you either have to be patient and wait for energy to replenish over time, or spend your cash on the green gems.  I don't think so...lol...I'll wait. Fun. Check it out!

I see a few reviews about the need to make pricey in-app purchases to complete quests etc... So far I haven't had that experience. I've put in between 15 to 20 hours of gameplay with no need to wait for energy to recharge even once or need to make a purchase to accomplish something. If you like to use bonuses in your match 3 games then yes you will probably want to purchase them. They can be obtained in the game as well though. So far I haven't come across a level that seems frustrating to beat without those bonuses.Overall I'm enjoying the game. I like the concept of rebuilding a city and what that entails with the points and goods like food or money that are earned by playing a typical match 3 game. There are 3 different modes that you play. Like having a particular amount of moves, timed, and using a flash light to illuminate just a portion of the scene. The graphics are pretty, there's a bit of a story, it's a cool game.For me so far so good. Guess I shall see in the higher levels if in-app purchases are an absolute and whether or not they accomplish little for the money. I'll update on that issue if need be.

Pretty typical match 3 game.  Great graphics, nice little story line to follow.  Seems to run slow at times on my Kindle, have to press on some items multiple times before they register.  I'd give this more stars but...it's absolutely maddening to play a game where you need to complete a level to find an item to progress (spending energy on each level of course until you run out and have to wait to play or buy it with real money) and then you finish the level and don't obtain the item you needed.  This has happened multiple times to me, and I've had to play certain boards even 3 times to get some items which is absurd.  If you successfully finish a board, you should always find the item that's supposed to be there!This game mechanic is basically a way to make you waste your energy in an attempt to get you to spend $$ to buy more and keep playing.  I'm all for throwing a bit of cash towards app developers that make a good game and entertain me, but I'm not going to pay for something when it's frustrating to play and it feels like the app is set up as a cash grab.  So while it's not a bad game and you can play for a little while with breaks in between if you don't want to spend money, be aware that once you get past the first 4-5 levels and each board starts costing more energy to play, it becomes less fun when you have to keep repeating those boards.  I'm also not a fan of match 3 games with levels that you have to complete in a set number of moves, they always get to the point where you never have enough moves to win unless you get lucky.  I'd rather play a game with timed boards any day.

column2: Different take on Match-3/Cradle of ... games
column3: I loved the Cradle of ... games I played on desktop or laptop in the past.  While this is clearly from the same developers an on the same vein, it has added features from such game types as Farmville, with energy used from performing tasks (in this case playing levels), and after erecting a building, you earn things from them, which have to recharge, and upgrading your buildings takes time where you cannot access the levels in those buildings.  I'm not a big fan of these features, but don't really mind them either.  What bothers me most is that you need to obtain particular items to finish collections or complete tasks for rewards, and you can play the level containing the item many times, sometimes even upgrading the building and then playing quite a few more times before you finally get the item.  The levels also change modes if you play them enough times, and some modes aren't much fun, but are required either to complete a quest, or to play a level enough to get the item you want.  It can be fun, but it can also be frustrating, when you cannot get an item you need because the villain has essentially poisoned the whole area and until you finally clear the "poison," you are limited to the first four buildings, and they get boring after a couple of days of heavy play.  I'm trying to get it clear, but a collection keeps sending me to a "poisoned" area (therefore not playable) for an item I need to complete it, which is needed to clear up the "poison."

First, let me just say that this game hounds you to spend real money more than any other game I've played. It even makes spending money a quest, which is laughable. Problem is, it's just not that good.Basically, it's just a bunch of fairly simple match 3 games wrapped up in a Egyptian era package. You play to collect food, building supplies and money to expand your town in a completely structured fashion. Your energy is very limited, an everything you do is dictated almost entirely by the game. In fact, the constant interruptions by the game are nothing short of annoying.The biggest problems I have with this game (other than it constantly asking for money and not allowing for any creativity from the player) mainly have to do with the match 3 games themselves. If you finish in fewer moves than allotted, you don't receive any materials for matches made with your leftover moves, which is stupid. Also, the new items do not fall straight down when matches have been made, which means you cannot play this game strategically. Without strategy, it's down to luck (or, more accurately, money) rather than skill, and if you fail a level because you get an unlucky board, you get nothing.All in all, it feels like a scam. Games such as this one that penalize players for their own flawed design should probably be avoided.

column2: Small annoyances that add up to big aggravation
column3: Let me preface this by saying that there's a lot this game gets right.  Graphics are gorgeous, sound is very good, concept is intriguing, and the story is meaty without being overdone.But the aggravation in CoE is greater than the sum of its minor annoyances.First up, it's Match 3, and so there are times when you're going to be left with squares near the top of the board that can only be matched with a lucky drop.  By itself, it's a minor annoyance, but that's the nature of Match 3.But then, after you pass the level, there's a chance you may not even find the object you're questing for.  You read that right:  even if you DO get past a level, you may still come away empty-handed.  True, you'll always get SOMETHING after a completed level; but whether or not that "something" is of any actual value, well...An example:  I'm looking for one specific charger that I need to finish a main story quest.  I've been searching where the game sends me for TWO DAYS at this point, and that ONE little item that I need, just flat-out REFUSES.  TO.  SHOW.  UP.  Again, by itself, it's a minor annoyance; low drop rates for quest items aren't unheard of.  But a low drop rate for quest items on the back end, after I've already had to deal with enough of a luckfest in the upfront game, adds up the annoyance in a hurry.But the topper is that it's energy-based, and you can only make so many attempts before having enough energy to take another atttempt.  This one item I'm looking for, is in an area that takes 11 energy; at three minutes per energy unit, that means a 33-minute cooldown if I run out.  By itself, it's a minor annoyance; energy meters are almost a fact of life in high-end FTP's.  But when you add it to the other two...Let me put this as succinctly as I can.  By itself, I have no issue with losing a Match 3 level to an unlucky late-stage drop.  By itself, I understand quest items can be hard to find.  By itself, I get that energy meters are the price of FTP gaming.Where I take issue, is having to wait half an hour or more, to play the same area for the twentieth time, hoping that I don't get jobbed by an unlucky drop at the end of the level, in order to, MAYBE, find a quest item that may not even show up.Individually, those are all minor annoyances.  In combination, though, the whole of the aggravation is much worse than the sum of the minorly annoying parts.

column2: Bringing the Vampire Girl to Life
column3: Vampire Girl has never read better. As an avid reader, it's always great to find different ways of enjoying a good read. This innovative approach to reading surely brings the books to life. This approach allows you to choose your characters and the style of clothing; however, with certain styles of clothing you have to have enough tokens in order to choose the fancier clothing. You cannot; however, decide clothing or appearance for the other characters, just yourself. In addition, you need to have enough tokens in order to choose certain phrases you want your character to say. Most of the interactive communication and styles of clothing are free, but in some cases you simply need more tokens. You acquire tokens after you have finished reading a chapter or if you want to purchase tokens.The background scenery was very colorful and brought all the characters to life. The site lets you know how much longer you have in each chapter which allows you to adjust your time accordingly. If you have to stop in the midst of the chapter, it will open up right where you left off so no worries.The only setback was the need to buy or have tokens. I didn't have enough tokens in the first book of the series; therefore, it would not allow me to finish the last chapter in the first book. However, you can pretty much piece together what happens but because of this feature I will only give it four stars.~Nicole

column2: REQUIRED micro-transactions ruin an otherwise interesting and fun game. Only for the wealthy
column3: I've read ALL of the reviews posted on or before 5-10 -19. Often it s seems for Chapters Interactive Stories, the main difference between most of the positive vs. negative reviews is based on the author's ability and/or willingness to spend money on countless micro -transactions to influence the stories. One person wrote that she'd spent $80 during one story. My personal feelings of micro-transactions aside, it's fine if individuals who can afford such things want to spend their money on a suit of armor or a ball gown for character's whose stories have a finite lifespan of 20 chapters, but what many people probably don't realize is even if you don't purchase diamonds or gems depending on the story your engaged with, eventually you'll have to buy the chapters just to finish a story. As soon as I completed chapter 7 and was told it would cost $2.99 for the next chapter, I realized this game wasn't for me and I deleted it.

And did I mention it's free?  That's a huge plus for me. Ultimately, the inclusion of 'choices' is a detriment to the ap, distracting and breaking the immersion without actually adding anything of value.  Even the 'options' included with the expenditure of diamonds change nothing and completely fail to add a personal touch to the stories, which is presumably the goal.  Your best bet is to identify the bad books as quickly as possible (trust me on this, don't press.on hoping it will improve out of respect for the prompt.  It won't.) and move on to the decent ones.

column2: This game made me hate Arnold Schwarzenegger
column3: I'll give you a quick overview of how this game works.  Go to your bank and ask for a nice crisp $100 bill, then walk to the nearest toilet and immediately flush it.  Try to do that again at least weekly, and ideally several times a week, until everyone else on the planet realizes that you have easily flushed the most money down the toilet and names you king.Seriously, some of the people in this games have spent thousands of dollars to stare at pixels on a mobile phone in some sort of digital chest thumping tournament.  I'm sure a few of them can easily afford it, but I know many really can not.  Maybe they are disabled, have a hard time socializing, can't leave the house... the game becomes a substitute for them.  Maybe they've sunk so much money into it they feel like they can't simply walk away - it becomes a matter of protecting your "investment."  The developers know this and prey on these people - every week a new sale comes along that makes your account worthless unless you spend more money.  Don't religiously check on your base?  If your shield drops someone else that has spent a lot of money can "zero" your base to teach you a lesson.  Busy on the weekend with your family? You haven't fed the game in a while so it's time to kick off a State vs State event where people from another server that have spent a lot of money can level your base.I could go on and on, but please people - take a pass on this game and games like it.  Don't let these morons use you like an ATM.  If you are playing and can't stop, get help!  If you have too much money and have no idea what to do with it, I can name thousands of alternatives that will take your money and put it to a much better cause.  And Arnold.. if you are reading this, for the love of all that is holy wash your hands of this abomination.  Take the fat paycheck they gave you, and use part of it to help people with addictive personalities find treatment.

column2: Play this if you have an unlimited disposable income stream.
column3: I am writing this review so that others can make see what my experience with the game was and then make their own decision. I downloaded this to get a "reward" from another game that I played. I was hooked in the first day and saw that the max base or headquarters level was level 30 in June of 2017. It is now October and the max HQ level is 250 if I recall correctly.I want to be the best and be able to conquer the game so I made my first purchase, I was promised an HQ level of "X", a commander level of "X", and completed research levels of "X". After my purchase I was not able to complete the items as stated in the "sale". I contacted the developer and after 10 emails I was able to straighten out my issue.This cycle continued until I stopped playing in August of 2017. What I found was that once I made it to a certain point, that for another mere $100 I could level up to another point and so on. I found that it is a never ending cycle.I spent a huge chunk of money on the game and found that, if you did not purchase the newest package your base, troops, research, etc. was obsolete. The newer base, troops, research, etc. always "destroyed" the last package release.When I started playing the items were consistent and everyone was "maxed" out. Epic war, LLC. is releasing new items every Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturdays currently. If you are NOT buying the latest and greatest you cannot "safely" accomplish the goals of the game which are to destroy other bases and hold control points.They (EW) come out with a “new” sale every few days that always state guaranteed “max”. If it was Guaranteed “max” then it should “stop” at that point and not continue to increase. The HQ was a max of 30, then 40, then 100, then 200, now 250. The commander, VIP, troops, research, each have levels as well. While one package may "max" out say your commander, you need another once to max out your VIP, or HQ, etc.The game depreciates faster than buying a new car, for example when they release something on Tuesday, it comes with say 100 items for $100 and you need 1,000 of those items to "max" out your base. Then when the new items come Thursday (or sometimes they come Tuesday night or Wednesday morning) they include the 1,000 items for $20-$80. Keep in mind that even though it includes the full 1,000 items for what you needed on Tuesday, it now needs 1,000 different items for another "upgrade" but it only comes with 100 of those items.There are constant glitches in the game that don’t allow the game to play properly. Also you are constantly missing items after the “purchase”. It generally takes three or more emails to the developer before they attempt to fix the issue. It takes another three to four emails after that before you have the items completed.The numbering and amount of items required went from you need 1,000 of this, to you need 1TT (TT= Septillion, yes it's a real number) of that same item to "level" it up. Currently (10-16-17) there are people with a power level of 1KTTT (Sedecillion), which require you to have an unreal amount of troops.If you choose to spend money on this game do some research, there are many ways to save money when buying packs, but as I said you need an Unlimited disposable income stream to play this game.I am happy to spend “some” money to play a game that I can enjoy and I would be happy to also pay to see the game progress, however when the game progresses three times a week it is theft and a scam.Good luck to you.

That does not mean those games aren't around anymore but new offers & participation have been stagnant in the last few years after a massive contraction. - That said, you'll like this game if you are into mmorpg and you won't be deceived by the ads with Arnold. It is one of the best games of its kind out there at the moment. Word of caution though: Success will only follow IF you will join one of the leading alliances with a high gift level (above 15) AND you are prepared to spend some $$ eventually ($5 - $100). After four months you will reach lvl 21 (of 30) and game play will become expensive because you will have to buy packages a lot more often. From the makers of Engine Age's "Game Of War - Fire Age", this one runs on the same engine and the devs (EW called here) are experienced and they've learned their lessons from other failed mmorpg type games; glitches are kept mostly under control and cheating (i.e. through script hacking) is not allowed. Devs have recently disallowed play on older devices with OS from before '15. They actually DO enforce their TOS. - Expect to put in anywhere between 15 minutes to upwards of an hour per day and account. Happy gaming.

column2: Fun, but not worth the expense and aggravation
column3: This game can be fun, and has a lot of potential, but is something of a bait and switch.  The first game pack can be purchased for only 4.99, and the next is 19.99...still not too unreasonable...but every one thereafter is a whopping 99.99. Considering how glitchy the software is, and always at the worst possible time, it's definitely not worth it unless you're independently wealthy. There is simply no way to effectively compete unless you're shelling out lots of money.  Game rules and explanations are rudimentary at best, and while there have been obvious attempts to make the game interface as intuitive as possible, it still has a very long way to go. All of this makes for a considerable amount of confusion for new players.  Customer support has generally been timely, but helpful or useful only about half the time. Whether you receive a support agent with a solid working knowledge of the game seems strictly up to chance.  Overall, for the exhorbitant prices being charged, this game needs to work much, much better. A real pity, because it does have some interesting ideas behind it. It's a crying shame they don't simply lower their prices, and try to make up for the difference by doing volume business instead. It would certainly leave far fewer players feeling as though they've been cheated.
