When I quit the first time I had just completed level 21 and within a few days they came out with level 22.  There is a constant push to spend money to keep your forces at a level to be effective.  Most packs cost $99.  After a year I came back and there now is level 60's. epic offered a catch up pack for $4.99. column2: The game can be very fun. The problem is that you can't grow your ...
column3: The game can be very fun.  The problem is that you can't grow your base and empire without spending a lot of money.  If you take the approach that this is a video game like you would purchase for the Xbox One or PS4 then dropping $75 isn't a big deal.  But if you were looking for a fun, cheap form of entertainment this isn't it.  You can't have fun if you can't get bigger.  And if you don't get bigger then the other strong alliances come in and destroy your base on a regular basis.I've dropped $25 so far on two Gold packs and I've become pretty strong.  But now I've reached the point where I need to drop another $50 to get myself past the level I'm at.  I am afraid that once I drop the $50 then it will only get me so far and I'll need to drop $100 to move up further.That's the other issue.  Each time you buy a Gold pack the next one you buy that will provide you any benefit is double the price.  And once you start investing it is hard to not keep investing so you can stay relevant in the game.  Or you walk away and eat the money you invested.UPDATED REVIEW - 4-16-2017:  So I invested some more $ and am up to $100.  I'm at level 22.  To get to level 23 you need a lot of Legendary Hammers.  Legendary Hammers are only available through the $99.99 pack purchases.  You can't win them through achievements, you can't gift them to other players.  There should be a way to continue to advance without sinking more money into a game.  It could be made to take a while to do, but it would allow for the casual gamer and the gamers that don't want to invest all of their money, to continue to play and advance.  As it is, I am stuck at lvl 22 and I will not invest more $.  I will continue to try and grow bigger at the level I am and be a very strong and formidable lvl 22, but I will never be able to compete with those that spend the $ to continue to grow.It is a fun game, but it is disappointing that I can't progress without continued investment.

It is a great strategy game, there are lots of areas to grow and there are always challenges to complete. However, I agree with the 1 star reviewers that if you want to be the BEST you have to spend money. Lots of it. Not even hundreds, I'm talking thousands. SO, if you go in wanting to be a top competitor, then expect that. But if your like me and just want to pass the time by building a base, working through what you can and making friends, then do that, there's definitely enough to keep you busy, but there will be areas of frustration where you'll want to unlock or do something and can't unless you spend money.So if you want to try it out, here are some tips:1. Stay shielded and build your base. If your base shield drops you will be attacked and you will lose resources. I only let mine drop if I want to get in a few attacks, then it goes back up. Don't get too frustrated if you get attacked because that's just part of the game. And you can lose troops on tiles as well so expect that to happen at some point too AND DON'T SEND OUT YOUR COMMANDER.2. Probably spend $5. Work through what you can first, but I've gotten pretty far on $5 as depending on what you get you'll unlock blueprints, a lot of speedups, research files etc. I may end up spending $20 but we'll see. Keep in mind once you spend 5 or 20 the cost of the packages goes up and stays up. After you spend that initial 5 you won't see a $5 one again so choose wisely.3. Time building up your base with challenges when you can. If you complete a challenge (like Build, Research, Train, Repeat) then wait for it to refresh before you start building up again.4. Try to join a large alliance. There are alliance challenges that reward you big for having a lot of alliance members that complete them. Plus you'll stock up on a lot of items by collecting alliance gifts and buying things with loyalty points (which you earn for free) in the alliance store. And if your members are nice they'll help you out with items and resources.5. Collect as many resources, speedups and research files as you can. Even if it seems like you're getting a lot, trust me, you'll need them later. Some research requires billions of resources, a million files and 1000+ days to complete so collect what you can.6. Research your butt off and use things like commander armor and mods to give your base some building and research boosts.7. Pay attention to state boosts. These change and sometimes one will pop up that will give you access to research that you didn't have before by providing the first 1000 files or 100% of the time and/or resources.There are lots of other things to mention but these will help you a lot if you decide to try it out. At the end of the day spending money is your choice so if you're prone to getting sucked in and spending too much then I would not recommend this game.

column2: so while I COULD comfortably feed my troops
column3: Been playing for about 2 weeks now... and I see a serious issue with toxic players. While the state I am in seems to have a few rules (most important is players are supposed to "stay in their own power brackets in attacking"), they are routinely ignored. How you do in battle is mostly based on how "powerful" you are... there is a numeric scale. After 10 days I was 200k. I have seen characters with over a BILLION in said power. Apparently, every week they have a "free for all" that starts on Fri night and lasts till Sunday night. I was almost looking forward to engaging with those around my "level" in the game. BUT, many hours BEFORE the start, someone with 50 MILLION power sent 250k troops to hit me (I have 20k troops). Wiped a weeks worth of work out. He took my "commander" meaning all the buffs such a character gives were gone.... so while I COULD comfortably feed my troops, I can't any longer. Then, the next day I get attacked again by someone with 180 MILLION pwr and 100k troops. Best analogy I can find is you go to a fight with your fists and someone brings a nuclear missile, the disparity really is that large.In "listening" to other players chatting, it became apparent that those like the 2 who wiped me out HAD to have spent over several thousand dollars buying "packs" that allow them to become as powerful as they are. AND instead of them playing on some form of level playing field, they get their jollies praying on those new to the game or who don't have the financial resources to compete. They literally laugh about the situation, called anyone saying "hey this isn't fair" as idiots to be targeted further.This COULD be an IMMEASURABLY better game if there was at least a sort of level playing field. The developer COULD make it so that to be attacked, you had at least a fighting chance. All over the map I see tons and tons of abandoned "bases" and I bet the majority of them saw what I see and gave up. Doesn't make for a very healthy game when work and effort are so easily wiped out by someone who spends hundreds & thousands. Somehow I am very skeptical the developer will make any attempt to create a more even playing field...

Let me put it this way.  This game is about as free as going to a restaurant.  You can walk into the door and wait to be seated at no cost but if you want to eat, you have to pay.  Yes, it's free to go into the restaurant but anything you want to do will cost you.  That's this game.  It should be called Money Sink.First of all,  packs are designed to get you to pay.  If you buy a $4.99 pack, you are never offered another 4.99 pack again.  Instead, you are bumped up to the next "tier" and have to pay more (i.e 19.99).  Then it goes up again.  The packs are always contain useless junk. For example, it takes 1024 of a level 1 item to make a level 6.  The packs they will offer you will only contain 1000 or 500 of that item (leaving you off by 24)  Thus you need another pack and now have a ton left over to waste (useless).They make sure to give you material crates because they've added 100's of useless materials to the game.  All the useful equipment take the same materials but those materials are considered "rare" so you hardly ever find them.  Instead you get a bunch of garbage.  And almost weekly it appears they are releasing new "useless" materials.  Why would I want to build armor with mediocre fighting and farming stats when you can build armor with great fighting and armor with great farming stats. If you are fighting, why do you need farming stats?  Stupid idea.  Most people just switch gear depending on what they are doing.Game has some huge memory leaks.  Will definitely slow your phone/tablet to a crawl causing a reset.Plenty of advertisements for upgrade packs.  You can never escape them as they are everywhere.  They place icons all over the screen so when you scroll around on the map, you accidentally hit them so they can spam more ads at you #smhAll new features require you to purchase packs.  Huh a free game but yet, to access any new feature they release, you need to buy a pack.If you don't have 10k+ to pay to play the game, don't bother thinking you'll get anywhere.  Big alliances have big spenders who won't wait a second to attack and drain a new player of all their resources and kill all their troops. Thus all your work for weeks (months maybe) gone in a few seconds.  But you can prevent this?  Just spend $$$ to buy shields and stay shielded all day.  Of course even these are scammy.  You can buy a 30 day shield for 45k gold but yet 3 day shields cost 2.5k gold.  So 10x 2.5 = 25k gold yet they figure people can't do simple math and charge 45k for a 30 day.  Yes, you don't have to log in every 3 days to apply but who buys a 30 day shield and never plays the game?  Big spenders of course who are about to go on that month long vacation.Lastly, it's buggy.  Every other week they are releasing a new feature that costs $$$ but rarely get around to fixing bugs.  It's like they don't have QA testers in house and depend on players because some things are obviously buggy (i.e. Timer for instant training was exactly 1 day yet it would return "Invalid Time")I can go on and on about this trash game.

it becomes an issue when you sit under the peace shield 24 hours each day.  Each state has a head of state who makes the rules and changes them at whim or whenever they are in a bad mood.  These players can have over 1 billion in power and you can't even scratch them.  For example I have a Level 21 base with 90 million power, today was nap which is a no attack period until midnight.  The leader of the state decided to change the rules today and gave 1 hours notice and believe me, this was a lot of notice for him.  On the drive home from work my peace shield expired even though I don't need it during nap I have learned to use it.  I sat in traffic and when I got home to check my shield figuring I had until midnight but would initialize it early, the head of state had already gone out and burned all unshielded bases.  Destroyed 125k traps, 185k troops and took my commander.  It will cost a lot to rebuild the traps and time as well.  I don't mind the time element here; however, I do mind that a guy with his daddy's credit card can buy so much power that it is virtually impossible to have any fair game play.  Several players gave up and joined his alliance, the old if you can't beat them join them.  But, when this leader is on state chat the way he speaks and treats people is worse than Donald Trump crossed with Hitler.  As if everything negative in the world is channeled through him and into the game aimed at everyone playing in the game.  What would help, the game makers making rules which all must go by including those who are head of state.  In this way, at least no attack times are predictable and stable.  Otherwise, you must be logged into the game constantly to see what the latest rules are.  Also, there are so many alliances who are allies of the head of state there is no one left to actually fight them.  Tonight's quick rule change and attack our our alliance made at least 6 players discuss quitting and 3 have quit in the past week.  Our alliance has 2 billion in power, this is disgustingly inadequate to do anything.  The head of state alone is 20 billion in power.  Have fun wasting your time and money.

Remember the good old days when you and your friends would take turns throwing $20 bills into a fire?  Then, after a few hours, whoever threw the most bills into the fire was declared the winner?  Wasn't that fun?  No?  Then, you probably shouldn't download or play Mobile Strike (or Game of War).  Your power level in the game is a function of how much you are willing to spend.  If you spend $100/month, you will be much more powerful than free players.  If you spend $500/month, you will be much more powerful than the $100/month players.  If you spend $1,000/month, you will be much more powerful than the $500/month players.  It's that simple.  If you are a free player, you will spend much time and frustration playing a crippled version of the game while the $$ players farm you over and over again while you can do nothing.  If you can put up with that for more than a few months, then bless your heart.If you are reading this review and have never really had much exposure to a true pay to win game, you might be thinking I'm exaggerating that someone would spend $1,000 a month on a mobile game.  Oh, I wish I was -- the bigger spenders (whales as they are known in the industry) easily drop that much and more.  In Game of War, this game's direct predecessor and almost identical clone that has been operating for a few years, the biggest whales have easily surpassed $100k in lifetime spending on the game.  And, while some can no doubt afford it, I am 100%, no doubt, guaranteed certain that many have gone into debt, maxed out credit cards, and ruined their lives and their families trying to keep up.  It is an addiction related to and probably very similar to a gambling addiction.  Machine Zone/Epic War (Same company) are VERY VERY good at getting you hopelessly hooked even if you think you'd never be susceptible to that kind of thing.I would not recommend it for anyone to play because:1) The gameplay is addictive, but not fun.  Most of the game consists of variation of clicking button to get awards or prizes.  If you get really into it, you will find yourself spending countless hours on it building, researching, training, opening, using times, logging onto farm accounts, trading, and more but most of this stuff soon becomes tedious chores you MUST do just to be able to keep your account competitive and the times you actually spend attacking other players are few and far between.2) There is always a bigger fish.  Any reasonable spending budget will be dwarfed by the biggest players in the game.  The only way to become a top player is to throw caution to the wind and probably max out a few credit cards.  Even then, there will always be someone else who is willing to spend a little bit more or has a little bit higher credit limit.  It's a never ending race you will never win.3) Important: If you have issues with compulsiveness, addiction (especially gambling addiction), self control, budgeting, unrestrained competitiveness or easily succumb to peer pressure, I cannot stress how important it is to never, ever start playing this game.  The very first time you open the app -- before you even start really playing -- you are bombarded with ads and offers to buy your progression in the game.  When you first join an alliance, you will feel pressure to grow your account faster so the alliance will be more powerful.  Every single new feature or new power boost they release will be behind a paywall that you will have to purchase.  You are the type of person they target -- people who have to play everything to completion, people who can't stop and walk away after losing $500 on the black jack tables, and people who have to be the biggest/best at something no matter what.It is quite common for whales in this game and others like to say things like, "I've invested $10,000 into this account." instead of "I've spent $10,000 on this account."  It's some kind of weird coping mechanism that they believe their money is being used to invest in something rather than being thrown away and it shows you how far gone most of them are.  While it's true that you can sell your accounts (against the terms of service of the game), you will usually only get a fraction of what you've spent in return and the buy/sell markets are rife with scammers on both sides -- people who take your money and not turn over the account or take it back after the transaction is complete or people who will take your account without paying.  Also, since it is against the terms of service, the account may be deleted if the game makers find out.TLDR: Stay far, far, far away.

column2: Crashes a lot. Good base and character building but very little else to play for
column3: I'm writing a revised review after 6-7 days of playing the game. I originally posted 4 stars, but knocking this down to 2.Starting with the positive, there are a few elements of the game which are quite enjoyable and some pretty in depth and have received some thought from the developers. The base building element is quite good and the ability to customize your character and bases strengths and weekends by electing where to invest your skills/research time or what modifications you make upon your gear is pretty good too. However, you soon realize that there is very little else to the game. Basically the battle / 'mission' elements to the game are just lacking. Missions are basically an endeviour of clicking a start button, waiting for somewhere between 2 minutes to 2 hours to elapse and then clicking a 'collect' button - I wish I could say it was more exciting but that's it. You can wage battles against your opponents however - sound more promising? Well, you basically pick a base to attack, send your troops in, and await for them to return to here the outcome. You do not see the battle, fight the battle, influence the battle or have any real sway over its outcome as far as I can see. So you spend all your time in the game bascially just increasing elements of your base from one level to the next. Furthermore, because all base items are chained dependencies upon each other, actually your base customization is really poor. You must upgrade your Wall to upgrade your HQ, and you must upgrade your Iron Mine (I think) to upgrade your wall and so on and so forth. The chose you have of what to build becomes simply a matter of 'how many' of each item you choose to build.Next on my hit list to highlight is the games undeniable drive to have you spend your money. My character is on level 19 and has a VIP level of 7 after quite a lot of hours played this week, but for the grand total of £3.99 you can start at level 50 which a VIP level of 30. Else, given the exponential increase in time it takes to build, train and research i imagine that would take about 1 month. If you don't want to spend you have a long waiting game ahead to be anywhere near those players who do. At every turn the game tries to pries you from this 3.99 investment with extra base items, unlocks for various things, huge amounts of gold etc. Its a bit too 'in your face' for my liking. I'm open minded to spending money on a game - but I first seek to see if its a game i'd like to play for some time - but alas if I spent money on this game, other than having a more powerful base I don't see what for - there's so little else to the game play that it just all feels a little pointless.The final point i'd draw attention to is the games reliability. This may not be the same for all - I guess it could be devise related but while sometimes I can play the game for over an hour, at other times the game might just exit every few minutes forcing a constant reload. It becomes really frustrating. I'm using an Amazon Fire 7" Tablet for the record.

I got the "Connect" version of the Ghost Radar after downloading this app, and have had some good fun with it. This version is much more simplistic, as all it is is the radar and words, but in all reality that's good enough. The Connect version has a "Vox" box added into it, but I honestly don't even know what I'm looking for with that, so it doesn't mean anything to me. It also has a camera added into it so you can take pictures, a flashlight button (that doesn't even use my actual light, just turns the screen white), an audio recording button (which can be fun to use), and a "night" mode, which turns your screen a dark red. There is also a tab which shows the time and date of all the past recordings you've done, along with past blips on the radar (and how close they were), and past words that have been said. The Connect app is cool if you're really wanting and/or trying to catch some activity, but if you don't really care all that much, this version will be fine. Only reason I gave it four stars is because I'm not 100% sure it's legit. Download it and see for yourself if you believe it to be real or fake.**Please note: The Connect version of this app requires it to "warm up" before getting accurate readings. Meaning it has to take a bit (I'd say it typically takes about 20-30 minutes to warm up) to adjust to all the surrounding noises before any of the readings could be considered legit. There are no lights on this app to show whether it's warmed up yet or not, (there's a red, yellow, and green button on Connect that indicate how warmed up it is) but I assume it's the same for this app and still requires warming up. That being said, don't trust or believe the dots that pop up or words that are said as soon as you open the app, there is a high probability that there is nothing paranormal about these. On an ending note, it is said that putting the scan frequency on the "Low" setting gives you more accurate readings as well, as it doesn't pick up as much stuff, meaning the stuff that it DOES pick up is more likely something paranormal. However, as the description is falsely put (and as Spudd Pickles says himself) your phone/tablet is not capable of picking up EMF (electromagnetic fields). The theory is that intelligent entities can pick up on the fact that they can influence words on your phone, or show themselves through it. Your phone does not and cannot pick up EMF signals however.

column2: This really works with IPhones!  No hassle or hardware.
column3: I have tried sever of these mirroring apps including the internal app on my Samsung 72”TV and for whatever reason I could never get it to work with I phones.  This is the first one that literally mirrors your phone screen.  ChromeCast  works for things that have casing ability but not showing movies and pictures on your phone.  Any video on the web or Facebook is exactly mirrored on this app.It does require the app to be open on the TV and on the phone but when you hit broadcast within 5 seconds your phone screen appears on your TV.

Maybe? The owners of this company read these? Your revenue model needs an additional stage...you go from free to 10 before a user has had time to deal with screen resolution.  This is a great concept—make it work. Can’t amazon fire help support you at all?

(I am actually not clear whether you CAN test the sound in the trial, because that’s how quickly it went by.) So I foolishly paid the $9.99 for the full version. Did the sound work then? I’ll never know! Because once I input the activation code, I could no longer get the screen to even mirror. Just the same error over and over again. column2: Get this if you enjoy being frustrated and miserable
column3: If you're looking to seamlessly mirror content from other devices to your TV to follow along exercise/dance videos, learn a new skill, or enjoy general entertainment on the big screen...this product isn't for you.However, if you would like to be constantly dissatisfied or disappointed, you've come to the right place! Enjoy the frequent buffering and frame skipping of an inferior product that will never be mentioned in the same breath of a ChromeCast, Apple TV, or Firestick. But who values reliability and quality anyways? Being constant is dull. AirBeam TV keeps things FRESH by spontaneously throwing in wrenches into your streamed content. This app will take your favorite videos and movies, and mindlessly chop-and-screw it until it devolves into a hot/disheveled mess that once resembled your original content. But hey, everyone loves a good remix. Remixes are awesome and always better than the original!And if you enjoy horrible customer service, you can always count on AirBeam TV to not be there for you. If you had questions or comments about the product, but are repulsed by the thought of talking to a human being, AirBeam TV will gladly send you through an infinite loop of automated responses while deferring all blame to the user. It's not enough that I've restarted my computer and modem, closed all other extensions/applications, and checked the internet connection of my TV...I probably need to give up my left kidney and bladder too for my video content to be streamed without a hitch.AirBeam TV's connectivity strength and resolution may be inconsistent, but your disappointment with the product will remain constant over time!

App works just fine. You need to download the app *both* for your FireTV or Fire Stick, as well as a .dmg file for your Mac.  Once both are installed and running, and both your Mac and FireTV are on the same wifi network, you will have an icon on the top bar on your Mac to connect your TV as a mirrored display.The Mac software is a free trial - runs for only about 5 minutes, so be ready to test-drive the things you want to mirror on your TV!  See if you like the results.  The purchase price for the Mac license is $9.99.For me there is about a 1-second lag between laptop and TV, which is fine for screen sharing with others in the room.  It's like teleconferencing software in that regard.  I have not used it yet for streaming video, but I have another app for that already.

column2: Get this if you enjoy being frustrated and miserable
column3: If you're looking to seamlessly mirror content from other devices to your TV to follow along exercise/dance videos, learn a new skill, or enjoy general entertainment on the big screen...this product isn't for you.However, if you would like to be constantly dissatisfied or disappointed, you've come to the right place! Enjoy the frequent buffering and frame skipping of an inferior product that will never be mentioned in the same breath of a ChromeCast, Apple TV, or Firestick. But who values reliability and quality anyways? Being constant is dull. AirBeam TV keeps things FRESH by spontaneously throwing in wrenches into your streamed content. This app will take your favorite videos and movies, and mindlessly chop-and-screw it until it devolves into a hot/disheveled mess that once resembled your original content. But hey, everyone loves a good remix. Remixes are awesome and always better than the original!And if you enjoy horrible customer service, you can always count on AirBeam TV to not be there for you. If you had questions or comments about the product, but are repulsed by the thought of talking to a human being, AirBeam TV will gladly send you through an infinite loop of automated responses while deferring all blame to the user. It's not enough that I've restarted my computer and modem, closed all other extensions/applications, and checked the internet connection of my TV...I probably need to give up my left kidney and bladder too for my video content to be streamed without a hitch.AirBeam TV's connectivity strength and resolution may be inconsistent, but your disappointment with the product will remain constant over time!

App works just fine. You need to download the app *both* for your FireTV or Fire Stick, as well as a .dmg file for your Mac.  Once both are installed and running, and both your Mac and FireTV are on the same wifi network, you will have an icon on the top bar on your Mac to connect your TV as a mirrored display.The Mac software is a free trial - runs for only about 5 minutes, so be ready to test-drive the things you want to mirror on your TV!  See if you like the results.  The purchase price for the Mac license is $9.99.For me there is about a 1-second lag between laptop and TV, which is fine for screen sharing with others in the room.  It's like teleconferencing software in that regard.  I have not used it yet for streaming video, but I have another app for that already.

column2: Better than buying an Apple TV, but comes at a cost
column3: This app is pretty impressive. The moment I got it set up it worked like a charm. It successfully mirrored the screen from my iPhone and iPad and I was very impressed. There is an occasional ad, but is mostly a minor inconvenience. Still better than paying $150+ for an AppleTV to do the same function. There is a subscription service to access new features and take away ads, but is not required to use the app. The only downside is the latency between the device and the TV as well as occasional bugs. Granted, the lag could be from my WiFi, however it seems as though some days it responds immediately and others it has a clear latency by as long as a second. For the occasional bugs, every once and a while the sound will not transmit over to the device. The app can also crash at random intervals for no apparent reason. column2: Does not work as a means of mirroring an iOS device to a FireStick
column3: March 3, 2020I was looking for an app that would allow me to display photos/home videos etc. from my iPhone & iPad to a non-smartTV via my Amazon FireStick.  This app supposedly does that using the Apple AirPlay protocol built in to the newest Apple mobile devices.  I downloaded the AirScreen app onto the FireStick from the Amazon website and installed it on the FireStick according to the instructions.  According to the pre-loaded tutorial video bundled with the app, I should then have been able to go to any iOS mobile device with AirPlay enabled and from the ControlCenter, scan for other Airplay compatible device connected to the same WiFi network (which the FireStick was) and select that device and begin mirroring.  Unfortunately the app was unable to detect either my iPhone or my iPad although both had AirPlay enabled and both were connected to the same WiFi network.I then called Amazon Tech Support and spent about an hour on the line with them while they logged in to remotely view my FireStick screen and operate it remotely.  The were unable to solve the issue so the called Apple Support, making it a 3-Way conference call.  The Apple support rep remotely logged on to my iPad and operated it remotely.  Again, no one was able to make the iPad connect with the FireStick.  Since I had already tried and had the same problem with an AirPLay enabled iPhone also, it seemed unlikely to me and to the Apple rep that both iOS devices were malfunctioning but rather that it was either the FireStick and/or the app itself that was the problem.  The Apple rep came to the same conclusion, so she departed from the conference call.The Amazon rep remained on the line and we did some further checks to determine if there were any other problems with the FireStick itself, which there were not.  Every other non-AirScreen related function of the FireStick appeared to be working normally so we all concluded that there must be a problem with the app itself.I had downloaded the free/demo version of the app, which claims to function fully without upgrading to the paid version, but with advertising pop-ups.  I was not going to pay to upgrade until i saw the app work as advertised, which had it done so, I would then have paid to upgrade to the ad-free version.  Accordingly I do not know if the upgraded version would have worked properly or not.In short, this app does not do what it claims to do and therefore should be considered useless for the purpose of mirroring an iOS device to a FireTV device.

column2: not entirely useless but casting is faulty and airplay quality is good but not great
column3: At some point while experimenting with casting from a paid app on my phone that has no ads, an ad appeared on the TV (via this app) and there was no way to dismiss it (see first and second pics).  I had to launch any other app on the fire stick and then relaunch AirScreen to clear the ad (merely exiting to home and launching AirScreen did not solve the issue).(Chrome)cast feature is buggy.  I could only get casting to AirScreen to work from chrome browser on a PC.  Text was readable, but not as good as when casting from Chrome to an actual ChromeCast Gen2.  Casting from any apps on my iPhone which cast very well to a legitimate chromecast did not work at all (see third pic).AirPlay from apps that support it did work, but video quality was reduced compared to AirPlay from those same apps to a legit Apple TV Gen3.  Forcing hardware rendering and 1080p resolution in AirScreen settings did not produce any improvement.Streaming from a media app (nPlayer/oPlayer) via UPNP did work, albeit with the same reduction in video quality observed with the other two methods.All in all, this app is a jack of all trades and a master of none.Finally, the constant prompts to upgrade to the paid version are laughable if not an insult to intelligence,  considering that it's a subscription, not a license, and the cost of one year is greater than the cost of buying an actual ChromeCast which would be a far better investment.As far as I can tell the only feature that purchasing the Pro version unlocks is ridding you of the prompts and grants you the ability to use AirScreen for more than 15 minutes as a MiraCast client - WHILE MIRACAST IS ALREADY AVAILABLE FROM THE FIRESTICK SETTINGS MENU BUILT-IN FOR FREE WITH NO TIME LIMIT (hold down home, select "mirroring").The only purpose I could imagine for keeping the free version of this app is to be able to use your Fire TV to stream good-but-not-great-image-quality content from iOS apps that support AirPlay or from a desktop Chrome browser.  I'd pay a few bucks to own an app that supported casting or AirPlay nearly as well as an actual ChromeCast or AppleTV, but this doesn't check any of those boxes.

column2: Does not work very well in Chrome
column3: I was looking for something to replace (on a Mac) Safari using Airplay to an AppleTV, with Chrome to a FireTV 4K. This app works, but barely, and not in any real usable way.With Safari and Airplay, the video stream seems to get redirected to the AppleTV device, replacing the video image on the Mac with a big black Airplay Icon mask, and the video/audio on the AppleTV is flawless, exactly what you would expect.With Chrome, and the built-in Cast facility, and this app on FireTV 4K, it appears to just capture the entire screen or current browser tab (you can select), and create a second video stream to the FireTV device. So you video on both screens. As opposed to Apple's Airplay that redirects the stream, making the computer do even less processing (because it is no longer displaying the video), the Chrome system seems to greatly increase processing, by continuing to play/process the video, along with capturing the screen and creating and sending a second video stream. I see the CPU use go way up, the computer stutters every now and then, and the display on FireTV is at a reduced frame rate, and sometimes even breaks up getting a bit pixelated. Now, if you have a crazy powerful computer, then all this may work fine, but for me and my older iMac, this doesn't even compare to the Airplay system via Safari. Note that this app also supports Airplay, but I did not try that, and my goal was to switch to Chrome gaining similar facilities to display on my TV.So, I think it depends on what browser you are using, how powerful your computer is, and what casting/streaming method you need to use - it amounts to try it and see. As for the basic app without any extra in-app stuff, it does work and can be used this way totally fine. It is fairly easy to setup and use, and there are a few pauses when you change streams (i.e. stop and restart casting) for ads, and for no particular reason. I will also be trying a couple other similar apps, to see if they do any better with Chrome. Hope this helps...

column2: For being a free app, I give it 5 stars
column3: I really had fun taking my son's hand drawn home floor design and creating it in this app. It does pretty much everything I needed it to do. The amazing thing is I was able to see some flaws in my son's design that he will update in his floor plan. The app does a great job of showing the length and width of rooms and total floor space, as well as the ability to put in appliances and furniture which gives you a real perspective on the size space you need. The developer is very easy to contact by email and he is continuing to improve the app. I agree with some of the improvements suggested in other reviews, but this app does 95% of what I needed and it's free to boot. For that I give it 5 stars.

Wasn't expecting much with it being touchscreen, but wow, what a great app!  Has furniture, shapes, multiple levels, tons of stuff.  I haven't dug deep to see if there are more items to download, but at this point it's the only thing I've noticed, lacks newer shapes of sinks, etc, but minor VERY minor issue.  We purchased a new home and are trying to get a concept of layout before moving in to save some time rearranging.  Highly recommended.

I like that it lets me design the room shapes that I need, but I wish it would let me change the shapes of the furniture (I.e., a triangular table). The furniture options are very basic, and I wish they would expand those, and it also frustrates me that if a layout is even on three sides of my design, and all rooms in my design are shown as being even, the fourth side or an attached room will inevitably be off by an inch. For someone who is OCD like myself, that is very annoying. Other than that, I like the program and use it often. I also like that the creators have updated it to allow you to put more than one label to a room, so you can label other room areas, such as sitting rooms, or furniture. I also wish they would add the ability to see your designs in 3D. If they would do that, I would be more than willing to pay for the program. Overall, it is a great program, and I have recommended it to others. It is a great value.

column2: What I wanted but comes with many frustrations.
column3: I'm the kind of person that moves around furniture a lot. When I first started doing it I would just move things hoping they would fit. I then started using graph paper to better plan the moving. Now that I found this app this seems like this is the best thing to be doing when it comes to planning out the moving.I would have loved to give this a better rating but there are too many frustrations with this app. First of all don't turn your device portrait style or you'll get blasted with ads. Landscape doesn't seem to show ads, and that's great. My main problem with this app is that it doesn't respond the same way each time. Sometimes I want to move an object and it'll move just fine, but other times it will resize itself instead of moving, very frustrating.Things I do like about this app:-You can measure the room out and all your furniture to your exact measurements.-You can add windows, doors, closets, and "dead space" so you really know where you can and can't move your furniture.-You can put things at angles.-You can save your design, kinda (I'll get into more of this later).Things I don't like about this app:-The save your design thing... Sure you can save it but there's a watermark on it. If you want to save a different size or save the plan without the watermark it will cost you money.-It's not responsive the same way twice. It's very frustrating when you try to move an object an it resizes itself. Now I know how the app works and I get that when the arrows appear it will resize the item but a couple of times it would do it while I was just trying to move the item and the arrows weren't displaying. If you have a small device this would be a very frustrating app to use.-Ads in portrait mode and block a good part of the screen.-You have to zoom in and out a lot if you are working with smaller furniture.-There are no desks in the premade shapes, I just used a table instead but I thought that was odd given that they had many other things including a chair!

column3: Ok, first, you ALWAYS get what you paid for. Free. So let's start there. Second, yes, of course, there are ads. I personally expected that and don't really mind. I've used the app quite a while and, for the most part just exit the ad and move on. Note, other reviewers said they tried to pay more for app without ads and were unable. Oh well.1 other review noted a limit to the number of plans. Huh? I've created about 25 with no end in sight. Another stated they had a hard time controlling room and furniture size. Room size is easy, there is a "click" control in the settings feature. Just turn it off. Play around with this and you'll see, it's hard to explain but it locks in certain sizes if you have it turned on and is VERY helpful if you are creating multiple variations on a floor plan on the same screen. It's EXTREMELY easy to turn off and back on this feature. As for furnishing sizes, yes, I find it frustrating too to put a small chair in my plan and, when moving it around the room, it somehow decides to increase in size and I can't decrease it. Plus, I'd like to have smaller things in the room sometimes than 2" and nothing in the menu is less than 2". But it's not that big a deal.In general, I really enjoy playing around with this program. I don't really understand one reviewers complaint about saving with a "watermark" (the only free way to save). I haven't personally found that to be a problem. My guess is? Simply that there is no privacy on a wifi type device and these free programs. Again, what do you expect? My plans aren't copyrighted but, frankly, why exactly would I care? I'm not an architect and these are just basic sketches of possible floor plans. If they were ever built, I could care less if someone "stole" them. One section is my idea for "homeless" cabins. Steel ALL you want as long as you help the homeless out. Great idea!Have fun and you will enjoy. Think it's private or professional or perfect and you will be disappointed.

Excellent application - we have been using it to draw up a floor plan in preparation for selling our house, and the integration with our Bosch PLC laser distance meter is really good. Draw a rough outline with all the bits of nooky-cranny wall you've got in a room, tell it to measure, and it shows an outline for each wall to measure, you use the laser meter to do the readings and it adjusts the floor plan of that room for you. Super easy, well put together.A small gripe is the stairs. It is difficult to see on the plans whether a set of stairs are emerging from the floor underneath, or going up to the level above. Be very useful to be able to mark this in some way (i know there are conventions for doing this on floor plans with estate agents and whatnot, and while i realise that be different in the 3D mode, being able to mark this somehow on the 2D plan other than just adding a label would be good).As a suggestion for improvement: Being able to select a bunch of bits and creating a new level out of them would be very useful (as well as selecting multiple bits and moving them around). Ran into this because i was a silly person who made the entire plan on one level before realising that wasn't possible, which turned what i thought would be convenient into something that was less so ;) My fault for not checking, but i think it'd be useful anyway.And a useful actually-new-feature for our purpose specifically: Being able to do ground plans, not just floor plans. We have an unusual layout outside our house, which i wanted to draw a plan of as well, but this app only does internal layouts. As it is called "Floor Plan Creator" though, it is understandable that an arguably tangential feature like something that is outside of a house isn't included, but again, thought it might be good for the author to know the desire for the feature exists :)

I got into a habit of watching the NFL Playoff games via Over the Top (OTT) devices such as Roku and Amazon Fire TV.  As someone who has gotten very familiar with OTT technology over the years I decided to test the Fire TV’s version of the CBS Sports app for Super Bowl 50 seeing as it was newly released and I figured that there would be a decent test in terms of traffic with a significant portion of folks watching the game via the app to have a chance to see the good and the potentially not so good of the app as compared to watching the game via CBS on my satellite dish.Beyond some delay issues in terms of what was going out on the live CBS feed on my satellite dish compared to the feed on my Fire TV, there were no issues at all streaming the game from beginning early on in the pre-game show right until the feed was cut off with an advertisement for CBS All Access featuring Stephen Colbert.  I was surprised given that the app for Fire TV is new how well it held up during a period where I’m sure there were many watching via the app across multiple platforms/devices, but it streamed perfectly.  Highly Recommended.

This app for me is a 1 star and I would rate it lower if I could. CBS needs to catch up with its competitors and show live TV. column2: FOX: fix the FF and REV!

column2: It has stereo audio only, like it's 1975 or something.
column3: I got this for both my AppleTV4K and my Amazon Fire Stick 4K to see the Super Bowl in higher rez (1080p/60) with less compression than the overly compressed 720p garbage Spectrum Cable spews out. For whatever reason, it didn't work worth a damn on the Fire (unless you consider sub-VHS quality and constant freezing to be OK), and on the AppleTV4K, where it looked fantastic, it went less than 15 minutes before it crashed. I suspect the servers had far more traffic than Fox and whomever they hired to do the streaming expected.However, the MAJOR disappointment was that the audio on both hardware platforms was 2 channel stereo. Despite the highly compressed video performance, at least Spectrum had decent 5.1 surround audio. I wound up just watching on Spectrum Cable.I would not have even written this review except that I noticed the stereo audio a few days before the big show, and contacted Fox Sports tech support to ask why, and they couldn't make up their minds while I was on the phone whether to just be condescending, or condescending AND rude. As a television engineer (now retired) for 45 years who knows exactly what he's talking about, it was like dealing with the DMV without the warmth you get from the DMV.Seriously, Fox Sports, hire some competent support people and then train them to be less snarky, especially when someone calls to ask why the outfit handling the Super Bowl stream is only capable of two channel stereo. And get whomever is writing your apps to understand that two channel stereo is what you get from the local PBS side channels, not a major event where I KNOW (because I talked to the guys in the truck doing the feed) that they were being handed 5.1 audio from the site.

column3: Sep 30, 2017 **UPDATE**I committed to cutting the cord over a year ago, and obviously the biggest drawback is Live Sports. My original frustration with this app pushed me to delete it, but today gave it a second chance (for a specific CFB game). Whatever update they did between then and now seems to have addressed any issues so I bumped it from * to ****. They fixed the constant need for authorization upon closing the app, the stream quality no longer clips audio (though certain graphics do cause short buffering), and they apparently have deals worked out with PAC12 Network allowing streams of 'some' of their games.Most of all, I was amazed at how well the PIP, Split screen and Mosaic features worked for watching multiple games. Easy, intuitive and seamless streams that are perfect for a Sat Afternoon of College Football. Aside from WatchESPN this turns out to be the best streaming sports app. The only reason it isn't a perfect 5* is the somewhat limited amount of live streams to choose from. The ESPN app offers all games on ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNNews, ABC and ESPN3 gives you games that aren't even broadcast. You can even tune in to the raw feeds of "Sky Cams" for certain games if you want a different perspective.Thanks to Fox Sports Go for updating this app, and it has been added to my favorites list. If you enjoy sports its a must have.*ORIGINAL*Decent quality app with a clean UI. HD Stream quality is okay, with occasional audio clipping. HOWEVER it requires activation/authorization FAR too often.If you plan on leaving this on the whole time... You're fine. But if you exit out of the app to watch something else and come back to it, expect to pull out your laptop/tablet to reactivate every. Single. TIME.It has required "Activation" FOUR TIMES in the last 24 hours. Four star app if this is ever fixed, but as it stands it is nearly unusable and not worth the continuous hassle. I restarted it and it took forever to fast forward back to where I was in the broadcast (10 or 15 second bursts to mover forward or back). Can't hold a button or make it go 2x, 4x, 8x speed to catch up. What a joke!!! Finally made it back there, but the video would freeze over and over through quarter 3 and I finally gave up with 10 minutes left in the 4th quarter. Thankfully, my team was winning handily and I didn't need to really watch the end.

The app is decent, but needs a lot of work. I have found that with many of these channel apps (ABC go, CWTV, etc.) the structure is missing certain things. While the app itself is organized in an easily followed format, I find that it is very unresponsive sometimes. If you try to open the app and click on a show, then an episode, and then play too quickly, the app has a chance to freeze and crash; like a lot.Overall if you missed an episode and need a way to catch up, the app is nice, if you can get past the freezing. A perk that is included is one episode unlock: meaning if you do not have cable or satellite and want to watch a current episode (You have to wait a week for episodes to be released). then you are able to watch one.

column2: Frequent channel buffering and pixelated video
column3: I was pretty excited when I first tried Fubo TV.  They have a wide selection of channels including the local sports channels I no longer have with my limited cable lineup.  Unfortunately, during my free trial period I experienced a lot of problems with the video being pixelated.  I thought it was just one channel, so I switched to the Weather Channel.  It worked well for a while, but then began to do the same thing.  This issue occurred while at my vacation house.  When I got home I installed the app on my Amazon TV.  There were no pixelation issues but no matter what channel I watch, at some point the video freezes and buffers.  This some times only occurs for a few seconds and other times I have to close and re-open the app.  It's too bad this channel doesn't appear ready for Prime Time.  I was looking forward to consolidating my video on Fubo and getting rid of Hulu and Sling.  Looks like at the end of the month I'll be getting rid of Fubo.

column2: One of the best options for streaming TV
column3: Let me start by saying that like many others I became a cordcutter due to frustration with ever-escalating cable bills. Plus I was already spending money on Netflix, Hulu and Amazon Prime so literally thousands of shows and movies available but still wanted a decent option for viewing live broadcasts and cable channels when away from home, which the cable company didn't provide. Therefore, when I initially cut the cord and returned my cable box and TiVo cablecard, I spent several months with DirecTV NOW, and also trialed the live tv options from Hulu, Sling, YouTube and a few others as well and either had issues with the interface, the channel selection or the price.fuboTV provides a robust assortment of channels and was the only option that provided access to local NBA coverage within the base package (which is priced at $45 and depending on which promo you get may be discounted for the first month or two). With the competitors, local NBA coverage was either unavailable or a paid upgrade.The image quality is superb, sharper than any image I've seen before as they broadcast in 4K. However, perhaps due to the speed of my internet connection (20mB/sec), oftentimes the image will be pixelated for a second when a program is initially loaded. I love the fact that I can watch on my Firestick, my phone, my laptop from anywhere and DVR the programs I'm viewing.In addition to viewing live tv, fuboTV provides an EXTENSIVE library of current and past TV shows (both from the major networks and cable channels) and movies that you can watch on demand, very similar to Hulu. Most of the TV shows are popular shows but some have are very good shows that I had never heard of before. Prior to last week, you couldn't type a title to search for a program or movies on the Amazon app, only browse alphabetically. Now that you can search on any device I'm a happy camper and I love being able to watch programs on any device. Also, if you need to login to an app such as CNN or SYFY, fuboTV is on the listing of supported cable providers.I have two minor quibbles:1. The standard DVR recording capacity is just 20 hours and it's $10 to upgrade, which gets you 500 hours of capacity. If they had an option in the middle for $5 I would go for it but as my objective is to save money versus having cable TV, I'm good for now.2. When you first open the app it will feature sporting events playing currently or later in the day and you have to make a few extra clicks to get to the program guide. Typically they will feature soccer games and as I'm not a big soccer fan I could do without this and would prefer an option to load the guide by default.

I purchased this so I'd be able to watch the Olympics in my room as I only stream TV in my room. I also wanted to evaluate it as a possibility of eliminating my satellite TV as it's cheaper. If I didn't want to try and finish the Olympics I would have canceled it on the first day! It has continually buffered. It seems to want to buffer 3 to 4 times a minute most times just long enough for you to miss something! It also locks up all the time. In addition it will sometimes give me the message that I have to many connections, which would be remarkable since I only have it in this one TV and no one else even knows I have it! Explain to me how a single connection can be to many? In short.... Absolutely horrid service!

Terrible app and service.  The only one I have ever experienced that was worse was SlingTV.  Both buffer constantly, freeze, and require reboots often.  I ordered this to watch NBC Sports Network so I was seeing all the 2018 Winter Olympics.  Don't count on watching your favorite competition without lots of interruptions.  I literally couldn't watch a single Luge run (all under one minute runs) without it buffering at least once if not more often.That's truly pathetic.  We have a stable and speedy connection and have no issues with amazon prime, netflix, youtube, and a myriad of other streaming types of content.If you're looking for a streaming service app, this one is a real drag.  Don't subscribe to these folks...  Run, don't walk away...

column2: Best value of all the Streaming services we tried.
column3: Had the absolute least missing channels my family watches vs all of the other services we reviewed, being 2. ABC and The CW were missing. About a week later they added The CW to there line-up. Very good service and quality, 3 available streams concurrent and 500 hours of DVR for $55 a month as of this writing. Hulu was missing 5 channels, ATT watchtv was missing more and on down the list they went. Almost none of them other then ATT and Hulu carry ABC since ABC is a Disney Property, and they want you to use their services. Not happening. The only downside we have had with Fubo.TV was using USA as the commercials (and the service tells you bottom left) how many commercials during the break, it would sometimes play 1 of 5 then 2 of 5 then 3 of 5 then go back to 2 of 5 then 3 of 5 then back to 1 of 5. Playing the same commercials over and over and over. I reported this issue to Fubo. So far no change. Using the USA app ( a cable or TV account like Dish or Direct etc, is necessary to use any APPS solo outside of Fubo), doesn't have that issue, nor amount of commercials as high as 15. Other channels within Fubo don't seem to suffer this bug.  I use it mostly for Netflix or Prime, so obviously no commercials. column2: Random commercials on certain channels are a feature, not a bug
column3: We switched to fuboTV from another streaming service because the other service dropped a key channel for us. The service works well enough, though for a live sports-focused streaming service, the lack of anything ESPN and the lack of alternate/back channel functionality on the remote are curious choices, but something we've adapted to.What really bothers me about fuboTV is their ad delivery. fuboTV has figured out a way to insert ad breaks into live events like soccer, which are generally broadcast without commercial interruption. My issue is that they are using this technology on channels that run pre-recorded programming that already includes commercial breaks. For example, when my kids are watching a show Cartoon Network or Nick/Nick Jr., in the middle of a show segment an block of one or two ads for products not targeted to children (Geico, Red Lobster, etc.) will pop up. The show returns when the ads are complete, but since the technology doesn't pause the underlying program, part of it is lost. Keep in mind that this is in addition to the pre-set commercial breaks in the programs where they will sometime insert local or regional spots over the national spots. I've contacted fuboTV about this issue on a couple of occasions, and while they seem responsive and it does stop for a while, eventually it starts up again. At this point I'm convinced that this is by design.Fix these things and I'll stick with fuboTV. Otherwise, I'm waiting for YouTube TV to be available on FireTV so I can switch.

FuboTV is absolute garbage. The service made watching TV and movies a frustrating experience. Constant playback issues, content freezing regularly and forcing you to restart the app, the inability to fast forward and rewind content... the list goes on.And the best part? They want as much as $90/month for content that has ADVERTISEMENTS. You can get that with Hulu for $10/month — and even that is stupid when there are so many other providers out there who offer ad-free content if you're willing to pay just a little. I have no idea how FuboTV is even still in business.

While I subscribed to fubo for sports programming, I quickly found out that the service uses bandwidth consistently throughout the day, even when when one is logged out of the app.  I quickly went over my monthly usage limit, and had to argue with fubo reps to terminate my service as soon as I found this out, rather than at the end of my monthly service period.  The company also does not refund any of the service fee if one cancels during the monthly service period.  Caution is urged, unless one has unlimited wifi.  And the company would be better served to clearly indicate this wifi usage on its web site, in addition to the fact that it issues no subscription refunds.  That said, the basic package of stations, and the sports programming, are good.

I can't believe how good the video quality is! If I had known this, I would have dropped PSVue a long time ago, especially because we love watching Bruins' hockey games. We can see the puck now! We only get 10 to 12 Mb/sec internet speed with our Wifi connection using the Firestick and the streaming quality far surpasses PSVue. No buffering now. I cannot understand all of these negative reviews. What on earth are they talking about? I was very skeptical to try FUBO due to all of the complaints. I'm sure that most of those complaints are coming from people who either have poor internet service or are terribly upset that they have to learn a new way to navigate their tv service. (paradigm shift anyone?) To be fair, there are some minor differences that may be annoying to some, like the fact that you have to schedule each and every episode of the shows you want to DVR. But DirecTV's satellite service had the same limitation. We became spoiled with PSVue's DVR functionality. Hopefully, FUBO resolves this in the future. We are paying the extra 5 bucks/month for one extra device and the extra DVR space. I am so glad that Sony dropped NESN!!! Thank you Sony for steering us to FUBOtv! Don't believe the BS about not being able to cancel your FUBO free trial. Just set up your account on the web and you can access your subscription from there. Simple. No one is trying to steal your money. I also had one quirky thing happen the very first time I logged into my free trial. I had two audio tracks playing simultaneously with about a one second delay between. I simply exited the FUBO app with the Firestick's home button, arrowed up to Amazon's top menu, over to "settings", down to "FireTV" and selected "Restart". While I was waiting for that to reboot, I decided to click on the help button of FUBO's website. I started a chat session with their customer service. They recommended deleting the app from the Firestick menu and then restart the Firestick but since I had already begun the reboot, I let it finish. I had no problems at all since then. So it was a minor glitch, easily remedied, and customer service was available within seconds! Outstanding, great job FUBO!!!

column2: One of the worst functioning Fire Tv Stick apps
column3: I'm doing a free 7 day trial of FuboTV on the Amazon Fire Stick I've had for about a year now. When I Was watching Dr. Who live Saturday night it woudln't go more than a minute w/o freezing, stuttering, dropping to SD, having the sound go but the picture freeze. My wife thought maybe it was just b/c Dr. Who was live streaming, so tonight we tried DC Legends of Tomorrow from a few weeks ago. It worked much better than Dr. Who, but about halfway through the screen went black but the sound kept going. Then everything stopped. Then it jumped back a bit. Just awful. I'd blame it on the WiFi or Fire Stick but really over a year of so many other services I've never had any problems like this.One thing which did work for awhile was hitting the Options button and changing the resolution to 480p from Auto in the drop down box. It didn't look very good but at least it played after that.I'll be stopping Fubo after the free trial and going back to watching The CW shows for free on The CW app. It has commercials, but it works like it should.If you want live streaming but don't need The CW channel PS Vue seems to be the best service out there right now. Not cheap, but the best experience. Philo is cheap, but the app is lacking. It does work though, unlike FuboTV.
