You have to record ahead of time. No on-demand. If you want to watch, e.g. "La Liga", you never know what game is going to show at a certain time.While living in Europe, we had dazn for sports streaming. That was less than half the price, everything was on demand (meaning you don't need to plan ahead and record) and you knew exactly which game was showing when. Too bad dazn isn't available here.

WHAT OTHERS HAVE MARKED THIS OFF FORContinuing to charge them after cancellation: I am continuing my subscription, so I cannot comment on this.Freezing: I watched the third place World Cup game and had no issues. I watched Leicester v. Man U and it only froze once when I took it to mobile and left the house. A few other PL games on NBC Sports have frozen for a minute or two. But overall, I do not get what others talk about when they say that it is so terrible. Even cable has its moments, sometimes much worse.Bad picture: Looks fine to me. Maybe the first ten seconds aren't great, but again, isn't that true with almost anything?Slow loading: Okay, here I have a hack. When I start fubo.tv from my Amazon Fire TV homepage, a loading circle comes up, often with the fubo background, but not always. It will rarely come out of this by itself. But I have noticed that if I press the back button, it immediately snaps out of it and doesn't take me back but instead takes me directly to fubo. Odd thing, but in the end, it's fine for me.You cannot rewind a live game, the way that you can on NBC Sports apps or Fox Soccer Match Pass, et al: Accurate. Goals may happen and you won't be able to see them if you are not there at the exact time or you didn't record it.MY MARKDOWNSPremier League: You think that you are getting NBC Sports, Bravo, USA (?)--every possible network you could in order to watch the Premier League (aside from the money-grubbing NBC Sports Gold). But you forget the obvious: NBC. It comes with your local Fox and CBS, but not ABC or NBC. I have found articles on fubo that say that with the TVEverywhere app, you can log-in to the NBCSports app with your fubo credentials and it will treat it like a cable subscription. This has not been the case for me. I am not clear why I was rejected, other than a message that said something like "We're sorry, this provider does not have retransmission rights in your region". From a fubo page, it appears that NBC in my market (Oklahoma City) is not carried (while others like Tulsa and tons of other markets are). I have confirmed this both on the NBC Sports site and on the app, where I have received the same message. So if I were 90 miles to the NW, then I would have this? This is not progress. The fubo article also says that I must have the TVEverywhere channel in my fubo subscription in order for this to work, yet when I search fubo packages for this channel, I find no such listing.Champions League: Heads up--I thought that I would be getting TBS & TNT, and the last I heard, the Champions League was moving to this family of stations in the coming year. But those are not actually included. I just overlooked it.How to make this better: NBC sucks. When it split its games across NBC, Bravo, USA, NBC Sports, it could act like it is helping the fan, but then when it puts some things on a platform like fubo and others, like NBC, not, then that's a big pain. It is either mistakenly not considering this or it is intentionally doing this for its own benefit to make things like this more cumbersome for the consumer, hoping that they buy something like fubo/sling and cable on top of it. I look forward to when NBC and others catch on to how they could make even more money by making life easier for the consumer rather than harder. After all, I hardly watch American football at all anymore. Everyone can turn you off.But what does that mean for fubo? I would like to see fubo make it easier to see NBC, or to at least have my questions answered. It knows that I want to see the Premier League. So list every game. When I click on it, tell me that it is on NBC Sports or Bravo, which I have, and take me there. If that particular game is on NBC Sports Gold, tell me that, and maybe NBC will pay for that ad. If it is actually on NBC itself, then give me a brief and clear instruction on how to watch NBC, and if I cannot, then please tell me why.I also don't find the guide that helpful. I prefer not to look at what is on TV currently because by the time you scroll through all your channels, if you want to go back up to the top and watch something that you saw up there, it takes so long just to get up there. I wind up perusing just the networks, where it lists them in rows of four, which allows me to scroll through to the channel that I want faster, if not the exact programming.WHAT IT GETS RIGHTI watch mostly BBC World News, HGTV, and sports-related channels. The Fubo network is pretty good--kind of like ESPN classic for soccer, but without actual game film. It also has Bein Sports, which has worked well the few times that I have watched it so far. The website is also pretty good.OVERALLIt does great with giving access to French and Spanish games via Bein Sports, which is nice. However, it offers access to only roughly 1/2 of Premier League games, due to some being on NBC itself and some being on NBC Sports Gold. And it does not offer Champions League games in English at all, although worldsoccertalk.com appears to say that I could watch Champions League and Europa League games in Spanish on Univision, which is on fubo. I don't have a problem with that if it will really happen. But what I want to see is an option where you can click on the sport and then the competition; it does have this, but if I am to judge by that, then that points out a few things: (1) No Serie A; (2) No Champions League or Europa League; (3) just 5/10 Premier League games on this particular weekend.As a stand-alone service judged compared to cable, I am pleased with this. It doesn't give you everything, but it does give you some international soccer extras and things like CBS Sports. Comparing to something like Sling, it appears that Sling wins on your regular cable networks, though they are comparable. But if you are really a big soccer fan, understand that you are basically comparing Bein Sports + $10 to TNT/TBS & ESPN, aka La Liga and Ligue 1 to the Champions League and whatever soccer ESPN offers. If you care a great deal about Mexican and South American games, then that will push up fubo in your eyes.

column2: All the Sports - Time Blocks May End Your Viewing
column3: Absolutely every sport you can imagine is on Fubo. No exceptions. Even the most obscure sports were available. Ultimately, we discontinued use of FuboTV for one reason. Each game or event has a specific amount of time. Until the program starts, you can't select it. When the time ends, REGARDLESS of whether your sporting event is finished, the stream stops. Period. No saved recording, no continued watching, it's just done.We switched to YouTubeTV and found we had none of the same issues. Sport options are severely diminished, but if you're looking for something that will stream all major football games, YouTubeTV is the way to go.If you're into Soccer/Cycling/F1 Racing/etc, Fubo is way better for you, but may result in missing the last parts of a game.

column2: Missing ESPN, but excellent enough you may not care
column3: Superb picture quality and audio quality. I have Verizon FiOS gigabit internet. The Roku version of the app is the superior version, with the ability to watch television in background as you surf the guide at the lower portion of the screen. There's also a regular vertical guide. Sling and Philo have picture-in-picture capabilitiy on mobile. Fubo TV does not. PS Vue does not, but is ending January 30th, 2020 anyway. Despite the lack of that little mobile convenience, Fubo TV mobile is superb in picture and audio quality. Fast & fluid. Same experience as on Roku and Amazon Fire stick. Can not speak to the experience on PC. Had no interest in that. Incidentally, the experience on mobile, I was making reference to the Android version. On Roku & Firestick 4k I don't like that sometimes I have to back out to another menu to get information on a particular program. But then it is only a few clicks away. Nitpicking. With the glaring omission of ESPN, almost every Sports channel that you could possibly imagine is there. So I will be supplementing this service with a base package subscription to Sling, which carries ESPN. YouTube TV does as well, but I don't desire a full package with YouTube TV. The base package on Sling is cheaper, and I only need the ESPN channels.  Awesome service that is equal in quality and in some ways surpasses that of YouTube TV and the others that are more popular like HULU Live TV. Those are also excellent cord-cutting alternatives, though. So choose the one that's right for you. I've made my choice. Hope this helps.Oh, and Fubo TV I understand is the only live streaming service that has 4k resolution built into the app. I have a TCL & Sony Bravia 4k TV's, and I can attest to the superb picture quality on both using the app. Thanks for reading!

I'm stunned by all the negative reviews for this service. I've run the gauntlet of streaming TV services. PS Vue, directTV now (AT&T TV NOW) sling tv and hulu + live. By far Fubo is the best I've had for many reasons. The best thing I'll say for fubo is this is the one I've had the least buffering with and I mean by a long shot. All of the other services were at times completely unwatchable. I've only had fubo buffer on me a few times for like a few seconds and never more then once in a night of viewing. Plus it's got the best channel lineup of any. The picture quality is noticeably better then the others I've had as well. It is a little pricey but still much cheaper then traditional cable.

column2: Cable company like channel bundling and laughable DVR concept
column3: Everybody hates cable companies and their practice of forcing customer to pay for bundles of channels just to get one or two that they really want. Now with fuboTV it seems they are trying to extend that practice to online streaming. All I want is the cycling channel but fuboTV requires me to signup up for their fuboPremier bundle (at $34.99/month) just to be able to add cycling channel (another $8.99/month). You'd think that with a demise of cable industry they would have learned their lesson.Second, their concept of "DVR" is laughable. With all the past shows stored on their servers (in the "cloud") - why is it that I need to actually mark future shows to record? Why can't I just go and watch any past episode that I missed? What is it, year 1998? Seems like another attempt by cable companies to screw up their customer and make it as hard as possible to get what I want.

I was on YouTubeTv, but wanted the Weather Channel and since Fubo was the same price, it would have been a plus. However, Fubo had too many cons. First, and most importantly, the forward button did not show images as it moved forward so I never knew where I was stopping; the ball on the progression bar was jerky - moved forward, then jerked backward then to the spot I wanted; and you had to push an extra button to get to the progression bar to begin with. Then, too many shows were incomplete - leaving seasons completely out. How can you watch season 3 if you haven't seen season 1 - you lose the whole premise! Then, unlike YouTubeTV where you could jump up to the season number and quickly go to a certain season, you had to pan through every show to get a previous one. I knew in the first day of the free trail that YouTubeTV was better.

column2: Fubo is Poor Service or No Service!
column3: Fubo was a mistake! Thought I would be able to watch the Super Bowl however it was only available in Spanish ( commercials were English), had to place a call to them 3 times then finally was on HOLD for nearly 25 minutes just for them to tell me the "English" version was not available to my area. This wasn't the first issue with them, I am disgusted with Fubo, save your money because Fubo IS NOT worth the fee they charge. I subscribed but as soon as my subscription comes due I will be cancelling. No Super Bowl for us.. READ the reviews available on google, Don't waste your money on Fubo

column2: ... the 7 day trial - I can log in fine on my laptop
column3: I just signed up online for the 7 day trial - I can log in fine on my laptop. Using the app on Fire TV however, it keeps saying incorrect password even though I know the password is correct (I rest it and can see it on my laptop). If Fubo wants to compete with other streaming services it needs to be more user friendly. For me, FuboTV is not worth the effort to see if I would switch from Sony Vue to this.

We have used this service for the last 5 months.  The attraction was getting Redzone, that being said the quality of the broadcasts are poor at best.  We have a 1g Wifi plus the smart tv is connected via Ethernet.  The ability to navigate the home screen with Samsung remote is not intuitive at all.  It doesn’t matter if you record or watch something live, the app seems to buffer excessively.  Watching the Super Bowl put us over the edge.  The picture was highly pixelated and images were indistinguishable.  As soon as our month is over, we are done.  Very disappointed. And it is not cheap.  We are going to do Apple TV.

We’ve been using Fubo for about a month and love it! We dropped DirecTv (pretty difficult to do) as the price was getting crazy. My son is a huge sports fan and the fact that Fubo has ATT Sportsnet was the clincher. It’s the only streaming service that has it. Otherwise, it’s only available with DirecTv or a cable provider.The price is a bit higher than I wanted to pay but it’s half of what DirecTv was charging and about 2/3 of Suddenlink’s cost. The interface is different, as they all are, and you have to get used to it but it’s not difficult at all. Have had no problems with scheduling or watching recordings. The “guide” will be similar to what you’re already using and is easy to navigate. It has tons of sports channels and most news options are available. For some reason, CNN is not available if that’s important to you. We’ve had no technical problems like buffering or anything.So far, we’re extremely pleased with Fubo TV and highly recommend it. Give the free trial a whirl and check it out. You have nothing to lose and it may just meet your needs.

this app is terrible on my FireTV Stick.  90% of the time i try to start watching one of my DVRed shows, it just kicks me back out to my DVR list.  also i have to force quit the app a lot because it gets stuck on a black screen.as for when i'm actually able to watch a show, it works okay.  the resolution isn't as good as i was hoping; it's only 720p which doesn't look great on a big screen.  and there are lots of gaps in my DVR recordings.  it's almost as if someone is periodically hitting a "30 second skip ahead" button or something.  will not be renewing my subscription when my trial runs out.

column2: Great for hockey fans but needs work on buffering
column3: I love this app because I didn’t want a cable package but wanted to be able to watch the Devils this season. Fubo is the only service that includes MSG and has an app on the FireStick. Since this review is on Amazon and about the app I will make it about my experience with the FireStick app.It’s great, when it works. I experience significant buffering and skipping, sometimes all out freezes that cause me to have to restart the stream. None of my other apps do this, so I have to lay the blame with the app. This can be incredibly bad when watching an exciting game and you get a freeze right as a big play is being made. So while I have been pleased with the service on ChromeCast and on my iOS devices the FireStick app needs some work.

column2: This is absolutely the worst product out on the market today
column3: I bought this service and cant log into my account using my firestick. I have searched all throughout the internet. I have changed my password 3 times hoping that would help. I deleted the app on my firestick and re-downloaded the application onto my firestick and it still doesnt work. I can log on using my browser. Not my amazon firestick. This is absolutely the worst product out on the market today. DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT it is not seamless, not intuitive and after you spend your hard earned money you will NOT be able to use your amazon firestick to log into the product you legally purchased. For the love of god do not buy this product. It is a huge waste of money, fubo should be working tirelessly, it is the world cup and they would get a massive following if they offered a great product, but they can not offer this product they want to laugh as my brasilian family weeps.

column2: Works great and you can take it anywhere there is decent WIFI
column3: I bought FUBO along with Sling and disconnected from Dish.  I use Amazon Fire TV recast and antennae for local channels. I use the Amazon Fire TV Stick on my home TV.  I  got FUBO because it has Fox News, which Sling does not, and Animal Planet.  I have traveled a fair amount and it works great on the road.  I bring my Chromecast dongle with me and cast FUBO to the TV I am using from my Iphone.  The picture is great.  I do love college football and FUBO has most channels other than ESPN.  Like all streaming services, if you like the channel lineup, you won't regret purchasing it.

1.  Pricing is deceptive.  Advertised at $54.99 but you are forced to take 2 add-ons at signup that increases price to $59.99.  2.  Large portion of the channels air classic TV.  Can get these for free with other apps.  3.  Experienced technical issues.  One time the audio began repeating. Tried changing channel,  closing app, turning off fire stick, unplug fire stick from tv, etc.  Audio continued.  Was like a horror movie.  Finally unplugged fire stick from outlet.  That worked.  Another time both TVs suddenly displayed a message that we had reached maximum devices.  Plan allowed 3.  Only 2 even had the app.  Same day,  little Later, streaming stopped during a live broadcast.  Was 10 minutes before I could get program back on.  Horrible 5 day experience.

I'm currently in the FuboTV seven day trial. Thus far, I've found a few bugs in the Fire TV app. (At least, if you're using the Fire TV Game Controller.) Pause, fast forward and reverse do not work. On the game controller, pressing the "A" button pauses Amazon, Sling, DirecTV Now and Playstation Vue playback. It does not, however, work with Fubo. Additionally, if you exit playback mid-program, there is no "resume" feature. Conversely, playback on a PC has no problems whatsoever. I just much prefer watching TV on an actual TV. (And yeah, I know, I can "cast" from my computer.)DVR recordings are limited to only 10. That's something I can live with because I'm only recording motorcycle racing on Bein Sports. That said, if I was using Fubo as my primary streaming service, that would be a deal breaker.As for image/video quality, there are no issues. It's on par with all of the other streaming services (aside from Amazon with their AMAZING UHD 4K playback.)I suspect FuboTV will fix their Fire TV app quickly, so I'll probably try them again in a few months. They are definitely on the right track, but the Fire TV app is certainly in its infancy.

Buffering issues!! this is the real deal breaker!!!and way to many unused channels that are being counted as "total channels" plus not all content is not HD,If I wanted standard definition I'd get basic cable. Interface is horrible, useless guide if you cannot select channel's from it.I've tried just about all online streaming services, playstation vue,sling,hulu and now fubotv. Buffering with fubotv is nowhere near as bad as hulu but it's a close second, also they advertise 70+ channel's however a lot of these are not being used, it's more like 40-50 channel's.

column2: Flasely Advertised the Eagles vs Cowboys Game
column3: It was advertised on Google search engine that the Eagles vs Cowboys game could be viewed on FuboTV. After signing up for the free trial, logged into the website and could not find the games broadcast on a search on the FuboTV website. I immediately cancelled the free trial subscription and after cancelling, I still continue to get emails about their services and links to reactivate the service. I have emailed them to confirm my cancellation (no response) and requested that no further contacted is needed because I do not deal with any company that advertises one thing and does not provide the actual solicited service. If the game that I was looking to view was blacked out or not available, it should have been indicated in the advertisement. I signed up and provided my credit card for services that were not provided. FuboTV completely wasted my time and after I cancelled the service, I am still receiving emails stating: Your trial is still activeIf you're no longer interested in watching fuboTV and you'd like to end your trial early, visit 'My Account Page' and click 'Cancel Subscription' and follow the steps to cancel. To visit 'My Account Page', click here.I have already cancelled FuboTV and not interested in hearing from FuboTV since I missed watching the game I wanted to watch already.

We do not like this app and will be cancelling. It does fine for live tv but if you try to watch a series it is horrible. When you pay as much as you do for this app and then they force you to watch 7 commercials every 5 minutes it gets old really fast. You cannot pause it during a commercial break either so if you have to leave the room you will feel like a kid again when you have to hightail it back in to watch.  If you pause the episode you are watching it will error out and then 9 times out of 10 you have to restart from the beginning. It will not let you pick up where you left off.  Forget trying to ff or rewind. It doesn't work. Also, if you are watching a series and you pick an episode you have already seen when you try to go back it exits out of the app instead of just the episode so you have to find your way all the back through. There are way better apps for way less money.

column2: terrible user interface, unreliable streaming, slow to connect, lower res "HD"
column3: Boy do I regret believing the reviews on Fubo.  Yes, they have some sports coverage that's hard to get elsewhere.  But it's not worth it.Firstly the user interface is really really bad.  Who designed this thing?  It's clunky, allows very little customization, gives limited information about shows, makes it difficult to change channels, etc. etc.Then you find that it takes some time after you switch to a new channel to get a non-blurry picture.  What?  Are you running this out of your basement, Fubo?And every so often there's an outage.  Unexplained and usually unreported, but there you go, you can't get that stream now.  Has happened to me more than once, and usually right when there was a "I don't want to miss this" event.  I've stopped keeping track.Finally, all the so-called HD streams are really at 720p, not 1080p.  There's one "experimental" 4K channel, rarely has anything on it.Yeah, I've already cancelled my service, just waiting for the current sub to drain.  (Yes, drain is the right term.)  I'm considering Hulu -- it has most of the channels I want, and works well with Fire boxes. I'll miss the occasional La Liga and Ligue 1 and Serie A matches I was able to catch, but I can't justify Fubo for access to the few games I have time to watch.

column2: Bait and Switch on the Free Trial
column3: I signed up for a 7 day free trial of Fubo.tv to test it out using my AmazonFireTV service. I wanted to review the channel lineup and the UI to see if it was a good cable TV alternative. When I signed up it asks for a credit card but says that only $1.00 will be charged. I signed up and moved on with the testing. Three days later I canceled the service and decided to go with another provider, but I had already been billed in full for the month.I contacted support and they told me that I already had an account. I had completely forgotten that 2+ years ago I did a free trial as well and didn't like it. If they had told me I didn't qualify when I signed up I wouldn't have signed up for the free trial. It said it would charge only $1.00 and then proceeded to charge me $45. Don't fall for this bait and switch.The UI is terrible anyway so I would advise others not to sign up. It's very difficult to use and the only good thing they offer is BeinSports.

column2: Junk doesn't work and bilks you after you cancel
column3: This has to be the crappiest app I have ever downloaded for streaming. It froze up every 20 seconds, did not have the BS how's to watch on channels you you pay for, reduced quality picture . Just a horrible experience. This App makes Amazon look bad. I'm still ticked off I paid for a month of service and received about 30 minutes of crashing d streaming. Amazon needs ton dump this app off their firestick

column2: I don't regret my choice, after the fact.
column3: I find the service good.  This change has reduced my bill substantially.  My bill will be $100.00 less per month all-in (that reduction takes into account that I have added services that I did not previously have - add-ons to FUBO).  I did not have the top of the line cable service from my provider.  Instead I had the third best out of four options from my provider.Is it more complicated than cable TV? Change means adjustment to a different format.  The learning curve is not overwhelming.  For those not well versed with changes in TV services I would recommend getting a younger family members assistance to make the change.  I chose to load FUBO via the Amazon Fire platform.  After the fact I found out that I cannot watch HBO on Amazon's platform.  I can stream it on my iPhone and iPad, as it can be streamed on other devices.  That is inconvenient, but not a deal breaker.  Solution, use the Apple TV platform, the Youtube's platform or I believe ROKU's platform.Note: the number of channels I had access to on cable totaled 220.  On FUBO it is substantially less.  For me this was not a problem, as I complemented what FUBO offers me with HPO and Disney (still I have the stated cost reduction).  I also have Netflix and am an Amazon Prime member, which I had before I left the cable service.  I have more than I have any possibility of ever watching.Best part of this change?  I no longer have a contract.  I can switch any or all of the services I have from one month to the next.

column2: Don't bother if you have Amazon Fire TV
column3: Amazon Fire TV implementation is terrible. No entry for "Settings" at the top. The navigation between features is much less useful than any other alternative internet TV offering that I've seen. Like when you press the menu button on Playstation Vue, you see the current show, the next couple of shows, and can switch to the Guide if you want. On Fubo, you press the menu button and you can change the video resolution, worthless. They really need to work on navigation for users with Fire TV. About the only thing that you get for live TV are select, the arrow buttons, and return. I assume the Roku is much better, not going to pay $100 to find out, though. The only plus is that the local stations seem to work well. Not the stuttering that I see on Playstation Vue local channel, or all the myriad of problems with the local stations on Hulu with Live TV. But the navigation with Fire TV is so bad, I can't use it.What I'd really like to do is rearrange the guide to put all the sports channels together at the bottom of the guide, instead of having some at the top, and another group at the bottom. Really wacky the way that the channels are arranged. Some are alphabetical like you'd like (the non-sports ones), and the sports channels are just disorganized.But in the end it doesn't matter. Unless I can find another way to use this app without the Fire TV, ain't going to happen.

column2: Some Problems But No Show Stoppers
column3: I must say from the start that the only reason I purchased this app for to watch the Giro d'Italia (Italy's version of the Tour de France). I use NBC Sports Gold to watch cycling but the Giro was not a covered race. A quick Google search led me to fubotv. I primarily watch TV through FireTV so I downloaded the fubotv app and then subscribed through my computer. I have been using fubotv for less than a week. Based upon that experience I offer the following observations.I am able to watch the Giro as I desired. There are quite a few other channels available but I have not watch any, for reasons to be discussed below. The picture quality is fine and as with all internet apps it is dependent on you internet speed/quality.My biggest disappointment is the limited capacity of the "DVR" feature. While it is true you can "record" shows for later viewing you are limited to three "recording" total. Also, you must watch those recording within 72 hours of there recording, after which they will be deleted. This limitation has prevented me from recording any thing other than the Giro (which is a 21 day race) which explains why I have on experience with other channels. This wouldn't be too bad except the DVR does not provide the ability to record a "season". Rather, I have to go the desktop each day and set the DVR to record the next program (in my case, the next race three days in the future). A "Season" or "Record All" option sure would be nice.Another limitation, at least from the FireTV standpoint, is that you can't set the DVR to record a show from your TV. You can access the DVR to play a recording but to set new recordings you must use a computer. Also, the schedule on the FireTV fubotv app is limited to about 12 hours in the future.Finally, I have noticed that when the app is paused and then resumed there is a lot of buffering time before the show starts again. I don't believe this is a ISP problem as the buffering is much longer than with PBS, NBC Sports Gold, HBO Now or YouTube.Bottom line, I am pleased to be able to watch the Giro "legally". The fubotv allows me to do this. The grips above are really are more observations than show stoppers. With that said, to get cycling with the DVR feature I am paying more than $40 per month. I will cancel my subscription after the Giro is done, not because of the app but because I really don't have any interest in the other channels. If fubotv offers some programming that your looking for I would go for it.

column2: Not worth the price and poor poor quality
column3: Poor quality and takes so long to load. I watched FOX sports North and it only worked for 5 minutes and lost connection.  Went to NBA TV to watch WNBA and same thing.  We watched the first half of a game and after the half time it never came back on until there was 1:00 minute left in the game.  Im on the trial first day and Im already canceling it.  SlingTV Blue with extra Sports is cheaper and more reliable.  DirectTVNOW just added CBS to its line up starting next month (Sept) and all I need is NBC live.  Hopefully FuBoTV will get better.

Good channel selection--I have 100 mbps and high download speeds--or so I pay my cable provider for high speed...do not think I get...as Fubo TV live jumps, shakes....always have to reset/restart to get good pic for a bit--about every few minutes--seemed to work fine for HGTV but not for sports...so not sure about fubo tv live at this time...not sure it is worth full price of $34.99--I might keep for a month--while on special...but if it keeps jumping around, then not keeping--would be nice to watch soccer--so far just used for a NFL game and a HGTV show--if it continues to jump/shake during sports--not worth it.

Fubo has lots of channels and gave me the option of adding on the NFL network.  The streaming works fine on my TCL Roku TVs and the only drawback I see so far is much of the content is in 720p and not true HD. Also 4k content is very limited. Sometimes they broadcast Fox NFL games in 4k. My TCL struggles with that channel but my Amazon fire tv works fine with Fox NFL 4k. With the Fubo app, I can install it on my iphone and all my apple devices so I can watch tv anywhere.  You can even stream it on a Windows laptop through the website.I did the free week trial before I finally selected Fubo as I didn't know anyone using the service so I was skeptical. We're saving about $100 a month by cancelling Comcast's phone and cable.  For the savings, I can put up with the lower resolution.

It has NFL Network and NFL Redzone and apparently a recently added full complement of ESPN channels. I have only been able to find NFL Network and Redzone on FuboTV so it's an easy decision.  It also has NBA TV.I have gigabit internet so streaming and picture quality are great. It also has all of my local broadcast CBS, NBC, Fox and CW channels except local ABC which is not good.  You can also set favorite channels on the guide. At the end of my trial, I'm cancelling my AT&T.The only downside is FuboTV dropped TNT, TBS and CNN so I'll use their respective apps on the fire stick. These are small sacrifices to have have have NFL Network and Redzone. You can get everything else on Fire TV.Disappointed live ABC channels are not available.

I started my trial on this because they advertise you can get local channels without a antenna.  When I downloaded the app and started using it I noticed that there were only 2 of the 4 local channels available so I emailed Fubo and was told that the local channels are only available in certain markets, meaning you need to live in a major city in order to get the local channels.  Another thing is if you there are a couple of things on at the same time that you want to switch back and forth on, you have to go back to the guide to go to the other station.  There is no last or back button to pick.  Stream quality and picture quality are good I will not continue my subscription because of the local channel issue, that and there are a couple other channels that I watch regularly on my Sling that are not on Fubo.  I can get them but have to pay for another package which puts the total monthly bill about $20 more than my Sling.  I will stick with the antenna for local channels.

column2: Everything was working fine for a few minutes then the app crashed
column3: I downloaded this app to watch the Peru vs Colombian soccer match on October 10. Everything was working fine for a few minutes then the app crashed. For the WHOLE game!. I had people over my house very upset at the situation!. I contacted the support team and they said that there were too many people streaming the game and the application crashed. This is not a good excuse! FIFA qualifier games and FIFA matches overall have a huge volume of viewers specially if the game is not being shown on a regular TV network and the application developers need to be prepared to satisfy that need special if people are paying for a membership!.......Now I don't know if can rely on this app and invite people to my watch because I don't know if it'll work.

This was the worst app I have ever encountered. I could never get on. When I tried to get help there was no place to email or contact  the website just kept directing me to their help site. They had a phone number you could call but it kept rolling over and making me choose an option every five minutes. Needless to say, I chose this app to see a football game, and I started one hour early to do so,  and I never got to see any of the game. I don’t even know who to contact to get out of my trial period.Horrible horrible customer service. I will be surprised if anyone actually subscribes to this service.

Our free trial is now over and we plan to keep Fubo basic.  We get all our favorite channels and some that our cable provider charged a premium for. In addition we have had no outages with Fubo in a week, but 24 hours of dead time on cable in the same period. The 1080 picture is better too.There are some nice pluses like 30 free hours of cloud recordings, and two day access to programs you forget to watch. We will save over a hundred dollars a month- I ditched cable this morning and only wish I'd done it a year ago.There are choices in streaming providers but FuboTV was by far the best for our tastes. Well deserving of five stars.I wrote the above yesterday and then read an astonishing number of bad reviews by others blaming Fubo and/or Firestick for buffering problems and poor picture quality. I think these authors are uninformed. If you want to receive a high definition picture streaming live then the critical issue is the speed and strength of your internet connection from your internet provider, not Fubo and not Firestick. Mine is 100 Mbp/s and there are very few obstacles in the way of the receivers. No buffering and a perfect picture is the result. So to those reviewers- I suggest you look there first and get more wifi speed or a good repeater before laying blame in the wrong place. Most technical reviews (like CNET and others) rate Firestick and Fubo as best in class.

got the latest update and this is great!....everything works great....and 500 hours DVR!....they seem to have fixed all the bugs from the earlier app version....and I did spend time with Fubotv support about some of the problems....and they seem to have listen very well.... to me it's well worth the money......and not having espn in no problem for me....they have all the channels I want...and the DVR!.......much better now with this update.....have tried all the others but to me no one beats Fubo....just saying.....

column2: First complete streaming service for my area.
column3: Streaming services take some time to get used to. We are used to instant on. I use Amazon fire sticks for my TVs, which are not smart TVs. Fubo has given us these necessary programing to make the switch from our very expensive cable. This is the first streaming service in our area to give live local programing. It also has a nice lineup of channels and you can add on or subtract. So all in all it is quite a value and has a nice favorites app so we don't have to go through the entire guide to find our most watched shows. It also offers 250 hours of cloud DVR in the basic package.I do find it a little tedious to work with, but that is likely because I don't have the smart TV.

Waste of Everyone's Time.. Don't bother with this garbage Streaming service. I got a 30 day trial every time I go to use this POS on the Firestick, I have to sign in every freakin Time, thats bull.... The channel line up is garbage, the UI is garbage, everythimg about this service is garbage... You want some good streaming service either Playstation Vue or DirecTV Now... But Hey don't take just my word for it, go get the joke of a free Trial and check it out for yourself... I can guarantee you won't like it...

column2: Left satellite company for Amazon Programs and Fubo TV
column3: I had been a satellite-provider customer for over 15 years and was becoming very dissatisfied.  I have to include Amazon in this review because of their great marketing strategy with Prime Video.  Also, if it wasn't for Amazon and showing Fubo TV as a potential channel, I could have missed this channel completely.  After reviewing the shows I was watching through satellite, and doing my research, Fubo provides all of the sports channels I like, my local channels (for real--my actual local channels!) and other channels I watched through satellite.  AND, they have a great DVR storage program and the channels I can still watch live.  I have no regrets; my family can watch their shows without add-on.  Everything dear to us is included.  Great job Amazon and Fubo TV; thank you!  Very satisfied customer.

column2: Cheaper and better than Satellite and Cable with better picture quality
column3: Very easy to use with Smart TV and fire stick. All the channels you could possibly want and many more! Best part is the cloud dvr that you can access from anywhere. We have only had it a week but so far very happy. Plus it is incredibly cheaper than cable or satellite providers without all the stupid shopping channels and garbage fillers to tell you have 400 channels. No contract and all the sports channels are included along with local networks. Actually much better picture quality as well.

We cancelled our very expensive satellite TV subscription. We bought antennas and Fire TV set up on both of our televisions. They canceled BEIN sports on most satellite providers, but FuboTV has 12 BEIN sports channels. My husband has more football (soccer) than he can watch. I get all of the channels that I ever want or need to watch. Don't wait to switch. The antennas are a cinch to hook up. The Fire TV is fool proof. I am very, very impressed with the set up. Our Alexa remote is a universal remote, controlling the TV and soundbar. FuboTV is inexpensive and has an amazing channel line up. Check it out!

column2: FuboTV repeatedly charged my credit card - User Beware
column3: Do NOT use FuboTV! I signed up for their free trial access and canceled the same day because they hardly any of my MLS games. The next month, out of the blue, they started randomly charging my credit card (which you had to give them for the free trail.) There was one charge for $384 from FuboTV!! I emailed their support immediately. They replied that they see the charges but needed my expiration date on my CC repeatedly to confirm. I wasn't going to give them any more CC info, so I went to my CC company to dispute the charges and they blocked FuboTV from any further activity. I can surmise that either they got hacked and didn't want to own it, or they are involved in illicit behavior. Either way, their "support" was not willing to do anything about it, even though they saw the problem. User Beware!

We did a one week trial during the World Series.  It was a little more difficult to set up than expected, but only took about 15 minutes, I guess.  At one point, we were just watching the video, and the stream just paused.  Did a netspeed test on my phone, and we had 200mbps download...stream still paused.  Had to restart the stream to get it going again.  Took about 5 minutes.  Also, the second time we started it up no audio, switched to Netflix and the audio popped in, then back to fubo and there was audio.For $65/mo I would just expect a better interface.  Enjoyed games 5 and 6 of the series, but then cancelled right away.  For the price, definitely not for us.

It kept saying that I didn't have network and yet my other apps like Sling or Amazon were fine. I understand that this happen to many people too. First Bad impressions are difficult to forget.

I signed up for this App to be able to watch the San Diego Fleet football teams games . After going through the process of signing up, when I attempted to watch the home opener on  Sunday February 17 , your App informed me that that particular game was unavailable. You selling point had been that I WOULD be able to watch AAF games .Very disappointing. I will not continue to use this App .David Cameron

column2: Great choice over cable for sports fans
column3: I am enjoying using FuboTV for watching all of my sports (baseball, football, golf, basketball, etc..).  The service is the only one that I have found that includes the sports channels that carry my local teams.  The only reason I did not give a 5 star rating is that while watching local channels like ABC it will skip back 30 minutes or so all of the sudden.  If you are not paying attention you will not realize you are watching a stream from 30 minutes in the past.  You just have to switch channels and switch back and it goes back to a live stream.  I have only noticed this on the local channels like ABC.  I did watch the Redzone channel this past Sunday and did not experience buffering which was great.

I recently moved and have been unable to get suddenlink cable or directv or dish satellite services to provide service at my location (too many trees for satellite and the cable company is a joke, won't even provide a quote to extend service) so I began exploring cable alternatives.  FuboTv has a great selection of channels and it works on the devices I have.  The stream quality has been decent with the limited bandwidth I have (approx. 15mbps) and the picture quality is good most of the time.  I suspect this has more to do with my internet provider than it does the FuboTV service, I will try to update when my speeds get an upgrade in a month or so.  The cost isn't bad, but when compared to other services, it is probably about $10/month higher than it should be.  I WOULD recommend this to others as a good cable/satellite alternative.

For one thing, the least expensive package is $55 and there are still commercials. During the free 7 day trial, I used this to watch the last season of Schitt's Creek before Netflix gets it. For that price, I expected there to be no commercials but there were tons of them. I don't get it. Why pay to watch commercials?I tried to cast it using the app on my phone but the quality was terrible. Using the app via FireTV was much better but the the sound would sometimes not be synced exactly, it would be a little off.I did not use this to watch sports which I understand is their main thing, so in the end this app just wasn't for me.

column2: The most channels Sports and Non - are in this app
column3: I have used Sling, Pluto, Hulu, and a few others - attempting to replicate the amount of channels you would have with satellite, and I am happy to say with this APP I have done it.  On Sling - they advertise local channels but you don't get all of them - with Fubo you do.  Sling you have about 50 hours DVR - here you have 500.  Sling does not have Oxygen, WE and a few other channels that I like and that are included here.Sports - I don't' care - but if you do - there is a ton to choose from.I did only give them 4 stars however for 2 reasons:A.  The volume on some commercials is crazy loud so you have to run and turn the tv down when they come on.B.  There is no continue watching or way of going to the last show you were watching from the Home Screen.  If you are not in your recordings - then selecting continue watching - you would not see anything else you had been in the middle of.  So when I pause and go back into the app - I have to manually search for the last show I was streaming, or watching to continue and have to remember that.  HULU, PLUTO, SLING all have that feature so if you were watching a show 2 days ago - you can find it rather than searching - and that makes a real difference!

I liked the channel line up.  I primarily wanted the regional Foxsports channel (my local teams) and Foxnews, Foxbusiness.After that I wanted the more popular cable channels...USA, TNT, WE, AMC, TCM, Hallmark, History, etc.The initial load time is fairly quick.The FF and REW function works well.I like that the cloud DVR recordings do not expire.I have noticed the picture quality occasionally deteriorates (probably more my ISP than Fubo).I cancelled because I had already signed up with another service.As soon as that service expires at the end of the month, I will come back to Fubo.

column2: Can not fast forward or rewind on FireTV or Roku
column3: First of all pros:1. Better Live streaming quality than Hulu. Last year I tried both for watching World Cup and Fubo was the clear winner.2. Lots of soccer Live streamingThe thing I don't like:1. Fast forward and rewind are not available on FireTV or Roku. It can be done on cell phone or lap top so it is not a technical issue.This is super painful because some of the video on demand sports contents have more than one hour extra recording before the real game start. I have to wait patiently for > one hour to watch a game. On the bright side, they just added "Resume" function recently. Before that if someone accidentally exit the game I would have to wait again. This is very inconsiderate and makes me want to drop.2. No ABC - This is not a blocker because I can switch to antenna to watch NBA, Oscar, etc.3. Recent some of the soccer games such as Woman World Cup by Telemundo are streamed at 960x540 with wrong aspect ratio. Video is letterboxed and players are squeezed short vertically.*Update on 7/8/2019 This issue has been resolved.4. Ads. Sometimes Ads does not work properly. For example, I was watching the TV show Heros, Ads started, indicating it is going to play 4 ads. the first ad played twice. then after the 3rd ad (Xfinity ad with two turtles), it went back to Ad 1. This cycle repeated again and again without moving on. In the end I had to give up on that show.

At $65 a month, I’m not really cutting my cable bill when you factor in internet. BUT I’d rather pay these guys than the cable company who just can’t seem to update to lower prices or offer you less and pay less.We have kids and this is simple to use and has all the stuff they want (“need” lol). Therefore you have to get both if you have kids because none of the kids channels are on the sports one.Give it a try; you won’t be upset.

column2: Too many sports channel but will try for a month
column3: So after using Att TV for a year, I wanted to try another service because Att’s app glitches quite often and can be slow to open the channels at times. I’ve been using Fubo for about 2 weeks now. It has most of the channels that I need but too many sports channel for me. I wish there was a package that did not include so many. We did away with cable in the fall and decided to try Fubu. It did not have one of the local channels that happens to be the one that Judge Judy was on. We adjusted to that by getting a good tv antenna and putting it on another tv. column2: Lagging compared to other devices that are streaming with Fubo
column3: The fubo TV app as a whole is the same across devices, I have it on iphone and ipad and the experience is the same. However, the fubo TV app on the fire stick lags about 20-25 seconds compared to having the same stream on iphone or ipad. Considering that the iphone/ipad are 10-15 secs behind a TV provider like spectrum, it makes it hard to view live sports so far behind. I am okay with 10-15 seconds behind but not 35-40 secs behind. If the Fubo guys can fix this and make all devices have the stream at the same time it would be awesome. For now, I am still using the lighting to hdmi converter and using my ipad to view fuboTV on the big screen.

column2: There's a Sneaky Catch to This Service.
column3: I think FuboTv is a very good service that provides great channels, including MSG so I can watch my Devils lose mercilessly every other day, BUT!!!!! Beware, there's a sneaky stipulation to their service.  You are unable to stream FuboTV on 2 devices at the same time if you are on 2 different wifi networks.  Example: my sister has a house and I have a house.  The home network is my house, therefore if she wants to watch fubo on a roku/firestick/ smart tv app/ apple tv / xbox at her house while im watching it at my house it is not allowed. This rule only applies to TV Devices.  So in that case she or I would need to stop using the firestick to watch fubo and start watching on our phones or laptops.  Extremely inconvenient for people using the same account in 2 different homes.  I spoke to fubo about it and they said there's nothing they can do and it's part of their contract.They need to make it so that we can pay maybe like $5 extra per month to add a TV Device outside of the home network cuz this is going to make me cancel their service.

I tried to cancel before my trial ended, but it would not let me log in. Now that it has charged my card, it will let me log in to cancel. This is a super shady practice. I cannot believe a business operates this way. I WANT MY MONEY BACK!!!There are much better services out there. I would go with SLINGTV. Do not use FUBOTV.

Great cord cutter app for FireTV or Roku. They offer plenty of sports channels but I watch mostly the local channels and news channel. Works great on my smartphone and iPad as well when I am not home, over WiFi. The app seems to always work well never see any buffering (unless there is a local internet issuse going on on - but i find that hardly ever to be the case.) They have a good lineup of channels for the money. The DVR feature works great. They give you 30hrs DVR time and offer more for a fee but 30 hrs for me is plenty! I like how a show may almost be over - just DVR it before it is over and you get the whole show! Nice!

column2: So glad there was a free trial
column3: The interface was confusing to me as a first time user which was a huge turnoff. There just simply wasn't enough value for me to pay $45 every month. column2: Disney apps did not come without a problem
column3: I like the fact that they added new channels in Aug 1 2020, but these new channels still to this writing 08/23/20 are not able to record, nor can you see any past shows on them. You can only watch them live.  These channels are Espn, NatgeoWild, National Geographic, espn2, espnNews, espnU, ACCN, SECespn, ABCNewsLive, CBSN, Disney, disney jr, XD, FX , FXM,, FXX,  They have promised this would be fixed, but this is the second time Fubo has told me that it would be fixed within a week but it still hasn't happened.  I wish their customer service would communicate and update us when this will be fixed.  I will update you when this finally happens.  I use the 4K Firestick.

column2: Problems with receiving channels & out of market games
column3: I tried FUBO tv. I first problem was I could not get out of market NFL games. The second problem I could not get ESPN. I contacted their technical support spent 55 minutes on phone, he could not fix the problem. He said the he would elevate the support call. Did not here back from support. Cancelled service. column2: If you have time to deal with all these inconveniences and miss the sporting events you really want towatch, then this is a good
column3: Not reliable application. Live streaming LAGS during main sports event (Real Madrid vs Barcelona),  DVR records wrong events (requested to record Mexico vs Jamaica, recorded a boxing fight), becomes unresponsive even if application is deleted and reinstalled. When you ask for technical assistance, you are ALWAYS told to delete and reinstall app and to check with your internet provider, contact your device vendor (i.e. Amazon, Chromecast, Roku, AppleTv, AndroidTV, etc).  Most viewing issues or wrong DVR recordings are FUBOTV issues. If you have time to deal with all these inconveniences and miss the sporting events you really want to watch, then this is a good app.

It has great options for channels however most of the sport channels (especially Bein Sports 3,4-10) has pretty much nothing going on all afternoon. There are so much streaming issues because of their servers issues. The only reason I'm so sure about that is I also use Play Station Vue and I dont have that problem with PS Vue. They need more work on their skin and they can make it a little more friendly user. I love the DVR options. But definitely doesn't worth 40 bucks a month.

column2: Almost a 5 star if they had ABC
column3: I would give this a 5 star but a local channel is missing for me as they have no ABC. But they do have everything else you can think of including the weather channel. (Big one for me in Florida)With all the others either stopping their services or continuing to go up in pricing I landed on Fubo. Not the cheapest and hope they don't start to go up, but I think the best out there. My only wish list is they has their GUI set up so you could have more than one profile so my wife could have her own set of favorites and a little more 4K. But all good otherwise.

If you are looking to watch your home team sports you may want to look else where. My wife is from New England and is, like most of New Englanders, a fan of all their sports teams. I was excited that we had found a streaming app that gave us channels that made her feel at home. She even started to tear up when she saw a Shaw's commercial.
