After I kept repeating I wanted to talk to a supervisor the rep put me on hold and came back approximately 40 seconds later to tell me that a supervisor wasn't available. How convenient!

The app sounds great for a soccer fan like me, however there are two main things that make suspicious about this app.First the free day trial seems like a fake because I was charged to my credit card immediately. Additionally, I was charged three times: one for 6.99 the plan I selected, one for 1.00 for no reason, and one for 0.00 that I have no clue why. I don't feel trust in those providers that attract you with offers that are not true.Second, their fire tv app keeps asking me to log in. And sometimes says that my password is incorrect, and then I need to reset it. It seems that my password is not protected with them.I hope they improve their app and their reputation, because the product they say the offer sounds attractive.

column2: I had people come over my house to watch the game and spent quite a bit on food and drink that was wasted. This is what I received the following day ...
column3: I subscribed to the service for the final South American Qualifying matches on Oct 10th 2017. I logged in at game time and 10 minutes into the game the whole system experience an outage until the last 3 minutes of the games. I had people come over my house to watch the game and spent quite a bit on food and drink that was wasted. This is what I received the following day from fubo TV ::Dear Michael,Last night’s outage was unacceptable. You chose fuboTV to stream your games and we sincerely apologize for when we fail to deliver.When we started fuboTV, our goal was to build the world's greatest streaming service for live sports. We aren't all the way there yet. But we promise that we will be. And we want you to be there when it happens.Our team is working through the details of last night’s outage. If you’ve contacted fuboTV via email or social networks, our team is listening and will respond as soon as it can.Every day we’re taking steps to make fuboTV the service we know it can be. We hope you’ll stay with us on this journey.Sincerely,David GandlerAlberto HorihuelaSung Ho ChoifuboTV co-founders"I agree it was unacceptable and a simple apology wont fix it. How about some free months of service so I can try it out and gain some trust in the service?

column2: I loved it and I cancelled it as soon as I ...
column3: I had Sling, I loved it and I cancelled it as soon as I saw Fubo’s list of channels. I didn’t know you guys existed until two days ago. Exactly the package that I need which Sling, PS Vue, You Tube TV, Hulu, Direct TV Now don’t provide for this price.Here are my thoughts on the 2nd day I’m using it. I have 200MB internet speed and a pretty good tech environment at home.Windows version is good.I mostly use, if not all the time Amazon Fire TV. Honestly, it looks like it is in beta version at most.Lots of buffering and pixelation. If you’re based mostly on sports, this is the most important feature. On live games, it worked better streaming on Chromecast from my phone.Stream Quality is not 1080p and 60hz on most of the channelsNot easy to surf the channels. I have to go back to the list to choose another one, when it should be the option to see what’s on the other channels while I’m on the current one.When I go back to the schedule, it defaults to Fox, the very first channel on the list and I have to scroll all way down if I want to go back to where I was previously watching.To make things worse, when I scroll up and down the list and I click the left side of Fire remote, it selects El Rey by default, no matter where I am. By now I’m completely lost of where I want to go.Close Captioning are horrible. 1 - There is no way to personalize the fonts, background etc. Too big and cover good part of the screen. 2 – They have to be selected on each channel and they don’t stay on when I change them.DVR is not available on Fire TVOn live sports tab, I clicked on Germany – Mexico game and something totally different showed upRW & FF don’t work.So, it needs some workSince there is no remote with numbers and no numbers assigned to channels, should be some kind of grouping, same as you have for sports. Sorting by News, Movies etc, depending on what’s on now and the channel type.Internet version on chrome is way better.It should be an option to add favorite channels and to be able to sort them to our preferences. Scrolling up and down it’s too much time consuming.I’ll keep Fubo for couple of months until the next soccer season starts and hopefully things will change, especially streaming quality.If I want buffering and low resolution games, I can find plenty of websites that show them for free.I’m rooting for you guys. I really, really like what you got going.

It's not the best or worst app for Fire TV. The app is easy enough to navigate, but nothing great. The picture sometimes pixelates or buffers.My main complaint is the FF/RW options! Why are we limited to 15 second skips? It would be far nicer if we could do a standard FF/RW. If I'm somehow missing how to do so, please let me know.Update: Added a star since you can press the FF/RW button repeatedly to add skip time in increments of 15 seconds. I've done as much as 3 minutes. I don't know if there's a limit. It would still be easier to have a regular FF/RW so I could watch any interesting ads.

column2: Not the best on Fire TV Stick
column3: I decided to stick with FuboTV after debating between different live TV streaming services, mostly because of their vast channel lineup, as well as being sports-focused (although the lack of ABC and ESPN is quite glaring). I haven't had any issues with the video quality or frequent buffering as some of the other reviewers, but I have noticed that compared to the FuboTV app on the a device like the Roku, the app on the Fire TV Stick is not as intuitive.First of all, it takes a long time to load, not just the app, but even starting up any channels. The circle will spin for a while before streaming finally begins. Another thing I am not too particularly fond of is the rewinding/fast forwarding capability. It's not very streamlined, and you end up going too far backwards or forwards, and have to keep messing around to get to where you want to be. I wish Fubo could implement a thumbnail system like Sling and YouTube TV so you can see exactly where you are in the program when you're rewinding or fast-forwarding. Once you click play, it takes another long time to load.I personally prefer the Fire TV Stick over Roku, but until FuboTV can incorporate a few more features which will help make the service much more streamlined and easy to use, I will use the FuboTV app on the Roku as it is slightly faster and more responsive.

I signed up to replace Sling TV when that service lost the NFL Channel and NFL RedZone. Fubo has both. Although it cost considerably more than Sling, it has a more stable platform that doesn't freeze up or interfere with other Fire TV apps like Sling did. The picture and sound quality have been great on my old 55 inch TV.  Fubo doesn't have CNN or other Warner channels; that's not a big deal for me but it could be for others. Overall, its the best solution for NFL fans who were left stranded by Sling.

Yet another service that throws software together overnight and puts it out to the general public to see who bites. They do not have a customer service department. You can not call them. There is a robot that will respond to emails days later that makes you thinks someone is responding. The user interface is poorly designed and they Do Not care to make it better. Just here to collect money. It is really sad that there is not one streaming service out there that is good today, Not one! It's all about collecting that money!

This is NOT just a sports streaming service. If you are looking for a streaming service that offers Hallmark, look no farther. Fubo offers all 3 Hallmark channels. It also offers the Travel Channel, Discovery Channel and History Channel. I offers live tv for 70+ channels which means a lot for me. It has local channels so when a storm comes I can actually watch the weather and warnings. Unlike the satellite company I had that went out when it rained. I love the streaming service. I have tried others and this is by far the best.

I continually struggled logging into Fubo app from both my Firestick and cell phone.  It kept saying that the username or password was incorrect.  However, I could log into my account with those same credentials.  I dropped it.

column2: Fubo great system needs TBS and TNT
column3: Ok this system is better than YouTube’s system.  I like the split view for sports.  You can watch 2 games at once.  I had the red zone on one channel and the local game on another.Now the issues. They do not have TBS TNT CNN all the channels AT&T own.  They also do not carry my local ABC channel in Charleston SC.I have yet to decide on either Spectrum YouTube or Fubo.  If Fubo had TBS TNT and my local ABC it would be no contest.  CNN who the hell watches it anyways.

column2: Buggy app lowers value of subscription
column3: FuboTV is functional and may be worth it for you if you have limited options to watch the programming they offer.  The app however could use a lot of improvement to make the service more appealing.  My experience has been the app  freezes from time to time when using the DVR function requiring a forced stop to reset the app. Functionality in DVR and in the program guide is weak.  Streaming slows from time to time causing lower resolution.

column2: Good quality, TV lineup, lacking in interface functionality.
column3: Good TV linup available, excellent streaming at home and mobile. Android TV interface is lacking with an impossible to use fast forward, it skips so fast it's impossible to accurately skip commercials. I would also like to see the ability to select stream quality for the sake of saving data.

I would give it 5 stars if it had all local channels  or at least regional national networks.  CBS, Fox and ABC.  None of these can show live shows. They claim to have all the sports and yet I would miss half the college games and all the live NFL.  That made the service useless. CBS is the most important because they have most of the prime time shows i watch. I am not going to wait days or weeks  to view repeats. Hulu's quality is not as good but it has all the local channels.

column2: Very good not excellent but recommended
column3: It's a great value and delivers all the channels that we had previously on Dish and later AT&T TV. One minor problem is the "guide." You scroll thru the channels to the end, but then you have to backup to return to the beginning. Also, the voice is slightly off from the video many times. Lastly, although you can use it on multiple TVs, you can only watch one TV for sports. It doesn't share well. I like it better than Sling with the above limitations. I give it a B+.

I am away from home for several weeks and my home town NFL team played its opening game on Sunday. I googled 'ways to watch' my team play. Up popped FUBOTV. The add said I could watch NFL games away from my local viewing area, which is true except they pick the teams I can watch, and my home team wasn't one of them. Needless to say, I missed watching my game.

column2: App is good, FuboTV's service is not.
column3: Terrible.  I signed up for the free trial to watch the USMNT play in the World Cup Qualifiers.  Feed goes down about 5 min before the match starts and is down until after half time.  Heard plenty of other complaints about how the services tends to crash during big matches.  Their support person running the twitter account seemed overwhelmed and kept suggesting temporary fix that wasn't working either.  They finally sorted out the issues and I did watch the 2nd half of the match on Fubo and it was fine.  Ended up canceling my free trial, so I won't be using this app any more.  As for the App itself, well designed, was fairly easy to navigate and find things.  It ran well until their service crashed.

We got this on the one week free trial to watch the Monday Night Football game. It took the better part of an hour to get it installed and working, only to get an error that said it didn't work on our Apple Fire device even though it was downloaded specifically for that device. We finally had to back out of Apple and go through Roku to get it to work. They are also extremely overpriced for what you get. For the money they charge for their basic service you could get several other channels or regular cable and still have money left over.

column2: Best app for streaming sports hands down with one exception regarding recording programs
column3: I like everything about fuboTV with one exception. I like to record my programs and watch later. However, I am forced to look for my show once a week and set them to record. This is annoying when I just want to watch the entire series of a program. I want the ability to pick the series and set it to record all episodes.Of course the one exception to having all the sports you want to watch is ESPN which you will need to subscribe to separate :-( I would be happy to pay a premium to get this as an adder to fuboTV.

I didn't sign up for a "Free Trial", but somehow it appeared in my Amazon account. Amazon couldn't help me stop the free trial, and it was like pulling teeth to deal with Fubo, although the reps were trying. It's expensive per month as far as I'm concerned (not a sports fan) and I was concerned they would start charging me after the Free Trial. My rating is based only on my frustrating experience and not on the quality of the streaming or content.

They already charged me and was watching a game and 15 minutes later I was disconnected and couldn't get back in. My internet connection is excellent. The Fubo website kept stating to try again later. I gave up. I want to unsubscribe.

Didn't get past the 1st day.  Froze (without exaggeration) every 30 seconds. Such a shame because it was very user friendly, had all the channels we wanted and was affordable but the constant buffering made watching any show impossible.

column2: advertised i would have been able to watch a certain ...
column3: advertised i would have been able to watch a certain game, and i sign up and low and behold, they didn't carry that channel after all.  wont be signing up for this one again.  i don't care too much for sports anyways but wanted to watch a certain game!

column2: This product or app has not worked for me. ...
column3: This product or app has not worked for me.  I entered all the data but it will not load the station, and instead wants me to reenter email etc each time, then says I already have an account.  I am in a closed circuit.  I will throw in the towel on this one.

column2: Sling TV does have 2 main packages (Blue & Orange) and if you get Orang Plus sport Extra you will pay $25 for 44 Channels BUT there is a good point with Sling Orange + Sport Extra that you ...
column3: I am using it for a week. I compared with Sling TV for sport channels, Fubotv does have more channels and you pay $35 for 76 channels, Sling TV does have 2 main packages (Blue & Orange) and if you get Orang Plus sport Extra you will pay $25 for 44 Channels BUT there is a good point with Sling Orange + Sport Extra that you have  on-demand or featured movies choice that you won't find with Fubotv. I am so happy for having all soccer, NBA, football and UFC channels together.Iif someone is looking for basic national channels plus some sport channels then you may go with Sling's Orange Package for $20. I searched and compared Play Station VUE, HULU, Amazon TV, Sling and Fubo Tv, and pricewise $35 for 76 channels and having all sport channels was the best choice for me.

column2: FUBO tv look elsewhere for live TV
column3: It may let you watch NFL just not Monday night football, my local channels were very laggy and you could not watch for more then about 15 seconds or so without a skip in the picture or audio. The over all picture i think was ok and it was very easy to navigate. It was convienant to watch missed shows, and the recorded playbacks were good with none of the above issues. But i already have a free option for that. Im looking for a "cut the wire" live and local channel option

column2: Maybe if you are a sports fanatic
column3: Streaming was fine although a station here and there was blurry. Channel guide operates so you have to go channel by channel.  If you are into sports and especially soccer it might provide greater value. 11 specific soccer channels and other soccer provided elsewhere. I didn't think the cost warranted the channel options. My current cable bill is cheaper and I get HD and some of the more popular channels that are included with Fubo.

column2: Good for sports enthusiasts with eagle eyesight and great internet.
column3: Folks, this is a sports centric service. If you want to watch soccer, this is your place. As well as All other sports.Their navigating screens have very small images of the channel logo. Can’t tell what channel it is on their live guide page.And not their fault, but I have to rely on Verizon for a reliable internet stream. Since Covid and WFH my internet is throttled back by Verizon, so it makes the FUBO service inaccessible at times because Verizon is messing with my internet.

Mu wife and I decided to try Fubo and so far we love it. The only issue we have encountered is not being able to set our Home location but this is due to our internet provider being LTE based. Other than that the fact that you can get virtually all the channels we had with Dish, you can DVR via the cloud and stream to different devices is a huge plus. If you are not sure about trying I would encourage you to do so, it is not HULU but again you do not see the issues with home location you do with HULU.

I signed up for the free week to give it a try, and to hopefully watch the SuperBowl in 4K HDR streaming quality - Fox Sports was planning to stream a high-res streaming game for the first time. It was not that good an image and it finally kicked into high resolution after about 5 minutes, and then crashed midway through the game. I had it going on two televisions so it was not my set. I also have ATT-Now (formerly DirectTV now) and I switched to that streaming version and it played well and looked sharp (I could not tell if - at their very best - one image was better than the other).I discontinued my Fubo service - I had intended to switch to it to save 15 a month or so - perhaps the demands of an enormous moment were too much for them to meet.

column2: BIG thumbs up for customer service!
column3: No ABC or ESPN means fewer stars. I watch a lot of live sports, and it seems that games are anywhere from ten seconds to over a minute behind cable, but that seems common with streaming services.One very important thing that is FANTASTIC is their customer service. Very extremely impressed with every rep I've spoken with, whether it was a billing or a tech question. Knowledgeable, personable, genuinely helpful. Can't emphasize enough how important that is!

Like a strange little 5 second repeat that makes you feel like there’s a glitch in the matrix.  It also will just randomly stop in the middle of a show and say it can’t play the requested video at the moment...try again later.  I have a brand new Samsung, unlimited internet and none of our other streaming services have these odd occurrences.  Also, I wish it had more 4K programming.  After football season’s over, we’ll need to reassess.

column2: Doesn't carry as much as advertised.
column3: I'm sure it's a fine streaming app. They advertised having a college football game I wanted to see. So I signed up only to find out that they did NOT have that game. Won't give my money to a company that lies in their advertising.

We are very disappointed because we thought we could get all of the NY Giants games (we've lost Fox on Direct TV). It sounded like the game on Sunday 9/22 would be streamed, but it wasn't.  We also found it difficult to navigate the app, but that could be our lack of experience.  All in all, we ended up paying for a month's viewing that we won't use and have discontinued the service. In our opinion, it was a case of false or misleading advertising.

column2: FUBO TV has all the sports I need except for ESPN and MLB network
column3: I needed sports and Live TV to replace Platstation Vue.  I tried SLING TV (horrible), YouTube TV, HULU Live, PHILO TV, etc.  FUBO TV has the easiest interface, and most sports channels included.  The biggest draw back is they do not offer ESPN nor MLB Network.  But I access them both through my Amazon Firestick using ESPN app and MLB Network through Firefox browser, both on the Firestick.  It's a little inconvenient, but it's just how it is.  I did the free trial on FUBO and I'm now on my 3rd month after I learned SONY was canceling Playstation VUE streaming service, which had every channel included.  I recommend FUBO.  No billing issues at all.

Get an amazon fire stick, download kodi, pay $10 a month to iptv realm and get 1000% more channels, all HD.  No blackouts on local sports teams.  It's sad that in america these crap companies have to blackout sports forcing us to give our money to oversees providers that don't have to play the games.

column2: I'm ditching FuboTv and going to Hulu January 2020
column3: Both of my subscriptions were just pre-paid for January but I'm getting rid of Fubo on January 24. The product was ok but had issues with subscriptions from day one. I held on for five months now but am sick and tired of when they update their software that I have to go through and reactivate most of the channels that are included. My current configuration is Firestick TV 4K with Fubo and Sling Orange for ESPN. I should have dropped both of these in September and stuck with Hulu only. I have had multiple FuboTv issues with my subscription especially Showtime and wasn't able to receive or activate multiple channels for weeks. FuboTv SOFTWARE IS BROKEN and desperately needs to be fix.

Poor picture,,,,constant streaming delays...looking for way out of my free tria. and it appears...as usual to be "obscured" and hard to do.  OMG.  It is the standard "free trial" trap!  I finally figure out where the opt out was....so I raised the review to 3 stars.  The only other issue I have is price.  I can add the channels on cable/satellite (that I want to watch) for the same price or less.  Value is not there.

column2: Fubo TV gives me all the channels I want
column3: Was using Sling both blue and orange, and Philio to get some of the channels I want but neither included some channels I wanted.  When I tried out Fubo TV, I immediately subscribed to it because it gives me all the channels I want and the streaming is flawless.  I added on the Family option giving me 4 simultaneous streams for extra $5 bucks. Cancelled Sling and Philio which equaled the amount that I am now spending on Fubo TV.

column2: Worst resolution of any streaming service available.
column3: Over priced for the terrible qualify.  Lacking major channels, I couldn't stand the constant blurred, grainy picture.  It looked worse than a 80's home video made by a 5 year old. Not worth the cost. It should be crystal clear resolution not grainy and blurred. Couldn't stand the free trial, canceled. I will not be a fubotv customer.

column2: Fine if you don't have cable
column3: A long way to go before I cut my cable.  Very clutsy interface and not user friendly.  Had lots of pixilation and drop in picture quality.  Support is poor.  NO ABC so my wife hated it.  Some of the games I wanted to watch were not available but I could stream them on my iPad.  Cloud service is basic and problematic -- can't fast forward while recording in session, cant programs until they are scheduled.Thought I hated my cable until this!

Very hard to navigate - most others (Netflix, Prime, Hulu, Roku, etc.) much easier.  Did trial for watching sports & Showtime - my teams NOT available & can get Showtime othe ways.  Can't use DVR for other than sports (not movies, tv)Not a good option all around

We signed up for FUBO mainly because they carry the A&E channel and the Live-PD programs.  They carry local Dallas-Fort Worth channels for CBS, NBC, Fox, and channel 21.  They don't carry ABC.  They carry HGTV, Animal Planet, Discovery, FYI, and several other channels including sports channels. They have a little star on the left of the channel to make that channel a priority, or first on the list.  We like to watch football.  FUBO carries Fox and FS1 where XFL football is shown. Not ABC which is a bummer so we have to watch another network for ABC programs. FUBO has a Guide that lists the channels, and we can even scan over to see what's on later in the day.  They also have the schedule for the next 5 days (I think, maybe longer.)  FUBO has a huge variety of movies, too.  So all-in-all we like FUBO!!

The service is pretty decent. Has most of the channels we need. Others we like we get from Philo. It is pricey though but, it’s still way cheaper than DISH. Then again there are not nearly as many channels (that you never watch) but.Stream quality is good, picture quality is good. Haven’t used the DVR service yet.This service is not I.P. Locked so you can watch it anywhere.

column2: works fairly well  but cannot abide the commercials
column3: For the most part this worked very well, a bit confusing about changing channels and viewing options. It was a wake up call as to how bad commercials are and how often they occur. I will not continue and will go back to streaming without commercials. This is not an issue with Fubo but rather an observation of just how bad live TV has become. Most commercials absolutely insult ones intelligence!

Does not work 95% of the time. If you would like to watch this on your firetv stick, understand that under peak load this app will not even start. When this app does work (games no one is interested in) expect lag, poor image quality, and tearing. Autogoooool. Stop wasting our time FuBaRTV.

The product has potential. It has the channels except for Turner channels. But, it you watch a highly watched sports event Fubo doesn’t have the bandwidth to deliver. You will get several “we’re having technical difficulties” messages interrupting the game. If you call customer service it’s an hour on hold to get a person who knows less than the customer. If you email they get back to you in a week. I had to delete and reinstall the app daily for six weeks before giving up. I was running Fubo on a 2020 Nvidia Shield Pro, the fastest streaming device available.

column2: At least 50% of the time you want to use ...
column3: At least 50% of the time you want to use it, it will error saying  "Sorry. We can't play this content at this time."

Would LOOOOVE to give them more stars but after canceling, they are STILL trying to charge my old card. I have tried and tried to get ahold of someone and I’m was on hold for almost an hour when I had to finally hang up. I ended up having to go to my bank and get a new card and I am STILL getting alerts from them trying to charge my old card. My suggestion would be use a card you can reload.

so i signed up for fubo tv, thinking their offerings for streaming would be a great deal. would be if it actually streamed anything. i got slow to no streaming altogether and then if or when the picture actually held, the quality was blurred and unclear. the selection of shows to watch seemed great. but of no use to me if they don't actually stream. hope others have better luck than i did.

fuboTV is a great streaming service for the avid sports fans.  plus there are other non-sports channels available, so on the down-time from your favorite sports team, there are many movies and TV shows for added entertainment.the downside to this service is the lack of a hockey central channel, NHL Network, whereas the NFL, MLB and NBA to name a few, have theirs on fuboTV..  this is a deal breaker, to say the least, because, you know, residing in this household are huge hockey fans.

I am so happy I switched to FuboTV.  It’s so fast, stream quality is amazing, so many channels with good pricing. I am very happy I dumped cable.  I was using Sling and I kept losing channels and my price kept creeping up.  The only thing I find irritating is when you fast forward/rewind you don’t see a preview as it’s moving so when fast Forwarding in the DVR over commercials you sometimes will skip the show.

column2: not the Answer unless you like missing 4th quarters, 3rd period, 9 innings or 2nd halves
column3: I MEAN 7TH GAME OF THE WORLD SERIES AND IT GOES TO OTHER PROGRAMMING IN THE 7TH INNING. HOW CAN YOU DO THAT AND EXPECT TO CALL YOURSELVES A SPORTS APP FOR FANS? This is a great app if you don't mind the games shutting off in the 4th quarter, 8th inning or 3rd period. On multiple occasions this app just shuts down because it ran out of time and in the most important part of games. And the price of $54 per month, you might as well get cable and you will be looking for other options if you are a sports fan after missing the 4th quarter, 2nd half, 3rd period or 9 inning one too many times.

This is the slowest and most difficult app of the roughly 50 downloaded on my Amazon Fire stick. It also did not offer all of the NFL games I was hoping to watch. I cancelled this option after my trial period because I could not believe how few shows it offered. I kept thinking there was something I had missed. It turned out the only thing I was missing was the shows I wanted to watch.

Enjoyable streaming service that is worth the money. Crisp, clear picture and fast loading. Virtually all soccer and a large portion of other sports except those broadcasted on ESPN. Overall, I am very happy. If I was to complain, it would be about the limitations with fast forwarding and rewinding. Also, a number of shows only have a small portion of their current seasons available to stream, as opposed to all of their episodes being readily available. Lastly, I’ve noticed that closed captioning, although available as an option during shows, does not always work. This may be due to the particular network the shows were being streamed from (in two instances of CC not working, the network was FX both times). The complaints listed are solely for full disclosure and hardly deal breakers for me. The almost infinite access to soccer, choices of network tv shows, and simplicity of the service trumps these minor annoyances.

column2: I had high expectations, but Fubo did not deliver
column3: I tried a free week trial of Fubo to watch Seahawks football games on the east coast. The first game was live but it was fuzzy in the second half and the second game I couldn’t watch live.  When I tried to watch it later, after I recorded it, I had to search around to find it, after I set Fubo to record it, and the ending was cut off.I also watched other shows but I experienced sounds and visuals not matching.  The biggest disappointment is not being able to watch old shows when I click on it. It shows the Fubo air date even though the original episode aired years ago.I won’t be subscribing due to all these issues which is disappointing because I read good things about Fubo for sports. Addendum : had issues cancelling.  Don’t cancel through the website or through email, call!!!

Horrible streaming.  Feed kept losing sound, then freezing, then going to a white screen before sending you back to the fubo home screen.  You have to reset the channel every 5-7 mins.I have fast and reliable internet service and no issues with the fire stick.Customer service only offered a partial refund $20/60.00 USD monthly advanced fee  (which could take up to 2 weeks to come back to me) and to close the account.  They said it could take up to 24 hours for a supervisor to call me back.  Unacceptable.Not worth the money.

I subscribed for cycling events only. I canceled after the 6 weeks were up due to the expense. Somewhere around $30/month. Customer service is very good. They are out of NYC and pick up the phone all day. Pretty easy to get someone.  Each person pretty knowledgeable about the service. Sometimes the missed events didn't show up after the event and I had to call. Its the same transmission as the NBC sports broadcasters. I am assuming thats why the high expense.

The channel selection is great (although having to go elsewhere for the Rose Bowl was odd).  Most channels are HD which is nice but the bulk of the live channels looked like they were shot on film -- lacking in contrast and perhaps a little color.The real disappointment came when I discovered that the sound was, at best, stereo.  This isn't a big deal with talking heads shows but it really takes something out of the experience when watching movies.I like the channel lineup, but the delivery needs to be improved.

column2: What a gem!  I have tried all the big streaming services.  Fubo is the best
column3: Been with Fubo since one of the others announced their demise.  What a gem!  I have tried all the big streaming services.  Fubo is the best.  It has all the channels I like.  It is sports oriented.  NFL games and redzone show first on Sunday.  Many ways to find something to watch.  Can choose favorites.  View by sports, tv, movies, channel, live, demand, DVR recordings.  It is all very easy to find.  No glitches, crashes, or video issues since I have had it.  Can’t say that about any of the others.

I really liked what I saw during the trial but I had some questions that have not yet been answered.  I could not find BBC which is a channel my husband watches all the time.  Also, I have a FireStick on my TV but not on my husband's.  He has a smart TV but I was not sure how to access FUBO.  If they ever get BBC I will definitely use this service.  Everything about it was great!

column2: Don’t trust anything that says it’s free!
column3: Tried to load it with no luck. Got the app on my k fire but it wouldn’t open . Now I have something that will charge me in 7 days that I can’t use . It takes almost a brain surgeon to figure out how to get rid of it! By the way in my surcharges for ways to get rid of it I found out it’s 69 bucks a mouth. If they said that up front my life would of been much easier. Oh well live and learn.

I did a lot of research on streaming apps that provided the most channels for the best dollar when I finally cut the cord with Spectrum. The pros are the channels and I'm happy to see 24 hour horse racing - TVG. Cons are the app buffers all the time and you have to shut the app down and relaunch it.  My internet speed and bandwidth is fully capable of handling a flawless experience but Fubo does not provide it.

I canceled cable and I'm using other platforms for entertainment. I have Netflix, Prime Video, and FuboTV. I had continuous buffering issue with Hulu and I'm running 100mbps/100mbps. Nothing else that I've tried had buffering issues. The only reason I got FuboTV was for football. It lacks many of the command features which cable has but other than that it's okay.

column2: Much better than a few years ago
column3: I had tried out FuboTV a while back and the stream quality, was terrible. Limited options and a very difficult system to deal with even for a cancellation. A friend recommended it a few weeks ago and I decided to give it a try. What a difference from what it was. Great quality. Streams well in 100/mps places with 10b/mps internet. Easy integration with my old fire stick.

Fubo has its strengths in sone sports the other options don't have.  I tried after YouTube tv but ended up going back to YouTube because of better channels and locals.  Using an external antenna for locals gave me a poor quality abc.  I didn't really get into dvr space in that week,  but YT has more.  Menus aren't great.  I could live with this if a better option didn't exist,  but it does.  Im trying to replace Vue, and none of the options measure up, but YT is closest.  I might go back to fubo next football season depending on if anyone else picks up red zone after vue's end

column2: Fubo is a ok service, minus all the glitches
column3: Futbi is a good tv package for the price. My complaint is the streaming quality; we have excellent internet service, and despite that there’s a few glitches from time to time, like you hear two different audio at the same time. I deleted the app and reinstalled it, but that didn’t fix it. Also, when you type on the search bar, it won’t let you go back to the home screen. I feel so frustrated that I might cancel this service.

They should add more channels such as ESPN and then it'd be great. We use it mostly for the local channels but it does have quite a few regular cable channels. I chose this streaming service over ALL the others out there after I tried them all. What I've learned is no streaming service can compete with satellite service but then again it's less than half the cost.

I did a trial of the $54.99 package, which seems to be their base now. The stream quality surprised me as being very good. The picture quality had no issues and the app was very user friendly both on the TV and from the web and phone. But, in the end the price was just too much. It gave local channels not named ABC. It had a lot of sports channels but no ESPN. My recommendation is to have a lower priced, like $30-35/mo non-sports package.

Signed up to get live NFL games, but was only able to access the same game that I can see locally on my cable. Did not give access to other NFL games on at the same time showing in other regions. Waste of time.

column2: Doesn't work with Fire Stick voice remote
column3: Not sure if this is an issue with Fubo or Amazon. I was considering this for my mother with extremely low vision since they carry the local channels but Amazon Fire stick would open the app but not go to a particular channel by voice.  Since she can't read the guide, this is a non-starter for me. column2: Perfect, but with a fatal flaw
column3: I had to give fubo high marks for stream and picture quality, and, really, ease of use is really very decent as well...unless you're into sports and happen to live outside what appears to be line of sight of the stadium. I tell you, the fubo app, menu, DVR, time shifting, all are absolutely superb. Then, if you're a sports fan, and happen to live outside the magic circle, the other shoe drops. Now, hear this: from where I live, just outside Seattle, I get the Seahawks games with Xfinity, Dish, hulu, att now, youTube TV, etc etc. But with fubo, what I get is an "Oops!" display with a notification blaming the NFL for blacking out the Seahawks. Its not the NFL, folks, its fubo going cheap-s*** with their content contracting. The irony of fubo's advertising themselves as sports centric isn't lost on me. The thing about that circle I'm within with every other TV supplier, is that every little bit it extends embraces that many more eyeballs...that just doesn't make sense. fubo was great on the phone until I asked why every other service carried the games to where I live. Since then, its been crickets. So. Try fubo. Maybe you're lucky enough to be "in area". But if you're not, and you ask why, you'll be ghosted. Nice.

column2: Overall Fubo is a good streaming experience
column3: The streaming seldom buffers, picture quality is great, guide is easy to use and there are tons of sports channels. That being said, having all the sports channels is nice but a few of those could of been used for other Network channels, instead of some of the sports stuff most people don't care about.

column2: Freezes a lot.  Have to log in a lot
column3: I like the channels that fubo offers, All my favorites.  The picture is clear when it gets focused.  Sometime looks pixilated for a minute or two.  I have to log back into fubo quite often. My picture will freeze, then I get the circle.  I have to exit out and come back in.  I do have a lot of devices running in my house, but my living room TV that has fubo is the only device that freezes.  Not the video gamer, not the fire stick TV in a bedroom, or the 2-3 iPads that are in use and 4 phones with no drops or freezes at all.  I have 200 mgb download speed and two routers.
They advertise all over the internet that you can get access to specific NFL games but when you sign up, they are nowhere to be found.....more costly than actual cable.

column2: There are better channel line-ups on other services....
column3: I use PSVue and love it. It has a Cloud DVR as does Fubo, which was the main selling point for me. These are the only 2 streaming services that offer that. So far. But Fubo is supposed to be for sports enthusiasts. It's marketed and advertised that way but ESPN is not available. Really? The premier sports network. No Animal Planet, or HBO.The channel line-up on every other streaming service is better than what they offer. Sorry, but I didn't like it.

Stream had constant issues despite internet connectivity being consistent on fire stick.Didn't have the same issue via my phone so a bit odd to say the least.UI is clean cut and simple to navigate but still can't get over how much issues there are.

Paying $44 a month for fubo is ridiculous. It plays the selected channel for about 1 minute before it loses signal and I have to exit out to the main screen and reload the selected channel. I shouldn’t have to do that with amount of money I’m paying. It makes no sense that when it loses signal, it will not regain it again unless I reload the channel. I know it’s not my internet because I don’t have problems with any other devices. Very unhappy.

column2: Higher priced plans and Poor Navigation
column3: I signed up for the week-long trial. I used once and cancelled the next day. Navigation is very poor and not user friendly. Has a good channel line-up, but cost is pushing the limits but now about the same as Hulu Live TV and Youtube TV. Just not willing to pay that much for a not-so-great experience.

column2: Really bad experience with this service
column3: Really bad experience with this service. My 3 first recordings did not work so I missed the games. They restored them 2 days after but obviously I already knew the results. Also very poor streaming quality. I hope they improve with time since the selection of sports event is best in market.

I wish i could give it 0 stars. The only reason i am sticking with it for now is because the competitor does not have more channel lineups.Every live game across all networks buffers. There is no buffering when i use the Fubo tv login credentials on the channel itself ( nbcsn for example).My internet speeds are more than 200 Mbps so that is not a reason for buffering.

I really love Fubo.  So easy to download the app and immediately start watching after making your account.  For the price I get a lot of channels as well as a lot of recording hours.  I can also use on all 3 of my TV's at the same time as long as I have a Firestick on each TV.

I enjoyed this service, but in less than a year, they're raising the price $10/month for channels that don't interest me. I am ending my subscription this month as the price is more than my DirecTV used to charge me. Very disappointed and unable to get any response over the phone or via email to customer service. If you sign up now, your cost will increase in August by $10.

This product is not as cheap as it once was however I do have a lot more channels. This product concentration a lot on sports. I really only like football which means that all the sports channels that it offers is a waste to me. It does have the hallmark channel which I like and some local news channels.
We're trying different streaming services. Fubo is by far the worst. It constantly hangs, and the picture is bad. It's also the most expensive. Terrible.

column2: Not bad but, definitely needs some improvement.
column3: So far this app has worked fairly well for me, had some buffering issues at the beginning but that was due to my slow internet service which eventually was fixed, the price is really fair for what is provided, I was paying before over $120,00 a month and I didn't have any sport channels other than just ESPN, that's why I dropped Direct TV. The only thing negative I can say for now is the "Subtitles and Captioning" that had recently been popping up on some channels, not sure thou if it is the TV networks but, that is annoying if you're watching a game, don't really have any options of function controls, so far I've having been able to figure out how to  get rid off the subtitled, in addition to it I also wish fubo TV will add on more sport channels, out of the 11 channels provided, 5 are about movies that no one cares about, I hope that fubo TV will improve it's service for more customers's satisfaction.

This is a great streaming service with most channels available except a few like TVOne and others. I am considering this service to replace my DirecTV Now/AT&T TV. The interface could be a little better and I wish it would continue to play the current channel while I browse the guide.If they fix that and offer a discount with Showtime, I'm sold.

I love FUBO can watch Fox News and Hallmark channels and ID and it has everything I like to watch without a locked in contract. It’s a bit pricey tho. And sometimes there a few kinks we need to investigate as to why it takes us out of Fubo at times

column2: I think best picture of the streaming services I have tried
column3: The only thing keeping it from being a five star for me is lack of TNT. For me they add enough sport channels to make this my choice despite no TNT. Price wise most cord cutters pretty much or not so much anymore just safe a little in most cases.

column2: Lots of sports! No decent programming guide
column3: I love the fact that this has nearly all sport channels (big exception: no ESPN!). B10, pac 12, fox sports, etc.. The only knock I give it is that it's hard to find out what's coming up. I think there's a lot more to fubo, if only I can find it!

I'm not much of a sport fan (aside from Golf), but the rest of the channel line up is great. It really has what I need, and trying some of the other services worked, but some interfaces and the service seems "clunky". Happy so far with the app (loads fast), and I can't judge buffering since I have ample streaming bandwidth. I'm past the trial service and looking at keeping this.

We started the fubotv on my husband's cell phone it worked perfect, we moved to the iPad it worked perfect but when trying to log in on the fire stick it would not log in at all, there is no option to log in with fb on the fire stick and that's how my husband started the account, when entering the email and password manually the account wasn't recognized. Other than that we love the app

Love, love that fubo has an actual guide! This was one reason I cancelled Hulu (no guide) also I love their pkg. It has a good variety of everything & it's easy to navigate. To anyone that hasn't tried fubo, I definitely recommend trying it out, it's a little pricey, but anything comparable to cable is gonna be!

column2: I switched to Fubo from YouTube TV and am so happy
column3: This is a big-time streaming service. Everything YouTube TV has and more. A ton of space for recording at a nominal cheaper rate. Far superior to Sling tv as well. I had no idea Fubo existed so I am pleasantly surprised. A customer for life.

I would have given zero stars if that was an option. Everything was in Spanish and I couldn't figure out how to switch it to English. I called the customer service number (which is automated) and it said it couldn't find my account. I cancelled it within 30 minutes of starting. Save yourself the headache. Don't waste your time. There are plenty of other options that work.

column2: The only streaming service that really let me cut the cord.
column3: I tried all the streaming services. they all fall short in either cable Channels or local channels. Fubo has everything I wanted. The only thing I will mention is I have 1 gig Fios and I was getting the buffering spinning circle. I had to reduce the quality, but still looks good my 4K tv.

This product helped me to watch a sports channel (Biensports) no longer available on directv my main cable provider. For some dispute between the two parties this channel was yanked from Directv line up. I am a ardent fan of soccer and missed the bien sports channel...  After research found fubotv to be my alternative to was biensports

Current PlayStation Vue customer looking for replacement streaming service.  Decided to try Fubo because they offer BET channel.  After signing up for trial, I saw my local ABC station is unavailable.  I cancelled trial after two days.  Not sure why it isn’t offered; tried to search rather internet for a reason to avail.  If you watch local TV, tread carefully.

What surprise me was the lack of staying connected. It couldn't have been my wifi because the other streaming apps did not lag or would time out like Fubo app did.  Twice I had to completely restart the Fubo app in order to get it going again.  Not happy whatsoever..

Quality is on par with cable and much better then You Tube TV. It takes getting used to as you can't go from one channel to the next (or I don't know how to do it). So far pretty happy and saving over $100 from my Comcast bill with Frontier internet.

Cost is just too high.  Not a service I would pay for.  Alot of these live t.v. steaming packages have the same problems that caused me to cut the cord.  Channels I don't want are bundled with few I do at a price I'm not willing to pay.

column2: I like this quite a bit
column3: I like this quite a bit. Has every channel that I am really interested in. Of course I will  add HBO and SHO. But this is what I was looking for. Docked one star for interface, UI is amateurishI ended up dropping the subscription. Buffers way to much and there is no way to setup recordings in advanced. Dropped to 2 stars

We signed up for Fubo TV thinking we would be able to get LIVE college football games. We especially wanted OU, but could not get any games. There are a few live games but many are pre recorded. The chat agent was very helpful to help me cancel the trial.

I don’t dislike anything about the app itself. The lineup and selection of packages is Pretty  darn amazing. I’m just hoping that their prices don’t begin to increase excessively in the future due to higher demand. We have the family package is the least expensive and we tried it with a 7 day free trial before purchasing. It has more in this package than Direct TV offers for nearly 3 times the price...which is utterly ridiculous! I’m so glad we stumbled on to Fubo TV!

Pretty much all the channels I want but for a sports streaming service, you are missing  a totally sports channel.You don't provide ESPN. Although I can do without most of their on air talent(less), I will miss their coverage of Monday Night Football and Saturday morning College Football coverage. I will need to subscribe to Sling TV in order to get ESPN and use my antenna for the ABC Network which Fubo doesn't have either. I will continue to try to find a streaming network that carries all that. Other than that, Fubo seems to be ok so far..

I have it one star because you can't give any fewer. I signed up for this to watch the Kentucky Derby, after they advertised they were airing it, only to find out they were only airing the preliminary races and not the derby. After the nightmare of the sign up process, I was very unhappy to find out I could not watch the race. Canceled immediately.

The channel choices are much better than on Sling and much easier to use. The picture is blurry at first, but then very clear. There have been some hiccups in streaming; it will start a stream and then restart before where it started. But once you know it can happen you get used to it.

column2: Great soccer coverage with enough local stations and general networks to keep you entertained
column3: Misses ESPNs soccer access, but otherwise indispensable for US fansWould be improved by ability to channel surf without having to back out all the way to the home screen, but probably more an issue with streaming than Fubo itself. Hulu seems to have realized that once you commit to streaming a show, they can load up the commercials and you are captive audience...makes one miss the ol' remote.

column2: Its good if you want bein and univision deportes
column3: The basic plan has only two valuable channels...bein sports and univision deportes...the other channels included arent really of any importance.. nothing to watch there and if you want more channels you have to pay more i think 9.99 is already more than enough for at least 4 important sport channels a month but its good if you want to watch the most important soccer leagues in Europe...for me its the spanish league in bein sports...never buffers or lags it streams with a very clear picture if your internet is fast enough....

It's not bad at all. The price is okay if you lack the skills to negotiate with cable or satellite companies or lack the time as a valued customer. I just had a problem with the audio being out of sync with the picture. It drives me nuts 🤪🤯😮. The free trial they offer makes it worth the time to  check out of it works for you.

column2: Content is good if you can get it working correctly
column3: Works ok. Had problems with pausing a video and having it start completely over and you can't fast forward. Also had problems with it recording shows that were labeled wrong. I clicked on the show that I recorded and it's a different show, under the show I thought it was', title. I like the channels it has though... when they work and don't show the loading circle.

column2: Best replacement for former Playstation Vue subscribers!
column3: I used Playstation Vue for a couple of years but when they announced that they were ending the service, I switched to Fubo! Not only does it have everything that Vue had (except ABC & ESPN) but it is HALF the cost! Can't be more pleased with this App. Has all of your sports needs (except ESPN) covered! NFL Redzone is included!

Checked it out and it might be very good however it is too expensive. The two 3stars I gave it is because not really sure how easy it is to use or how good the streaming quality really is. Wish it was cheaper as I'd love to try it.

column2: Got it for the World Cup
column3: Overall a good app for sports although while watching TV series, the feature to move to the next episode is missing (i.e. the binge watcher feature ;-) but a great way to get World Cup Soccer from all the sources. It is even better than the Fox Sports app and it is getting many of its content from them! go figure.I was happy to get Mr. Robot season 3 ahead of the Prime videos but I have not browsed thru their contents to see the depth and breadth of the available media. The interface is somewhat confusing compared to the other major streaming content providers such as Netflix and Amazon Prime videos.

I like everything about Fubo. My problem is I have a limited budget and it’s just too expensive for me. I had to give up my local cable service as they just kept raising their prices. Fubo is a better value than your local cable or your satellite service.

column2: Very nice but too expensive for me
column3: Great selection of tv shows & movies. I was happy to find an app I could finally watch Dr. Phil on but disappointed I can’t afford to buy it. Love the DVR feature. Just wish you could pick which channels you want & only pay for those

column2: If you love watching LA LIGA and you don’t want to pay ...
column3: If you love watching LA LIGA and you don’t want to pay crazy prices on cable to get the additional channels, this is your best option.  The quality is phenomenal and the features that allow you to record the games is extremely useful.  You can also watch games from other countries in Europe as well as South America.

The only problem is it does not have the abc channel which is channel 7 in chicago. I would have given it a 5 star, but since it doesn't have that channel which is one of my favorite channel. I rate it 3 stars. Overall everything else is great.

Pricey! I have +DVR  Many times the sound doesn’t match the lips and when I stop and restart it the sound is still going and I can’t get it to stop so I have to go onto a different network like amazon prime to make it stop then I can go back and restart it. It’s a PAIN in the neck!  They need to fix that problem.

They make it sound like ALL SPORTS ALL THE TIME. That is not the case, most is stuff you can stream for free elsewhere, it would be a good “ go to” app if you have nothing but the crazy $65a month is stupid. I will cancel after trial.Clear picture, easy to use. You will have to make your own choice.

I signed up for a free trial. Did not like how the sporting events lagged. It has taken me 3 days and contacting customer service and I still have not been able to cancel.  They make it impossible to do so. Be sure it is what you want, or you’ll have a headache trying to get out of it.

No problem with download. This app works great. I had used DirectTV now and it did not work so good. Had to keep deleting the app and reloading. So I got rid of it and downloaded FUBO. It works great! Very little buffering, even though my speed is not very fast.

Fubo runs better on the Firestick than it does just on my Smart TV with the Fubo App. The guide is much more user-friendly using the Firestick.  We use it at home, and we also used it while in our summer house. A very cost-effective option for TV.
This app was not user friendly, it was difficult to maneuver from channel to channel

It is an OK streaming service. Way overpriced in my opinion but the 7-day free trial was nice to enable me to watch the college football playoffs. I will not be purchasing the monthly subscription at its current price.

Hate the fact you can't watch a channel while you scroll through another channel.  Also unlike youtube tv on your phone you can't watch it while you are multitasking using another app. Only plus it has the MSG channel.

There are better choices out there. I was most dissatisfied with Fubo's closed captioning. Being hearing impaired, I depend on closed captioning. With Fubo one has to turn on the CC for EVERY time they want to watch a program. With the other streaming providers.... turn it on ONCE and done!!!

I cannot tell you just how much I love having Fubo.  I could not afford Direct TV anymore and my daughter suggested I give Fubo a try.  I can watch everything I like and  it doesn’t cost me a fortune. There is no contract which is wonderful.Wish I had switched a long time ago.

I downloaded this app just so I could watch Mexico vs. USA in the World Cup qualifiers. The audio was ahead of the video by about 2 seconds and it was really hard to watch. The announcers and crowd would get all excited and then 2 seconds later I would see a shot on goal. I finally just turned the sound off and watched the game. I won't be keeping this app.

I really like it so far, on day 3 of my free week.  Only way to stream ATT Sportsnet so I can watch my Astros.  Noticed a technical issue on a Sunday afternoon and emailed them, surprised to get a reply within an hour saying they were working on it.  Pretty sure I will be staying with Fubo.

I had Youtube TV but they dropped NESN and I needed it for the Bruins games. Fubo has all the sports, but for some reason they don't have ABC. I fixed that with a small antenna and I get 30 channels free over the air.

This is just another version of cable service. List of stuff I don’t care to see. Nice that it had ESPN and some sports but cost too much to just get ESPN. I can do with those sports. So too costly for what you get.

Tried watching sports, hgtv and a movie. In each case, one of two things would happen every 5-10 minutes1. video freezes while audio continues, then video "jumps" to the current location of the audio. You miss several seconds of video2. video and audio repeat the last several seconds of what you watched. So, as you're watching a show, suddenly you're rewatching the last 5 seconds or so. It happens quite oftenNB: have a dedicated 60 mpbs internet line; watching via FireTV Stick, located about 3 feet from the router. No other devices consuming wifi or internet at the time.I've since read that this is an issue with FuboTV. I don't experience these problems with Netflix, Prime video, Hulu, Youtube or when casting from a mobile deviceThat being said, the interface is horrible. I preferred my MediaOne (or whatever it was in those days) cable interface in the 90's to this. No search capability at all. Can't continue to watch a show while scrolling for another. No last channel or favorites concepts. So, in 2 days, prior to the end of the trial, I'll switch to Sling and compare.

Was disappointed when It continually stalled when I used it. I Could not find many get programs I wanted to watch. I was hoping to see many college football games since I no longer subscribe to cable or direct TV.

Along with many other web offers, I found this one to be very difficult to understand, and even more difficult to access. Plus, the terms, such as "when will my offer be renewed?" were very difficult to determine.

column2: Would be nice, if it did anything.
column3: Nothing worked. None of the links. The connection would time out trying to connect, in WiFi and without. When it finally loaded and I clicked on any of the channels, they said the link was broken. Definitely not worth $30 a month.

Easy to use.  Local channels and more.  Great picture.  Better than all the competing apps and we've used them all.  Got this just to watch the NFL playoffs but kept it because it was better than the competition.

column2: No buffering. NFL games stream flawlessly.
column3: I finally left DirecTV. I tried Fubo out before subscribing because I wasn't sure if the quality would be good enough for me to be willing to switch.Stream quality is great. I watched an entire Chargers game with no buffering. I've used 3 TVs at once with no issues. Channel selection is great. No boxes.My Sony TV is the only one I could get Fubo on without having to use a Fire Stick. But a fire stick is much better than a cable box.

column2: Only good comment i have is that the video resolution was ...
column3: Very little NFL content, no Chicago bears at all and I live near Chicago.Only good comment i have is that the video resolution was good.

column2: Cancelled trial subscription after a few hours
column3: Although the price and offering sounded good at first, there were several show stoppers. There is no ABC service currently. I missed that when reviewing available channels. The web interface for fubo.tv would cause my browser to freeze. The additional charge for DVR services seemed excessive. I cancelled the trial subscription before I had a chance to give that a try.

Waste of time. Went though a complicated process to do a free trial and as it turns out, I'd never be able to watch the teams that I want to watch because they are out of market, but this was never mentioned until AFTER I went through the signup and paying process.Cancelled. Will never consider again.

column2: Pic quality sub par for sports
column3: Picture quality for sports not good at all. Worse than youtubetv which is poor as well. Picture looks less than 720 for most sporting events. They only have FOX 4K which isn’t enough to get me to sign up at this time. They also don’t have TBS, TNT, and regional FOX sports networks. Expensive and DVR is limited unless you want to pay even more. Will let free trial expire. May look into it in the future if 4K offerings are expanded.

column2: I really like the interface of fubuTV vs other streaming apps
column3: I really like the interface of fubuTV vs other streaming apps.  The fact that they have B10 network along with a great variety of other premium sports channels is enough for me.  No ESPN on the base level but that wouldn't really bother me til around college football season anyway.

very inclusive lineup but most of which i could care less. why can't i pick just the channels i want and just pay for them. why is the channel lineup so bloated with channels nobody watches. what a racket!

column2: has great channels! & on demand options... I dont watch sports
column3: has great channels! & on demand options... wish the initial page is slightly different im not into sports so i use the guide maybe provide the option for intial pg to start as sports or guide w channels. Im canceling as will get channels w xfinity cheaper for now will see what happens in 12 mos
Never could get the service working. downloaded app, then setting it up it wouldn't take my credit cards.. now I can't delete it. Sick of these BS apps and setups

Everything about Fubo—installation, picture quality, ease of use, DVR—was superb except two local channels were missing and the price could have been lower. The price would be acceptable if those two channels had been included.

The ad said I could watch the game. Yeah, it records the game and you get to watch it after "the live event". Then they want $45 a month? I don't think so Tim. I thought I could watch a live game. This app didn't even make 24 hours.

We never could get it downloaded.  Hopefully I have cancelled this app.  It's impossible to know.  There's no place to send and email to cancel the 7 day free-trial.  I intend to fight it if they charge me.
Glitch. Glitch. Glitch. Buffering. Buffering. Buffering. Very poor channel guide. Worth the free 7 day trial ... after that, your wasting your money.

Can't cancel my "free" trial - they have done everything possible to scam money for subscription I don't want. Was just trying to get my dad on it to watch a football game, and now I can't get off of it.

We were excited to use the app to watch the super bowl with our friends tagt were over for a party and it only streamed the game in Spanish.  A disclaimer would be appreciated when you download the app.

column2: If you’re for sports this is it chief
column3: Was not very easy to use it said I can watch the billboard awards live it’s obviously not live cause it was not on the channel, also I had to search it In the search box this streaming app is mostly for sports that’s it

column2: Good option for the avid sports fan
column3: I signed being interested in streaming alternatives for general TV viewing and was very impressed. The variety of content was better than other streaming services that I have viewed but as with everything, it comes with a price. For me, 70 bucks a month is just too expensive. If I was homebound, I would seriously consider it but I am not and therefore have other entertainment alternatives that I enjoy and therefore don't spend enough time watching TV to utilize all the benefits.

I'm happy with the number of channels we get , very compatible with cable ( we ordered extra channels). Get all the channels we love and the picture is clear. My only issue is that occasionally the sound will be behind the picture along with the live sound so you get a echo like effect, then if you change the channel that previous channel sound stays on. I found that if you restart the fire stick it re-sets and fixes the issue. Overall very happy with Fubotv

I was able to stream some sports not available on other apps.  The monthly fee is a little steep for me as I don't watch much sports.  For someone who's a real sports fanatic, it'd be worth the price.

column2: Too much money for the few I'd watch
column3: The stream quality wasn't great. Buggered and stalled from time to time even froze. My biggest problem is the price. $700 a yr for the same collection of channels everyone is offering of which you only watch maybe 10.

I found this service to be so-so and too expensive for the price/channels available.  Cord cutting is supposed to be cheaper than the cable companies.  Fubotv makes we want to go back to my cable box.

column2: Did not like the user interface
column3: Very annoying to watch part of a movie and then to come back later and not have that movie resume at the point you stopped.  Happened more than one and the forward feature was "unavailable".  Not my cup of tea.

The picture quality is very good and the channels exceeded my expectations since I had never heard of Fubo tv. The only downside is it do buffer a little more than other streaming services I have used and that is why I gave it 4 stars. But all in all its a great choice especially for sports fanatics like myself.

I am crazy about international and domestic soccer.  I finally found where to watch all of it !!  And also watch all football and base ball i want.  No complaints.  It decently priced ( not the cheapest, but not too expensive either).  greatly recommended.

We have enjoyed this trial.  However, we are having issues with streaming.  It takes forever to change a channel and when you finally get there it takes forever for it to load so you can see.  Our current TV streaming is a lot faster.  With that said, we enjoy the channels more on the fubo TV app and we only have one more day to totally make up our mind if we can tolerate that constant streaming issue.

column2: Fubo tv may be pretty much be for soccer fans.
column3: Fubo tv did not meet my expectations in any way. The cloud dvr especially sucked as it did not let me watch a recording while it recorded. It only let me do so after it was done which is ridiculous if you ask me. Not to mention some of the major free local networks not included. Hello Fubo, if I could but an HD antenna and get these, why would they not be part of the package???

I did  Free Trial hoping to be able to watch my NFL football team play, since it advertisements say that you can! WRONG! This is not much different than having your regular local TV Channels, UNLESS you want to pay extra for other channels, STILL NO WAY to watch my NFL games!! VERY DISAPPOINTED, CANCELLED FREE TRIAL AN HOUR AFTER SIGNING UP! WASTE OF TIME..

While my husband requires CNN Live and MSNBC Live, there is enough content on Amazon Prime ($13 monthly), Hulu ($15 monthly), and Peacock TV (Premium Membership $10 monthly w/no commercials).  Fubo TV at about $64 monthly is not worth the pricetag any more than Youtube TV is worth its $64 monthly nut providing CNN Live, MSNB Live and NBCSN (Premier League).

column2: I would love this streaming service if.......
column3: Rated it 3 stars because of the lack of ESPN.  The local and "cable" channel line up is solid - do you know I would actually pay more per month for this service if they offered ESPN?  Too many prime time events to miss with no ESPN - which is the deal breaker for me.  If and when they bring on ESPN, I'll be switching to fubo TV, for picture quality, ease of use and streaming quality.  If ESPN is not on your wish list, go with fubo TV.

Quality selection of movies news sports etc. I don’t miss anything having Fubo. Enjoying everything about it. Great selection. Only thing That I might not be too keen on is that the Harlequin channel is not included. Other than that  I am highly satisfied.

The lack of major sports channels, and an interface that needs improvement are the main reasons I decided not to continue with FuboTV.  For example, when you navigate back to the Guide, you lose the present channel's sound and picture.

Layout is a little odd/confusing. I wish it would open to the guide right away, instead of its own homescreen. Only NFL channel missing for us is ESPN, which I would love the option for, even if it was extra. Otherwise, there's a pretty decent mix of local channels and others, such as Cheddar.

I signed up for the free 7 day trial service to see if I might be able to catch Blackhawks game on the Regional Sports NBC channel. Which I was able to do. The first night I tried it out, I couldn't watch the local pre-game show but the game came in fine. Clear picture, no issues, all the intermissions there and the post-game show. I came back the next day and caught what turned out to be the Swedish Hockey League on another channel - Eleven Sports. It was broadcast in English and so it was interesting to watch some European hockey.  KHL hockey games are also shown.The app through the fire stick is a little clunky and I have yet to figure out how to get the description of TV shows when in the channel guide view. column3: I was keen to test Bein Sports on fubo tv and was pretty happy with the coverage of non-football events like F1 racing and rugby. The problem I had with this app is the flakiness of the connection. We have a 75Mb broadband link (cable) which supports all the main on-demand movie channels (Amazon, Netflix, Hulu, Crackle) with no problem. Live apps like Twitch and CBS work fine, as did SlingTV (which we cancelled due to content rather than quality of experience). But fubo tv is a hit-or-miss experience where you often have to back out and retry 3-4 times before getting a reliable connection. When it finally connects, the quality is great - but the effort needed to get there is frustrating and not up to par for an online streaming service in 2016. We cancelled the subscription as a result but would be happy to try again (pun intended) in a few months.

column2: Good line up but otherwise very very poor. Only useful for live games
column3: The options for streaming sports are limited, but fubo is not the answer. Although they have a good selection of options, the service overall is extremely poor.The apps are atrocious. The majority of the apps available, including for roku, the worst of them, are very poorly functional. On roku you can only watch live - no access to your DVR, prior games, or even to fast forward or go back. Plain simple live is the ONLY option.If you use chromecast or other way to use the app on a phone or tablet, it is slightly better, but as you cast to tv, the fast forward and all other commands no longer function, unless you stop casting.Then comes the worst part of it - say you recorded a game, or want to watch a game that happened a few hours ago. First, you need phone or app - again, no roku functionality (they have been on beta for over one year). Second, good luck watching it all. The app saves what they think is an average time for the game, and if it is a bit longer, you miss the end. On football and baseball, you reliably lose the end of the game more often than not as they record only 3 hours!!!!Bottomline, barely useful, and only for live games.
