column2: Pointless - The content is available elsewhere. Sometimes for free.
column3: It seems Fubo has missed the point of the  cord-cutting "targeted streaming content service" trend. Or, at least, they want you to think it's cord cutting. Unlike NFL, NBA and MLB apps that offer the user the ability to focus on just the content they are after (baseball, hockey, US football), Fubo delivers packages of fairly low bandwidth sports streams that force you to channel surf in order to find the content you're looking for. (Let's face it, there are hundreds, if not thousands of football matches going on around the world all year long),The truth is, when you're forced to buy bundled packages that resemble what you are already paying for with traditional "cable tv", you've just exchanged one cord for another. For most people, internet and standard cabe tv use the same physical wire to the house. Using Fubo to stream the same channels means you are actually using a SLOWER (lower bandwidth & quality) stream to watch the same channels in lower quality. PLUS you are paying for the additional data/bandwidth usage that goes against your monthly allotment...- And before Fubo says "but you can watch on computer or mobile device"; most cable providers already offer mobile apps or web access to live channels. Most major networks already offer mobile/web access to streaming content if you can prove you have a traditional cable tv contract. (NBC/ABC/FOX/SKY etc..) - So (MAYBE) Fubo has missed the point on cord cutting and targeted streaming, (MAYBE) Fubo knows but wants people to think it's a cable/cord killer service, or (MAYBE) Fubo is an initiative sponsored by a major cable company to rope former customers into a service that, at it's core, is exactly what people are trying to get away from or already paying for.NOTE to Fubo: The point of targeted steaming apps is to allow customers to pay for ONLY the channels they use. HBO, Showtime, Cinemax, Mhz, MLB,, Netflix, Amazon Prime all do this very well.. So if Fubo REALLY want to impress customers, they will figure out a way to corral all of the network relationships they've made into apps or options within their app that allow customers to purchase focused content like EPL, Europa League, Bundesliga League, specific team matches or cup competitions without the need to channel surf and slog through irrelevant content to find the content they're seeking. Otherwise, there's really no point. The content is available elsewhere. Sometimes for free.

column2: FuboTV Service is OK and may be Right for you but some Services needs to be improved.
column3: Note:  I have not used the Amazon App for FobuTV.  This review is for FuboTV service.  I sign up for FuboTV from their website & have only used them for little over 2 weeks now.  I replaced Google TV service with FuboTV due to Google getting out of TV Service & for new customer suggest either YouTubeTV or FuboTV.  I could have kept Google TV Service but if they're not accepting new subscribers, then sooner or later they'll dumb those who have changed off or drive up the price to make you change.  On the plus side I will be saving $$$ by going to FuboTV instead of Google TV, which was part of my decision to switch now instead of when Google makes me.Is FuboTV service right for you?  Maybe I can help.  I really don't like doing review, because my general experience is only 2 type of people normally write a review.  1) Those that are extremely happy with the service & 2) Those that are dissatisfied with the service.  Me, I'm neither extremely happy or dissatisfied, which is why I'm actually doing this review.  I'm a highly Technical Network Administrator for a very large manufacturing company for over 30 years.  I'm the person in our Division of our Company that makes Technology works.  That being said, I know how I would like FuboTV to work/the way it should work.FuboTV Channel vs. it's cost.  This is a decision that each person must decide for them self.  For me, once Disney/ESPN came to FuboTV it had the channel I wanted most.  What I mean by wanted most is, it didn't have everything I wanted but if I got/changed to FuboTV service, I wouldn't be going looking for another service to get any additional stations.  (That wasn't true for any other service that I looked into like:  YouTubeTV, Sling, Philo, or AT&T.  OK, AT&T might also have the channels but didn't like the cost or DVR Service they offer & wouldn't try them because of it.)  YouTubeTV was close but still missing some channels & didn't like the ideal of losing my DVR after 9 months.  Also FuboTV really doesn't have many of mine local stations & from what I can tell unless you live in the top 5 or 10 cities in the US, it probable won't have very many or yours either.  What I did was buy an antenna for about $40 & get about 20+ local stations.What I like about FuboTV:*  Has the channels I wanted/could live with without adding another TV Service provider.*  Price for the channels I get.  (After paying for cable bills & seeing them always going up, glade to have it finally come down some.)*  DVR 30 Hours with option for 500 Hours & you can keep your recording as long as you want them.  (Most review will say that YouTubeTV has the best DRV services.  I don't agree.  I would rather have only 500 Hrs. of DVR & be able to keep shows for the length I want to keep them, then to have Unlimited Recording but lose all recordings after 9 months.  But that's me.)*  Ability to mark channels as Favorites & have them appear on top of the menu.  (You're also able to re-order your Favorites, in case you want to add one to your list & have it move to the top your menu.)*  Profiles - Each family member can have their own Profile*  Different View of the Stations you want (Standard TV Guide or by Network).*  Pause Live TV (it works my not very well)*  Max of 3 concurrent steaming (YouTubeTV allows 4)What I dislike about FuboTV: (Some will be the same as I like but will explain what I dislike about it.)*  Profiles - Yes it's nice to have them but when I replace my cable server with FuboTV service, every time I launch FuboTV, I have to select the Account Profile to use.  It needs the ability per device to set a default Profile it'll auto logon/use.  Once on that device, I can always change if I want another Profile.*  Pause Live TV - Great must have in live TV service but FuboTV Pause just doesn't work all that well.  1)  Once you un-pause & try to skip a commercials you don't have any indication when to stop the skip.  Give me a preview of what I'm skipping, so I know when the commercials are off.  (YouTubeTV give you a preview when skipping the commercials.)  2)  Rewinding Live TV doesn't work if the shows goes off.  If a new TV show has just started 10 seconds ago & you want to rewind to the end of the last show due to walking out of the room of somebody was taking to you, you can't rewind to see it again/catch what you missed, even though it's only been off 10 seconds.  Come on give user 10 to 30 minutes to rewind once a show goes off, in case we want to go back.  3)  If you like to binge-watch live TV, then due to #2 Pause reason above, your in trouble.  I like to pause live tv to 30 to 90 minutes & do something else.  Then come back & watch the station I paused & skip the commercials.  Doing this on FuboTV will cause you to miss something you wanted to see.  Once the show goes off you paused on, you're in trouble.  It will let you finish watching the show you hit pause on but if also want to watch the show that comes on after the show you paused, when I pause, ff, or look at menu, the show stops.  I have to go off the show, then back on it or go to view Live to start watching it at that point in time.  Anything that was paused is now gone.  (This has cause me to miss many things I wanted to watch.)*  Profiles Recording are only available to the Profile that recorded the show.  OK, keeping the who record show per profile separately is not necessarily bad but give me another options to view all profiles recorded show too.  So if I want to watch something my wife/child has recorded I have to log onto their profile to watch it.  Then when I'm done log back onto my profile.  The total DVR recording (either 30 Hrs or 500 Hrs) is shared across all the profiles but not the shows.*  Max of 3 concurrent steaming, needs option to have 4/match YouTubeTV, which allows 4.What I would like to see:  (This list excludes fixing what I dislike, which I think needs to be fixed.)*  Does anybody remember ever using Picture within Picture?  Why not bring it back with Internet Live TV services.  Esp. for a TV service that really boost about all the sports show they have.  Would love to spit my screen have 2 current live Football games going on it & simple selecting the left/right side would change the sound to that game.  (This may just be me but I would love to have the ability to watch 2 live TV Stations at the same time.  Yes it would be smaller on the screen but with 50, 60, 70, 80, 100+ size in screens today, don't really think that would be a big issue.  It wouldn't be for  me.)  I've seen some people mount to TV on the walls to get this function.  (One of the TV is usually smaller then  the other to get this function but this make me think I'm not alone i wanting this feature.)

column2: Dont Bother if your a cable cutter
column3: Hello, My name is Brian and I'm a cord cutter (all together " Hi Brian")  So I have no cable service any longer.  This App only works if you have a current contract for cable service.  not for nothing guys, if I had cable service I would not bother with Amazon Fire TV in the first place.  You need to learn you customer base, dont offer apps like this if your not able to deliver, or rewrite your agreements with the networks to allow access even if we have to pay a small fee.

This app is virtually useless. Primary detractions:1. Playback is unreliable in quality and seamlessness.  This is not a problem I have with other apps. Every 20 seconds or-so I get a yellow 'buffering' loop that takes 20 more seconds to return to streaming (now at substantially decreased quality). My internet speed is fine--and, oddly enough, provided by NBC's parent company.2. Commercials cut into programming. I got the app to watch the 2018 Olympics and it cuts into live competition to show ads. It might be tolerable (but shouldn't happen at all) if it was a rare fluke; but it isn't. It happens every couple minutes; absolutely ruining the watching experience.3. The commercial-to-program ratio is something like 2:1. I am spending twice as much time watching commercials as I am programming.I can only surmise that NBC really doesn't want one to actually use this to enjoy their programming.

column2: Another Useless App That Requires a Cable Provider
column3: What exactly is the point of a streaming app that requires a provider connection? If I already have a provider service, that probably has a DVR device, this app (and the service it provides) is completely useless. NBC Sports, please hop into the present and provide a true streaming app.No one needs cable any more so drop the provider requirement and join the new paradigm.

We are trying to watch the olympics with the app and they show the same commercials in the same order over and over and over again, and about every 5 minutes! It is to the point of cruelty and torture, really. It makes me not want to watch anymore. They even interrupt the events!!  I don't ever want to buy or support Koch, eat McDonalds, use IHC, or watch Mamma Mia ever!!  The way they are forcing the ads is definitely having a negative effect that I am sure the sponsors did not intend and are not paying for.

All the time. I can't clear the error.In the past few days, I have uninstalled the app an reinstalled it numerous times... all in some combination of rebooting my Fire TV, deactivating my account, signing out of my NBC Sports account on my laptop and Chromebook and yelling at my TV.Short of resetting the Fire TV to the factory default (not ready to go nuclear to watch the Premier League without fake sound) there is nothing I can do to correct this problem.  I've wasted hours trying to fix an issue that is not mine.I have sent this same message and photos to support@nbcsports.com.  It is NBC's responsibility to develop an app that works, and it is Amazon's responsibility to offer and distribute products that are promised to work.

column2: Disappointment.  Have to wait for HOURS for life stream to be over to watch it from the beginning.
column3: Disappointment.  You can't watch live streams from the beginning, it starts playing from the actual moment you turned it on.  If you have to watch something you've missed you have to wait until the life stream is over and moved to the replay area.  Rewinding of the replays is not easy and precise, so I try to avoid using it.  You can't rewind through the commercials but that is expected.  You also will need an account with a cable company so if you are a cable cutter, you are out of luck.  Overall experience is quite disappointing and ruined the Olympic experience a bit.  No wonder Olympic tv ratings are very low.  A lot of people cut cable but NBC failed to provide a good alternative for watching it.  If I wasn't huge Olympics fan, I would just delete it and skipped on the games.

column2: Terrible app/experience; can't access live content because of technical problems with subscription authentication requirement
column3: The app says I can get access to content if I'm a Dish Network subscriber (I am) and my Dish programming includes NBC Sports (it does). So I:1. Got an activation code through the NBC app (Android version running in Amazon Fire).2. Entered it at nbcsports.com/activate3. Received this message: "Congratulations, you've successfully activated your device and can now watch NBC Sports. It may take a moment for your device to update. You have access to NBC Sports video from the following networks: NBCSN . . . ."4. Then this message from the app: “You do not have a subscription to view the requested content. To upgrade your programming go to mydish.com/programming and then log back in to view content.”Support from Androidtv@nbcdigital.zendesk.com and support@nbcsports.com was useless. They said "In order to view live content in the NBC Sports app, you need to have a cable subscription that includes the USA network." My Dish Network programming does include the USA Network. So I'm not allowed to watch NBC's commercial-saturated lives sports programming because I have Dish instead of cable? That makes no sense.

column3: Yes, you still have to already have cable/TV for this to be of any use, yet if you already have cable/TV then why would this be of any use.....??  I just don't understand how these stupid networks still don't get that1.  The internet is not a fad and it is not "the enemy".2.  There's millions of people out there that won't see your stupid commercials if you don't make it possible.  NBC finally got the hint and made the Super Bowl available, but not the Olympics...(?)  The only time I miss TV is for things like the Olympics, the Final Four, Super Bowl and Stanley Cup.3.  If you're selling commercials to companies and then excluding millions of viewers, you're not making as much money as you could selling "potential viewers" to your advertisers....4.  No, I don't expect everything to be free; I'm willing to pay something on pay per view basis so......... what's the problem, TV networks?  If I didn't know better I'd think TV was run by a bunch of rich, old white guys who don't even realize how out of touch with things they really are.  Reminds me of the time IBM sold a worthless computer program to a stupid kid named Bill Gates for $30,000...........

It's too bad that the people at the NHL and NBC Sports have not figured out that customers are trying to use these apps because they have cut their cables. Many customers, like myself, are tired of paying large bills for unwatched stations while cable prices continue to climb. I am a huge Pittsburgh Penguins fan and wanted to watch the post season games, but the NHL and stations like NBC will only grant access to the games if customers provide their cable company information. If these stations don't catch on soon, they will get left behind, like newspapers and video rental companies The Internet has changed everything. NBC can either adapt or become irrelevant. More and more people are cutting their cable connections. If NBC wants to have customers, then it needs to grant people access to the games who don't have cable. I deleted the NBC app from all of my devices. Hopefully, Root Sports or the NHL will come through for fans. Then NBC will be a distant memory, like Block Busters.

I'd like to write a review, except the app doesn't work... at all... on multiple FireTV devices and models. both the original model and 4k 2nd generation.It simply says:ERRORAn error has occurred.Even after clearing the cache and uninstalling and reinstalling, nada. Bupkis.What really pisses me off is that a quick online search reveals that this is a common problem that has been going on for close to a year. I want my money back for my Gold subscription.

I've tried it at home, at work, at my parents house, and at friend's houses. It's not supposed to used the SSO for cable cable provider authentication, but I've tried using credentials from multiple providers anyway in case they were trying to make the switch.I've tried it on devices spanning three different generations of FireTV.It's not functional on ANYTHING. When you click open, you get the NBC logo with a spinning yellow circle for approx 1 second, then a message that says:ErrorAn error has occured.Options from that point are cancel or retry.This persists after clearing of cache and data, reinstalling the application, and even resetting the firestick to defaults.When you finally do get through to NBC support, they say they're working with Amazon to find the problem. That's the same thing they told me during the Boxing Day games, December 26th.UPDATE: This app still does not work. 7 months later the exact same error persists across all Amazon Fire TV devices.

My only issue with this app is that every time you click on an event, it makes you watch a 30 second ad. This is just a little annoying, especially when you know you are missing stuff. But otherwise, this is a great app. It offers the main sporting events that NBC has, like Sunday Night Football, hockey, etc. Additionally, it offers some unusual sports, like various tournaments (tennis, badminton, Esports, luge) as well as the Olympic and Golf channels. Lastly, it offers highlights, interview, and other short videos. Oh, and replays of full events. Just a note: a lot of unpopular sports do not have commentary or even sound equipment, so don't be thrown off when the World Billiards Tournament Game is silent. Also, you do have to have a corresponding TV subscription.

column2: If you're getting errors read this!  Poorly deployed app, but they have the monopoly...
column3: If you're getting an error when opening the app, or loading content, you can't have any ad blockers active.  Bypass your PIHole, remove ad blockers from computer, whatever. That fixes the problem.As for the app, it sucks. The ads are as every 1-star review describes, constant, unrelenting, and repetitive. Hockey games aren't so bad, but the Olympics were terrible.  Needing a subscription is expected, but a cable account is ridiculous. Just give a non-cable cutter friend or family a few bucks and use their account. The app is slow and sluggish. Just have to deal with that.  I would say use every means necessary to circumvent the traditional "Pay us to watch, watch our advertising, and we'll black out what we want" mentality of the networks. There are lots of options out there. The sooner everyone ditches the status quo and hits their pocketbooks, the sooner they'll revamp the pay structure to get customers back.Cancel Netflix.

I'll try it out on something not as popular but the buffering made it rather annoying.

If one gets fed up with that and selects another feed, like I did at first, then the whole process starts over with the initial commercial blast.

You get your TV set up, then suddenly in a couple of weeks, you have to re activate.  That requires your computer and signing into NBC sports each time with a special code. Pricing is outrageous for what is screened for free in every other country of the world. The live stream in the six nations rugby I was watching is good (as it comes from the U.K.) but abruptly stops at half time to be replaced by strange wind like noises around the empty stadium. column2: It's not a free app if you can't activate it on their web site to continue watching.
column3: We have a HD antennae for our TV and don't need Dish, Direct or Cable to watch TV. We downloaded the NBC Sports app so we could watch the Superbowl on the network if our reception went out on our antennae. That was fine and helped when we lost the air signal for a few minutes. But a few days after when we wanted to stream the Olympics live, they had a countdown on our watch time and then NBC Sports stopped working and they wanted us to register to activate it again. column2: The Amazon fire stick has been a good little functioning device that allows me to stream conventional ...
column3: I purchased an Amazon fire stick and downloaded this channel APP along with many other channel app's.  I wasn't aware I would be prompted for a review from Amazon for each channel downloaded (or I wouldn't have downloaded 90% of them.)  If there are no previous words to this paragraph and a three star review, then it is obvious I haven't had the time nor inclination to review the channel APP.  I do often review items for seller discounts and therefore I am expected to leave reviews for every item purchased.  The problem here is I didn't purchase any of these channel apps, they were all free for download and use.  I will eventually get around to either reviewing each channel or deleting them from my Amazon fire stick, however when they are deleted from my fire stick the review requests remains.  Due to the fact I am rated on my ability to leave a review for all my Amazon purchases, I must leave this wordy explanation for my review explaining the fact that I wish I had not been prompted for a review on a free channel app.  The Amazon fire stick has been a good little functioning device that allows me to stream conventional shows over my home wifi and internet and although it's not the fastest device (click and wait sometimes) it does function as expected for a small HDMI stick over wifi.  I only wish there was a way to disable the requests for reviews on free channel apps.

column3: Clunky interface, random commercial insertion on replay events, poor search interface on replay events, and loading screens are why I will only use this NBC Sports interface if I can't hook up my laptop to the TV for some reason.Also, I really do appreciate the fact that NBC is allowing Olympic viewing on replay but the interface is not very friendly.  Please go back to the interface that was in use for the last Summer games.(EDIT) I have upgraded my rating after looking at the Fox Sports Go app which has no replay of previous events.  Looks like illegal straming from a dodgy website will be in order for the World Cup this year.  Awesome job Fox (sarcasm) to make this app look like 4 stars instead of 2.

column2: Hey NBC:  the Olympics is about sports and athletes....not your celebrities
column3: The South Koreans apparently did an excellent job of hosting and producing the games. The opening ceremony was awesome and the venues seemed to be world class.  However, the NBC coverage, seemed more focused on celebrating the NBC announcers, network, and commentators. NBC seems to have forgotten that it was about sports and  the athletes and constantly injected politics, social issues, and overstated crises with the games or athletes. NBC seemed to repeatedly ignore the immense accomplishments and hard work of the many Olympic athletes from many countries. They blew it by not covering some key races and devoting time to too many fluff segments (e.g Today Show hosts learning how to ski. ). Hopefully, ABC, CBS, or FOX will provide the coverage next time.

column2: No commentary except background noise which sometimes includes the track commentary in German!
column3: I liked to idea to obtain all the skiraces, including both runs in the technical events.  Like last year I head difficulty in adding the site on my computer even after getting rid of blockers and updating Adobe. Finally installed Opera for this !  I had to hire a tech to do all this.  Bought Firestick to watch on TV which works fine except the picture is not really that good and sound is just sound.  No commentary!  Called NBC, complained and was told it would be passed up the ladder and maybe next year something would happen!  Unbelievable rip-off, but what can you do if you want to watch ski races.  I speak German and French, thus can pick up some of the track announcer's commentary, but that really leaves out a lot.  Don't speak Finnish, Norwegian or Swedish and for Swiss German, I need closed captioning!  Just wish NBC would do better.

column2: Poor Interface for the Olympics, but was able to see everything.
column3: I was very excited to hear about this app as it would ease a lot of the watching of the Olympics and finally we really were going to be able to watch every part of every event.  I started on some early weightlifting and we saw 15 seconds of lift, 4 minutes of commmercial which came back with announcers obviously well into some conversation.  Fortunately, that annoying aspect was not occurring near the end of the games, so I suspect NBC reacted to the early criticism.The one thing that would have been really nice was to be able to see a schedule of events (overall and within an event) so that one could more easily find what they were looking for.I look forward to their updates for the 2018 Winter and 2020 Summer Games and will use it to watch various NBC Sporting events as well.

If you still have the NBC Gold app, keep it for awhile. For two weeks I've tried to watch a subscription *I paid for* and it wasn't available. I opened the "old" Gold app and there it was. And the old app remembered my so I didn't have to log in everytime. This one keeps making me authenticate. And as for authentication, how's this flow: scan a barcode, be taken to a website to enter a code, and what's that get you? A login screen. Why not just give me the login screen to begin with. And btw, that's not to say the Gold app was gold, it had plenty of issues, but I wanted to think they'd put some thought into a "new" app before asking customers to switch.Update: Edit to one star, this just gets worse and worse and they don't care.

I installed the app, signed onto my service provider and everything was working great.The next time I tried to login, i just get the "Error An error has occurred" message and can't do anything.  I did everything that was recommended,  resetting the Fire TV Cube, clearing the data/cache, and fore stopping the App.Seems to be a consistent problem and the only known solution online is to do a hard reset on the device.  That is terrible.  Works fine on Playstation and Apple TV....

This app is useless to me, as it repeatedly produces an error message that states that I do not have access to live streaming when I sign in using my cable provider (DirectTV).I want to use this app to watch Premier League soccer, but am unable to do so due to this major glitch/error in the system. Upon doing a google search, I found that many other people who have DirectTV also have this issue, with no resolution.I even considered buying the NBC Sports Gold Premier League subscription, only to learn that there are major restrictions on which games can be viewed. What a rip-off.Hey NBC, you’d make a lot more money if you actually took the time to learn what consumers actually want and need. Look at many of these reviews... Clearly I’m not the only one who is unhappy.

I gave NBC Sports one star for their Olympics Coverage because the system wouldn't accept 0 stars. NBC spends much more time on their sophomoric, platitudinous, saccharin-speak side bar stories, pushing their philosophical and ideological psychobabble, than they do on the Olympics, the athletes' actual Olympics' activities, and even the actual main events and performances themselves.Moreover, NBC is guilt of just the same sort of audience-abuse I remember from the last time they aired the Olympics. Saving prime events and prime performances NOT for Prime Time, but for very late in the night ... all the while while stringing their viewers along hour after hour with teasers saying so-and-so coming up, etc, without adding "in an hour or two".  5 Lemons for NBC!

column2: Of Course You Need a Cable Subscription!
column3: No, I'm not being sarcastic.  Lots of people are confused because this app has NBC in the name, so please allow me to clarify.  The NBC Sports app is the streaming app for the NBC-owned cable sports channels like NBCSN, Golf Channel, etc.  It's no different than other apps for cable sports channels like ESPN.  Generally speaking, the only "free" sports you will find on network TV anymore are NFL games.  In my area (St. Paul), the local MLB, NBA, and NHL teams are all broadcast on regional sports networks (RSNs), which are only available through a cable TV package.  Every now and then you might find a Sunday matinee on network TV for the Wild (NBC) or T-Wolves (ABC), but 99% of the time it's on cable.  So yes, you need to have a subscription to stream it.The reason I'm giving it 3 stars is because the frame rate is only 30 fps.  Sports are generally broadcast in 60 fps for better picture quality during fast action.  ESPN and Fox Sports both offer 60 fps, but NBC Sports is still only 30 fps.  What gives, NBC?  It's 2019!  Get your act together!

Impossible to watch with all the freezing and buffering.I am hardwired via ethernet with a 50 mbps fiber connection (which usually tests closer to 60 mpbs) and the streams from this app are unwatchable making the app worthless.  I can stream the game on my tablet via my cable provider's app flawlessly and I can stream other apps on my fire tv without issue so there's no doubt it's the terrible NBC Sports app that is giving me trouble.  What can you expect for a free channel - what's that? Oh that's right, NBC Sports requires a costly cable subscription even for games streamed live OTA via antenna.  What can you expect for a paid channel?  Apparently nothing.

column2: You don't have cable, you can't use this, except briefly on a phone.
column3: Sure enough, if you don't have a regular cable account, you won't be able to use this on Amazon Prime Streaming. However, I was able to load it on my phone and it operated fine,, for about 45 minutes. I just wanted to watch curling, and though I find anything watched at the scale of a smart phone to be inadequate,  I guess it worked well enough for a brief time. I think the app popped up a notice that only clips would be shown after I had used up my intro watch unless I was on a cable service.I think this is a failure of Amazon to negotiate this with NBC sports. If it had been an Olympics duration only app, that might have been fair. It would be understandable if it was all NBC news when their business model involves contracts with cable networks, but for a short duration, it might have made sense.

I've tried over and over to view live sports broadcasts using this app on my Amazon Fire, but never been able to.  I receive their confirmation that my subscription is approved after activating the account and confirming my provider connection (Sling TV), but then wait forever for the screen to update as promised.  It never happens.  I've contacted them for assistance and spent countless fruitless minutes following their suggestions to complete the connection, but it never helps.  Even though I've received subscription confirmation numerous times, each attempt to view a live broadcast is rejected with the notice that I need to upgrade my subscription.  No information is given how to do that, and their technical support folks don't offer any such advice.

column2: App is free, content is not
column3: Amazon advertises the app as free, and it is. But they never said the content was free. If you are expecting to get free content, that’s like downloading the Netflix app and expecting to get all their movies for free. It doesn’t work that way. Having said that, Amazon should make it more clear that you are required to have a cable provider to access the content.

column2: If I had a cable subscription I wouldn't use the app. For god's sake this is 2018.
column3: Cord cutter here. I see an NFL game advertised on NBC. Great matchup. I download the app to watch the game. The app lets me watch approximately a half-hour's worth of pregame coverage before cutting out and telling me to enter my cable provider information. Holy Sh*t. What an absolutely ridiculous system you've come up with, NBC. If I had a cable subscription I wouldn't use the app, nor would I have Amazon Fire TV. Who is the marketing whiz who came up with this utterly boneheaded business plan? Jesus, just charge $5 a month for your app & let people buy your content a la carte. This is infuriating and worthless. Do you guys not want to make money? Your app is totally worthless and unnecessary and your business model is seriously flawed. Get with the times. Another disappointed customer...

column2: It was easy to set up with my digital projector and FireTV stick but the app has some problems!
column3: I loaded this app onto my Amazon FireTV stick and I am watching Sunday night  NFL football live on a 11 ½ foot diagonal screen. The video and sound quality are excellent. Unfortunately when commercials are playing, sometimes NBC blanks the screen with a spinning wheel. The football game does not start playing again when the commercials are over. It forces me to back out of the game and start it again and then the picture is perfect. Doing this though is frustrating. When I opened the app I was asked to log into the provided address and activate the streaming service by entering my device type, the access code shown on the screen and my cable TV provider. I use ATT U-verse as my cable network. I was instantly connected with the message that my service had been activated and I the game that was coming on which was the Sunday Night NFL football game.  Two weeks later is asked me to register with my cable provider again. Why?I am now watching the NFL game between the Seattle Seahawks and the Carolina Panthers. This is a good  app but it has some performance issues. How can the game broadcast be perfect HD quality but NBC doesn't want to show the commercials and it messes up the broadcast.  If this issue was fixed the app would be a 5 star app but as it is I rated it 3 stars. I can watch the game but I have to survive the commercial streaming issues

This NBC Sports app flat out does not work.  I have two firesticks and am holding onto a basic cable account just to use apps like this, and it has not worked for months!  You login, the screen never updates, you try every combination you can think of but you always end up getting this 'An error has occurred' message.  It 100% does not work, and neither Amazon nor NBC have any response or seem to care at all.  I am shocked at such a major network/product has this little effort or care for what would be a highly used app.  FYI, for golf events I've found ways to use the Internet browser and manually go to the video stream URL, which sometimes works, sometimes not.  Ended up buying a Roku just to avoid this frustration.

column2: Have to re-register AND select cable provider EVERY TIME
column3: This is the ONLY app I've found on Fire Stick that makes me re-register AND re-select my cable provider EVERY single day I use it. I'm not joking. I'm not exaggerating. Every single time. It is beyond annoying. I love watching skiing, bobsled, luge and skeleton, but I'm so tired of going through the steps that I just don't bother anymore.12/2/2020: Today I finally gave-up on this, and the standard NBC app. Wanted to watch the Baltimore-Pittsburgh game. Not only had to yet again connect to TV service provider, but then the app told it failed to load content. I'm done... Not worth the headache. Finally deleted both NBC apps.

NBC could not care less about their streaming app or the people who pay to watch it's content. Words cannot describe my hatred of NBC Sports and this application but I will try, for the people. First off, it is so full of bugs and glitches that it makes for a truly frustrating watching experience. There is no escape, however, as they have you by the balls owning the exclusive rights to some of the best sporting available.  You will have to sign in and verify your credentials to the app so many times, I have nbcsports.com/activate as one of my most visited websites. Once you've gained access to the content you willing pay for it gets even better. There is nothing quite like waking up at 7am eastern standard time to watch some Premier League football only to have the app tell you it is unable to play this asset over and over again. If you are watching a sport that a decent amount of commercial breaks be prepared to have quick cuts to those commercials, so quick in fact that parts of the game will be cut off.  Also be prepared to see the exact same commercials for an entire year/season. You will be reciting the Liberty Mutual ads by heart in no time. Games will lag so far behind normal game time that you have to actively avoid your phone to not see spoilers. To be clear this not an internet speed issue as I pay for decent download/upload speeds. If you love sports you will find this app as a necessary evil, but it will suck out as much of your soul as possible and then charge you the NBC Gold price doing so.

I have been unable to load the app for two months.  Only receive “an error has occurred” when I load the app on my fire stick.  I have tried restarting app and fire stick and signing out of other apps.  No solution available on multiple internet searches.  NBC needs to fix this.

column2: Got email about Olympics on Fire TV.....
column3: And found out I couldn't get to anything without "downloading the NBC Sports app" and after doing so, since I AM a cable cutter, I was informed after a poorly-identified "preview" that I was pretty much SOL for watching anything further. I HAVE Fire TV because I DON'T HAVE cable TV. Which Amazon knows. So that was a sleazy bait-and-switch  move as far as I'm concerned, and makes me LESS likely to follow future suggestions to get more involved in the Amazon ecosystem. I use Firefox TV to watch Netflix and it looks like that's pretty much all I'm going to do with it.

column2: YOU Have to have CABLE service to watch LIVE sports!!!!!
column3: this is stupid, I bought the app so I could cancel my cable service ,  so I did all that and then first game I went to go watch they wanted me to log in with my cable user id and password. I called them and said I don't have cable anymore since this is the only channel I wanted to watch.  they told me that I would need it .... and it was over 24 hrs and I couldn't get a refund.  I said the lady said when I called I could watch 180 live games  he said well there are more than 180 live games the rest you have to watch after 9pm on replay unless you have the user id  make long story short after fighting with them for an hour they refunded me...

I needed this app to get hockey back! Overall, I love the app and have no complaints except it was excruciating to log in with my cable service. It took me about 45 minutes to log in with a code on my computer because my internet and cable are on two separate accounts and it kept defaulting to the wrong one. The NBC Sports website wasn't particularly responsive when it came to pairing my Fire TV either. Make sure you log in asap and not wait until a game is about to come on!

column2: Failed to work on Amazon Fire Sticks
column3: I was unable to get this to work on any of my Amazon fire tv sticks.  Got to the point where it wanted authorization from the web and after typing in the code from the tv, the web page stated it was successfully activated.  However the screen did not change on the tv (still showed the code) and now when I try to start the app it gives me an error.  Tried uninstalling and re-installing and on two different fire sticks with same results.  Frustrated so gave up.  App works fine on my phone.

column2: Live Stream Buffers Frequently During Big Events
column3: The live stream is terrible for big events. It kept buffering and dropping out during the Superbowl, while it operated perfectly during the 6 hours of pregame coverage. For an app that is not free I would expect the stream to be (mostly) clean. I wouldn't bother paying for this app until they can improve the live stream, which sports are heavily reliant on.

column2: NBC Sports INDYCAR commentators also carried on NBC Gold
column3: NBC Sports did a good job at St Pete and I fully expect the rest of the season to go as "smoothly", relatively. The professional commentators were a pleasure to see on the net and I appreciated the consistency of the weekend broadcasts. However, to further promote the sport itself, which is still in its year-by-year upswing in both spectator attendance and TV ratings, I would have preferred NBC Gold offering free practice and qualification runs and a smaller charge for the race itself this year only. This would promote more transference of the website over the continuation of buying NBCSN cable for motor racing only.

column2: Horrible implementation but the only app to watch the Olympics. :(
column3: This app is the official app to watch the olympics but it's just so horrible.  When watching replays, you play the same two commercials over and over and over.  The commercials cut in before the results of a race are announced and when they end, the next race has already started.  It's a replay for crying out loud.  Put in the commercials BETWEEN races.  Why is that so hard?When trying to watch something the app says is "Live", it just sits saying Coverage to begin shortly and never does anything.The whole system is just bad bad bad.

column2: Needs a better user interface and ability to move around content.
column3: So the download is only a short free trial. You get about 45 minutes worth of time, most of which is dedicated to playing commercials. You can't fast forward though anything either.Tried watching a previously recorded event, and it was not clear from all the opening credits whether I was on the right event, after a few minutes of watching and not being able to fast forward I went back to the selection screen. It was the right event, so I clicked the event again. It started from the very beginning, and with no ability to fast forward, I got to watch the intro all over again.Eventually, my 45 minutes was consumed, with me watching perhaps only 10 minutes of material.I was under impressed.
Cuts to commercial about every two minutes.  This app is a colossal waste of my time.  We’ve had live streaming apps for several years now and this is what NBC lays before us?  Complete garbage.

column2: Spoiler headings should be eliminated altogether like "Zlatan puts United ahead
column3: Needs work. You can't fast forward or rewind streams using. When you try to fast forward, the app isn't recognizing the the button pressess on the remote. The app just starts blinking. Often it doesn't recognize the remote control at all. I use mostly for EPL replays, one, the location of highlights means you have to avert your eyes for spoilers. The titles are often spoilers. Replays should be a the top. Spoiler headings should be eliminated altogether like "Zlatan puts United ahead." Just title it "X v. Y highlights"  The exact same thing plagued the app during the olympics. Not that i care about olympics as this is about the app when it isn't Olympic mode. Sometimes a soccer game will resume where you left off sometimes it doesn't. There is no discernible pattern.A huge problem is often EPL soccer matches are not added to the app in a timely fashion. The game can end and it can be a day or two before it's available. Forcing you to illegal means to get the game shortly after it ends. Worse you can often log on on the phone and see that the game is actually listed for streaming.Note: I have the app on Roku too and it has the exact same issue as the layout is almost identical.Understand this:1. The app is requires you have a cable subscription. It is NOT a substitute cable service. It's not free.2. This is for the NBC Sports Channel (a cable teir sports channel) NOT broadcast NBC channel (the basic channel)

Thank you for the free 30 minutes of viewing the Olympics.  Also, thank you for the 20 minutes of commercials that also counted towards that free 30 minutes so really, 10 minutes of the Olympics.  So, what I should really say is:  Thank you for the free app that I have to have a TV/Cable service to use properly (which is the exact same EXPENSIVE service I got rid of)  So, this is a pretty useless app for those of us that Cut the Cord.

column2: Terrible functionality. I would rather watch a less than legal stream
column3: This app is terrible. I cannot find any way to turn on closed captioning. The playback controls are basically worthless. While watching the NHL West Final, I paused the game and intended to fast forward during the commercial break to catch up. Turns out it is impossible to rewind or fast forward. Ended up missing two goals when we went back to the live game.

Where do I start with a review of the NBC Sports app? It works, so that's a plus. There are many other apps out there for sports, but not any others which play NBC Sports, such as the Olympics. Other apps allow one to organize the offerings based on the league and date. There is no such organization with this one. Instead, you get a scrolling list of live events, a list of replayed events, and highlights. And NBC, which advertised that you can watch the Olympics anywhere and anytime, didn't bring this functionality to the Fire TV Stick. Not impressed.

NBC sports runs terribly during live events. They require you to have a paid subscription to watch half the events you follow under one sport wether you are linked to your cable provider or not. During live events the streaming tends to jitter and jump or just all out crash so you have to restart the app and go back to what you were watching. NBC butchered the streaming of Supercross, race times are always varying, sometimes you can watch the qualifiers and some races you can’t, some races you have to have the paid subscription to watch live and some you don’t. It’s ridiculous. Thank you for ruining the one and only sporting even I follow each year.

column3: This works for Olympics on Fire TV Stick without a cable provider but watch the glitch. When racing restarts we will then restart your subscription?

Absolutely a waste of time.  No search feature available to find events, backing to arrow through  is ridiculous. Beyond that, all you have is NBCs "highlights"  edit and worthless commentary; with more commercial length than actual event coverage.  I long for the days when ABC was the leader in sports coverage. Live events, factual and to the point auditories, and no political or broadcast politics. It has 1 star because I cannot rate it lower. In diving it would rate a failed dive.

All I have to say Bob Costas where are you? column2: Cuts out at the most inopportune times
column3: Have a sling subscription but the feed quality is marginally better with the NBC app so watched a couple NHL playoff games via NBC app.  Multiple times, the app got hung (spinning icon) and did not recover.  Have no interruptions with sling so sure seems to point to issues with the app itself or the way NBC streams.  Without a doubt, it always seemed to hang on a breakaway, power play, or the last few seconds of a period (see pic). What a scam. Gave me a 30 min preview then I needed to subscribe to channelvia paying them I guess?Plus, I turned channel off to save time for end of AFC game, but NO..30 Min preview timer continued to run whether I was watching or NOT!Oh NBC, you had your chance...C Ya

column2: Completely useless! You advertise this as a free app
column3: Completely useless! You advertise this as a free app, and get my hopes up that I can watch the Olympics. Low and behold I need a cable subscription to actually use this. Not free! What a joke!I own a Fire TV so that I don't have to get cable. I'd be happy to pay a small monthly fee for such an app to allow me to watch sports without having to subscribe to a bloated cable package.Pull this from the market, and revisit when you get it right for us non-cable subscribers.

Imagine a world where you can watch the Olympics on your favorite streaming device. Like, I dunno, your Amazon Fire Stick. Well, after downloading the NPC Sports app to do just that, I am still left imagining. I configured it with my cable subscription credentials to authorize my access to the rich pagentry of the Olympic games (and why this step is necessary when I get my internet access through my cable service is beyond me, but I digress...). Anyway, after launching the app, I was able to watch every trailer, athlete interview, promo, and sports advertisement related to the Olympics -- just not the actual Olympic games themselves. No curling in this house. No downhill skiing with this app. Not one moment of the heart-pounding thrill I expected from cross-country flaming luge skating that had so captured my hopes this year. If you're into watching droll (read: not at all droll) NBC talking heads drone on about sports cliches, this is the app for you. But don't expect to watch an actual sports with it.

Had a challenge downloading to the IPAD. When I was on the phone with support they walked me thru the process. (Thank you!) I asked about compatibility with TIVO and was told "sure...no problem" I was later informed by TIVO, nope and probably not going to happen. I was watching the President's Cup Golf Match. With about 2 hours remaining in the event and the match all tied...They ended the broadcast. WHAT IS THE POINT. I had to wait 12 hours after the event to watch it on NBC Network.  One last comment, if this is live streaming...why so many commercials? I honestly think there were fewer on the network airing.

column2: I can't get this app to work on my FireTV
column3: Not sure what is going on with this app but I own it and I can't get it to run on my FireTv.  I get an error message saying "An Error Has Occurred". I have deleted the app and even brought my tv down to factory setting, wiped it clean and then started from scratch. The only app this happens to is the NBCSN app. It's frustrating and disappointing!

column2: NBC Sports Does Not Make the Podium.
column3: We purchased NBC Sports so we could watch the Olympics.  There are only about 2 weeks of this special event and then another 4 years wait till the next set of Winter Olympics.  We wanted to indulged! Since NBC owns the broadcasting rights to the Olympics, this seemed like a smart, simple purchase.  We quickly learned this was neither smart or simple.  'Error' resulted in missing what was supposed to be ice skating when the programming froze for more than 20 minutes.  Morning televised programs are aired again later in the day.  (102 events people!!! Why replay the SAME ones?!?!). And in some random competition with itself, NBC will show one event on NBC Sports and a completely different event on NBC...So, I can watch what I paid for or watch what is free through my TV antennae.  ???  There 92 nations competing in 102 events, and preliminaries to some of those events, and semifinals for some of those events...It thought I would be able to see all of the Olympics with this purchase.  Clearly, I was mistaken.

column2: I love the Premier League on nbcsports
column3: I love the Premier League on nbcsports, and SF Giants games, especially on the firestick. It is HD and my comcast is not. I also love the replays. It's fantatic.However I have 2 complaints. 1. There are too many ads in the replays. We wanted to watch US Ice Skating replay and there were so many ads I decided it was not worth it. That defeats the purpose of the ads. And, 2., I have to reactivate it too often to watch replays. I'll get a notice saying I'm not a subscriber even though I'm logged in. I have to sign out,and resign in, by going to nbcsports.com/active and type in a code This is an irritating "feature".  Overwall, I still love the PL and quality of shows and otherwise ease of use.

It’s a well laid out app with lots of content. Picture quality is excellent. I have it 3 stars because while it’s a great app, I couldn’t access the channel/content that I wanted to. My tv provider is SlingTV and I have NBCSports in my package. The Sunday’s Nascar Race came on Sling but I missed it and forgot to record. On the Nascar page, they said that the race came on NBC and if I wanted to stream the race I could do so on the NBC app OR the NBCSports app. So I download NBCSports app and I enter my tv provider. The race is on there but I can’t access it. It tells me there is an authentication error. I decide to try the NBCSports Track Pass because it appears that I’ll have access to all the Nascar stuff, including the Nascar Cup Series....but I don’t. So I went thru all that just to try and watch the Nascar Cup Series Race and couldn’t. I was very annoyed. The app really deserves 5 stars but that’s why I’m giving it 3.

Ever since NBC decided to remove just about all winter sports from the basic app and requires the purchase of the Gold package I have no use for this app anymore. What a shame they felt the need to take this away after years of it being available even though I still need to login using my cable credentials and could watch it on cable when home. Unfortunately I'm not quite often in the winter.

NBC have had a couple of seasons to fix this app but it's never any better.  It seems the design emphasis is on ensuring they have their money and have spent little effort on the usability.  The quality of the streaming has been very poor recently - I'm barely able to distinguish players/sportsmen is gets that fuzzy at times. Since I need this to watch EPL games I'm stuck with it - a monopoly NBC seem to count on.

column2: Quality: Picture quality varies significantly while watching. It ...
column3: Quality: Picture quality varies significantly while watching. It is very inconsistent as the quality will go from low grade HD to 30 year old broadcast quality which can be hard to watch. I have a 150mb Connection Speed which is reliable and I test my connection frequently, receiving a minimum of 90mbs. This should be more than sufficient to watch anything. I have tested this against other services such as Hulu and Netflix which both work very well without interruptions.

column2: Are you tired of commercials yet? No???
column3: I love the olympics. But NBC’s algorithm of when commercials will play will suck the life our of you. It’s totally off and I hope you like seeing the same 5 commercials over and over again. Bright side: stream is clear and servers haven’t crashed on me. But after seeing a Toyota commercial for the 7,346,568th time, I think im going to stay away from buying a Toyota. Sorry Toyota. Im sure your cars are great.

column2: Appears well-conceived but orphaned for maintenance/development.
column3: Frustrating site.  I watch live F1 and IndyCar when I can.  I try to watch Full Event Replays if I miss the live.  The site controls are balky.  Sort by sport 1) doesn't always work, 2) doesn't stick through struggles to find the event.  If play can be successfully accomplished, the stream is generally smooth (Occasionally hangs for buffering, and I'm cable hardwired!) and the picture quality is good once the stream is established.  It can be awkward but it's the best that formula motorsport fans have got.  For that we're appreciative.  Perhaps more awareness that followers are more likely to employ their PC or smart TV rather than a phone and seek out the replay to watch the process rather than simply the result, would lead to improved/better optimized site for such consumption.

The App was fine until the hidden "trial" period was over. A detail that should have been mentioned before allowing people to get tied up. I find it unnerving that NBC would find it in their hearts, on Thanksgiving Day no less, to con people to get into this App just for the National Dog show. I guess NBC didn't save enough of their "Seinfeld" and "Friends" money to just be a pal and let us streaming folks watch the F#@king dog show!

column2: Consistent buffering even with 100 MBPS speeds.
column3: I use this app primarily for streaming F1 and NHL games but recently it's been barely usable. The buffering I experience is only with this application. I even purchased a new Fire TV upgrading from a gen 1 Fire Stick thinking it could be the issue but nope. Zero issues when streaming Netflix, HBOGO, Showtime but NBCSN... buffers all the time. Live, replays, you name it, buffering. Other devices I use in the same location are getting 100+ MBPS speeds so buffering shouldn't be an issue if it wasn't for the application itself. Streaming from the NBCSN website on my laptop doesn't seem to hiccup so once again must be app related. Can't wait for F1 to have their own streaming service so I ditch this garbage application and gladly pay someone to have a good quality app/stream.

column2: So disapponted that this is being forced to watch coverage ...
column3: So disapponted that this is being forced to watch coverage of the Winter Olympics.  We cut the cable but cannot get NBC over the air in our location.  So planning to watch this was squashed when you must have a paid TV service.  What happened to network television that has always been free.  Shame NBC.

I have cable in the living room of my house but I wanted to watch the golf channel in the master bedroom. The golf channel part of the app isn't available unless golf is actually live. the mobile app is fine. Right now the golf channel is replaying last years events. I go to the NBC sports app and its says check back soon. This is crap. If I wanted to watch it on a small screen, the iPad is fine. But i don't. Figure this out

Love it! Got to see the 'red men' Liverpool F.C. play when none of the channels were carrying the game live. I used Amazon's fire stick to download the app and watched the match live in glorious HD on the telly instead of the phone/PC/tablet which can also be used. All you need to do is register and tell the app who your service provider is, it's that simple.Highly recommended for any footy fans (and lot's of other sports), when your team is playing but not being shown on any cable/satellite channels that particular day.

Pixelated games of hockey are hard to watch cause you can't see the puck.  Freezes up almost every game towards the end of the game. Super annoying when it's a game in overtime. Then I restart it to try and get it going and end up having to watch commercials and then I miss the end. It has happened so many times crazy.On the "Live" page,  the start time of games disappears and a "play" emoji appears, way before the game starts.They also have been playing the same ONE commercial for over a year.  Yeah, I've been a customer for like 2 years and the same commercial has been the only commercial they use.

We are happy to have the app to watch some sports.2 things re: user interface- it would be great when logging in to a series if it automatically went back to what we were watching rather than having to navigate through the whole app again-it would be nice fast forwarding to be able to see the image rather that just the time with fast forwarding.  We are using a Firestick

Once up and running, the app is okay and provides what I need to watch the winter Olympics. However, it never loads the first time and always requires me to "retry" loading it. The tabs also do not load by themselves and require that I shut the app and reopen it to get a fresh listing. No issues with viewing video so it's not a huge deal, just an inconvenience. I should also add that I am using a fire TV or fire TV stick when using this app

column2: OK for now; navigation/streaming quality could be better. Activation problem browser related.
column3: I downloaded for Olympics coverage on my Fire TV Stick. Live events are easily found, but locating link to completed events can be a challenge because you have to scroll through as many as 300 events/highlights (so far) to find the one you want to see—there is no search tool. Quality of streaming is not outstanding, but most full events as well as excerpts of interviews and short features seem to be available if you look long/hard enough.As a side note, I initially had difficulty activating the app on my PC; clicking the "activate" link in my browser failed to go to my carrier's website, which was required for final activation. However, that seemed to be a browser issue. When I switched to another browser with extensions not loaded, activation went smoothly.

column2: I wouldn't even give it one star if I could ...
column3: I wouldn't even give it one star if I could.  This app requires you to have a cable TV service provider in order to view anything.  If you had cable, why would you need this app?  I have service on local channels through an antennae.  Don't they realize people can still view TV through an antennae and don't HAVE to have cable/satellite services?  UGH!

Was at a rental house this summer while the 2016 Summer Olympics were on and wanted to watch Micheal Phelps in a race in my bedroom.  Turns out that the tv in the room was not hooked up to an antenna or cable and was only set up for Netflix. (Who would do this at a rental house?)Anyway, plugged in my fire stick and downloaded this app.  Did some verification through a website that showed I had access to NBC through Comcast and I was on my way.  That was the only bad part of this process.Went from no Olympics on the TV to watching Michael Phelps win a gold in under 5 mins.  Yay. :)

column2: I onlywatch motor sports on this channel and am tired of ...
column3: I only watch motor sports on this channel and am tired of the excessive ads and the poor graphics.  They continuously put advertising on the "ticker tape" standings bar and then start the ticker tape over again and you can't see what is going on in the back of the pack.  The commentators are incapable of tracking back markers that make significant progress during the race and only focus on the top 5 or so performers.  During the recent Bristol races the ads ran so long you missed significant parts of the race.  With all their camera coverage, they frequently can't adequately show incidents on the track.Also, they don't allow enough time for an event and change channels without any notification making it almost impossible to DVR anything.  I thought Fox Sports was bad, but NBC Sports is really terrible coverage and their arbitrarily changing channels is a huge hassle.

Once I ran the gauntlet to get connected to ESN+ it works as expected. However the picture takes a minute or so to clear up from a dirty lens look. The play by play announcers were disappointing. I specifically subscribed to get 8 Kansas basketball games as result of a deal the Big 12 put together. Hopefully ESPN will improve the signal feed and on court talent.,

column2: Dreadful in a Moment of Need
column3: In a moment of need the App was dreadful. The App failed to load on a number of attempts. When it would load it would crash and go back to a spinning gear and ultimately not initiate. column2: Critical function doesn't work and no evidence NBC even considers it a problem.

column2: Great content, poor app. Very frustrating.
column3: Unfortunately all of the sports that NBC has purchased are trapped behind this incredibly frustrating app. I’ve used it for years now, and I would guess I’ve been asked to authorize the app more than 50 times. Netflix, Hulu, heck even crackle aren’t constantly prompting for logins.Browsing a program is also difficult. Of course I don’t expect to fast forward through commercials, but seeking a point in a replay is done by skipping ahead 10 seconds at a time. It does feature a seek function by pausing and fast forwarding, but that doesn’t work.If it worked as designed it would be outstanding, but as seems to be the theme with the traditional networks, it doesn’t. I’m excited for the day Netflix picks up the Premier League and Amazon the NFL.

column2: Not a fan of this app
column3: We watch alot of hockey.  Watching it on this app streaming through our Amazon Firestick is painful and frustrating.  The picture keeps skipping, buffering for 1 minute and coming back fuzzy.  The commercials are the same 6 ones and they cut to a commercial while the game is still on progress, not during a stoppage in play.  We keep having to force stop, clear the cache and start it up again only to find the game we were just watching is not listed.  Not at all user friendly.  Not impressed.

column3: Glitchy.  I have several streaming subscriptions and I wanted to watch a sports event not offered, so I downloaded the app for my Amazon Fire TV.  Bar none, this was the worst experience... many pauses in the show.  losing 5 - 20 seconds of content when it came back.  The screen quality was not as good as Hulu or Playstation Vue

column2: Close to Perfect with one nagging miss.
column3: This would be perfect if you could fast forward through previously recorded event. column2: Grateful for the stream of the NFL

I'd even pay a small amount to continue to have few commercials and more content.

column2: NBCSports App is heading in the wrong direction
column3: Unlike a lot of reviewers, our household does have a cable subscription. This app - like ESPN's - has been paring away at what content is available to its subscribers. Rather than giving their customers what they're paying for, NBCSports has chosen to go the nickel and dime route. This is why people are cutting the cord. This is why revenue is down. The "we're losing money so we need to charge more for less" is the reason sports channels are hemorrhaging money. Paywalls for content that's already behind a paywall isn't going to win any fans. The writing is on the wall...

column2: Enjoyed Tara and Johnny covering the skating I learned much ...
column3: Enjoyed Tara and Johnny covering the skating I learned much from their comments. In my opinion there seemed to be more coverage around select athletes.than other team members.  Did not see much about the Jamaican bobsled incident or the fact that Nigeria has a bobsled team and both teams I believe have women with USA connections.  The alleged controversial comments from some of the members of the coverage team further detracted from my enjoyment.  To me the Olympics are a platform where a diverse collection of highly trained,motivated,skilled and eager athletes from all over the world compete, representing either their own country or a country of which they meet the requirements necessary for representation as set by the IOC.

column2: Free programming, but a little behind..
column3: Watched the superbowl via the NBC Sports app on our firestick. 4 stars for letting a program that big be free. It was awesome that they provided a live stream for no cost. Most companies wouldn't dream of doing that, so I was very impressed. That said, we had it running on another tv at the same time pulling from an actual cable company and the NBC app was significantly behind, by like 30 mintues or so, so that was a bit of a let down. But again, it was free, so I'm not complaining. Just a little inconvenience when you want to have it running in two rooms at once (living room + kitchen). I'll continue to use the NBC app though as long as it stays free like this. Thanks, NBC and Amazon!!

column2: Liked that the offered Superbowl 52 for free
column3: Liked that the offered Superbowl 52 for free. Very disappointed with quality of the video stream. The plays were very blocky/lagged and the annoying interruptions that the presentation would resume momentarily were frustrating. It was almost as if they were hiding/overwriting commercials or covering for worse lag. Wish I would have watched it somewhere else. Hopefully they will do better with the Olympics, or I may have to setup an Over-The-Air antenna again (last one was destroyed by hurricane).

I have this for watching golf, I like the fact that I can watch starting in the morning and not having to wait till the Golf Channel or the networks start to cover the tournaments normally later in the day after most of the morning times are over.  With this service I can watch the morning rounds.

column2: Amazing Olympic Games coverage on Amazon Fire TV
column3: The Olympic Games represent the highest accomplishments of the athletes who have made it to these games in Brazil. As a native South American, I am tremendously proud of these games being held in the continent of my birth and, as far as I have witnessed, the great success that is being accomplished by the host country. I'm very appreciative of the coverage which is available on NBC Sports through my Amazon Five TV service and I am able to follow all of my favorite sports through this brilliant service. This is by far the best streaming service I have in my home at the moment.

I dislike that I cannot activate this app. I contacted Amazon before I purchased Amazon Fire Tv stick to make sure I could use the NBCSN app so I could watch the NASCAR races. I was told by Amazon that yes it was included with Fire Tv. I cannot activate this app without an account number from my cable provider which is Dish Network. However, my cable is included in my rent. I called our resident services, they have no access to the cable account as it is a corporate account. They suggested I call dish network. Dish Network told me to call corporate. So again I contacted Amazon only to be told to contact NBC. I tried, to no avail. How do I activate NBCSN? I am an Amazon Prime member and the only reason I purchased the Amazon Fire Tv stick was for NBCSN.

column2: Poor quality, commercial breaks bleed over game time
column3: The app forces me to activate it every time I use it.  I already activated it once and watched a stream so you'd think it would remember that.  Streaming quality isn't good and commercial breaks seem to get stuck on a black "coommercial in progress screen".  When stuck on the commcerial in progress screen the game continues behind the scenes so you end up missing parts of the game.  Honestly I hope NBC drops this app, I would prefer to continue watching my favorite hockey games on SlingTV but doubt that will happen.

column2: Good quality stable HD streams, easy to navigate on Fire TV
column3: This app works fine. The video quality is good. Slight motion blur, but this is common with all streaming apps. I'd really like a sports app in 1080@60hz, but I don't think we'll see this until ISP's stop capping bandwidth use.Also, I find it a little silly that people mark the app down because you need a cable subscription. This is a premium cable channel. Yes, you'll need to pay for it. Yes, even for the app. How could you expect anything different? What, they'll just give away their channel in an app when everyone else has to pay for cable to get it? What sense does that make? At least they don't charge you an extra monthly fee like so many other apps do. If you're already paying for the channel via cable, then you get it on mobile too. This is common sense and has nothing to do with how well the app itself works, which is actually quite good.

column2: Not happy. It would be nice to have clear app requirements & apps that actually work!
column3: It never worked. Signing up for some of these apps is very misleading. Prior to downloading,  the app does not tell you before you download it that you must have cable or satellite or a membership to Hulu or any of the other server type apps in order for the apps to work.  So it's a waste of time to download then set up the account and then find out at the end of setting up the account that you need one of these other services in order for the app to work. Apps need to be more upfront with what's required before you do all the downloads.

column2: Frequent verification and the interface needs work.

column2: Seems useless. Wouldn't work with Uverse

column2: Missed the end of a Double OT Playoff Game because of this app
column3: For the most part, this app is all right, but there are some serious issues with the continuity of streaming. It has spells where the streaming is very choppy and blurry, and it is completely unwatchable. This is NOT due to internet connection, because I have switched to other streaming apps and had no issues. Most recently, I've been watch the Stanley Cup Playoffs on the app. In the Ottawa-Boston series, the game was in double overtime, and they took a commercial break. After the commercials were finished it showed the "coverage will resume shortly" graphic. When the broadcast finally resumed, the Bruins were celebrating the game-winning goal. Whether this was negligence or some issue with the stream, it is unacceptable.

column2: I've rated this app poorly mostly due to terrible streaming performance
column3: I've rated this app poorly mostly due to terrible streaming performance. How I came to use this app and my experience is as follows: I recently gave traditional cable the boot and have been using PlayStation VUE for TV service. The most recent NASCAR race was not available on the NBCSN channel but was available through this app. I was curious how well this app would work for a live sporting event and decided to give it a shot. I searched for the app via Fire TV's universal search and was able to find it with ease. Upon installation you have to go through an activation process that requires you to prove you have a cable, or similar, provider; this is not unlike many other pay tv channel applications. Once I completed activation, via a computer, the app was instantly accessible. The interface is sparse yet straightforward and I was able to quickly find the race and stream it. Unfortunately, it would stream for about 5 minutes then pause and show a buffering icon, there was no way to get the content to continue streaming without restarting. Upon restart everything worked properly again... ...for about five minutes and then everything froze. I repeated this process four times with the same result. My Fire TV's WiFi signal is listed as, "very good," and other streaming services I use (Netflix, PlayStation VUE) worked fine. I was excited to give this application a try, but don't see it as a viable option for watching live content at this point.  I plan to test it again at some point and see if the experience changes.

column3: EDIT: dropping a star.  Was trying to use this to watch the Olympics, but the interface is really not good; a lot of events are labeled as "live," but then when you click on them you get a "slate" (TV jargon) about the event being over; every item you can select starts with a commercial, and then you watch the commercial and end up with a finished event or, often enough, video playback issues that require you to restart it (getting the commercial again) and then getting another fail.  Then there's the titles they were choose.... instead of X vs Y in SPORT as the title, they'd spoil it by saying X defeats Y in SPORT.  The only reason to get this app is because you have no other choices.It worked, and it's not terrible.  We watched the olympic opening ceremony last night; the video quality was generally very good, but there were occasional quality drops, and after some time we'd lose the stream entirely, causing us to go back to the home screen and re-select the video feed; it seems to always start off with a commercial - so you're missing content while you re-acquire the stream.This happened after a couple of hours, so I figured if it would stream that long without a glitch, then it's acceptable - but then it started happening more frequently.  After the third time we switched to another TV that had the cable box on it and just watched the rest uninterrupted.I'd give it one star if I were rating the coverage, though!

column2: The Content is not free, and I'm more than OK with that
column3: This is a great app, as it provides additional coverage and replays of sports from the NBC family of networks, where NBC is permitted by their contract with the leagues, associations, or other governing bodies to show them. During the English Premier League campaign, it's a handy app to have in case your team isn't playing one of the featured games. Olympic coverage has been great for watching replays of events that I missed or live events that aren't front line (Think Canada Ladies Football or Curling).Don't let most of the other reviews cloud your judgement, this provides quality playback for content that I pay for with a cable subscription. Most of the 1-star reviews have outlandish expectations that because the app is free, they should also be receiving content that is paid content elsewhere. The review pool is full of these ridiculous expectations.If you're trying to get NBC Sports content after cutting the cord, this isn't the app for you. They don't currently have a paid-subscription app, maybe try Sling TV if you're looking for access to the content.As for the performance, I'm on 100Mbps  internet provided by Optimum (also my TV provider), and very rarely have any issues playing back in HD (resolution dependent upon programming) while using a wired ethernet connection. Only during the Stanley Cup Playoffs did I encounter any technical issues, and that was with the placement (or misplacement) of digitally inserted ads during the course of play.Excellent Uses for the app:- Live Coverage of events not on broadcast channels- Replays- Making the channel portable to TVs without cable access (ie. Secondary Bedrooms, Travelling in hotels)

column2: A good start on an NBC sports app, but with plenty of room for improvement.
column3: The NBC sports app is a huge improvement over the prime-time coverage, but the app still needs work. It can be difficult to navigate among events; the olympics ended up being a single string of several thousand individual events, with no search option, and a paucity of informative labeling. To recognize the individual sports you had to identify the thumbnail image -- there was no accompanying text describing the event. Playback was generally good, with nice high resolution imagery, but from time to time the feed would fail or compression artifacts would interfere. I don't have any trouble with this streaming most video, so I have to assume it is the app or (more likely) the back-side server. There is no option to watch an event part way and then return to it at the same point, and searching and scrolling functions are awkward. Still, despite these problems, this is how I chose to watch the Olympics; the prime time broadcast is dead to me.
