I have a 10 month old Siberian Husky who already enjoys watching TV whether it's Animal Planet, National Geographic Wild or even a football game. In the right mood, she will watch any TV program, especially one featuring animals or dogs with a surprising amount of focus. We downloaded this app at about 2:30am on our Fire TV and woke her up from a pretty deep sleep just to see if it interested her. She watched for about 15 minutes straight until we made her go upstairs for bed (and turned it on up there).A lot of the negative reviews tend be from people's who's dog didn't care too much or that were having issues with the stream a couple years ago. From the hour or so we've had it on it works perfectly fine and offers on demand selections as well as live programming that fits the time of day. My dog personally couldn't take her eyes off the stimulation video and relaxation video we played when we first got it. The content certainly seems dog orientated which is neat. Lots of dogs eye view of everyday life, various dog clips, and relaxing scenery. I won't lie though, the overnight program is trippy but I guess if it works for dogs, it works. Certainly not made for human enjoyment though to be honest, I find it very interesting and find myself watching just to see what's next.If your dog already likes watching TV, they should like this. If not, they may not. But the service is what it is so I wouldn't be discouraged by the people leaving one star reviews just because their dog didn't care for it or because they thought a channel scientifically designed for dogs would interest them too.

I'm glad I'm in the free trial month or I'd be very angry to be paying $10 a month for a non-working service. We have highspeed internet and no network problems. This is definitely a product issue.

Silvy, a Great Pyrenees, responded with attention and interest to many of the clips. She looked attentively at the larger dogs and the scenes of travel, vistas, and moving shapes. The sounds seemed to calm her and to make her alert barking, a major characteristic of her breed, much less frequent. A good investment!

This is a waste of money, do not buy. You would do better turning on a free youtube video of dogs and just loop it. This service had a lot of kinda neon shading around stuff that caught my dogs attention for a minute of 2. That was it. They would show videos that were supposed to keep you dog engaged. Nope. One video was people walking around in China. No, not one dog, little sound, just people walking!! These videos are not for dogs, these are for the people with this app to take your money. Steer clear. Not worth it
I've used DogTV since their launch; it helps my dogs occupied and calm while I'm away and when I'm busy at home.In fact, I turn it on for me too. It calms me down; helps me focus on my work. :)

My dog gets sad when I go to work and nests in my bed. Well she developed the bad habit of ripping sheets... despite going for walks before I leave for work. So I bought a tv for the bedroom and got dogtv for her and she just loves it. I mean seriously. She watches it and loves it. The exposure part of the day where the content is designed to helping lessen doggie angst.... works. My girl used to run away from or attack the vacuum... now, she lays on the bed and just watches me. No freaking out!!!! It’s a good investment.

I have a high strung pom (imagine that) and when we moved to working from home we had a hard time adjusting.  DogTV made that so much easier!  Raja gets to play with his toys from 7:30-9:30, then I turn on DogTV and he LITERALLY watches the TV, then gets lulled into a mid-morning nap.  I get my morning calls/meetings done.  Then we have lunch playtime!  His sister, who just wants to be attached to me, isn't as into it, but for Raja is is perfect!  I donwloaded it on my Amazon Firestick and it is so easy to use!

column2: App needs a lot of work, not user friendly
column3: I wanted to like this service.  But it was glitchy, hard to understand the app to get it to work.  Multiple clicks to try to get the sections to activate.  I’m no slouch to understanding the works of most apps and services, but this one was pretty bad and unresponsive.  Maybe I should have asked my Border Collie.  I cancelled the service.  Maybe when they get their app working properly I might try again.

column2: I've enjoyed watching this with my pup
column3: My dog has watched this on occasion with me. The sounds are what seems to get her attention. It has worked to keep her occupied while I work from home in the evenings.Plus I honestly get a kick out of the videos sometimes too. The dogs look like they are having fun.

column2: Interesting concept; seems to help my dog
column3: We had 2 dogs and recently had to put one down.  Until we get another dog, DogTV seems to keep our dog "company" while we are away during the day.  We keep it on the live TV stream for him.  The images on the screen, the sounds, the voices... it seems soothing to him.  Definitely watch the overview/welcome video that explains the science/process involved in the programming.  Very nice that the first 30 days are free, but even after that when it starts costing $10 per month, we think it will be a worthwhile purchase if it helps to keep our dog comfortable without his sidekick.

column2: Make cheaper but it's great for my Blue Heeeler, Chihuahua mix and Parakeet
column3: My bird and dogs love this. I have a camera I check in on them and they will be laying on the couch watching this. Meanwhile, my bird is as well and tweeting away at it. Gave four stars because I feel it is a little expensinve, hence why I not longer subscribe; i cannot afford it.

column2: Fun for me and the dog
column3: I enjoy using the Dog TV. My dog is content to just listen. He seems so relaxed when I leave the house. He lays on the couch and listens to the music. I can play it on Fire Stick TV. I also play it on my desk too computer at night. It has nighttime TV with soothing sounds. It also helps them when storms are coming through, to have a little background music. I like watching it too. There are informational videos and educational ones as well.

column2: DogTV turned anxious pups into calm couch potatoes
column3: I have an anxious pittie and a mischievous beagle at home. Typically, they have humans since we also have a large family, but occasionally, we go where they cannot so they are left home. The first few times were hard, neighbors let us know of the pitties cries and the beagle howls. Also, they trashed the place.  We found don't and now when we have to leave them home, we come home to calm dogs. No more cries or howls and no more messes.

column2: Great, but needs IT to fix the bugs.
column3: Our dog loves Dog TV but it stops and buffers all the time and if you are not there with the remote to start it, then it's no use.  If we leave it on when we have to leave our dog home alone, we can check our security camera and it is always stopped within 10 or 15 minutes of us leaving.  It's not our internet since it doesn't do that when we watch a movie or binge watch a show.  Dog TV needs to fix the problem  or we will cancel.

We have a Wyze camera in our living room and turn Dog TV on when we go to work (our dog is home alone for about 3.5 hrs) and he loves watching Dog TV! The camera records motion and he constantly gets up to go up to the tv and puts his front paws onto the fireplace to try and get closer to the screen. It is super cute to watch and it seems to entertain him. He used to just lay by the front door and sleep and now he seems much more entertained while we’re away which were thankful for!

Loved loved loved this! My golden Henry gets so excited. His eyes couldn’t move fast enough to watch it all. He ran back and forth with the dogs and balls on tv. When we tried the relaxing videos he laid down and watched. So funny.

column2: Shocked that our boy actually pays attention
column3: We have a hyper active husky mix so I didn’t have high expectations for his interest in this but I gotta say he likes it...and I feel better throwing it on the living room tv while we’re at work and he’s waiting for the dog walker to come by, otherwise he just sleeps on the couch doing nothing but checking out pet cam I’ve seen his head up looking at the tv from time to time and it’s calmed him down when we’re home. That being said it onlyKeeps his attention for a minute or two at a time but he genuinely seems to like it

My dog and I like the app. I even purchased an annual subscription. The problem is that it only plays a few minutes at a time before crashing. I've cleared the cache, I've cleared the data, I've uninstalled and reinstalled, I've signed out and back in, and I've done every combination of the above. Nothing works. Fix the stability and I will gladly change my rating.*updated review - - They fixed it.

column2: She use to look like Cujo barking and trying to get to the other ...
column3: My dog loves to watch TV and she loves her dog TV. It has helped her anxiety so much when we go on walks. She use to look like Cujo barking and trying to get to the other dogs and that scared a lot of the people in our neighborhood. Since DogTV she has calmed down a lot.

column2: Needs more Dogs and Less Dogs POV camera shots.
column3: I think DOGTV is a great concept and would love to be able to give it a 5 star rating, however I sometime think they are trying to make the show more appealing to us humans instead of our four legged friends.  Maybe it’s just my Tamaskan dog Lyka, but she could care less about watching sceneries or even sceneries from a dog’s Point Of View (POV).  What catches Lyka’s attention is to see other dogs playing and the more dogs the merrier!

column2: I DID NOT ORDER DOGTV.  REMOVE FROM MY ACCOUNT IMMEDIATELY.
column3: Apparently, this is another channel/app like YouTube TV that makes it literally impossible to unsubscribe.  I love dogs, but I have no idea what content is worth $10 a month to amuse a pet.  I was curious -- I clicked on it and backed out immediately when I saw DogTV was not a free channel, but I bet I'll get charged for it anyway and have to fight with Amazon for the next 6 months to get charges removed.

The application itself is great - my dog does watch the shows. But for the price and the number of times a week that the service is "offline" ~ 2/4 times a week. Shutting off randomly throughout the day as well for server issues - its not worth the subscription fees. You can find the same materials on YouTube. I also find that putting on a stimulating children show does the same trick in keeping her attention.

column2: Dog TV menu did not function as-advertised
column3: After downloading the app we were given 3 options.  The 3 never provided a "gateway" for Dog TV to play & we could only watch 3 'commercials' for Dog TV.  Since we'd already downloaded & installed the app - this was kinda nonsense. No big deal - we hadn't heard of this app & only wanted to check it out.  Within 20 minutes on installing - we uninstalled this app.

column2: My dog seemed to lose interest
column3: At first I thought this was a great idea and my dog seemed to actually watch it. She wasn't one to ever notice the TV, so I thought this was going to be great. I put it on two TVs when I went to work and every time I wold peak in on the cameras she was in a different room looking out the window.I definitely think it is made for them and grabs their attention, I guess my dog just prefers to wait for the mailman or Amazon man rather than watch TV.

I love this for my dog and she loves watching it but the app crashes constantly. I've been emailing with the support team and they don't seem to know why it crashes but you can see from other reviewers that it is definitely an issue with a LOT of people. Such a shame since when it works it works SO WELL for my dog when she's home alone. If the technical issues are fixed I will definitely change my review to 5 stars

Check out the attached photo of my Miniature Schnauzer “Hubie.” He goes crazy when DogTV is on our 12 foot big screen.  He chases the other dogs, barks at them, and has a great time. I think DogTV is wonderful entertainment for a dog.

My Daisy loves watching DOGTV! The relation segments put her to sleep, and simulation and exposure videos hold her attention, and if I put it on before I leave the house, she seems much less anxious than usual when I come home! I have so many cute videos of her watching!

I absolutely loved this app. Have been using since May, however as of last week it has quit working. I get an error message saying I am already subscribed, but the app will not open. I have reset my Fire stick, removed and re-installed Dog TV and still have not had any luck. After reading many reviews, this seems to be a common issue. It's pretty unfortunate as this app was great for my dog.UPDATE as of 1/3/19: Well it got me again! Dog TV managed to function properly for 2 days then ONCE AGAIN suddenly stopped working. Extremely disappointed, when the product works it's great, but I give up.

Couldn’t resist trying out some new entertainment for my best friend at such an affordable rate and while working from home during the pandemic.  Absolutely love it!  DogTV has live feeds and a variety of programming for your bubba, including stimulation, relaxation and goodnight streams.  They also have informative and educational sessions for us pet parents.  We’ve even caught our kitten watching!

This was a TV channel it wasn't something to wear I wasn't impressed with it I couldn't get my dog interested in it I even sat here in front of the TV and forced him to watch it at least one episode he had no interest in looking at the TV or listening to anything on there sorry not a good fit for us!

column2: He ACTUALLY watches it and has a favorite "show"
column3: I was amazed that he ACTUALLY watches it! He even knows the sound of it coming on and runs to the tv! I did the free trial, but we will be keeping it. I haven't found a "repeat" feature yet; I hope there is one. I am about to return to work post COVID, and it would be a great addition to his "home alone" ritual.

column2: If you have dogs, DOGtv is 100% worth the cost!
column3: I try to keep the costs of my various monthly subscriptions down so I'm pretty damn picky in what I subscribe to. That said, this is a must for us. We have two German Shepherd mixes - one of which is incredibly vocal - but when we turn on DOGtv they are calm and relaxed within 3-4 minutes, watching all the dogs have fun on the big screen. =)

column2: Gets her attention and is to see her watching TV.
column3: Our Golden Retriever watches television very intently. she actually gets excited a certain parts of some of the videos. Everyone enjoys watching her very active viewing.  The only downside is that the available selection is limited and some scenes are looped repeatedly, so even a dog can get bored after while.

Dog loved it, the only problem was the price, I wouldnt pay that much for something the dog would probably get bored with, dogs mostly sleep and play, they don't sit around long enough to pay that much for a channel. Our dog watched for a few mins each time I put it on then fell asleep

column2: DOGTV has value far beyond the price point
column3: It is so easy to use on the Amazon platform.  I was very happy to find it is able to be used with my fire stick.  Now, no matter where I have my puppy, he will be able to watch and enjoy DOGTV.  The programming is educational as well as entertaining and relaxing for my dog.  My favorite thing about DOGTV is the color filter that is used and the attention grabbing sounds.  I have noticed such a difference in my puppy when I’m around or gone and have DOGTV on for him.  He is more calm, relaxed, plays with his toys when there’s stimulating programming and stays out of things he shouldn’t get in.  The value of DOGTV is immeasurable.Thank you so much to all the people that make DOGTV possible.

I originally downloaded this because I felt my dog needed more than a quiet house when I had to leave him home. They have a few 1 minute videos (like previews) but anything longer than that you have to pay for. Which wasn't stated before I downloaded it. It is very interesting and looks amazing, i just don't have the money to spend on all that.

column2: App Wants You To Pay Even If You Subscribe Through Another Provider
column3: Unlike most pay TV services, the DogTV app doesn't allow you to log in and watch via the app even if you have a paid subscription through another provider. If you are paying a monthly DogTV subscription through Dish Network, you shouldn't have to pay to watch through the app.

The idea is cute and I'd like to have something for our two pups to watch especially while out of the home. But the price is way too high. Not gonna happen here.The review options also needs work. As the categories "Thickness", "Warmth" & "Sheerness" have zero to do with a TV show for dogs.

column2: Works well on AppleTV but NEVER on Fire Cube!
column3: Just to let you guys know I’ve been dealing with same horrible things drops connection every few minutes on Fire Cube! Delete reset reinstall didn’t help. Finally downloaded to my AppleTV device and it works FINE so there’s clearly an issue with Amazon app! Works fine on laptop and phone too! So if you really love the content you’ll need to use on a different device! Frustrating but good to have the options! I have not tested yet on our Roku... but just do not use it on an Amazon device.

column2: Shuts off for no reason, overpriced.
column3: I was skeptical about this channel, as I am about most products claiming to be for dogs but are really designed for consumers. I was impressed by the content and that both of my dogs appeared to watch with interest. As other reviewers have stated, however, the app repeatedly shuts down, making it useless. A good idea, but not functional. And definitely not worth $10/mo when there are already animal-related channels that don't cost extra.

column2: Doesn't stream? too bad, they've got your money
column3: After about one month of back and forth with their tech support I requested to cancel my account, only to find out it is now just not auto renewed.  So I have a "streaming" app that I cannot use for another 10 months.  Loved the idea so I jumped in for the annual subscription price after the trial period - (which by the way worked perfectly, of course).  Buyer beware, very unstable app.  Didn't mind the price tag, if it would have worked.  AVOID, until they can get a handle on the bugs.

column2: They won’t cancel despite my request!
column3: What I thought would be a great idea to keep my pooch company, turns out my dog is terrified by the images on DOGTV and despite my written attempts to cancel, they keep billing. I even get billed TWO TIMES EVERY MONTH because I accidentally clicked the purchase button twice. I am beyond frustrated and only now realized there’s this review function. It might be good for somebody’s pet, but not mine. All I’ve received is acknowledgement of my request, no follow through. I don’t have $20 each month to throw away as I’ve never turned DOGTV on after the first day. Bummer.

Works wonders! We bought a dogtv subscription last month while my dog was in a cone, to keep her entertained but calm, and I was shocked by just how much she loves watching it. Curated and programmed by actual dog behavioral experts I read, so no wonder it's effective. Lots of videos for different thi6, including relaxation, stimulation, and calming. Also introduces your dog to new sights and sounds. My dog has opened up and become more inquisitive in the weeks since we subscribed. She loves it!

column2: One of my dogs loves it. He sometimes quietly ...
column3: One of my dogs loves it. He sometimes quietly watches the tv. Sometimes he jumps around and barks at the TV. My other dog could care less about it.

I really wanted to like this app and as a whole I do. My main issue that it continues to have playback issues. I’ll start the app and it will run fine for about 10-15 minutes and then stop and an error message appears. I have uninstalled several times and still have the same issue. I had to cancel my subscription. I don’t want to pay for something that isn’t working properly all the time. I’ll have to find something else to keep my dog calm while I am at work.

column2: Great Idea but it doesn't work
column3: As much as me and my dog love Dog Tv, it simply does not work on the firestick!  I am not sure if it is the same when you get it through your cable company but as of right now it is not worth the investment.  It keeps kicking me out and stating there was an "error in the playback", for the monthly fee I pay, I expect this to work. At this point, I am thinking of saving my $ and just playing the 15 hours dog tunes on youtube for free.

column2: Can't seem to get this channel
column3: Even though I subscribed with my Dish network subscription to date haven't been able to get this channel up and running. "Never fear when D is here" found an acceptable alternative, The Pet Collective, the girls just love the station!

Tried the free content to see if my dog would watch or listen to the channel. It caught his attention for about 30 seconds or less. That was it. He  pays more attention to the mailman. :) I enjoyed watching it more than him. oh well
I love this. I feel so much better leaving my babies with this channel on.
My dog watched it for hours.  The only reason I no longer have it is that I am traveling in a camper and don't always have reception.

Constantly buffering then just quits. They haven't addressed this since it first came out with the streaming opinion. My dog likes it but it's useless to leave on for her while I'm gone because it stops playing. Very disappointing.
This is fantastic for dogs with separation anxiety! Our dogs will watch by the hour and they do interact with it.

There's not enough room here for me to say everything that's good about DogTV. It works, my 6 dogs love it, they have stopped barking at birds & the neighbor's dogs barking, & it's wonderful to have on overnight for them.

column2: Not only does our dog love it,  our cat does too!
column3: We ordered DogTV for our dog who has a hard time resting during the day with noises going on outside. It's perfect to have on in the background while she rests. If they have a "Stimulation" program on the live feed,  we always have the option to turn on the "Rest" or "Relaxation" program on demand.  This was a huge selling point for us.  We rescued a cat 2 months back and found out that he loves it as much as our dog does! We have to wipe our TV screen off frequently now,  from him trying to bat the stuff around on the TV, but it keeps them both occupied. We highly recommend this!

column2: charges your card without your permission!
column3: First of all, It's a garbage app.secondly, I was charged for 3 months with no alert that a charge was being taken out of my account. there is no easy way to see this on the My Account screen, which leads me to believe that they are hiding these charging apps on purpose hoping customers wont notice

I believe it’s clickbait. I wanted to use this. They’re like oh it’s free and then you download it only to find out it’s a recurring monthly subscription fee. Easier just to turn on YouTube and find tons of videos of dog playing.

column2: This was an accidental purchase.  We hope you will drop it from our account.
column3: Our dog was not attracted to the television.  On occasion he will respond to a dog barking on TV and always responds to doorbell rings on TV.  At 11 years old, I don’t think he is going to change.

It's mostly a lot of people just walking dogs with some music, occasional squeaky toy sounds, and at some points, a whining dog - which is annoying.  One of my dogs did look at it, but then went to look out the window instead.  If it was free, I might consider keeping it (probably would not), but for $10 a month, it's definitely not something I feel is worth the cost.

I've been billed for this since summer. I don't have access to it on any of my devices. No matter how many times I go to their website to try to log in it doesn't recognize me. Subscribing to this is dangerous
My dog and I watched the trailers and she was hooked! I’m so excited!

column2: This is definitely made for dogs!!
column3: My dog absolutely love watching dog tv!  I love the fact that it it continuous and you don’t have to worry about it stopping when you are not home.  It definitely captures her attention.  I sometimes find myself watching it with her. Also, It makes me less anxious leaving my dog alone. Now I can just put on dog tv and know my dog is content on the house.
We can't even get it to run our free month! It keeps repeating the sign up thing!
Perfect for animal lovers and it is children friendly.

column2: Great content, love DOGTV, app needs some love.
column3: First let me say that I absolutely love the content in the firetv app for DOGTV.  My dogs are even more well mannered just by having DOGTV on for them.  I use to have other calming stations on for them but there is something better with DOGTV.  Now the reason for the three stars is because I use to have DOGTV through DIRECTV and it ran beautifully and the FireTV app will pause a few times and then go back to the main DOGTV screen.  This doesn’t help me at all when I leave for work at 20 minutes after it is back on the app screen.  I will update the ratings if the app can get fixed.  Other apps run just fine and don’t cut off on FireTV.  Please help my girls enjoy DOGTV more.

It's a cute idea but there isn't much for the dog to watch. There was maybe 6 videos and 1 live channel for dogs specifically. Most of it is geared towards humans. It also did not keep my dogs interest at all. I tried to show her things, I turned the volume up loud, I even said "look doggie" and then she would just run to the window. Very difficult to find where to go to cancel subscription for free trial.

I have purchased several of these to use for a variety of set ups to secure my dog. Perfect for hotel balconies to keep your furby from slipping between the railings! If I choose to do so, i could attatch them together and have a gigantic playyard for kids or pets! In fact I have three connected together as a barrier fence to separate my front and back living spaces and they each have their gate opening for easy access.

I use to love this channel for my dogs. When I moved I cancelled and then tried to reactive it but when I tried it said I already had a subscription. Then when I went back it still said I needed a subscription. I just saw on Amazon subscription “apps” that I have been billed for this service every month since August.
Sucks!!! It doesn't offer anything but what should be commercials. If there is anything else, you can't see it unless you pay. I don't pay for things that I know nothing about.

column2: Looking and listening to what is in this app
column3: I thought it would be a free channel so my dogs would feel comfortable when we leave to go someplace.  I didn’t think it was worth it, I did even get a sample of what to expect.

I don’t know if the dog would enjoy this or not because it stops playing within a few minutes - repeatedly gives Playback Error message.  I have spent over an hour restarting the video, but it doesn’t play long.  Not worth the time I invested and definitely not worth $9.99 a month!

Our dogs & cat watch. Good for separation anxiety. The color is automatically adjusted so your pet can see it the way they need to. Your pet can best view it using HD, or 4k or better, though there are a lot of just soothing sounds.

column2: Nearly no content, would be ok as a one time charge
column3: There is basically no content for the app and it's pretty insanely expensive to have a monthly fee without any, but it'd be great if there were more since our dogs seemed to enjoy it.

Unfortunately, I have to give Dog TV 1 star.  Please don't get me wrong, I truly Dog TV!  I am subscribed to it via my cable provider.  My toy poodle Sonny love watching it!  It is just that it doesn't work on my fire TV stick.  It is always crashing and I always have to keep subscribing to it.  It is not accessible to blind users.  I use the voice View feature on my fire stick.  As far as the programing, It is  great and does keep your dog happy, and relaxed.  I really hope that they do fix the app soon.

Dog TV isn't just for dogs! As much as it keeps my 2 mutts engaged. The kitten likes it too. They see much like dogs do.I have noticed a calmness in my puppy since we started leaving Dog TV on for him during the day. Even some of the programming we enjoy. I highly recommend giving it a try in your home.

Dog tv has been a godsend for me! I’m now working from home because of this virus, and I have an Australian Shepard puppy, and that guy can get rowdy! When mama needs to work or make a call, I just turn dog tv on, and he settles in to watch his favorite show!!! This has been the miracle I needed!

column2: Humans and Dogs Enjoy Dog TV
column3: My dogs enjoy watching and/or listening to Dog TV.  I put on their channel whenever I leave them home alone.  We also watch it together to get away from regular tv and all the conflict in the world these days.  I find it quite relaxing!  The Dog TV Challenge gave me interesting tips on getting my dogs to be more engaged in their programming.

column2: DO NOT USE THIS APP - horrible billing practices.
column3: Horrible app - awful billing practices.  I purchased via Amazon and now they are billing my credit card as well for the same purchase in addition to monthly charges they've billed me annually as well.  DECEPTIVE.  Unless you want to go legal don't waste your time with this horrible company.

column2: Free version isn't what you will ever use
column3: I downloaded the free version to try it out and was sadly disappointed.  It may be good for some but do be able to have any features, you will have to pay for this.
Love this. We have dogs and have used this quite abit. My dog also has anxiety when we're fine so well put this on sometimes or one of her favorite movies

column2: The channel needs a wider variety of programs.
column3: The channel needs a wider variety of programs. I was surprised that many lasted less than 5 minutes.  The library must need populated from you tube. I couldn't find very many different programs. All their shows can be seen during 7 day trial period.

column2: .....Would be great if these dog shows were really free.
column3: ......I thought they were free, but you must pay for this service.......My dog could watch hours of free dog  videos on "You Tube " for free.

column2: Amazon: let us know when you lower the price for this.
column3: We watched the preview options and while we can tell that our dog watched  some of the content, we just cannot justify paying $10 a month for an app. A one time fee makes more sense.  Similar content can be found for free on YouTube. Amazon: you've got to lower the price if you want people to subscribe.
This is not free! You get a quick video on why it works and a quick free vid sample.  Then, there's a subscription charge. That should have been said on the download screen. Smh.

I took a look at it because I was interested in what kind of programs there are that my dog may find interesting. I was mostly looking for something to turn on for him when I'm not home. But $9.99 per month is more than I pay for any of my TV apps. I can't see paying that monthly price for something that won't be on very often.

Dog likes this app but it keeps kicking me off and asking me to sign in and it says not valid! Before that it kept having to be uninstalled and reinstalled do to error messages. App doesn’t work constantly!!
After thinking i wanted to get DogTV i found out that there is a 9.99 a month charge after the initial period...for this reason i decided not to continue

I do have a trial subscription to DOGTV, it appears to only work in the Silk Browser through DOGTV website, too much trouble starting the browser and logging in, although my pup appears to love watching it. Too bad this company doesn't invest any effort in a easy to use Fire TV app.

I was never able to watch even 5 seconds...for whatever reason, couldn't get the app to work on my smart TV after multiple attempts.  Message on screen kept saying something was wrong with the servers and to try again later.

Terrible. Paid for a one month subscription and cancelled. Extremely limited content.- I honestly thought this could not possibly be the content.  My dog was not the least bit interested and the repetitive music just annoyed me. Absolutely not worth the subscription fee.

I love watching this with my dog. Not only is it great to keep your dog or dogs occupied but it has all different material that they play. After watching it many times there is deffinatly a wide variety of content on there. I would highly recommend to anyone who leaves there dogs home alone for a while!
Its like cat nip for dog. I dont know how it works. High saturated colors and ambient sounds makes my dog come out of nowhere and sit right in front of the tv. Its hilarious

the UX is a little clunky. Some basic concept information would go a long way to validating the merits of the service, as well as pushing justifiably toward a premium option. Sadly, nothing there.

column2: A great station for my Grand-dog
column3: My grand-dog loved watching this station. He watched it whenever his family went out. Sometimes he watched it with his family together. I think it's a great station. However, when I tried to set it up on my TV, for some unknown reason to me, I had a frustrating experience and was not able to watch it. I've found an alternative. I'm sorry.
Would rate 0 stars if I could because such BS to find they’re just hunting for subscription fees. Not paying for this ridiculousness.

column2: Didn't keep app long enough to rate it fairly

We have a 4-year old rescue dog from Tennessee who has been living with us in NYC now for almost a year. She struggled a lot with separation anxiety, boredom, and exposure to loud sounds early on which naturally improved with time and trust. I only wish we knew about DOGTV then! Our girl just loves it. During the "Relaxation" programming she mostly just naps, but she is so attentive during the "Stimulation" and "Exposure" programs. It's hilarious to watch her staring.  We play the programs intermittently when I'm tidying up the house or when we leave her alone for a little while. I will admit that some of the sounds in the background can get a little annoying after awhile (phone ringing, birds chirping, babies crying, etc.) but it's totally worth it to see our girl so happy. I've been recommending it to all my dog owner friends.

column3: This app took a couple seconds to review my Fire tablet files, which takes all other apps several minutes.  That seems odd, too fast to be accurate.  Then it told me I had 3 GB of space to be freed up and 4 viruses that need to be removed. All for the bargain price of $4.29 to buy the actual app that does anything. Bait and switch at it's finest.  I find it strange that I suddenly have 4 viruses that have never been found by any of the various, well trusted, virus and malware apps I currently use.  Especially since they were found in a 2 second scan.  The only way to get ANY more information is to buy the upgrade.  Let's look at the 3 GB of space that I will "free up".  I know that by doing so I will loose a great deal of data that I very much want to hold onto!  I have had this happen to me in the past and it took me weeks to replace all the side loaded music that was deleted.  Please be sure you know what will be deleted, and you are okay with it, before clicking the button to free up that much space.I was hoping for a free app that would do what others will do.  I don't need to pay over $4 for a solution that is offered for free, actually free, elsewhere.  There are a lot of great apps out there and they deliver what they promise.  I just wish more developers worked that way.  Most people don't mind paying for a quality app.  I don't mind either if the real price is stated up front.

column2: A Potentially Useful Utility - Especially for Tablets with Less RAM Memory
column3: It is difficult to give a product like this a fair evaluation when it is installed on a new device that is functioning properly. Temporary files are constantly created and usually mostly eliminated by the programs you are using as they are terminated. Unfortunately not all programs are well behaved and some leave stray temporary data behind. A program that is not properly shutdown can likewise leave garbage behind. The net effect is that the programs have less ram memory to operate in which can lead to slower performance. If this program is performing  as its creator claims, it should maintain a better over all level of performance.  The best way to test how well this program works is to download the free version and run the scan. Write down the results. Periodically rerun the scan (especially if you have down loaded programs, games or surfed the web). If the scan is valid the amount of garbage files should gradually increase. If it appears to be finding an increase in garbage files then it is probably not a scam. If the free scan always gets exactly the same results even after relatively heavy and varied use I would definitely question its worth. Hopefully this procedure will allow you to prove for yourself whether or not this program is a scam.

Bait and switch!Looks at your kindle and then tells you that you have to download another app you pay for to get it to do anything.My Kindle Fire HD 8 (Fifth Generation) is dyingMy constant companion, my Kindle Fire is in its death throes. It is very sad to watch.I bought my first Kindle (the generation 3) in late 2010 and immediately fell in love with it. I loaded it up with Amazon’s E-books. It was only black and white with limited internet capability but it was a great device. I really liked the chicklet style keyboard. I still have that first kindle today and it is still working. What a fun device!  On the 28th of September 2011, I upgraded to the new Kindle Fire Full Color 7” with Multi-touch display and Wi-Fi. This gave me greater connectivity to the internet and the books were slightly easier to read. Finally, in 2013 I ordered the latest Kindle Fire HD 8 (Fifth Generation) which had better contrast and an 8.9” screen. Amazon also claimed that it had 15% faster page loads. It has a 167 PPI display and was the lightest Kindle at 5.98 ounces until 2016's Kindle Oasis. This is the one that became my companion. This is the one that is dying at three years old, a mere child. We will get to the culprit who I accuse of committing this slow, painful and tortuous death in just a minute.On the 14th of December this year Amazon sent out an update Fire OS 5.3.2.1. This free software update added the Amazon “Rapids” app plus some other general improvements and performance enhancements. Well, since I hadn’t ordered the “Rapids” app, just before Christmas (22 December 2016), I decided to uninstall the app. My Kindle Fire, which had been operating beautifully in all modes before, now began to display some quirkiness. Just minor annoyances at first: a very slight delay when calling up a book, the battery recharging at a bit slower speed, auto-connect to my Wi-Fi was intermittent, and my Tumblr App was failing to load pictures. Then I made my first mistake (that day). In order to uninstall the “Rapids” app I went through the normal “uninstall” procedure and found that I could not uninstall or delete the “Rapids” app. I decided I needed a stronger uninstaller and went on the Amazon web site and downloaded an “uninstaller” app. When that didn’t work I decided that perhaps I needed a virus checker and malware cleaner. So I went back to the Amazon web site and ordered Malware and Virus Cleaner for Fire devices (OxCleaner) as soon as I ran this one it showed I had several pieces of Malware, Megabytes of trash, and 97 virus errors on my Kindle. For just $4.49 -- it recommended that I down load another app Malware and Virus Cleaner to actually clean up my Kindle. Yet another app Optimizer & Trash Cleaner Tool for Kindle Fire Tablets was also recommended to clean the “trash” as well as the viruses. Like a fool, I bit on this deal and downloaded the $4.49 program. I ran it and within seconds it came back to inform me that everything was “hunky dory” – my Kindle was “good to go”. Suddenly, I noticed my Kindle battery was draining much faster than usual but besides that everything seemed okay. Just to make sure I performed a 40 second off/on switch reset to give my Kindle a fresh start.Shortly after this I noticed that one of my books did not open and I called an Amazon Customer service representative. Julius D. was extremely helpful and very patient with me and we spent nearly an hour on the phone as he guided me through several attempts to fix my Kindle. The only area he seemed unfamiliar with was what the “Rapids” app was and how to uninstall it. Outside of that he took me through nearly every procedure possible to fix the device except a total factory reset. After that I contacted two other customer representatives who were unable to provide a satisfactory explanation for how to get rid of “Rapids”. It was then that my Kindle began to die. In its death throes it constantly threw up black screens; it seemed to take forever to go from one screen to the next and often just went to black screen; the battery would drain in a matter of minutes and recharging took hours; I had to re-download books that had been there before, it began struggling to open a book and my little kindle just went to a white or black screen. (Choke!) In spite of all the problems I began experiencing with other programs, the persistent “Rapids” app just stayed where it was and it would open intermittently. I began to conclude that the “Rapids” app was the culprit that was killing my kindle. I ‘asked’, no,  ‘pleaded’ with several customer service representatives to delete this app. Amazons policy was that if they put this poison app on my kindle there was absolutely NO way to remove it. This was the first time since I had signed in to Amazon since 1994 that their customer-centric commitment failed. It had failed totally and now my faithful companion, my Kindle, was dying a slow and excruciating death. It had taken the poison pill and there was no antidote. “Good bye, Kindle I loved you with all my heart.”Yes, I am buying a new one, but it is just so very sad to see an old friend go.

column2: A good security camera monitor that takes technical skill to use and set up.
column3: This app allows you to monitor your video security system at home.  Please be aware that if you are not on a WIFI you are using your mobile device’s data plan and you may be using a lot of data transferring videos and photos.  You can actually make your Android device a mobile DVR.  Remember.  Don’t forget your data plan limits.I own and use multiple security camera and DVR systems within my home that monitor and record the video on internal hard disk drives.  All of them are accessible via the internet and WIFI as they all come with their own Apps that allow interfacing to my Android and Apple devices.  This software is thus redundant for me to use.When I first scanned my network for cameras the system found none.  It is because it was on the wrong WIFI network and I had to change the WIFI settings for my Samsung tablet to the same network that the security system is on.  If you can’t find your camera you have to go to your smart device settings and change the network access.  If you have not used that WIFI on your device you will have to know the SSID and the password for that WIFI system to sign on.Once I scanned the right network the system found my servers, security cameras and my ubiquity Network system.  I logged into the Foscam system and the app then asked me what the camera password was.  Remember you can lock your security DVRs and even individual cameras for privacy and you will have to know that data to sign on.  Upon entering the correct data the camera location popped up and displayed the camera’s live video.By tapping on the live video I was able to see the camera video full screen and touch the record icon and record the video.  You are also able to use the camera motion detection systems to minimize the amount of transferred data and only collect data when movement is present and being monitored.The benefit of this app is that you may be able to combine multiple camera networks into one app for monitoring and checking.  Just be aware that if you are not on the same WIFI network the ability to see the video may be blocked by your cable modem.  That is a long discussion and it is not possible to cover here. You can possibly even add in local camera if you have their IP address like a local school or weather network.  As part of a demo you can see random action cameras working around the world that are public for example.This is a nice app but again I warn you to be aware of your mobile data plan limits.  If you are not on a WIFI you could be using up your expensive data plan and get a big mobile bill from your supplier.  It will take some skill to connect and use this app and you should be aware of that requirement.  The app does work and deliver what it promises.Permissions:• Record audio• Modify or delete the contents of your USB storage• Full network access• View network connections• Draw over other apps• Control vibration• Prevent tablet from sleeping• Install shortcutsThis app contains adware using Google Mobile Ads (AdMob).  Google Analytics is integrated into the AdMob interface, giving the developer powerful and deep insights into their customer database.  It also contains and uses Dropbox while it states the app does not use 3rd parties to send file and data?  Dropbox is used to transfer larger files between locations using the internet and Dropbox services.  The app also uses HockyApp which is an Analytics program aimed at beta testing that can monitor the user and determine language used, device type and other data.  HockeyApp is owned by Microsoft.The app installed 16.59MB into my device memory.  I moved it to my SD card and it left 5.75MB in my device memory and it transferred 14.25MB onto my SD card.

I like being able to press a button to have it discover all of the cameras on my network. The only problem I have with this is that it will use the local IP address to add it. If you plan to use the app away from home (outside of wifi range), you'll need to adjust the (advanced) IP settings accordingly. Also depending on your home setup, you may have to forward a couple ports etc.The PTZ (pan tilt zoom) is great -- you can use a single-button option, where you press and it moves a little, or you can use what I'll call a "continuous" version where you swipe and control the movement more fluidly.I really like having almost ALL of the same options the manufacturer's own software provides. Kudos to the developers on a great product!I received this product for free around June-ish -- I can't remember if it was an Amazon promotion or one from the developer. I only was able to review it now since I only now have compatible IP cameras. With that said, trying to add a camera that isn't network-discoverable (through the built-in search option) offers plenty of manufacturers. column2: Glitches and No Response From Support - UPDATE
column3: UPDATE - I raised my review by one star, as the App was updated and I reinstalled it to test the newer version. Some of the cursor navigation glitches have been fixed. The interface seems a bit more responsive now and the focus follows the command accurately. Now you can actually edit your individual camera setup details.The frame rate is still very slow and suffers from drop-outs despite being used in a Gbit wired LAN.This App is not ready for prime time in my opinion. It has numerous glitches, such as the inability to get to certain options from the camera setup menu (the cursor just jumps up to the header instead of going "right"), and the "back" button doesn't always go back or to where you expect it to take you.Also, when you change some options, the changes do not "stick", so when you go back to that screen, it is not configured as you expected, but has defaulted to a different value.I wrote an email to the 'support" developer, but all I got was crickets.Maybe if you have a really simple system, this might work for you, but on my 6 camera setup, it's slow, buggy, and crude. I'm going to uninstall it.
